articleTitle: Classification of Dongting Lake Wetland Using Time Series Sentinel-1 Radar Data
abstract: Wetland classification using multi-temporal remote sensing data and the similarity matching of characteristic curves has attracted attention. This paper analyzes the time series Sentinel-1 data, and proposes a wetland classification method based on similarity matching of time series curves, which are described from shape and distance, and constructs a multi-dimensional similarity evaluation index. The initial result is obtained according to the minimum distance of the time series curve. Then, using local time change boundary constraints, the results are optimized. The research area is the Dongting Lake Beach Wetland, and the Sentinel-1 GRD data of 2020 is collected using Google Earth Engine platform. Comprehensive evaluation of Canberra's distance and cosine angle can improve the accuracy of woodland and reeds; The boundary constraints of changes from January to February can improve the error of water bodies being divided into mudflats. The overall accuracy in this paper can reach 89.5%, which is higher than the random forest. In this study, only a small number of samples were used to map the distribution of wetlands with 10 meters resolution in Dongting Lake, which can provide decision-making opinions for the early warning, prevention, protection and restoration of ecological risks in the lake area.

articleTitle: A differential SAR Tomography inversion method based on Distributed Compressive Sensing
abstract: Over the last 20 years, SAR Tomography has emerged as one of the most powerful tools to map and monitor the 3D/4D structure of the earth surface, especially for complicated urban scene. Corresponding reconstruction algorithms have been evolving toward higher accuracy and finer resolution. Conventional spectrum estimation methods, i.e., plain Fourier transform, Capon filtering, MUSIC, SVD etc., suffer from limited baseline span and irregular spatial sampling. Whereas Compressive Sensing (CS) based methods i.e., standard CS method, Distributed Compressive Sensing (DCS) method, Multi-look Compressive Sensing method (MCS), can achieve much higher accuracy and super-resolution by exploiting sparsity or multi-looking. In a complicated urban scene, pixels of different characteristics correspond to different optimal CS-based methods. To achieve the best comprehensive reconstruction result for a whole scene, an adaptive selection of methods based on analysis of pixel scattering characteristics is proposed. Real data experiment is conducted on 31 TerraSAR-X/TanDEM-X strip mode images, and result comparison with the well-known SL1MMER algorithm has validated the proposed method.

articleTitle: Identification of Coal and Gangue via Millimeter Wave Imaging with Corresponding Optical Photo
abstract: The identification of the coal and gangue are essential in the coal preparation process. Combining with imaging processing technologies (like de-noising, enhancement, and feature extraction), the imaging-based technology accomplishes the coal-gangue identification while avoiding the shortcomings of traditional methods (radiation, pollution, etc). However, environment factors (light, dust, temperature, etc) would greatly influence the identification results. A millimeter imaging combining with the optical photo technique is proposed for the recognition of coal and gangue. First, the millimeter wave (MMW) imaging results of the ores are achieved by the Range Migration Algorithm (RMA). Second, the profiles of the ores in the corresponding optical photo are adopted by the Seeded Region Growing (SRG), which are transferred to the MMW images for further identification. Furthermore, a simple threshold-based strategy is applied to compute the coal ratio of each ore to achieve the identification. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed strategy is of great potential for nondestructive identification of coal from the gangue.

articleTitle: Visualization of Human Posture Based on Radar Time-Frequency Spectrogram
abstract: Visualization of human postures is of great significance for research in areas such as autonomous driving, smart home monitoring and AR human interaction. However, RGB cameras and two-dimensional radar arrays commonly exploited for visualization of human postures have problems such as susceptibility to environmental interference and high cost. Based on this, the paper proposes a method to visualize human postures using radar time-frequency time-frequency spectrograms. A stepped-frequency continuous wave (SFCW) radar is needed to obtain radar time-frequency spectrograms in one direction, which realizes the visualization of human postures from the initial state of human and radar time-frequency time-frequency spectrograms. Experimental results demonstrate that this algorithm effectively solves the problem of using multiple radar information to visualize human postures.

articleTitle: Joint Route Optimization and Multi-Dimensional Resource Management for Multiple Airborne Radars System in Target Tracking
abstract: In this article, a joint route optimization and multi-dimensional resource management (JRO-MDRM) scheme is developed for multiple airborne radars system in target tracking application. The basis of the proposed scheme is to minimize the target tracking error and probability of intercept of the underlying system in the meantime by jointly optimizing the route planning, transmit power, dwell time, waveform bandwidth, and pulse length of each airborne radar node subject to certain system constraints. Since the corresponding variables are coupled in both objective function and constraints, and the resulting optimization model is non-linear and non-convex, an efficient solution algorithm, incorporating particle swarm optimization and cyclic minimization techniques, is put forth to deal with the above optimization problem. Simulation results illustrate the effectiveness of the developed JRO-MDRM scheme.

articleTitle: Tracking Stream Quality Issues in Combined Physical and Radar Sensors for IoT-based Data-driven Actuation
abstract: In this paper, a stream quality tracking for measurements from combined radar and physical sensors is developed. The authors proposed the use of RDF stream processing system and semantic rules to provide semantic reasoning for tracking erroneous data points from real time sensor readings. We demonstrated the effectiveness and the efficiency of the approach using the dataset produced from smart home project. Experiments were conducted with simulated arbitrary sensor values for inconsistent and missing sensor readings at various data points. The results was able to show the feasibility of the approach and that quality requirement of sensor streams can be verified at lower granularity level (data layer) of smart actuators.

articleTitle: The RCS calibration method for on-orbit Lungeberg lens reflector
abstract: We propose a RCS calibration technique based on the on-orbit Lungeberg lens reflector, and studied the method of calibrating the observation angles between the radar and the satellite based on the measured data. The calibration accuracy is verified in the experiments, and can be controlled under 0.7dBsm. The work promotes the effective calibration and accuracy evaluation for ground-based radars.

articleTitle: Hybrid Beamforming for Minimum Outage via Stochastic Approximation
abstract: We consider an outage based approach for hybrid beamforming where the channels are modeled as random vectors drawn from an unknown distribution. Our formulation can be applied to both point-to-point transmit beamforming as well as single-group multicasting scenarios. In this paper, the way to design the hybrid precoder is first to design a fully digital (FD) precoder dropping the hybrid structure constraints, and then, with the desired FD precoder, to design the hybrid solutions employing a delicate mapping strategy. Numerical results are included to illustrate the effective performance of our methods.

articleTitle: Accurate Doppler Model Analysis of Geosynchronous SAR
abstract: In order to reduce the difficulty of imaging in geosynchronous synthetic aperture radar (GEO SAR), it is necessary to maintain the zero-Doppler centroid throughout the whole satellite orbit, which can be realized by adjusting the radar line of sight (RLS) in real-time. Considering the ultra-long synthetic aperture time of GEO SAR, the variation of RLS within the synthetic aperture cannot be ignored. Focusing on this problem, an accurate Doppler model of GEO SAR is proposed to accurately calculate the Doppler parameters. Finally, the effectiveness and necessity of the proposed model are verified by simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Task Allocation Optimization for Multi-Target ISAR Imaging in Radar Sensor Network
abstract: Inverse synthetic aperture radar imaging techniques, which can provide the fine structure of the targets for subsequent identification, have been a hot topic in recent years. When multiple targets appeared in the detection coverage of the radar sensor network, it is necessary to study the task allocation strategy of the multi-target inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging tasks to obtain high-quality ISAR images under the limited radar resources. Obviously, there are competitions among the targets for radar resources to obtain high-quality ISAR images. The purpose of the task allocation optimization game is to accomplish the multi-target ISAR imaging tasks with higher quality under limited radar resources. After analyzing the relationship of ISAR image quality and radar resource, the task allocation optimization problem can be constructed as a non-cooperative game problem, where the targets are the players. Then a genetic algorithm is applied to search the optimal solution of the game, where is also termed as Nash equilibrium solution. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An IF Module for Hyperspectral Microwave Radiometer
abstract: In this paper, an IF (intermediate frequency) module of hyperspectral microwave radiometer is presented, including its structure, components and specifications. And what's more, a key technology to optimize FPGA resources in FFT algorithm is also proposed. Test results show this IF module works very well and can also be used in many other remote sensing application.

articleTitle: Polarimetric Characteristic Analysis of Complex Marine Aquaculture in Sanduao Coastal Zone
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data make up for the deficiency of visible light data in marine aquaculture monitoring due to its imaging characteristics. However, the characteristics of marine aquaculture can not be effectively extracted by single polarization and multi polarization data. In this paper, Freeman polarization decomposition is utilized to extract the characteristics of full-polarimetric GF-3 and radarsat-2 data. We analyze the polarization characteristics of complex marine aquaculture in dense marine aquaculture area and the factors affecting the effect of polarization characteristics. Finally, we set threshold according to the polarization characteristics of marine aquaculture and extract the floating raft aquaculture and cage culture in Sanduao coastal zone.

articleTitle: The Radar-Communication Integration based on the Frequency Diverse Array Beampattern
abstract: In this paper, the transmit beampattern of frequency diverse array (FDA) is used to realize the integrated function of radar and communication. The focused mainlobe and suppressed sidelobe of the beampattern are used to detect the target to realize the radar function. The phase of the sidelobe at the communication position is precisely controlled to embed the communication information, so as to realize the communication function. Different from the phased-array, the FDA is utilized here, thus the beampattern should be decoupled and optimized on the angle-distance dimensional space to approach the desired beampattern. By taken the frequency increments between the FDA antennas as the optimization variables, a beampattern optimization problem is formulated, and the genetic algorithm (GA) is utilized to solve it. The proposed FDA-based beampattern scheme can improve the security of communication due to the two-dimensional information transmission. Simulation results verify the effective of the proposed radar-communication integration scheme.

articleTitle: Computational interpretability of multilayer preceptron used for SAR image target recognition
abstract: The achievement of deep neural networks (DNNs) in the computer vision has aroused great concerns in the synthetic aperture radar (SAR) automatic target recognition (ATR) field. As a simple but effective model, the multilayer perceptron (MLP) is widely used in SAR image target recognition. However, the black-box problem could limit the development of DNNs in SAR ATR. In this paper, we explore the interpretability of MLP from the perspective of computation process of its forward propagation. By using the matrix representation, the function is studied that the angles between parameters and features as well as features magnitudes. Besides, the feature statistics is adopted to discuss the effect of nonlinear activation functions. Finally, some experiments on the MSTAR datasets are carried out and analyzed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Extended SPICE Algorithm Based on the Group Sparse Model
abstract: In this work, an improvement of the SPICE algorithm based on the group sparse regression problem is proposed. By applying the group sparse array model, an improved covariance fitting criterion is obtained, thereby avoiding cumbersome model order estimation. The algorithm can be iteratively decomposed into a group of convex optimization problems, and each problem can be solved in a closed form. In addition, through simulation experiments, we have obtained the relationship between the algorithm grouping and the number of grids and verified that the angle of arrival of the incident signal is in the same group and in different groups. The numerical results show that the algorithm has a good estimation performance.

articleTitle: UAV Swarm SAR New Concept and Fast Time Domain Imaging Algorithm
abstract: Due to the weak battlefied survival capability and angle of view absent, conventional single platform unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) SAR application can hardly form compr ehensive observation for a long during time. UAV swarm (UAVS) SAR application is a new application of SAR imaging. However, considering UAVS-SAR multi-platform configuration, coherent processing needed performed both in a time interval and even between different UAV platforms. Existing both frequency-domain algorithm (FDA) and time-domain algorithm (TDA) are unable to realize coherent processing on time and spatial dimension efficiently. In this paper, a new concept of UAVS-SAR configuration is proposed, and based on which a fast time-domain algorithm is developed for UAVS-SAR imaging. Finally, the simulation experiment are applied to validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed algorithm.

Author Keywords: unmanned aerial vehicle swarm synthetic aperture radar (UAVS-SAR)

articleTitle: Target Level Change Detection in Multi-temporal SAR Images Based on Prior Position
abstract: Change detection of target level in SAR images is an interesting topic, which can be used in many important applications. In view of the image processing problem of target change detection, especially the practical problem of analyzing the target change information quickly in multitemporal spaceborne SAR images, this paper puts forward a method to detect the SAR image targets quickly in different periods based on the prior information of target location. In this method, a large number of SAR images are observed to analyze the probable positions of the targets. In the test images, we only need to detect targets and detect the change of targets in prior positions. This paper analyzes the increase, decrease, and relative position change of the target in the next time relative to the previous time from the perspective of quantity and position. Compared with the true value of real images change detection, this method can achieve 89.6% accuracy.

articleTitle: ESPRIT-enhanced Method for DOA Estimation with Acoustic Vector Sensor Array
abstract: This paper discusses the direction of arrival (DOA) estimation by using an acoustic vector sensor array, and proposes an Estimating Signal Parameters via Rational Invariant Technique (ESPRIT) enhanced method which can improve the DOA estimation performance. Specifically, by exploiting the rotation invariance of the received signals, the initial DOA estimates can be obtained using the ESPRIT method. Then, by performing Taylor expansion and total least squares methods on the initial estimates, the offsets can be compensated and fine estimates can be obtained. Simulation results show that the proposed method can successfully estimate the DOA using an acoustic vector sensor array and can achieve better estimation performance than the traditional ESPRIT method.

articleTitle: A High Integrated 3d Packaged 64-Channel TR Module
abstract: A 3D packaged 64-channel TR modul with high integration is proposed in this paper. The power divider units, multifunctional chip, three-stage amplifier, attenuator, phase shifter and single pole double throw switch circuits are integrated in a multi-chip module (MCM) with monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) and surface mount technology (SMT). Multi-layer microwave board is used to implement the routing of DC, control and RF signals. The RF adapter is used to interconnect the different boards. Moreover, in order to solve the compact space requirement of two-dimensional phase-scanning antenna. Technologies such as integrated chip, vertical interconnection and three-dimensional assembly are used. It has the characteristics of high integration, small size, light weight and so on. According to the measured results, in the operating frequency band(13.7Ghz~14.5GHz), the 64-Channel TR module with 3D packaged achieves the receive gain ≥15dB, receive noise figure ≥3.5 and transmit power ≥23dBm.

articleTitle: Experimental research on the structure model of the cable rod antenna
abstract: Based on the design requirements of lightweight and controllability, the static loading test was carried out on the small 1.5m×1.5m pole antenna structure using three types of heavy object mounting methods at the center, 1/3 angle and 1/3 span for aiming at the RMS limit of 0.5mm to achieve self-adaptive profile accuracy control. The result show that the front RMS is less than 0.5mm when the load is small, At this time, no active control is required to meet the actual use requirements; When the load increases, if the RMS is greater than 0.5mm, the control system is activated, and the RMS can basically be adjusted to 0.5mm. Compared with working condition B (1/3 angle) and working condition C (1/3 span), the active control effect in working condition A (center) is the most significant.

articleTitle: A Semantic Cognition Enhancment Network for Interference Detection in Sentinel-1 SAR Image
abstract: The existence of radio frequency interference (RFI) can cause partial image degradation, image interpretation errors, and parameter extraction deviations. The precise detection and localization of the interference is the premise step for successful mitigation. However, the shape of weak interference is changeable and lacks a unified mathematical model, while its energy difference with the surrounding background is very small, which makes it difficult to be detected in complex environment. This paper proposes a semantic cognitive enhancement network for RFI detection in Sentinel-1 SAR image. Through the fusion of dilated convolution, cross-layer connection and self-attention mechanism, it can effectively improve the detection performance of weak interference under the condition of small sample training.

articleTitle: Target Detection with Optimal Power Allocation and Quantization for Distributed MIMO DFRC System
abstract: In this paper, the problem of detection in a power-bandwidth-constrained distributed MIMO Dual-Functional Radar-Communication (DFRC) system is considered, an optimal power allocation fusion scheme is investigated by joint analyzing the influences of interference and quantization error on detection performance. Firstly, we describe the influence of interference and quantization error on detection, and derive the numerical relationship with detection probability. On this basis, a constrained maximization problem of detection probability is proposed to balance the trade-off between these two factors in order to obtain higher detection performance, by using Yalmip optimization tool, the approximate optimal power allocation is derived. Finally, numerical results confirm the superiority of our method.

articleTitle: Generalization of single-frequency threshold based on 1-bit quantization in synthetic aperture radar
abstract: In this paper, a 1-bit SAR quantization model based on single-frequency threshold is generalized for different applications due to its strong representation ability. The 1-bit quantization is able to simplify the SAR system by reducing the quantization level of each sample to only 1 bit. As the single-frequency threshold can be determined by amplitude, frequency and phase, different 1 bit quantization models, such as zeros-threshold, fixed threshold, and even multi-bit quantization, can be represented by varying these three parameters and their time-variant characteristics. Based on the generalized 1-bit quantization model, the SAR imaging and the deceptive jamming against SAR can be significantly simplified with guaranteed quality.

articleTitle: High-Order Range Variant Motion Compensation for Airborne SAR With Extremely Large Elevation Angle
abstract: For airborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging with extremely large illuminate elevation angle, the influence of range variant envelope error and phase modulations will be more serious, and traditional two-step motion compensation (MoCo) fail to image accurately. To solve this problem, a new MoCo approach is proposed to improve the imaging quality of this situation. The real data experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Investigation and verification on Wide-Area Target Detection under Sea-Clutter
abstract: Maritime traffic safety management and emergency rescue have put forward higher requirements for sea surface target detection in recent years. As an active remote sensing method, SAR can provide all-day and all-weather remote sensing detection information, and it is extremely urgent to search and detect sea surface targets in wide-area with high effectiveness. This paper presents the investigation and verification of circular scanning synthetic aperture radar (CSSAR) system for targets imaging and detection in a wide-area of sea surface, parameters affecting the imaging performance of the system are discussed, flight experiment for sea surface target detection is introduced, using airborne CSSAR system. The most fitting distribution based on probability density function (PDF) of sea clutter is obtained by the statistical analysis of sampled sea clutter data, CFAR target detection based on this sea clutter model is realized. The imaging and detection results of ships on the sea surface during the experiment are given, and the resolution performance and location result of angle reflector with fixed position are evaluated. It will be shown that the CSSAR system can achieve wide-area target detection under sea-clutter efficiently.

articleTitle: Atmospheric effects reduction in GB-InSAR applications
abstract: The atmosphere can affect the propagation of the radar signal in free space. The refractive index and consequently the propagation speed of the radio signal, depends on atmospheric parameters and therefore can vary over time and space. This may limit the capability of an interferometric radar system to detect tiny changes in the terrain. This paper proposes a method to mitigate the effect of the atmosphere that makes use of an optimization algorithm and a parametric model of the refractive index that derives from the ITD-R refractive index model. The proposed approach has been tested on real data acquired using a GB-SAR system, cooperative corner reflectors and a weather station. Data have been acquired continuously for three days. One of the cooperative scatterer was placed on a millimetre graded tripod and has been moved during the measurements to better assess the algorithm when a scatterer moves.

articleTitle: Fast-moving Target Detection and Imaging in Microwave photonic SAR
abstract: Microwave photonic radar realizes ultra-wideband radar waveform, which can break through the technical bottleneck of high-resolution SAR. However, there still exists several problem in fast-moving target detection and imaging in Microwave photonic SAR, included moving targets defocus and Doppler spectrum split. In this paper, one method combining azimuth frequency modulation compensation with azimuth deramp is presented to refocus fast-moving targets. Finally, simulation results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Waveform Design of Multi-Carrier Phase Coded and Frequency Modulation Signal
abstract: The composite waveform of multi-carrier phase coded and frequency modulation signal is an effective method to solve the integration of radar sensing and wireless communication. This paper mainly discussed three different types of waveforms: multi-carrier phase coded signal (MCPC), linear frequency modulation (LFM) in phase coded waveform, complex modulation of multi-carrier phase coded and frequency modulation Signal. In order to suppress radar interference and various clutter, a novel complex modulation waveform of MCPC and LFM using orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) is designed. Signal models, formula expression and time-frequency characteristics are analyzed comprehensively for all of the conventional and novel waveforms. Numerical simulations and practical applications show that it can achieve good performance for anti-jamming and clutter suppression in the field of radar and communication by using the proposed complex modulation waveform.

articleTitle: Multi-subaperture Trajectory Estimation for Stripmap UAV SAR
abstract: The estimation of two-dimensional motion parameters is the premise of high-precision synthetic aperture radar (SAR) error compensation. In strip mode, it is difficult to directly estimate all phase errors in one range block, so it isn't accurate to estimate the trajectory using the whole range block. In this paper, a two-dimensional displacement estimation process for multi-rotor multi-rotor unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) SAR is proposed. It divides the whole aperture into several subapertures, then select several range blocks in each subaperture and calculates their phase error gradients, next restores the two-dimensional displacement one subaperture by one subaperture. Considering that the velocity error will cause envelope error, it uses multiple iterations to decrease the influence of velocity error. Finally, the feasibility is verified by simulation.

Author Keywords: unmanned aerial vehicle synthetic aperture radar (UAV SAR)

articleTitle: TomoSAR 3D Focusing Method Via Linear Error Estimation Based on Mulipass Subimage Registration
abstract: In this paper, a high-precision linear error estimation method based on subimage registration is proposed, to solve the problem that the linear error between tracks affects the focusing effect of multipass TomoSAR. Firstly, establish a multipass TomoSAR echo structure, analyze the effects of linear errors between different tracks on two-dimensional imaging algorithm. Secondly get the image offset between the sub-images to rebuild the trajectory. Finally use of the tomographic three-dimensional imaging algorithm to process the echo, and introduced a three-dimensional auto-focusing algorithm to remove residual motion errors. The effectiveness of the method is verified by simulation experiments.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Squint-mode 3D InISAR Imaging Based on Cross-Range Scaling and Coordinates Transform with Two Antennas
abstract: The image distortion arises in the InISAR 3D imagery when the radar works in a squint-mode. To eliminate the error of coarse precision in traditional three-dimensional (3D) Interferometric Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (InISAR) imaging algorithms on squint-mode, this paper proposes a novel approach to reconstruct the 3D image of non-cooperative moving targets with two antennas, which uses the cross-range scaling to obtain the initial azimuth coordinate of the target. Additionally, Coordinates Transformation (CT) of Image Projection Plane (IPP) is applied to rectify the image distortion by correcting the acquired azimuth and range coordinates of the target. Finally, InISAR technique is used to attain the altitude coordinates of the target, and then 3D image of the target is formed by the obtained 3D coordinates. The effectiveness of 3D imaging and the accuracy of cross-range scaling of the proposed method are demonstrated by simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Multi-user Dual-function Radar-communications System Based on Circulating Code Array
abstract: To ease the shortage of the spectrum resource, a dual-function radar-communications (DFRC) system based on circulating code array is proposed in this paper. The relationship between the spectrum of the synthesized signal and the spatial angle is firstly analyzed. By utilizing this relationship, different frequency bands can be allocated to multiple different communication users located in different spatial directions. Radar and communication receiving processing procedures are analyzed secondly. At the communication receiver, the relationship between the spectrum of the transmitted basic waveform and the spectrum of the synthesized waveform of circulating code array provides the possibility to demodulate the communication symbols from the received signal. The proposed DFRC system requires only one transmitted basic waveform to implement multi-user communication transmission and radar detection simultaneously. It is verified that the designed method can use different modulation schemes to simultaneously transmit information to multiple communication users located in different directions without sacrificing radar detection performance. Simulation results are presented to validate the performance of the designed DFRC system.

articleTitle: Optimal Radiation Sequence Arrangement For Low Probability of Intercept
abstract: Both low probability of intercept (LPI) capacity and tracking capacity are important issues for modern radars. However, there usually exists a trade-off between these capacities. To solve the trade-off, the problem of radiation control is studied and the optimal radiation sequence arrangement is provided. This paper reveals the upper bound of the tracking performance under the condition of a given LPI capacity, which shows some remarkable significance for engineering applications.

articleTitle: Application of Antenna Technology in Radiometer Systems
abstract: The advantages of radiometer in the application of Earth remote sensing are outstanding. With the development in recent decades, the application field is vast, which puts higher requirements on the performance of radiometer system. Meanwhile, the antenna is much more difficult to implement. This paper describes the antenna technology from performance requirements. For mechanical scanning radiometer, 7-m mesh reflector antenna is the bottleneck, and it is difficult to break through the key technology in the short term. To avoid this difficulty, synthetic aperture radiometers and pushing radiometers have been developed.

articleTitle: The LCMV Pattern Synthesis Based on Partition Optimization for Cooperative Detection using UAV Swarm
abstract: Cooperative detection using unmanned aerial vehi-cle (UAV) swarm has many obvious advantages such as better spatial resolution, high flexibility and lower cost so that it is favored for military. Compared with the traditional dense planar array, the pattern of the UAV swarm suffers higher sidelobe level and serious grating lobe effect due to its three-dimensional (3D) random and sparse array. In this paper, we propose a lineary constrained minimum variance (LCMV) method based on partition optimization for pattern synthesis of the 3D UAV swarm array. Firstly, the null-to-null beamwidths of the azimuth and elevation are calculated, respectively. Then the azimuth-elevation pattern is divided into four partitions including three sidelobe regions and one mainlobe region. Finally, the levels of above three sidelobe regions are individually optimised to each reference value via LCMV algorithm. The proposed method can achieve different sidelobe levels and has faster convergence over the state-of-the-art two-dimensional union pattern synthesis method. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Efficient Backprojection Algorithm Based on Spectral Splicing
abstract: This paper introduces a fast back projection synthetic aperture radar imaging algorithm based on wavenumber spectrum splicing. The traditional algorithm establishes the polar coordinate system with the center of the sub aperture as the origin. It needs to constantly re-establish a new unified polar coordinate system for projection and fusion, which requires a large amount of calculation. In order to deal with this problem, this paper first proposes a novel fusion method, which splices sub-aperture images in the wavenumber domain, and then completes the image fusion, which accelerates the imaging speed. Finally, simulations are presented to demonstrate the efficiency of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Human Activity Classification with Adaptive Thresholding using Radar Micro-Doppler
abstract: Radar systems are increasingly being used for healthcare applications for human activity recognition due to their advantages for privacy compliance, contactless sensing, and insensitivity to lighting conditions. The proposed classification algorithms are often very complex, hence requiring significant computational resources. We propose an adaptive thresholding algorithm used as a ‘mask’ to highlight the region of interest from the micro-Doppler signature. The mask is then applied to spectrogram information. These masked signatures are used for handcrafted feature extraction and classification. A quadratic-SVM classifier is employed based on the features from the information acquired. The preliminary results show that an accuracy of 91.3% is achieved using sequential forward feature selection with feature fusion. Based on our initial result, a Naïve Bayes combiner is used to improve the overall performance further. With this strategy, the accuracy of classification reaches 92.5% for six activities. Additionally, we compare our findings to those of other models utilizing the same database. The results demonstrate that high accuracy can be achieved when adaptive thresholding is used with the SVM method, and computational resources may significantly decrease.

articleTitle: DDMA-MIMO Radar Maximum Unambiguous Velocity Extension Based on Global Optimization Phase Modulation
abstract: Doppler division multiple access (DDMA) waveform shows great orthogonality for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar. However, it leads to a serious velocity ambiguous problem and hinders its application in automotive radar. In this work, a maximum unambiguous velocity extension approach is developed for DDMA MIMO radar by using a global ergodic optimization phase modulation during transmission. To be specific, we take the cumulative sum of the peak amplitude difference of global as the optimization cost function to obtain modulation codes. Furthermore, a matched filter phase demodulation carried out at the receiver to determine the results of angle measurement and velocity expansion. Finally, the simulation analysis and real-data experiments demonstrate our approach effectively improves velocity ambiguity resolving capabilities of DDMA waveform and suitable for massive MIMO array in nowadays automotive radar.

articleTitle: An Improved Deep Network with Fusion of Physical and Residual Information for Radar Echo Extrapolation
abstract: Precipitation Nowcasting tasks have important social impact and economic significance in disaster warning, planning, etc. Currently it uses methods based on radar echo extrapolation. Some recent works have introduced deep neural networks into the field of radar echo extrapolation, where radar echo images are arranged in temporal order as inputs to the model. Previous works usually use convolutional neural networks(CNN), recurrent neural networks(RNN) or a combination of both, which do not fully exploit the partial differential equation relationships implied behind the radar echo motion. In this paper, a physical cell is incorporated into the original deep neural network, to add physical constraints to the data-driven model and collaborate with the LSTM variant cell to accurately model the trajectory and appearance of moving objects. The experiments achieve better predictions than the original model on the synthetic moving digital dataset and the realistic radar echo dataset.

articleTitle: Multi-task Planning for Cooperative UAVs with Integrated Radio Frequency system
abstract: Integrated radio frequency (RF) is the development trend in the field of detection and situation awareness. However, limited by the small load capacity of the UAV platform, the integrated RF amounted on a single platform is hard to both have wide-area and comprehensive sensing capabilities. One possible approach to solve this dilemma is to use multiple UAVs to perceive the scene in a cooperative manner at the same time, instead of relying on only one UAV. Inspired by this, this paper mainly discusses the node selection and resource scheduling problems faced in cooperative UAV platforms with integrated RF, when performing several tasks simultaneously. Considering the complexity of the scheduling problem, the UAV cooperative conditions are discussed firstly. Then, based on the characteristics of irregular and ad hoc UAVs' cooperative networks, a general multi-task planning model is generalized, in which not only contains input conditions, constraints, fitness functions, and other basic elements, but also the scheduling strategies on the timeline. With this modeling manner, the scheduling results can be obtained by solving an optimization problem. Furthermore, to solve the given optimization problem, a specific heuristic algorithm is designed. At last, a simulated UAVs cooperation scheduling scenario is carefully designed including multiple tasks to be performed, such as cooperative location, cooperative detection, and jamming, whose results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Transceiver Design in the Presence of Eclipsing Loss for Spectral Coexistence
abstract: Radar system design for the detection of targets with unknown actual range in spectrally crowded environments is a challenge due to the increasing demands for spectrum and the possibly experienced echo eclipsing. Assuming unknown target echo delay (TED), this paper deals with robust joint design of the radar code and receive filter bank guaranteeing spectral compatibility with the surrounding electromagnetic radiators. The average signal-to-interference-plus-noise-ratio (SINR) at the output of the filter bank is considered as the performance measure to optimize under both similarity and spectral compatibility constraints on the waveform. Through an appropriate reformulation of the resulting non-convex optimization problem, we devise an alternate optimization algorithm which sequentially improves the average SINR and converges to a stationary point. Each iteration of the algorithm, involves both a convex and a hidden convex optimization problem which can be solved via the rank-one decomposition procedure. Finally, the performance is assessed by studying the trade-off among the SINR, spectral shape, and autocorrelation.

articleTitle: Waveform Design of Conformal MIMO Radar for Polarization Parameters Estimation
abstract: Waveform design for conformal multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) is complicated since the polarization diversity should be taken into account. In this paper, we con-sider waveform design for colocated conformal MIMO radar. Polarization of signals in the transmit mainbeam is optimized for a higher estimation accuracy of target polarization scattering parameters. A waveform optimization criterion is formulated that aims at polarization transmit beampattern matching, cross correlation sidelobe suppressing between different polarization components, auto correlation sidelobe suppressing in both po-larization channels of mainbeams, and cross correlation sidelobe suppressing between waveforms from different angular sectors. The optimization problem is solved by using the Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP) algorithm. Numerical results with a 3-dimensional transmit beampatterns of an antennas array show that auto and cross correlation sidelobes are efficiently suppressed, and the target polarization parameters are estimated in a higher accuracy, compared with waveforms unoptimized.

articleTitle: Low-altitude Wind Shear Detection Method Based on Dual Tunable Q-factor Wavelet Transform for Airborne Weather Radar
abstract: Airborne weather radar is an important means of detecting low-altitude wind shear for modern civil aviation airliners. The accuracy of wind speed estimation is the key factor affecting the detection effect of low-altitude wind shear. In this paper, a novel method of wind shear detection based on dual tunable Q-factor wavelet transform(D-TQWT)is proposed. According to the different oscillation characteristics of ground clutter and low-altitude wind shear, the morphological component analysis method is used to sparsely represent the wind shear and the ground clutter signals on the wavelet basis functions with different quality Q factors, and the noise signal is eliminated by solving the BPD optimization problem. Then, referring to the frequency energy distribution characteristics of signals under different Q factors, the effective separation of wind shear and ground clutter signals is realized. Finally, the sparse wavelet coefficients representing the wind shear signal are reconstructed to obtain more accurate wind speed estimation results. The experimental results show that the difference of signal oscillation characteristics is used in this method for dual tunable Q-factor wavelet transform, which can effectively distinguish wind shear signal and ground clutter signal without designing the clutter suppression filter, especially in the close interval of frequency domain, so as to obtain more accurate anemometer results.

articleTitle: A Modified Tracking Algorithm for NSHV Based on Aerodynamic Model
abstract: In order to track the near space hypersonic vehicle (NSHV), we propose a tracking model containing aerodynamic and kinematic information using interacting multiple model (IMM) algorithm with accruate speed prior information. Because traditional maneuver models are difficult to describe the complex movement characteristics, which involves large-scale high-speed mobile, large flight cover, etc., fault-acceleration model with surface damage model and external disturbance model are proposed. With the model, the state equations are constructed and the system dynamic error is deduced taking variable structure multiple model (VSMM) algorithm as the flitering algorithm. Moreover, an adaptive method for the change of control variables is proposed for setting parameters apporiately in the situations when a prior information is unknown. Simulation experiments are conducted to validate the superiorities among all tracking algorithms in this paper.

articleTitle: Radar 2021 Technical Papers
abstract: Radar 2021 Technical Papers.

articleTitle: CRB Analysis for Mixed-ADC PMCW MIMO Radar
abstract: We consider a mixed-ADC architecture, in which most receive antenna outputs are sampled by one-bit analog-to-digital converters (ADC's), and one or several outputs by high-resolution ADC's, for phase-modulated continuous-wave (PMCW) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar systems. We derive the Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) for the mixed-ADC architecture PMCW MIMO radar to characterize the best achievable performance of an unbiased target parameter estimator. The study of CRB demonstrates that the mixed-ADC architecture with a relatively small number of high-precision ADC's and a large number of one-bit ADC's allows us to drastically reduce the hardware cost and power consumption while still maintain a high dynamic range needed for automotive radar systems.

articleTitle: Marine Targets Detection for Scanning Radar Images Based on Radar- YOLONet
abstract: Traditional radar target detection algorithms are mostly based on statistical theory. They have weak generalization capabilities for complex sea clutter environments and diverse target characteristics, and their detection performance would significantly be reduced. In this paper, the range-azimuth information obtained by scanning radar is converted into PPI image, and a Radar-YOLONet is proposed and used for radar image target detection. The model includes CSPDarknet53, SPP, PANet and Power Non-Maximum Suppression layers. The prediction frame coordinates, target category and corresponding confidence are directly given through the feature extraction network. The network structure strengthens the receptive field and attention distribution structure, and further improves the efficiency of network training. The verification using the constructed X-band navigation radar PPI image dataset shows that compared with the traditional constant false alarm rate detector and the two-stage Faster-RCNN algorithm, the proposed method has significantly improved detection performance under certain false alarm probability conditions. It is more suitable for various environment and target characteristics.

articleTitle: A Joint DOA and TOA Estimation Scheme for 5G Signals Under Array Modeling Errors
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of direction-of-arrival (DOA) and time-of-arrival (TOA) estimation in the presence of array modeling errors for the fifth generation (5G) signals. A joint estimation scheme based on the two-dimensional multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm is proposed. It employs a pre-calibrated space-frequency manifold rather than the ideal closed-form manifold to counteract the direction-dependent array modeling errors. However, the pre-calibrated manifold does not exhibit the Vandermonde structure in angular domain even for uniform arrays, preventing the usage of the spatial smoothing technique. Since the 5G signal usually occupies a large bandwidth with a wealth of subcarriers, a modified smoothing strategy which only smooths in the frequency-domain is proposed to recover the rank of the covariance matrix. The proposed scheme is demonstrated to calibrate the direction-dependent array errors accurately in a multipath-free anechoic chamber. Its effectiveness in multipath-harsh indoor environments is also validated by both the simulated and the real-measured 5G indoor channel data.

articleTitle: Radar-based Human Activity Classification with Cyclostationarity
abstract: Human Activity Classification with radar has made significant progress in the past few years. In this article, we propose a cyclostationarity-based approach in this field of application. Feature extraction, selection, and activity classification as it detects micro-Doppler is made starting from complex-valued cyclostationary statistical functions of the reflected radar signal. The human activity can be recognized with up to 92.6% with the real part, 95.4% with the imaginary part and 95.4% by the combination of real and imaginary part.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Range-Angle-Doppler Processing Approach for FDA-MIMO Radar Based on Sparse Reconstruction
abstract: The airborne frequency diverse array (FDA) for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar can resolve the problem of clutter suppression and parameter estimation in range ambiguity. However, the sufficient independent identical distribution (IID) training samples may be not available to estimate the accurate clutter covariance matrix in practical applications. To tackle this issue, a method of adaptive range-angle-doppler processing based on sparse reconstruction is proposed in this paper. By exploring the sparsity of clutter spectrum distribution in transmit-receive-Doppler domain, the clutter spectrum distribution is recovered with sparse Bayesian learning algorithm (SBL). A little training samples are utilized to reconstruct the clutter covariance matrix, which dramatically reduces the tough requirement for the number of training sample. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Fall detection based on MIMO millimeter-wave radar
abstract: With the increasing aging of population, the safety monitoring of the elderly has become extremely important. Among the unexpected situations that endanger the physical health of the elderly, falls are unpredictable and can cause significant damage if not rescued in time. In addition, the fall problem is not the same for forwarding fall, backward fall, and lateral fall, and it is of great significance to distinguish the different directions of the fall. Therefore, this paper proposes an algorithm based on the millimeter-wave radar for real-time detection of the target fall action and fall position localization by real-time processing of the reflected signal of the detected person and obtaining the distance, speed, angle, and other information in the motion state of the detected person. The above information is integrated and analyzed to accurately judge the detected target's fall action, distinguish the different directions of the fall, and obtain the exact position of the fall. Ultimately, the experimental results show that the algorithm can distinguish the different behavioral actions of the detected personnel to meet the fast and accurate discrimination of the target person's fall and its direction. More importantly, the statistical measurement results show that the fall detection accuracy rate exceeds 90%.

articleTitle: Enhanced Range-Dependent Beampattern Using Frequency Diverse Padded Coprime Array
abstract: Frequency diverse coprime array (FDCA) can effectively eliminate the range-angle coupling by selecting virtual frequencies randomly from the second-order statistics of the receive signals. However, the beampattern of this structure is limited by the randomness of frequency offset and the degree of freedom (DoF) of antenna array. In this paper, to improve the performance of beam focusing, several array structures of frequency diverse padded coprime array (FDPCA) are proposed. The proposed schemes can obtain more focused beampattern in virtual domain and enlarge the DoF without the increase of physical element number. The effectiveness of proposed method is validated by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: ISAR Target Recognition Based on Capsule Net
abstract: Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) has been widely applied in automatic recognition of sea, air, and space targets thanks to its all-day, all-weather, and long-range operational abilities. But because of the inherent distinct characteristics such as the time-varying unknown effective rotation vector and the changing range and azimuth sampling rates, the field of ISAR ATR is facing many challenging problems such as image rotation-sensitivity, scaling-sensitivity, and translation-sensitivity, etc. This paper proposes a robust recognition method based on Capsule Net. In this structure, Capsule Net can extract the robust features of the deformable ISAR image. For the ISAR image database generated from electromagnetic (EM) echoes of four satellites, the proposed structure achieves higher recognition accuracy than traditional methods.

articleTitle: BiLSTM Based Phase Modulation Detection of Radar Emitters
abstract: In modern Electronic Warfare (EW) systems, recognition of the intrapulse modulation schemes of intercepted Low Probability of Intercept (LPI) radar signals in real-time is a crucial survival task. Lately, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) had proven effective for emitter recognition but the problem lies with the recognition of phase-coded waveforms at low Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR). We propose a Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory (BiLSTM) network-based recognition technique for the analysis and recognition of phase-coded waveforms. In order to avoid heavy processing, the time-domain radar signals are directly fed as an input to the BiLSTM network for recognition without any preprocessing and feature extraction. The BiLSTM layer can extract the contextual information of signals well and is followed by a fully connected layer. Finally, a softmax classifier is employed to accomplish the recognition task. Six distinct types of phase-coded waveforms are simulated corrupted with Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) with the SNR ranging from −10 to 10 dB. It has been demonstrated that the proposed methodology considerably enhances recognition accuracies over existing techniques.

articleTitle: SAR Ship Targets Detection Based on Correlation Filters
abstract: In previous target detection research, most algorithms focus on the targets in optical images, which is different from SAR images in terms of feature information and dataset. For the dataset of SAR ships targets with small samples, we proposed a correlation filter algorithm that can achieve robust detection under small sample and high false alarm rate. The algorithm consists of two parts, coarse CFAR detection and false alarm elimination. Inspired by the filter method of the kernelized correlation filters (KCF) algorithm, we propose a false alarms elimination algorithm that can distinguish false alarms by comparing the correlation maximum values between the detection results and the filter obtained through template tensor. An experiment is conducted on our SAR ship dataset and the results demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm.

articleTitle: SAR Target Recognition Using Simulated Data by an Ensemble Multi-scale Deep Domain Adaptation Recognition Framework
abstract: Obtaining lots of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data for automatic target recognition (ATR) can be unrealistic in many situations. Relatively speaking, electromagnetic simulated SAR data is easier to acquire. However, there is an apparent distribution gap between the electromagnetic simulated data and the real data. It is not suitable to use the simulated data for recognition directly, and thus the way to apply the simulated SAR data for recognition is worth considering. In this paper, we focus on a challenging recognition problem of training solely on simulated data and testing on real data. Firstly, a multi-scale feature extraction module is used for robust feature extraction, which aims to make the extracted feature more generalized for both simulated data and real data. Secondly, the idea of domain adaptation is considered to learn a representation trained to jointly optimize for classification and domain invariance. Thirdly, an ensembling technique is applied, and an ensemble multi-scale deep domain adaptation recognition framework is proposed. The Moving and Stationary Target Acquisition and Recognition (MSTAR) benchmark data set and an electromagnetic simulated SAR data set are used for verification, and experimental results illustrate the effectiveness of our methods.

articleTitle: 2D-CNN-Based AoA-ToA Estimation in Presence of Angle-Dependent Phase Errors Using Pico-cells
abstract: Many advanced location-based services and network optimization applications in the fifth generation (5G) mobile networks rely on accurate location awareness. In view of this, we investigate joint estimation of the angle-of-arrival and time-of-arrival of mobile user equipments using 5G pico-cell base stations. In practical scenarios, the measured phase of the channel state information (CSI) is distorted by angle-dependent errors induced by hardware impairments. To solve this problem, we propose a estimation algorithm based on two-dimensional (2D) convolutional neural network (CNN) in this work. Specifically, the spatial and subcarrier dimensions of the CSI are organized into the input matrix. Then, the features are extracted through the 2D convolutional layers. The 2D-CNN is further incorporated with a MUltiple-SIgnal-Classification (MUSIC)-based region decision method. As confirmed by numerical results, the proposed frame-work can effectively fit the non-linear angle-dependent array error and improve the accuracy of positioning.

articleTitle: Metric-based Meta-Learning Model for Few-Shot PolSAR Image Terrain Classification
abstract: Deep learning models have been successfully applied to polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) image terrain classification. However, they usually need many labeled samples from the current PolSAR image to be classified to train the model parameters, which fundamentally limits their application. In this paper, we propose a metric-based meta-learning framework for few-shot terrain classification (MML-FSTC) of PolSAR image. The proposed MML-FSTC firstly utilizes the collected base labeled samples (BLS) from typical PolSAR systems to learn an effective transferable three-dimensional convolutional neural network (3DCNN) to extract features for terrain classification. Then, by mimicking the few-shot learning of human, MML-FSTC integrates additional samples, whose label spaces are probably different from those of BLS, and proposes a meta-learning strategy for terrain classification that consists of multiple few-shot training episodes, each of which has very few labeled terrain samples and potentially different labeled space. By minimizing the cosine distance of the support and query deep features, MML-FSTC finetunes the pre-trained 3DCNN in the meta-learning stage, and utilizes a metric-based cosine distance function to predict the classification. The classification results demonstrate the superiority of MML-FSTC for few-shot PolSAR image terrain classification.

articleTitle: Multiresolution Jamming Recognition with Few-shot Learning
abstract: The few-shot learning method, based on multiresolution feature extraction, is proposed for the recognition of jamming signals, including range gate pull-off (RGPO), velocity gate pull-off (VGPO), and range-velocity gate pull-off (RVGPO) jamming signals. The general jamming recognition technology is mature, but a large number of training samples are needed. In this paper, the prototype network is used for few-shot learning that taking features extracted from wavelet decomposition and empirical mode decomposition (EMD). It is shown that the proposed method has a good recognition effect under the condition of few samples.

articleTitle: High-Resolution ISAR Imaging Based on 2-D Fast Sparse Bayesian Learning
abstract: We address the problem of high-resolution ISAR imaging in a Bayesian inference framework. Firstly, the probabilistic graphical model is constructed by imposing the sparsity-promoting Gamma-Gaussian prior to the distribution of scattering centers. In order to eliminate the issue of matrix inversion in conventional Sparse Bayesian Learning (SBL), a 2-D fast SBL is then proposed to improve the computational efficiency. Experimental results have demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed method in sparse-aperture and low signal-to-noise ratio scenarios.

articleTitle: A THz Video SAR Imaging Algorithm Based on Chirp Scaling
abstract: In video synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging mode, the polar format algorithm (PFA) is more computational effective than the backprojection algorithm (BPA). However, the two-dimensional (2-D) interpolation in PFA greatly affects its computational speed, which is detrimental to the real-time imaging of video SAR. In this paper, a terahertz (THz) video SAR imaging algorithm based on chirp scaling is proposed, which utilizes the small synthetic angular feature of THz SAR and the inherent property of linear frequency modulation. Then, two-step chirp scaling is used to replace the 2-D interpolation in the PFA to obtain a similar focusing effect, but with a faster operation. Point target simulation is used to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Resolving Range and Velocity Ambiguity Effectively and Efficiently with GPU
abstract: Resolving the ambiguity in both range and velocity domain is one of the essential issues for the pulse Doppler (PD) radars using medium pulse repetition frequency (PRF) waveforms. The existing solutions are mainly based on the Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT) and its variations and extensions, but these algorithms typically have an unsatisfactory accuracy and are highly complex in computation, especially for the case of a large false-alarm rate. In this work, we proposed a new approach to tackle with ambiguity based on the partial distance matrices (PDM) and implemented it on the NVIDIA graphics processing unit (GPU) platform. The evaluations based on both Monte-Carlo simulations and real measured data present the advantages of the proposed approach in accuracy and efficiency. The results also show the proposed approach can be utilized as a real-time algorithm even for a low-threshold detection scheme.

articleTitle: Deep Unfolding of the Half-Quadratic Splitting Algorithm for ISAR Image Super-resolution
abstract: This paper targets on an effective and interpretable model-based deep learning method for Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) image super-resolution. Due to the intrinsic hardware limitations of the radar system, ISAR images are typically blurred and of low-resolution which lead to difficulties in down-streaming tasks including target detection, recognition and classification. The traditional model-based methods would be less effective when competing with the data-driven meth-ods. However, these deep learning model seldom has a good interpretative formulation to be studied mathematically. In this paper, we propose an unfolded half-quadratic splitting network (UHQSNet) that establishes a hierarchical network by unfolding the iterative optimization process into the fine-designed network architecture. The experimental results on a three-target ISAR datasets show that the proposed UHQSNet gains significantly better performance than both of the model-based method and deep learning method.

articleTitle: Radar HRRP Signal Re-ID via Deep Learning
abstract: High-resolution range profile (HRRP) is often used in radar automatic target recognition (RATR) tasks. The performance of HRRP classification has received promising results with convulotional neural networks (CNN). However, in real-world application, it is difficult to obtain sufficient HRRP data with all aspect-angles for training the networks, especially for non-cooperative targets. Such insufficient HRRP data dramatically hampers classification performance. Thus, the proposed work introduces re-identification (ReID) into the HRRP recognition. A suitable model based on CNN for HRRP signal is proposed in the proposed work. Experiments on public datasets demonstrated that the proposed methods outperform the CNN-based classification model in target recognition.

articleTitle: Clutter cancellation in passive radar from the perspective of maximum likelihood
abstract: Clutter cancellation in passive radar is gaining increasing interest. The extensive cancellation algorithm (ECA) has received a range of applications in passive radar clutter cancellation. However, the ECA suffers from great computational complexity. Several variants of ECA have been proposed to increase the computational efficiency. Among those methods, a parallel implementation algorithm obtains an interesting conclusion that, the cancellation weight vector of ECA can be calculated as the weighted mean of several weight vectors, each of which is computed using only a small segment of the reference and surveillance signals. The algorithm can get very similar cancellation weight vector compared with the ECA, but increases the computational efficiency. However, the derivation of this algorithm in the original paper is very complicated and not straightforward to be understood and the obtaining of the final conclusion is not explicit. In this paper, we rederive this algorithm from the maximum likelihood (ML) perspective. We can get the same algorithm, but use a very simple and straightforward derivation. Furthermore, we show explicitly how the finial conclusion is derived, by making some assumptions on the statistical characteristics of the illuminating signal, which is not discussed in the original paper. Finally, we analyze through simulations how the assumptions made on the illuminating signal affect the estimation of the cancellation weight vector.

articleTitle: A Low-Complexity Joint AOA and TOA Estimation Method for Positioning with 5G Signals
abstract: This paper proposes a novel joint angle-of-arrival (AOA) and path delay (a.k.a. time-of-arrival, TOA) estimation (JADE) method for the fifth generation (5G) signal based positioning system. Conventional methods combine angle and delay into a parameter pair and apply super-resolution methods to the large-dimensional space-time/frequency data matrix. The proposed method reduces the computational overhead on the basis of two observations. Firstly, 5G base stations have unbalanced resolutions in temporal and spatial domains, with temporal resolution much better than spatial resolution, especially for those established for indoor coverage. Therefore, the proposed method employs the iterative adaptive approach (IAA) to resolve multipaths in the TOA domain, then applies the spatial digital beamformer subsequently to obtain AOA estimates. Secondly, based on the Vandermonde structure of the delay signature matrix, fast Fourier transform is employed to accelerate the spectrum computation of the IAA method. Comparing the proposed method with the popular multiple signal classification (MUSIC) based JADE algorithm, the estimation error increases by 72% and 26% in numerical simulation and in real-measured channel data, respectively. However, a reduction of nearly three orders for computational cost is achieved.

articleTitle: A Convolutional Neural Network for Heterogeneous Ship Images Classification
abstract: In this work, heterogeneous ship images classification has been implemented by using Deep Learning techniques. The main goal of our study is to build a classification model that performs well on data collected from two different sensors i.e. optical sensor and radar sensor. We have proposed a binary classification solution. Our goal was to separate the ship images from the others. We selected a convolutional neural network (CNN) as our classification method and SoftMax as the prediction method. A CNN model was trained from scratch during which we obtained an accuracy score of 97.16%. We also used techniques such as transfer learning and fine-tuning to improve the previous accuracy. We finally obtained 99.30% as training accuracy. During the testing phase, 93.06% was recorded as the best performance.

articleTitle: Maximum Likelihood Direction-of-Arrival Estimation via Rank-Constrained ADMM
abstract: The maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) is known to provide benchmark performance for direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation. Due to high nonconvexity of the MLE problem, however, effective implementations of the MLE are rare in practice. In this paper, we consider DOA estimation with a uniform linear array and formulate by using re-parameterization and majorization minimization the stochastic MLE as a series of rank-constrained semidefinite programs that are solved using the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Numerical results are provided to illustrate the superior statistical performance of the proposed method as compared to existing approaches in the absence/presence of coherent sources.

articleTitle: Moving Target Tracking Based on Shadow with Unsupervised Deep Track in Video-SAR
abstract: The moving target is always defocused and shifted out of the scene in image sequences in video Synthetic Aperture Radar (video-SAR), which makes moving target tracking be a formidable challenge. In this paper, a new moving target tracking method based on shadow with unsupervised deep track (UDT) is proposed. Our track network is built on the Siamese network framework and is trained on a series of unlabeled SAR image sequences with unsupervised learning way. Meanwhile, we use the trajectory detection technology to get more accurate tracking results. Finally., the processing results of the real data are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Scattered Wave Deceptive Jamming Method Based on Genetic Algorithm against Three Channel SAR GMTI
abstract: To reduce difficulty of obtaining jamming parameters, combining scattered wave deception jamming method structure with genetic algorithm, a scattered wave deceptive jamming method based on genetic algorithm is proposed against three Channel SAR GMTI. Four-dimensional jamming parameter searching problem is separated as a one-dimensional optimization problem and a two-dimensional optimization problem, which will reduce computational burden and jamming parameter acquirement time and raise fidelity of deceptive jamming. In addition, the problem, that tolerance of Doppler rate mismatch is difficult to describe, is solved by transforming an objective function of the two-dimensional optimization problem. By utilizing jamming quality parameters, simulation experiments are provided to verify the effectiveness of SGA method against the three-channel SAR GMTI.

articleTitle: Ship Target Micro-Doppler Feature Extracted by Multi-Synchrosqueezing Transform and Inverse Radon Transform
abstract: Ship targets with oceanic waves appear a unique micro-Doppler (m-D) feature, which is important for target identification. In this paper, we propose a method to extract the features of ship target based on Multi-Synchrosqueezing Transform (MSST) and Inverse radon transform (IRT). Firstly, we analyze the complex relative motion between radar and the ship target. After the envelope correction, the echo is a sinusoidal frequency modulation (SFM) signal mixed with a remained time-varying phase. However, it is a challenge to extract the m-D feature directly. Thus, the MSST is used to enhance the TF spectrum concentration, in order to extract the remained phase with m-D characteristics accurately by IRT. The experimental results prove the effectiveness of the proposed method and the accurate estimation of micro motion features.

articleTitle: Enhanced Detection in Automotive Applications Using Bistatic Radar with Cooperative Roadside Sensors
abstract: The state-of-art automotive radar modules normally operate in the monostatic mode and little research has been done on the ability of a vehicle to operate such application when the transmitter is located externally, a setup commonly referred to as bistatic mode. Our proposal here is to combine the communication potential of fifth-generation (5G) new radio (NR) with the merits of bistatic radar to advance the existing automotive radar technology. This application can be envisioned in a smart highway where a vehicle switches to an economic mode, and the long-range radar modules rely on cooperative roadside transmitters (communicating via pre-determined protocols) to locate targets in its vicinity. Computer simulations show that this proposed application can outperform the monostatic equivalent.

articleTitle: A new Six-Component Decomposition based on New Volume Scattering Models for PolSAR Image
abstract: Polarimetric target decomposition is a significant means for feature extraction of PolSAR image, which plays an important role in describing the scattering characteristics, physical structure, composition and other details of grounds. So in this paper, a new volume scattering model is proposed and applied to a new six-component decomposition, which decomposes the coherency matrix into surface scattering, double-bounce scattering, new volume scattering, cross scattering, oriented dipole scattering and compound dipole scattering. The proposed method can effectively improve the decomposition quality of PolSAR image, and its visualization presentation is more accurate than the existing decomposition methods. It is more robust in urban areas, suppress the problem of volume scattering overestimation, describe the complex environment in more detail, and obtain better scattering characteristics of man-made targets. The validity of the proposed method is demonstrated by the data of L-band fully polarimetric ESAR images of Oberpfaffenhofen area, Germany in this paper.

articleTitle: Ground-Based ArcSAR Interferometry and Sensitivity Analysis
abstract: Compared with the linear-scanning ground-based synthetic aperture radar (GB-SAR), ground-based arc synthetic aperture radar (GB-ArcSAR) can achieve a larger range of scanning and is gradually being used. GB-ArcSAR can use both vertical and horizontal baselines to achieve interferometry. This paper introduces two interferometric measurement methods of GB-ArcSAR and carries out sensitivity analysis. It is verified based on simulation data.

articleTitle: Enhanced Signal Processing Method for Integrated Detection and Jamming System Considering the Complex Environment
abstract: The integrated detection and jamming system (IDJS) aims to pose a jamming threat to the enemy radar, and perform target detection in the meanwhile. To pose an effective jamming, the frequency spectrum of the transmit signal of IDJS has to overlap with the operating band of the enemy radar. As a consequence, the transmit signal of the enemy radar (TSER) would also cause interference to our IDJS, thus degrading the target detection performance of IDJS. Such interference, however, was generally ignored in current literature on IDJS, which may lead to ineffectiveness in practice. In this paper, we propose two methods for IDJS to separate the interference of the enemy radar from the echoes of IDJS and enhance the target detection performance. In the first method, a time-varying filtering (TVF) is established in the short time Fourier transform (STFT) domain to suppress TSER. The second method is an enhancement of the first method. The sparsity of illuminated area in time-frequency (TF) domain is utilized and an adaptive dictionary based sparse recovery algorithm is derived to recover echoes of IDJS loss resulting from TVF. Simulation results indicate that two proposed methods can both effectively separate the TSER and echoes of IDJS for detection, and the IDJS can achieve excellent interference effects on enemy radar at the same time.

articleTitle: Analysis of Spatial Decorrelation in Radar Scattering from Sea Surfaces
abstract: This paper investigates an analytical correlation function to characterize the sea surfaces and its implication to predict radar backscattering. We adopt the modulation concept to describe the decomposition of the roughness scales of the sea surface. In this modulation model, the roughness of the sea surface is determined by the modulation length and the baseband correlation length. Preliminary results show that the proposed analytical correlation function agrees with the correlation function of the H18 sea spectrum, which is valid for a wide range of frequencies and wind speeds. Besides, the empirical relation between correlation length and wind speed and wind direction is thoroughly examined. To verify the validity of the modulation model, we compare the backscattering coefficients between the H18 spectrum and the modulation model. The results demonstrate that the modulation model keeps good agreement with the H18 spectrum concerning backscattering behavior.

articleTitle: Robust Indoor Target Tracking Based on Track Matching
abstract: Radar-based indoor target tracking has received a lot of attention in recent years. Due to the occlusions caused by furniture or building structures, the tracker could only produce several short tracks. In this paper, a track matching scheme is proposed for indoor target tracking, where the Hankel matrix completion technique is utilized to estimate the missing data and the rank of the Hankel matrix is used for track association. The proposed algorithm doesn't rely on the prior knowledge of the dynamic model, which could be an effective complement to the existing tracking frameworks.

articleTitle: A Two-Stage Wall Parameter Estimation Algorithm for UWB Through-the-wall Radar
abstract: The knowledge of wall parameters in through-the-wall radar imaging is important since it is the guarantee of high precision target localization. Hence, this paper presents a two-stage wall parameter estimation algorithm to retrieve the unknown distance, thickness, and relative permittivity. In this approach, the time delays of the front and rear surfaces of a wall with respect to all potential wall parameters are calculated by specular reflection and refraction point approximation. Since the echoes of all antennas will constructively accumulate only when the time delays are equal to the true value, the image intensity generated by the back-projection algorithm can be used to discriminate the parameters. Finally, electromagnetic simulations demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can precisely estimate the walls parameter and is flexible for different array structure.

articleTitle: Feature Refinement Deformable Network for Aircraft Detection in SAR images
abstract: Aircraft with advantages of mobility and carrying ability plays an indispensable role in modern transportation areas. However, detecting aircraft in SAR images still meets serious challenges due to discrete spatial distributions of back-scattering points, diversified gestures of aircraft as well as complex surroundings. In this paper, a Feature Refinement Deformable Network (FRDN) is proposed by carefully designing a Feature Fusion Attention Module (FFAM) and a Deformable Latent Convolutional Module (DLCM).Moreover, FFAM is designed to fuse structural and abstract features and highlight significant information of aircraft effectively. DLCM focus on capturing significant features of discrete-distributed back-scattering points of aircraft. The contributions of FFAM and DLCM are carefully exploited and the detection performance of our method is compared with other specific and general CNN-based methods on a self-built SAR aircraft detection data-set.Experimental results illustrates the effectiveness of our method for aircraft detection in SAR images.

articleTitle: A 3D Geometry Reconstruction Method for Space Targets Utilizing Improved ISAR Image Sequence Energy Accumulation
