abstract: As for space targets with unknown motion, the accurate projection matrix cannot be obtained in advance, which makes the three-dimensional (3D) geometry reconstruction method based on inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) image sequence energy accumulation (ISEA) inapplicable. To tackle this problem, a joint factorization and ISEA-based method is proposed. Firstly, the range-Doppler measurement matrix can be formed through the steadily tracking of a small number of feature points in the ISAR image sequence. Then the factorization method is utilized to estimate the projection matrix, which reflects the projection relationship between the 3D geometry and corresponding ISAR image sequence. Next, when projected to ISAR image sequence, feature points with larger ISEA values can be regarded as the true scattering points on the geometry of the target. Therefore, all the scattering points can be reconstructed by searching the feature points with maximum ISEA values. Experimental results based on simulated point model verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Stacked Stereo Graph Convolutional Network for SAR Image Change Detection
abstract: Graph convolutional network (GCN), as a powerful semi-supervised graph learning algorithm, is effective for graph-based feature extraction and classification. It has great potential in extracting and classifying high-ordered spatial structure information in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images. In this paper, to detect the complicated structural changes in SAR images, a stacked stereo graph convolutional network (SSGCN) is built by combining a stacked stereo graph model (SSGM) with the GCN. The SSGM is built to extract the spatial, temporal and hybrid spatial-temporal information between bi-temporal SAR images. Then the SSGM and GCN are concatenated to construct a hierarchical SSGCN model to execute further the feature depiction and classification. The spectral graph convolution and traditional 2-D convolution are implemented layer by layer to infer the labels of the graph nodes. To show the effectiveness of the SSGCN change detection method, SAR images obtained at the area of Chaohu basin, Anhui, China are tested in the experiments.

articleTitle: Modeling and Characteristic Analysis for Air-Space Based Bistatic Radar
abstract: Air-space based bistatic radar is a new radar concept of space-based radar, has strong anti-jamming ability and can economize satellite payloads. However, given the fact that the transmitter and receiver of the radar system are placed on airplane platform and satellite platform respectively, the Doppler frequency is determined by two platforms, which makes the clutter characteristic more complicated. This paper considers the actual beam exposure range, establishes the clutter model of air-space based bistatic radar and analyzes the performance of space-time adaptive processing (STAP) in different configurations. Experiment results show that system performance is greatly influenced by configuration and that air-space based bistatic radar is feasible in certain configurations. This can provide references for the study of air-space based bistatic radar.

articleTitle: Grid-Less DOA Estimation via Sparse Linear Array Using One-Bit Measurements
abstract: Recently one-bit quantization has been widely used in field of signal processing because of its advantages of low cost, low power consumption and high sampling rate. This paper studies the problem of estimating the direction of arrivals (DOAs) of source signals via sparse linear arrays (SLAs) using one-bit measurements. By constructing an augmented covariance matrix from the sample covariance matrix, we can realize gridless DOA estimation using root-MUSIC on the augmented covariance matrix and solve more sources than the number of sensors. Two covariance fitting criteria, including maximum likelihood and Wasserstein distance, are introduced into one-bit sparse array DOA estimation. Numerical simulations demonstrate that Wasserstein distance based criterion has good performance both in accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Dual-band high range-resolution microwave photonic radar based on coherent fusion processing
abstract: A dual-band and high-resolution microwave photonic radar is proposed using polarization multiplexing with an in-phase/quadrature (I/Q) de-chirp receiver. In the proposed radar, a dual-band linear frequency modulated (LFM) wideband signal is generated using a dual-polarization Mach-Zehnder modulator (DPol-MZM) while a microwave photonic I/Q de-chirp reception is proposed to achieve dual-band LFM de-chirping simultaneously based on the dual-polarization optical hybrid. In addition, the de-chirp signals from two bands can be further processed for coherent fusion processing to achieve higher range resolution. In the proof-of-concept experiment, frequency-stepped LFM signals covering 17.9-25.1 GHz and 24.9-32.1 GHz which crossed K-band and Ka-band are generated and processed with image-rejection over 31.9 dB. A high range resolution of 1.14 cm after coherent fusion is also achieved.

articleTitle: Fundamental Limits on Detection With a Dual-function Radar Communication System
abstract: This paper investigates the fundamental limits on the target detection performance with a dual-function multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) radar communication (RadCom) systems. By assuming the presence of a point-like target and a communication receiver, closed-form expressions for the maximum detection probability and the transmit waveforms achieving the optimal performance are derived. Results show that for the considered case, the dual-function system should transmit coherent waveforms to achieve the optimal detection performance. Moreover, the angle separation between the target and communication receiver has a great impact on the achievable detection performance.

articleTitle: Potential of Reducing FMCW Radar Mutual-interference Using Nonlinear FM Signals
abstract: The state-of-the-art automotive radars are mainly implemented by using linear frequency modulated continuous wave (LFMCW). Unfortunately, the widespread use of LFCMW increases mutual interference between automotive radars. Compared with LFMCW, the nonlinear frequency modulated (NLFM) signal has a flexible distribution in the time-frequency two-dimensional plane. These nonlinear fixed time-frequency distributions have a certain potential for solving the mutual interference problem. It is possible to introduce NLFM signals in the current mainstream LFM radar and alternate these two different signals in different situations respectively, thus the mutual interference could be reduced. Therefore, this work firstly designs the NLFM signal with good performance based on Legendre Polynomials, and then analyzes whether there is an interference problem between the NLFM signal and the LFCMW.

articleTitle: A RLSN-based Current Statistical Model for Target Range Tracking
abstract: In classical “Current” statistical model, maneuvering frequency is normally set as typical value, and an acceleration limit has to be set. In order to break this limitation, this paper utilizes recursive linear smoothed Newton method to predict acceleration. An analytical solution of target maneuvering frequency is then achieved, by which the need of setting maneuvering acceleration limit is avoided. Meanwhile, adaptive calculation of process noise covariance matrix is accomplished. Moreover, usage of simplified Sage-Husa filter to realize an adaptive update of measuring noise covariance matrix is established. Simulation demonstrates that the proposed algorithm is with a better range tracking performance.

articleTitle: Analysis of Left-right Ambiguity in Multichannel Radar Forward-looking Imaging
abstract: Forward-looking imaging has important applications in aircrafts’ landing, autonomous navigation, and obstacle detection. However, faced with low azimuth resolution and left-right ambiguity, conventional monostatic SAR can't achieve high-resolution imaging of forward-looking areas. In this paper, by sequential reception of multiple receiving antennas located along the cross-range direction, a multichannel radar forward-looking imaging configuration is constructed. Then based on the equivalent phase center(EPC) principle, the approach to avoid left-right ambiguity is analyzed. Finally, the simulations are given to illustrate the effectiveness of the analysis.

articleTitle: Improved DOA Estimation with Extended Coprime MIMO Radar
abstract: Among various sparse multiple-input and multiple-out (MIMO) radar, coprime MIMO radar is fonud to be attractive because it owns a sparser structure. Generally, the uniform sparse arrays of the transmitter and the receiver are coprime, which determines the unique direction of arrival (DOA) estimation. In this paper, an extended coprime MIMO radar is proposed to obtain improved DOA estimation. By enlarging the inter-element of receive arrays properly, the unique angle is ensured to be determined by the ambiguous DOA estimates of transmit and receive arrays. Therefore, unitary estimation of signal parameter via rotational invariance technique (UESPRIT) method is used to obtain ambiguous DOA estimations, and the unique angle can be achieved by finding the coincide result from the ambiguous DOA estimation. Benefits from the enlarged array aperture, the estimation performance of the proposed coprime MIMO radar outperforms conventional coprime MIMO radar, which is demonstrated by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Vital Sign Detection Using Multichannel FMCW Radar
abstract: Multichannel frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar system can improve the accuracy and reliability of the vital sign detection. A vital sign detection algorithm for multichannel FMCW radar is proposed in this paper. The proposed algorithm utilizes the maximum ratio combing (MRC) technique to combine the phase signals from different channels. And the variational mode decomposition (VMD) algorithm is applied to decompose the combined phase signal into a number of intrinsic mode components. Finally the respiration and heartbeat signals can be accurately reconstructed using the mode judgement criteria. Experimental results have shown that the proposed method can improve the estimation accuracies of respiration and heartbeat frequencies using the multichannel measurement data.

articleTitle: Parameter Estimation Method of High-speed Maneuvering Target with Phase-encoded Signal
abstract: The phase-encoded signal is a Doppler-sensitive signal, which limits the use of the phase-encoded signal in radar systems. When detecting high-speed maneuvering targets, the modulation of the Doppler frequency to the intra-pulse signal causes serious distortion of the echo signal, which leads to a poor pulse compression result and affects target detection and parameter estimation. To address this problem, a high-speed target parameter estimation method is proposed. Compared with the existing algorithms, the high-order motion information of maneuvering target is employed in this paper. The simulation results prove the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Improved Smoothed $\ell_{p}$ Norm Minimization Algorithm for Direction of Arrival Estimation
abstract: The direction of arrival (DOA) estimation algorithm based on sparse reconstruction is a research focus in the field of signal processing. Considering the computational difficulty of <tex>$\ell_{0}$</tex> norm optimization, various approximate <tex>$\ell_{0}$</tex> norm optimization algorithms have been proposed. So far, the convex relaxation way, <tex>$\ell_{1}$</tex> norm optimization algorithm for DOA estimation is widely researched due to its high resolution and stability. However, those convex methods have limitations in sparser solutions and computational complexity. In this regard, the algorithm proposed in this paper aim to solve above problems with <tex>$\ell_{p}(0 < p < 1)$</tex> norm optimization. The proposed algorithm can resolve closely spaced and coherent signals using one snapshot in the presence of proper noise. Furthermore, adaptive <tex>$p$</tex> strategy is used to obtain more sparser solutions without losing stability. In addition, the proposed algorithm uses the accelerated quasi-Newton method, which leads to an improvement in computation time.

articleTitle: Robust adaptive beamformer based on minimum dispersion with a broad null by linear programming
abstract: The standard minimum dispersion distortionless response (MDDR) beamformer can provide a performance improvement for non-Gaussian signals compared to the minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) beamformer. However, the variety of the direction of the interference may have a great influence on the performance of the MDDR beamformer. To solve the problem, a robust beamformer with a broad null by linear programming is proposed for sub-Gaussian signals. Unlike the beamformers based on the minimum variance criterion, the proposed beamformer minimizes the <tex>$\ell_{p}$</tex> -norm of the output and meanwhile constrains not only the target response to be unity, but also the average power of the interference's dynamic angular sector to zero. The resulting optimization problem is cast as a linear programming and hence can be solved efficiently. Simulation results indicate that the proposed method offers a significant performance improvement if the direction of the interference varies with time.

articleTitle: Denoising of UAV Micro-Doppler Signatures Based on BEMD and Wavelet Transform
abstract: In recent years, the detection and classification of UAVs has become a hot issue. The difficulty is that UAVs have very small RCS and usually fly at low altitudes. Radar echo contains strong noise, clutter and other interference. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a denoising algorithm combining bivariate empirical mode decomposition(BEMD) and wavelet transform based on UAV micro-Doppler characteristics. First, the pre-processed radar signal is decomposed into complex modal components by BEMD decomposition. Then the peak value of the autocorrelation function is used to automatically select the IMF components containing the micro-Doppler feature to perform wavelet threshold denoising, and finally the micro-Doppler signal is reconstructed. Experiments were carried out using simulation and measured data of UAV rotor blades. Experimental results show that the proposed method has a significant denoising effect at low Signal-Noise-Ratio(SNR).

articleTitle: Dual mmWave radars fall detection using the Stockwell transform
abstract: Elderly fall detection based on radar technology has recently drawn more and more attention because of the advantages of privacy protection, all-day working, and non-intrusive properties. Numerous time-frequency representation methods have been used to extract fall signatures. However, the measurement of peak-peak Doppler frequency using short-time Fourier transform and wavelet transform is limited due to weak energy in the high Doppler frequency area. A method for human fall detection based on Stockwell transform with dual mm Wave radars is proposed in this paper. Two mmWave radars are vertically placed to collect human motions in different directions, and the Micro-doppler features of human motions are obtained using Stockwell transform. To enhance the feature for recognition, extracted ridgelines from two mm Wave radars are fused in the time-frequency domain. And the model trained by a convolutional neural network (CNN) is used for fall recognition. 960 fall motions and 720 non-fall motions from 60 volunteers were collected, and the experimental result shows that the proposed method can produce a recognition accuracy of up to 94.14%.

articleTitle: Manifold separation and polarimetric element space based parameter estimation for polarimetric monostatic MIMO radar
abstract: In this paper, a manifold separation technique and polarimetric element space-based direction-of-arrival and polarization estimation algorithm for monostatic polarimetric MIMO radar is proposed. Polynomial root finding technique is involved in the proposed method and thus the proposed method is computational efficient. To ensure the Vandermonde structure of the Fourier basis, transformation matrix is defined in this paper. The transmitter and receiver are uni-polarized antennas of arbitrary configurations and diversely polarized antennas of arbitrary configurations, respectively. Cramer Rao bound is also derived to compare with the performance of the proposed method. Simulation results are conducted to verify the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Based UAVs Resource Allocation for Radar-Communication Integrated System
abstract: Due to the limited mission accomplished by a single unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), radar-communication integrated system for group UAVs has attracted more attention in military and civilian fields. In this paper, the resource allocation problem is addressed for the group UAVs using the radar-communication integrated system. Large number of UAVs leads to the complexity of the resource allocation problem, so we propose a reinforcement learning-based methods. A novel reward combining both the mutual information (MI) and the communication rate (CR) is defined, where the MI is used to describe the detection performance and the CR is for that of the wireless communication. The implement of reinforcement learning for radar-communication integrated system for group UAVs includes deep Q network (DQN) and dueling-DQN algorithms. Simulation results show that the resource utilization in the radar-communication integrated system is improved effectively for the group UAVs.

articleTitle: Time-varying Vibration Compensation for FMCW Lidar Signals
abstract: Frequency modulation continuous wave (FMCW) lidar 3D imaging system may suffer from time-varying vibrations which will affect the accuracy of ranging and imaging of a target. The system uses only a single-period FMCW lidar signal to measure the range of each spot; however, traditional methods may not work well to compensate for the time-varying vibrations in a single period signal. To solve this problem, we propose a time-varying vibration compensation method based on segmented interference. We first divide the time-varying vibration errors into primary errors caused by the vibrations with a constant velocity and quadratic errors. Second, we estimate the coefficients of quadratic vibration errors by using a segmented interference method and build a quadratic compensation filter to eliminate the quadratic vibration errors from the original signals. Finally, we use the symmetrical relations of signals in a triangular FMCW period to estimate the vibration velocity and establish a primary compensation filter to eliminate the primary vibration errors. Numerical tests verify the applicability of this method in eliminating time-varying vibration errors with only one-period triangular FMCW signal.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Classification for Polarimetric SAR Images Based on Cross-View Tensor Product Graph Diffusion
abstract: The scattering feature plays a crucial role in the polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) image classification. In most cases, the commonly used feature concatenation is adopted to construct the similarity matrix, thus leading to the discriminability loss of some single-view features. To solve this problem, this paper proposes an unsupervised PolSAR image terrain classification method based on the cross-view tensor product graph (CV-TPG) diffusion. Multi-view learning can effectively integrate the data sets from different views, moreover, the diffusion based on the CV-TPG is capable of mining the intrinsic affinity along the manifold structure of data. First, the PolSAR image is over-segmented into many superpixels. Second, five feature vectors are extracted from the PolSAR image via superpixels to form three high-dimensional feature vectors, resulting in three corresponding similarity matrices with the Gaussian kernel. Third, multiple CV-TPGs are obtained by the tensor product operation based on three similarity matrices, then CV-TPGs are linearly fused for applying the diffusion process to achieve a more discriminative similarity matrix. Finally, spectral clustering based on the diffused similarity matrix is adopted to perform terrain classification. Extensive experiments conducted on the Oberpfaffenhofen data set demonstrate that CV-TPG diffusion can effectively combine the characteristic information of multiple views and achieve higher classification accuracy, compared to five other competitive state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Time-Frequency Characteristics of the Near-Field Micro-Doppler Effect in Passive Radar
abstract: In this paper, the time-frequency characteristics (TFC) of near-field micro-Doppler (MD) effect induced by blade rotation in passive radar are analyzed. Firstly, the electromagnetic scattering mechanisms corresponding to different blade flashes in the spectrogram are summarized. It shows that the TFC of the blade echo are composed of the TFC of the tip scattering points echo and the mirror reflection points echo. On this basis, the signal model of the near-field blade echo is established, and the TFC of the above mentioned scattering centers are derived, which together constitute the TFC of the whole blade echo. The results indicate that the blade flashes in the spectrogram of near-field MD effect present more complex shapes and characteristics than those under far-field condition. The simulation and experimental results validate the analysis conclusions.

articleTitle: Sidelobe Suppression by Phase-only Tapering with Integer Linear Programming
abstract: Phase-only tapering for sidelobe suppression is a simple method of phased array design due to the simplification of antenna manufacturing. When using digital phase shifters, considering the quantization of the phase, we employ integer linear programming to adjust the phased shifter and get a better pattern. The proposed method combines a fast sidelobe formula with a power reduction mathematical technique. Finally, we conduct numeric experiments to verify the proposed method.

articleTitle: Joint Optimization of Radar Assignment and Resource Allocation for Target Tracking in Phased Array Radar Network
abstract: This paper proposes a joint optimization strategy of radar assignment and resource allocation for target tracking in phased array radar network (PARN). The main purpose of the proposed strategy is to coordinate the radar assignment, transmit power, and dwell time of multiple radars to improve the target tracking accuracy, subject to several transmit resource budgets. The analytical expression for the Bayesian Cramér-Rao lower bound (BCRLB) is derived and adopted as the objective function to quantify the target tracking performance. Subsequently, a fast and effective two-step solution algorithm, which incorporates the interior point method and cyclic minimization framework, is proposed to solve the resulting optimization problem. Simulation results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the developed scheme.

Author Keywords: Joint radar assignment and resource allocation

articleTitle: Exponential FDA-MIMO radar mainlobe jamming suppression based on DL-EVE algorithm
abstract: When the training data contains target signals and the target steering vector mismatch for multiple-input multiple-output with frequency diverse array (FDA-MIMO) radar, the performance of mainlobe jamming suppression will be sharply declined. Considering that the nonlinear FDA-MIMO radar has no grating lobes in the range dimension, an exponential FDA-MIMO radar jamming suppression method combining diagonal loading and eigenvector elimination (DL-EVE) is proposed, which make full use of the correlation between the target steering vector and the signal subspace. Simulations show that under the conditions of low snapshots and low input signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), compared eigenspace based beamformer (ESB) algorithm, the proposed method can still effectively suppress the mainlobe jamming and output a higher signal-to-jamming and noise ratio (SJNR).

articleTitle: Optimization of Distributed Jamming Signal of Space-Time Adaptive Radar
abstract: In modern radar countermeasures, airborne and spaceborne radars play an important role. In the detection process of airborne radars, strong ground clutter will be generated. Space-time adaptive technology (STAP) has a good effect in suppressing clutter. As an adversary, it is particularly important that interference to STAP. Based on the previous STAP distributed interference, this paper studies an MPBI (M-Penalty-based Boundary Intersection) decomposition algorithm to optimize the effective interference of multiple jammers to multiple radars, which makes up for the shortcomings of the traditional method in which a jammer interferes with an intercepted radar. MPBI is used to solve the resource scheduling problem of interference pattern, interference power and the multi-objective optimization problem of interference power allocation in the multi-to-multi scenario, which improves optimization result.

articleTitle: Waveform Design based on Majorize-Minimize for FDA-MIMO Radar
abstract: In this paper, the waveform design under constant modulus constraint is investigated for the purpose of minimizing the sidelobes of the auto-correlations and the cross-correlations in FDA-MIMO radar. At the design stage, the problem is converted to an optimization problem to obtain the unimodular sequences with good auto/cross-correlation properties. Specifically, to solve the equivalent non-convex problem, the majorization-minimization (MM) method is utilized, where an approximate objective function is minimized. At the analysis stage, waveforms are embedded in the FDA-MIMO radar to evaluate the performance of the joint transmit-receive beampattern. Numerical results corroborate the performance of the designed waveforms.

articleTitle: A Broadband Reflectarray for Millimeter Wave Applications
abstract: An Millimeter-Wave (MMW) broadband reflectarray, which consists of metallic three parallel dipoles loaded by double square loop units, is investigated in this paper. The enough phasing range of 420° and nearly linearly reflected phase curve benefit from the stable outer square loop, which adds a resonant structure and implements relatively stable local periodic environment. The reflectarray is designed and simulated, which covers an aperture of 64×64 mm<sup>2</sup>.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Advantages of Quantum Illumination Radar by Using Radar Equation
abstract: Quantum radar uses the strong correlations of entangled photons and has a great potential to improve the detection sensitivity. Recently, many research results have been achieved in theoretical analysis and experiments on the performance advantages of quantum illumination radar. However, there are limited researches on its detection range. Based on the analysis of the noise tolerance of entangled state photons, we study the advantages of quantum illumination radar in detection range based on radar equation. It is shown that the detection range of quantum illumination radar is larger than that of classical radar in some regimes due to the strong noise suppression ability of quantum radar.

articleTitle: Ship detection using spaceborne rotating fan-beam radar
abstract: In order to meet the need of ship detection on the sea surface, a ship detection method using spaceborne rotating fan-beam radar is proposed. This method uses rotating fan-beam radar to transmit wideband LFM signal, carry out range high resolution and azimuth high resolution, and discover the ship on sea surface through Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR), obtain multiple observation information of the ship. Through the observation data of azimuth angle, doppler frequency and high resolution range profile, the ship length, ship velocity can be calculated, to realize the ship detection. The simulation results show that this method can discover the ship on the sea, get the effective ship information, and prove the ability of ship judgment.

articleTitle: Detection and Tracking of Multiple Human Targets with an UWB Monopulse Radar
abstract: A prototype ultra-wideband (UWB) monopulse radar for human detection and tracking is presented in this paper. Short pulse combined with linear frequency modulation is used as the transmit signal to obtain the required bandwidth, which guarantees high range resolution. Monopulse processing is utilized to enhance angular resolution without the need of high directivity antennas. Multiple target detection and tracking are achieved by signal and data processing algorithms. Performance of the proposed radar and algorithms are demonstrated by experimental results.

articleTitle: Coherent Fusion for Multistatic Forward-looking SAR with Flexible Topology using Generalized Matrix Pencil Algorithm
abstract: Multistatic forward-looking synthetic aperture radar (MF -SAR) can obtain high-resolution radar imagery of the area in front of the receivers. However, it is difficult to fuse the multiple measurements when the echo data are sampled with gaps. The quality of reconstructed imagery of the MF -SAR depends on the strict topology and the data fusion methods. To improve the imaging quality with a flexible topology, a coherent fusion method for MF -SAR using the generalized matrix pencil algorithm (GMPA) is proposed. First, the MF-SAR system consists of one stationary transmitter and two receivers is established. The reasons for limiting the topology structure of MF -SAR are analyzed. Second, the generalized bandwidth synthesis direction of the wavenumber spectrum is defined to effectively extrapolate the gap data. The projected measurements are corrected to align the wavenumber spectrum data. Finally, the matrix pencil algorithm is adopted to composite the spatial bandwidth observed by the leading receiver and the following receiver along the generalized bandwidth synthesis direction. Numerical simulations and experimental data are carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Long-time coherent integration method combining pulse compression and Radon fractional Fourier transform
abstract: In the conventional coherent radar signal processing process, cascaded processing which executes pulse compression and coherent integration in sequence cannot theoretically achieve the maximum accumulation of echo energy for high-speed maneuverable targets. The output results of the cascaded processing have deviation of target's peak position, and even have problems such as the broadening of main lobe, the loss of gain and the increasing of sidelobes. Therefore, a long-time coherent integration method combining pulse compression and Radon fractional Fourier transform (PCRFRFT) is proposed in this paper. Taking advantage of the correlation between signals, the method combines two dimensions which is the fast time (intra-pulse time) dimension and the slow time (inter-pulse time) dimension, then the acceleration is also added as another dimension of the search parameters. The method compensates the intra-pulse Doppler shift, the inter-pulse Doppler shift and acceleration simultaneously so as to realize the target gain maximization. Experimental results show that the performance of the joint processing is better than that of the cascaded processing.

articleTitle: Low-altitude Wind-shear Wind Speed Estimation Based on Improved Auxiliary Channel
abstract: Due to the amplitude and phase error of array elements, the clutter suppression performance of airborne weather radar is reduced, resulting in the inaccuracy of low-altitude wind-shear wind speed estimation. In this paper, a method of low wind-shear wind speed estimation based on improved auxiliary channels with less calculation is proposed. Firstly, the space-time interpolation method based on the modified steering vector constraint is used to correct the distance dependence of the clutter. Secondly, select the auxiliary channels according to the clutter energy distribution of the bin to be measured to construct an adaptive dimension reduction processor. Then, the adaptive dimension reduction processor is used to filter the radar echo in space-time two-dimensional. Finally, the experimental results show that the proposed method can achieve clutter suppression and get accurate wind speed estimation.

articleTitle: FDA-SAR Imaging Algorithm Based on Beam Scene Matching
abstract: Traditional SAR imaging system is always accompanied by excessively high sidelobe levels, which cannot improve the comprehensive detection probability of the target. However, The traditional windowing method cannot balance the main lobe widening and sidelobe suppression. Frequency Diverse Array(FDA) radar has received wide attention from academic community because of the range-angle-time three-dimensional coupling characteristics of their transmitting beams. Based on previous studies, this paper proposes the concept of imaging scene and beam energy matching, and improves the frequency diverse array radar echo baseband signal model, so that the FDA can be better applied to synthetic aperture radar imaging. In addition, this paper proposes a FDA-SAR range-dimension matched filtering method. This method can better gather the point target energy in range dimension, without increasing the time complexity of the algorithm; it has a better sidelobe suppression effect while narrowing the mainlobe width, so that the FDA-SAR system can still obtain high-quality and clear scene images under strong noise.

articleTitle: Foliage-concealed Target Detection Based on Deep Learning in Low Frequency UWB SAR Images
abstract: Low frequency ultra-wideband synthetic aperture radar (UWB SAR) has the well ability of the foliage penetration and high-resolution imaging, which can detect foliage-concealed targets in the forests. However, the low frequency UWB SAR images often contain many non-target strong scattering points like thick tree trunks. This paper proposes a foliage-concealed target detection method based on the deep learning in the low frequency UWB SAR images. First, based on the CARABAS-II SAR dataset, the low frequency UWB SAR dataset of foliage-concealed target and corresponding annotation is generated by random cutting and data augmentation. Then, a convolutional neural network (CNN) is designed for prediction of the foliage-concealed target, and the output is a predicted image of the same size as the input image. Besides, the generated dataset is used to the designed CNN, and the training is stop when the network converges. Finally, based on the characteristics of the network output result, the variance filtering and binarization operations are used for the post-processing of the network output image, to obtain the final prediction result. Experimental results show that the proposed method can realize the foliage-concealed target detection in low frequency UWB SAR images and ensure the rapid detection of multiple targets with the high accuracy.

articleTitle: A Design of Broadband TR Module Based on 3D Silicon Package
abstract: For the needs of highly integrated TR modules for active phased array radars, this article introduces a design method for broadband TR modules that can be used in phased array systems. The volume and weight of the TR modules can be significantly reduced by the method. A 2-18GHz broadband TR module was designed and made by the 3D silicon package. The size of the TR module is <tex>$16\text{mm}\times 16\text{mm}\times 1\text{mm}$</tex>, and the weight is 0.6g. The RF performance of the TR module was optimized by HFSS. Its output power of is greater than 31dBm, the receive gain is greater than 30dB and the noise figure is less than 5.4dB. The design method can be widely used in highly integrated TR modules.

articleTitle: Radar Polarization Diversity Technology for Low-altitude Targets
abstract: When the radar detects low-altitude targets, the mirrored target seriously affects the performance of radar detection and elevation angle measurement. The influence of the mirror target on the radar elevation angle measurement is generally described by a two-point source glint model. There have been many domestic and foreign literatures on low-altitude target detection, but they have not paid enough attention to the important influence of radar polarization. This paper mainly studies the suppression method of angle measurement error based on polarization diversity, and compares the simulations for different polarization diversity methods. The simulation results verify the superiority of the performance of this method.

articleTitle: Cognitive Radar Waveform Optimization Based on Improved Bald Eagle Search Algorithm
abstract: Aiming at the problem of slow convergence speed and insufficient solution accuracy in cognitive radar waveform optimization of the bald eagle search algorithm (BES), we propose the improved bald eagle search algorithm to optimize cognitive radar waveform. In this paper, the waveform optimization problem is solved by optimizing the waveform pulse width and frequency modulation. Population position is initialized by Tent mapping to improve the quality of initial solution, and Gaussian perturbation is used to speed up the convergence and jump out of the local optimum. The results of simulation show that the improved bald eagle search algorithm converges faster, and target tracking accuracy based on the improved bald eagle search algorithm waveform optimization is higher.

articleTitle: Mainlobe Jamming Suppression Method Based on Combination of Spatial and Polarization Domain for Distributed Array Radar
abstract: Main auxiliary joint distributed array radar can form a larger aperture by using a smaller number of unit radars, so as to obtain spatial high-resolution characteristics. However, in the case of mainlobe jamming, its output performance will be greatly affected. In order to solve this problem, this paper proposes a spatial polarization domain joint mainlobe jamming suppression method for distributed main auxiliary joint array radar. Firstly, the spatial polarization steering vector is constructed by using the different polarization characteristics of main array and auxiliary array. Then, the jamming polarization state and direction are estimated by using the spatial polarization steering vector and the received signal. Finally, the minimum mean square error (MMSE) criterion is used to calculate the beamforming weight vector for mainlobe jamming suppression. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm and advantages over traditional beamforming methods.

articleTitle: Ionospheric Clutter Image Segmentation Method of High Frequency Surface Wave Radar Based on the Improved Deeplab Network
abstract: High Frequency Surface Wave Radar(HFSWR) can achieve over-the-horizon detection, which effectively detects and tracks the ships and ultra-low altitude aircrafts, as well as the acquisition of sea state information such as icebergs and ocean currents and so on. However, HFSWR is seriously affected by clutters, especially sea clutter and ionospheric clutter. In this paper, we propose a deep learning image semantic segmentation method based on optimized Deeplabv3+ network to resolve the automatic detection of ionospheric clutter that uses the Range-Doppler spectrum images of HFSWR during the typhoon as experimental data, which avoids the disadvantage of traditional segmentation methods that require a large amount of a priori experience.

articleTitle: Single Snapshot DOA Estimation Based on Learned Modified Smoothed L0 Algorithm
abstract: Based on the sparsity of signal, sparse recovery (SR) method can use single snapshot data for high-resolution Direction of Arrival (DOA) estimation of correlated signal sources. However, typical SR methods suffer from the problems of parameter setting difficulty, high computational complexity, and low recovery accuracy, limiting their practical applications. To solve these problems, based on the theory of intelligent learning, this paper unfolds the Modified Smoothed LO (MSLO) algorithm into a deep network, proposing the Learned MSLO (LMSLO) algorithm. By developing the deep LMSLO network and based on a complete training dataset, the proposed method can learn the best parameters of the MSLO algorithm, e.g., the approximation parameter, the iteration step, and the steepness factor, hence improving the convergence performance of the MSLO algorithm. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can obtain higher DOA estimation performance with lower computing cost than the SLO and MSLO algorithms.

articleTitle: Atomic Norm Minimization Based DoA Estimation with Lens Antenna Arrays
abstract: The conventional multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) structure is impractical for large-scale arrays due to the huge hardware complexity and power consumption. This paper studies the direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation with the promising lens antenna array (LAA). The main challenge is that not all incident signals can be received due to the limited number of RF chains. Therefore, the antenna selection procedure is proposed to select the subsets of array elements for receiving low dimensional signal data. Then, we formulate an atomic norm minimization and its dual problem to recover the original signal. However, roots finding based DoA estimation is no longer applicable in the LAA scheme. To circumvent this problem, we construct a trigonometric polynomial according to the relations between dual variables and the spatial frequencies, and maximum value search over a small interval is adopted to compensate for the power leakage errors. Numerical simulations show the superiority of the proposed algorithm by comparing it with state-of-the-art algorithms.

articleTitle: Improved Method of Human Vital Sign Parameters Estimation Based on Hilbert-Huang Transform
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel method for estimating parameters of human vital signs in a frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar system. Specifically, we first introduce the signal model of human vital signs in the FMCW radar system. Then, the Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) and variational mode decomposition-Hilbert transform (VMD-HT) algorithms are used on the signal components after pre-processing to estimate respiratory rate (RR) and heart rate (HR), respectively. Finally, the simulation and experimental results validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: CFAR-Guided EfficientDet with Improved Loss Function for SAR Target Detection
abstract: Target detection has been a hot topic in the field of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image analysis. In this paper, the one-stage object detector EfficientDet is applied in the SAR target detection. Since the labeled SAR data is limited and the SAR scene contains only a small number of target areas, the imbalance problem between positive and negative samples is serious in the network training process. To solve this problem, we introduce the Average-Precision Loss (AP-Loss) into the loss function of the class prediction net of EfficientDet. In addition, we integrate the binary indicator map obtained by the two-parameter constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detection into EfficientDet to guide the generation process of anchors. The experimental results on the miniSAR data demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Author Keywords: imbalance problem between positive and negative samples

articleTitle: Multiple Target Track-Before-Detect Using Sequential ML-PDA
abstract: The maximum likelihood probabilistic data association (ML-PDA) algorithm is the optimal detection algorithm in the maximum likelihood sense, but it has a key limitation that it is restricted to the single-target case. In this paper, we propose another ML-PDA algorithm for multi-target scenarios, called the Sequential ML-PDA (SML-PDA) algorithm. The SML-PDA algorithm can achieve multi-target detection and tracking without knowing the number of targets in advance. The simulation results prove the rationality of the SML-PDA algorithm. And the SML-PDA algorithm is applied to the measured data to validate its performance in real scenarios.

articleTitle: Mismatched Filters Design to Reduce Range Sidelobe Modulation of Pulse-to-Pulse Diverse Waveform
abstract: We consider mismatched filters design in this paper to reduce range sidelobe modulation, which occurs when employing pulse-to-pulse waveform diversity in PD or MTI systems and induces additional clutter leakage. We illustrate that the clutter leakage in sidelobes is proportional to its slow-time variance of the compressed outputs. Therefore, we suggest an lp-norm like summation of the variances over the sidelobe as the metric, such that we can minimize the average or maximum clutter leakage by tuning the exponent. Meanwhile, we also consider the range sidelobe level and signal-to-noise ratio loss in the multi-pulse compression stage. We solve the resulting optimization problem using conjugate gradient method. To accelerate the problem solving, we devise closed-form formulas to calculate both the objective function and its gradient via fast Fourier transformation. Numeric results indicate that the proposed method can handle filters design of very large length and set cardinality.

articleTitle: Centralized Multiple Moving Target Detection Using Multistatic Radar System
abstract: This study investigates the problem of the multiple moving target detection using multistatic radar system (MSRS). A detector based on generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT) is presented with unknown target location and velocity. A lack of information about accurate target location will cause an error in registration. Some spatial resolution cells of no targets gather observation data of targets, which leads to extra false alarm, called “ghost target”. Therefore, “ghost target” is discriminated and the interferential amplitude is estimated by maximum likelihood estimation (MLE). Subsequently, the GLRT detector is modified to reduce the false alarm and detect target. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can suppress the interference while accurately detecting multiple moving targets.

articleTitle: A Probabilistic Model-Based Robust Waveform Design for MIMO Radar Detection
abstract: This paper addresses robust waveform design for multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) radar detection. A probabilistic model is proposed to describe the target uncertainty. Considering that waveform design based on maximizing the probability of detection is intractable, the relative entropy between the distributions of the observations under two hypotheses (viz., the target is present/absent) is employed as the design metric. To tackle the resulting non-convex optimization problem, an efficient algorithm based on minorization-maximization (MM) is derived. Numerical results demonstrate that the waveform synthesized by the proposed algorithm is more robust to model mismatches.

articleTitle: A Novel Chaff Cloud Recognition Method Based on Wideband Polarization Radar
abstract: Chaff cloud recognition (CCR) is a vital anti-jamming way in modern warfare. The existing recognition methods have poor performance in complex electromagnetic environment. Therefore, in this paper, a novel convolutional neural network based CCR (CNN-CCR) method relying on wideband polarization radar is proposed. First, the chaff cloud echo is simulated at different stages, in different polarization types and sea conditions. Second, the CNN-CCR is built, whose inputs are the range profile sequences on the same range unit detected by the greatest of constant false alarm rate detector (GO-CFAR). Finally, the effectivity of our proposed method is verified by the simulated data. The experimental results show that our proposed method can effectively address the CCR in high sea conditions and high jamming-to-signal ratios (JSR).

articleTitle: SAR Image Change Detection Based on Geometric Mean Operator and Extreme Learning Machine
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image is independent of atmospheric and sunlight conditions and can be acquired under all weather and all day. As a part of SAR image application, change detection has high practical value, such as urban sprawl detection, hazard assessment of earthquake areas. In this paper, we put forward a new difference image (DI) generated by geometric mean operator which combined with log-ratio, neighborhood ratio and normal difference operator, and retained the advantages of each operator. Then, a change detection method of SAR image based on extreme learning machine (ELM) is used to classify the pixels in two original SAR images to form the final change image. Experimental results on two real SAR image datasets show that the proposed difference image generation method is robust to speckle noise, and the change detection method based on the new DI operator and ELM can effectively detect variation information in multi-phase SAR images.

articleTitle: Semi-supervised Open-set Recognition of Radar Active Jamming
abstract: With the emergence of various kinds of complex radar jamming, radar jamming intelligent recognition technology has increasingly become the key to electronic counter-counter measures. To achieve radar jamming open-set recognition with a small number of tagged samples, Generative adversarial network-based pseudolabeled convolutional neural network (GAN-PL-CNN) model is proposed in this paper. Firstly, radar jamming is modelled, and the radar jamming datasets with known and unknown types are established after time-frequency transformation and image processing. Then, the adaptive pseudolabeling method is used to achieve semi-supervised recognition of radar jamming by combining the learning capability of convolutional neural networks and the characteristics of pseudolabeling to increase labeled samples intelligently. Finally, generative adversarial networks are introduced to enhance the recognition ability of the model and the discrimination ability of the unknown type through the game between the generator and the discriminator in the iterative process. Experimental results show that the GAN-PL-CNN model achieves 89.7%-95.1% for known types and 30.7%-86.8% for unknown types at 3%-6% labeling rate. As the number of labeled samples increases, the recognition effect becomes better and has a greater ability to exclude unknown type.

articleTitle: LFM-MSK Spectrum Constraint Method Based on Pulse Edge Correction
abstract: The combination of radar and communication makes them give full play to their respective advantages such as high power and wide bandwidth, therefore, the integration of radar communication has recently received widespread attention. The design of the integrated signal is the key to achieve integration. Linear Frequency Modulation-Minimum Shift Keying (LFM-MSK) modulates the communication information to the LFM signal via MSK. LFM-MSK combines the features of LFM and MSK. However, it has a problem of spectrum extension. This leads to severe neighbor frequency interference, which has a great impact on the performance of the system. To solve this problem, this paper proposes an LFM-MSK spectrum constraint method based on pulse edge correction. The first step is to derive the number of codes to be adjusted. Then the special MSK signal is modulated at the edge of the LFM. Simulation results show that after the edge correction, the spectrum expansion is significantly improved and the spectrum of LFM-MSK is constrained to the design bandwidth. This avoids interference from adjacent channels and improves the electromagnetic compatibility of the electronic system. The innovation of this paper is to propose a special MSK modulation method on the LFM edge to solve the problem of LFM-MSK spectrum expansion. Compared with the traditional method of simple splicing of LFM and integrated signals, this method can more effectively constrain the spectrum to the designed bandwidth

articleTitle: Point Cloud Features-Based Random Forest for Road User Classification via Millimeter Wave Radar
abstract: Vehicle-mounted millimeter-wave(mmWave) radar sensors can meet the requirements of vehicles for the all-day and all-weather sensing of the surrounding environment. The mmWave radar can produce one to dozens of target points for ordinary road users, and such sparse point cloud data lead to difficulties in classification. When there are fewer or even only one point in the target-level point cloud, which usually occurs when the object is tiny or far from the radar, the classification accuracy of this type of object will become very poor. To improve the classification accuracy of radar-based road users, we propose a new feature extraction and hierarchical classification algorithm for mmWave radar point clouds. We extracted 6-dimensional and 125-dimensional features for single-point and multi-point objects based on the range, azimuth, velocity, and radar cross-section (RCS) of point clouds measured by the mmWave radar to characterize the motion, attitude, position, and material of the road user. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, we evaluate our method on the publicly available dataset. Compared with the traditional algorithm, the overall classification accuracy of the proposed method is higher. In addition, this divide-and-conquer strategy also improves the classification performance of single-point objects.

articleTitle: A Novel Interference Suppression Method for DTMB-based Passive Radar
abstract: A novel interference suppression method is proposed for digital television terrestrial multimedia broadcasting (DTMB) based passive radar considering sampling frequency offset (SFO) compensation in reference signal reconstruction. A sub-band recursive least square (RLS) interference cancellation algorithm is introduced to reduce the computational load. A scheme for reference signal processing is proposed via analyzing and comparing the results from different reference signal processing methods under different reference channel conditions. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is verified via measured and simulated data.

articleTitle: Individual Intelligent Recognition Method Based on Fingerprint Features of Radar Emitter
abstract: Aiming at the problem of radar emitter individual recognition with unintentional modulation feature, a method of emitter fingerprint identification based on deep learning is proposed. In this method, the deep fingerprint features of radar emitter are extracted by deep Convolutional neural network, and the fingerprint feature library is constructed. Through similarity calculation, the individual recognition results of radar emitter signal are obtained. The results show that the new method can effectively identify both known and unknown emitter individuals.

articleTitle: Antenna Selection for Enhanced DOA Estimation: Exploring the Symmetries
abstract: The performance of direction of arrival (DOA) estimation using antenna arrays is fundamentally determined by the array configuration through its influence on the Cramer-Rao bound (CRB). Thus, antenna selection strategies may be employed to reduce computational and hardware cost while optimizing the DOA estimation performance. This is done by choosing the optimal subarray that minimizes the CRB for a particular DOA or range of DOAs. However, the cost of solving this optimization problem is quite high. In this paper, we study the symmetries of the cost function that is used in implementing the antenna selection for enhanced DOA estimation in order to gain significant insights into the structure of the problem and consequently achieve significant reduction in complexity. In particular, we derive a group of transformations under which the cost function is invariant. This group then allows us to reduce the domain over which the optimization problem is to be solved.

articleTitle: A Probabilistic Jamming Strategy Model for Frequency Agility Radar Anti-Jamming Problem
abstract: With the development of electronic warfare, the jammer is much smarter than before and can adopt different strategies to jam the radar. To design efficient anti-jamming strategies, the radar anti-jamming problem is recently modeled as a Markov decision process (MDP) problem and reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms are used to solve it. However, common RL algorithms needs a large number of interaction samples, which is not realistic in practice. To address this problem, we propose a probabilistic jamming strategy model for the frequency agility radar (FA) that can learn the unknown jamming strategy through fewer interaction samples. Based on proposed model, a jamming strategy is first expressed by a series of unknown probability matrixes and weights. Then, the FA radar is used to induce jammer to emit jamming signals and collects samples of radar-jammer interaction in MDP. The model parameters are estimated by means of maximum likelihood estimation (MLE). Finally, RL algorithm can be used to train the anti-jamming strategies through offline interaction. Simulation results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Satellite Attitude Estimation Based on ISAR Image Sequence Interpretation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for the estimation of satellite attitude based on ISAR image interpretation. The solar panel of the satellite is segmented from the initial ISAR image using Pix2pixGAN network, and morphological method is used for edge extraction according to the parallelogram characteristics of the solar panel. According to the projection process of ISAR imaging, the optimization function for the 3D absolute attitude estimation of the satellite solar panel is established, and the attitude of the satellite is solved by iteration. The experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Phase Unwrapping Based on CFAR Detection for Multi-baseline InISAR
abstract: A phase unwrapping method based on constant false alarm rate (CF AR) detection is proposed for multi-baseline interferometric inverse synthetic aperture radar (InISAR). Aiming at the problem of ambiguity number estimation error under the condition of phase noise, Chinese remainder theorem (CRT) and cluster analysis are utilized to acquire the probability distribution of phase noise. By introducing CFAR detection, the novel method reduced the error probability of ambiguity number estimation. Through simulation, it is verified that the novel method can effectively suppress phase noise and obtain accurate phase unwrapping results.

articleTitle: Coastal Sea Surface Temperature Inversion from Microwave Radiometer using Radial Basis Function Neural Network
abstract: A radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) method is proposed to retrieve sea surface temperature (SST) in global coastal waters by passive microwave (PMW) radiometer measurements. Based on the RBFNN method, an optimal feature combination for the model input layer is obtained. The best parameters setting of the model is determined by grid-search method. Finally, a prediction model of RBFNN which is suitable for SST inversion of coastal waters is constructed. The inversion accuracy of the model was evaluated using the new data. Results show that SSTs retrieved by this model has a mean bias of <tex>$\mathbf{0.071}^{\mathbf{o}}\mathbf{C}$</tex> and root-mean-square error (RMSE) of <tex>$1.18^{\mathrm{o}}\mathrm{C}$</tex> in the global coastal waters. The accuracy of this model is not bad and can be used as an effective supplement to the SST inversion in coastal waters.

articleTitle: Off-Grid Sparse Bayesian Learning Algorithm for Compressed Sparse Array
abstract: The compressed sparse array (CSA) structure combines the advantages of the sparse array and compressed sensing, which not only reduces the number of antennas, but also decreases the number of RF front-end channels, thus obtaining high estimation performance with low complexity. However, the existing under-determined direction of arrival (DOA) estimation algorithms for CSA are based on compression reconstruction so far, where the accuracy and resolution of estimation are limited by the off-grid effect. Focusing on this problem, this paper proposes an estimation algorithm named CSA-based off-grid sparse Bayesian learning (CSA-OGSBL). The proposed CSA-OGSBL algorithm presents a system model in which we consider the unknown variance into the signal vector of interest and improves the traditional off-grid method through updating the grid points iteratively. The superiority of the proposed CSA-OGSBL algorithm in terms of estimation precision is identified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Anti-intermittent Sampling Jamming Method Based on Frequency Agile Radar and K-means
abstract: Frequency agility can greatly improve the low interception and anti-jamming ability of the radar by randomly changing the carrier frequency from pulse to pulse. However, the emergence of intermittent sampling interference makes it face severe challenges. The jammer intermittently samples and rapidly transmits the intercepted radar signal in the time domain, forming a series of false targets in the current pulse repetition interval (PRI). Because those false targets are highly similar to the true targets, the radar cannot detect and track the true target correctly. To deal with the problem, an anti-intermittent sampling jamming method based on frequency agile radar and K-means is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the radar emitted signal is designed in the form of intra-pulse frequency coding and inter-pulse frequency agility. Secondly, the K-means, a machine learning-based algorithm, is applied to judge whether there is jamming in the echo. After the interference being suppressed, the orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm is adopted for high resolution range-Doppler reconstruction, realizing the moving target detection (MTD). Theoretical analysis and simulation experiments verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Modified Omega-K Algorithm for Bistatic Forward-Looking SAR Data Imaging
abstract: Accurate two dimension frequency spectrum (2D FS) with acceleration, two-way range coupling terms, and spatial variant Doppler parameters are main problems to be solved in translational variant bistatic forward-looking SAR (TV BFSAR) with curved trajectory. For these issues, a modified Omega-K imaging algorithm is derived in this paper. The maximum usage of 2D FS based on method of series reversion (MSR) is achieved by linear range cell migration correction and 2D FS is linearized in bistatic range by using high-order polynomial fitting. Then, a method of azimuth resampling is introduced to implement compensation of spatial variant Doppler parameters. And the small-aperture data is focused in the azimuth frequency domain to avoid azimuth aliasing without padding zeros. Finally, the raw bistatic SAR data verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method

Author Keywords: Translational variant bistatic forward-looking synthetic aperture radar (TV BFSAR)

articleTitle: Monitoring of Lake Area Changes from SAR Images Based on Convolutional Neural Networks and Markov Random Field
abstract: Monitoring of the distribution and changes of inland water is an important application of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data interpretation. Water extraction from SAR images is a challenging task because of the complexity of imaging conditions and the various land background. In this paper, a supervised classification method is proposed to delineate the lake water area from SAR images based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and modified Markov Random Field (MRF). To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, the Sentinel-1 datasets are used to delineate the water area of Lake Shijiu and Lake Nanyi in the downstream Yangtze River Basin. The experimental results show that the performance of water bodies extraction from the two lakes is satisfactory. Moreover, the changes of water area of the two lakes in the downstream Yangtze River are revealed, and a serious expansion has been found in the lake surface area due to the large rainfall in July 2020.

articleTitle: Target parameter estimation approach for FDA-MIMO radar in spatial colored noise
abstract: A target parameter estimation algorithm for frequency diverse array multiple-input multiple-output (FDA-MIM 0) radar in spatial colored noise environment is developed. This algorithm makes use of the temporal un-correlation of spa-tial colored noise and constructs a four-dimensional covariance tensor to remove the influence of spatial colored noise. The four-dimensional tensor is transformed into a three-dimensional tensor by using the properties of generalized tensorization of parallel factor (PARAFAC) model. The transmitter and receiver steering matrices are obtained by PARAFAC decomposition. Then angle and range is estimated by LS approach. This algorithm not only removes the influence of colored noise, but also utilizes the multi-dimensional structure of tensor data to enhance the estimation performance. The performance of the method in this paper is more outstanding than others. Numerical experiments show the superiority of the method in this paper.

articleTitle: DOA Estimation via an Augmented Unfolded Coprime MIMO Configuration of Transceiver Reversal with Enhanced Degrees of Freedom
abstract: This paper proposes an augmented unfolded coprime MIMO configuration of transceiver reversal, where the transmitter adopts an augmented unfolded coprime array, and the layout of the receiver is obtained by flipping the transmitter. From the perspective of the sum-difference co-array (SDCA), the closed-form expressions for the range of consecutive lags, the number of discrete lags and the degrees of freedom (DOF) are derived. Moreover, the sparse reconstruction method of interpolated virtual elements is employed for direction of arrival (DOA) estimation. Compared with the conventional coprime MIMO configuration, the proposed MIMO can provide more DOF and larger virtual aperture. Simulation results verify the superior performance of the proposed MIMO configuration.

articleTitle: A High Resolution Parameter Estimation Method based on CINTAF-HAF for Cubic Frequency Modulated Signals
abstract: Aiming at the problem of parameter estimation for cubic frequency modulated (CFM) signals, a method based on high order ambiguity function (HAF) and coherently integrated nonuniform trilinear autocorrelation function (CINTAF) is proposed in this paper. In this method, the CFM signals are demodulated to quadratic frequency modulated (QFM) signals via the HAF, and then the CINTAF is applied to realize the parameter estimation of QFM signals. Through the scaled Fourier transform (SFT) and fast Fourier transform (FFT) operations, the QFM signals' energy can be quickly coherently integrated in the CINTAF. The analyses and simulation results show that the proposed CINTAF-HAF superior to other algorithms in terms of parameter estimation resolution, at the same time, the proposed method remains good anti-noise performance and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Plug-and-Play ADMM for Sparse ISAR Imaging
abstract: Under the condition of sparse aperture, sparse signal recovery (SSR) theory is generally utilized to obtain radar images. However, the existing SSR methods require heavy computation with a lot of iterations. Recently emerging plug-and-play (PnP) prior technology is a flexible framework that combines the forward imaging model with the prior model. Inspired by this, we proposed a novel PnP framework for sparse ISAR image reconstruction, which utilized a complex-valued convolutional neural network to denoise ISAR images and learn prior information. Thus, the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) based imaging algorithm combined with the trained denoising network can take advantage of learning-based methods and model-based methods. Simulation and experimental results show that the proposed PnP-ADMM imaging algorithm can obtain high imaging quality results while maintaining efficient computation compared with the state-of-the-art sparse ISAR imaging method.

articleTitle: Deconvolution Technique for InSAR Phase Restoration
abstract: Interferometric phase generated from coherent processing from Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) plays a vital role in large-scale deformation monitoring and digital elevation model (DEM) generation. Due to the coherence loss between acquisitions, the produced interferometric phases contain noise, which affects the application performance of interferometric SAR (InSAR) phases. Most state-of-the-art InSAR phase restoration methods are generally based on the nonlocal filtering processing scheme. In this paper, we propose a data-driven approach which formulates the InSAR phase restoration problem from a deconvolution perspective. Then, based on the learned convolutional filters from the data, we then obtain the denoised InSAR phases via solving a sparse coding problem. The proposed method can not only suppress interferometric phase noise, but also avoid the staircase effect and preserve the details. The experimental results on synthetic and one RADARSAT-2 dataset, respectively, demonstrate that the proposed method achieves the best performance among those previous state-of-the art nonlocal InSAR filter-based methods.

articleTitle: Domain Knowledge Enhanced Deep Neural Network for Limited Data SAR Vehicle Target Recognition
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) target recognition faces the challenges that there are limited labeled data. Recent limited data SAR target recognition algorithms overlook the domain knowledge of the target. Domain knowledge enhanced deep neural network (DK-ConvNet) is proposed in this study, which considers the azimuth angle, the length-width-ratio and the targets' area of SAR vehicles, to overcome the over-fitting problems of limited data. The information of vehicle domain knowledge is merged to the probability output of A-ConvNet. To extract the domain knowledge accurately, the segmentation results in the SARBake database are also used. All experiments are conducted under the public moving and stationary target acquisition and recognition (MSTAR) database. Our proposed DK-ConvNet has achieved 72.2% and 93.1% under 10-way 10-shot and 10-way 30-shot in standard operation condition (SOC), whose labeled samples are randomly selected from the training set and DK-ConvNet demonstrated advantages in accuracy compared with other limited data classification methods as well.

articleTitle: Array Calibration Method for Sensor Position Errors Based on IWO-PSO
abstract: In view of the problem that array errors lead to the performance degradation of the high-resolution direction of arrival (DOA) algorithms, we proposed an offline array errors correction method based on the invasive weed optimization (IWO) and particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm for sensor position errors. By using an auxiliary signal source with known azimuth, and combining the basic principle of subspace and the IWO-PSO algorithm, we transform the array errors solution into the parameter optimization problem, and modify the original steering vector with the estimated array errors. After correction of sensor position errors of linear arrays, good DOA estimation performances are obtained. In addition, the proposed method has no special requirements on array structure, and can be extended to the sensor position errors calibration of other arbitrary arrays.

articleTitle: An Automatic Point Target Interpolation and Profile Extraction Method based on SAR Spectrum Image
abstract: Interpolation of point target and profile extraction of side lobe direction are the key steps of SAR image evaluation. Based on the correspondence between time domain and frequency domain features of SAR point targets, this paper proposes an interpolation and profile extraction method based on spectral image of point targets. Firstly, a complete spectrum is obtained by image segmentation of the extended spectrum, and then corner detection is performed on the extracted spectrum. Finally, the frequency domain zeros are added to the extracted spectral image to achieve time-domain interpolation, and the angle of sidelobe expansion direction is calculated according to the corner detection results for two-dimensional section extraction in time domain. In this paper, the proposed method is used to interpolate and extract the point targets under various SAR imaging geometry conditions, such as High squint SAR, spotligth SAR, sliding spotligth SAR, and GEOSAR. The experimental results verify the accuracy and applicability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Flexible Priori Proximal Bayesian Learning for High-Resolution SAR Imagery
abstract: The conventional high-resolution synthetic aperture radar(SAR) imagery based on Bayesian learning encounter the problems of static and inflexible of prior. In this paper, a novel Bayesian learning algorithm based on flexible prior (FP-Bayes) is proposed for high-resolution SAR imagery, in which a new flexible prior is introduced to represent the rich features of target scene. However, the model becomes complicated due to the intended prior, which is hard to be solved by the classic Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling algorithms. Therefore, the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) is applied to this problem. Considering the potential function of the posterior distribution is likely to be non-differentiable, the proximal operator is introduced, and the proximal-HMC (P-HMC) is developed, which is capable of solving the sampling problem of this posterior. To this end, the high-resolution SAR images can be obtained. In the experimental part, the raw SAR data is utilized to verify the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed algorithm. The phase transition diagram (PTD) is also adopted to analyze the imaging performance quantitatively.

articleTitle: Multiple Orbital Angular Momentum Vortex beams Generation With Narrow Divergence Angle using metasurface
abstract: In this paper, one multiple orbital angular momentum (OAM) vortex beam with narrow divergence angle reflective metasurface composed of <tex>$31\times 31$</tex> elements is proposed, which can generate different propagation directions and OAM vortex beams with different OAM modes. The reflective metasurface is composed of rotationally symmetric subwavelength units and the range of the reflection phase can reach <tex>$\mathbf{360^{\circ}}$</tex> by controlling the structure size of the unit. The designed reflectarray is modeled and simulated using full-wave electromagnetic simulation software at the center frequency 26 GHz. The simulated results confirm that OAM vortex beams with narrow divergence angles are successfully generated above the reflective metasurface.

Author Keywords: Multiple orbital angular momentum (OAM) vortex beam

articleTitle: A Pessimistic One-bit LMPIT for Non-circular Sources with Single Channel
abstract: This paper presents an invariant test to detect the existence of non-circular echo in circular additive noise. The observation is extend with its conjugate complimentary and quantized by preserve its sign only. We firstly show the test statistic is equivalent to the correlation factor. Then we resort to evaluation its performance by using the first two moments, and matching them with well-studied Gaussian distribution, which admits a pessimistic formulations for both hypotheses. Numerical results validate our theoretical calculations are accurate for large sample regime.

articleTitle: 5G Multi-Base Station Optimal Deployment for Communication and Illegal UAVs Detection
abstract: To detect illegal unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) while guarantee the communication quality simultaneously, an optimal deployment problem for 5G multi-base station cooperation system is investigated in this paper. The multi-base station deployment optimal problem is solved by proposing an improved iteration algorithm, Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO). Firstly, an evaluation model of multi-base station deployment is established by determining the deployment position and antenna declination angle of each base station using effective detection coverage and effective communication coverage as two objective functions. Then, to obtain the optimal deployment result, a test region whose center is Chengdu Tianfu Square is chosen. Finally, by comparing performance between traditional uniform deployment and the optimal deployment obtained in the test region, the superiority of optimal deployment is verified.

articleTitle: A Method of Solving Ambiguity Based on Single Baseline Rotating Interferometer
abstract: The performance of most previous multi-channel two-dimensional direction of arrival (DOA) estimation array systems is pretty sensitive to various model imperfections, while the static single channel interferometer can only achieve one-dimensional direction estimation, thus the relationship between DOA estimation accuracy and the non-ambiguity scope needs to be weighed. In this paper, we propose a solving ambiguity method based on single baseline rotating interferometer. The baseline length is far greater than half of the target signal wavelength. The rotating interferometer rotates at the angular frequency, therefore the phase difference of a series of sampling points are able to measured. In addition, we deeply analyze the selection basis of sampling points pair and the source of angle measurement errors. In view of the limitation of the traditional algorithm on the maximum phase difference of adjacent pulses, an algorithm based on ambiguity numbers search (ANS) is introduced to obtain the correct ambiguity numbers and estimate the two-dimensional angle by using the cost function in the paper. The simulation results show that the proposed method is feasible and effective.

articleTitle: Wideband SIW Cavity-backed Microstrip Antenna for Wide-angle Scanning Phased Array
abstract: In this paper, a novel Ka-band wideband substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity-backed slot antenna with wide-angle scanning is proposed, which consists of the SIW cavity, the spindle-shaped aperture and the stacked patches. The SIW cavity-backed and four slots etched on the top patch are adopted to achieve a wideband antenna. Moreover, the SIW cavity helps to decrease mutual coupling between adjacent antennas. A 5x5 rectangular lattice array is designed and analyzed by HFSS. The results show that the element antenna can achieve about 11.5% bandwidth (33–37 GHz), and the main beam of the E-plane scanning array antenna can scan from 0 to 60 degrees in the frequency band with a gain fluctuation of less than 4.3 dB and the sidelobe level of less than -13 dB. For the H-plane, when the array scans from 0 to 60 degrees at different frequencies, the peak gain of the array decreases by 3.8 dB.

articleTitle: Ship Detection for Polarimetric SAR Images Based on Anchor-Free Network in High Sea State
abstract: Ship detection of polarimetric SAR (PolSAR) images has been developed for marine monitoring due to the abundant scattering features.
