However, PolSAR images in high sea state generally contain serious surface clutter interference and targets are blurry, which both hamper the performance of ship detection. To overcome the issue, a novel anchor-free ship detection network is proposed for PolSAR images. In the proposed method, polarimetric scattering features are extracted by polarimetric decomposition firstly, and multi-head anchor-free detector is developed to improve the detection performance of ships in high sea state. Moreover, Shannon entropy normalization and center-penalty are developed for optimization of model robustness, which aims to enhance the robustness of the detector. Experimental results on the GaoFen -3 dataset in high sea state demonstrate that the proposed method has superior detection performance than other advanced deep detection approaches.

articleTitle: Space Division Multiplexing Waveform Design for Radar Communication and Navigation Integration
abstract: With the gradual miniaturization, high integration and strong compatibility of satellite electronic system loads, equipment with multiple functions needs to be integrated. And in order to reduce the occupation of spectrum resources and rationally allocate system resources, multi-domain and multi-functional integrated waveforms are designed. For electronic systems with limited payloads, especially satellites, the selection strategies for satellite radar, satellite communications and satellite navigation are studied. Starting from the design of the waveform, this paper verifies the feasibility and effectiveness of applying different radar communication and navigation integrated waveforms in the multi-dimensional domain through simulation experiments and performance analysis of the signal processing results.

articleTitle: Feature point bidirectional matching and 3D reconstruction of sequence ISAR image based on SFIT and RANSAC method
abstract: In this letter, a matching and three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction method is presented for space target by using inverse synthetic aperture radar image sequences. Firstly, The ISAR images are preprocessed by morphology. In order to realize and improve the association of feature points of ISAR image sequences, the paper proposes a bidirectional matching approach to increase the number of matching-point, based on Scale Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT) and Random Sample Consensus (RANSAC) method. Finally, use the matrix factorization method to realize the 3D reconstruction. Experiment confirms the effectiveness of the proposal.

articleTitle: System Architecture of Intelligent Radar
abstract: To improve work efficiency of detection mission in complex electromagnetic environment, supported by rapid development of present electronic information technology, the concept of intelligent radar has attracted wide attention. This paper summarizes the content of intelligent radar, and based on the analyze of the architecture of traditional radar, two architectures respectively for intelligent sensing and intelligent decision are proposed. The research direction for the realization of intelligent radar is also provided.

articleTitle: A Brightness Temperature Reconstruction Method Based on Tikhonov Regularization for Mirrored Aperture Synthesis
abstract: In mirrored aperture synthesis (MAS), the inverse problem is severely ill-posed, which can affect the accuracy of the solved cosine visibilities. Ultimately, errors in solved cosine visibilities degrade the quality of reconstructed brightness temperature images. In this paper, a brightness temperature reconstruction method based on Tikhonov regularization is presented to alleviate the ill-posed characteristics of the inverse problem. The simulations and experiments are carried out to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Obstacle Height Estimation through Vehicular Radar Interferometry
abstract: Considering the issue that traditional vehicular millimeter-wave radar (MMWR) system is incapable of providing height information of pavement, a method based on angular measurement using interferometry technique is proposed to the height estimation of obstacle existing in road and the reduction of phase errors introduced by random fluctuations of ground radar cross section (RCS) in addition. The estimation of direction of arrival (DOA) is implemented via the utilization of delayed phase corresponding to each receiving channel and further recover on the height of road. The height of obstacle is estimated to be height difference between obstacle segment and surrounding ground segment. The verification of feasibility and validity of the method is conducted in the ultimate part. It is indicated by processing results of raw data and analyses that the method proposed has applicability to the height estimation of obstacle in a realistic environment.

articleTitle: Local Low Range Sidelobes Waveform Design with Cognitive Levels Using Particles Swarm Projection Optimization
abstract: In modern electronic warfare, radar with knowledge-aided waveforms has shown significant flexibility. In this paper, the method named Particles Swarm Projection Optimization (PSPO), is introduced to design local low range sidelobes waveform under non-convex constraint and randomized initialization. Firstly, the mathematical problem corresponding to multiple non-cooperative targets or interference is formulated considering different threat levels. Furthermore, using the alternating direction decomposition idea, the original problem is divided into triple-variable ones, which could be solved via particles projection. Here, PSPO assisted by swarm intelligence and learning factor, would enhance the global optimization convergence under unimodular non-convex constraint. Finally, simulations and numerical results show comparisons with several other methods.

articleTitle: Dynamic constraints and optimization problem for cooperative search-track mission planning
abstract: Management and mission planning over a swarm of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) remains to date as a challenging research trend in what regards to this particular type of aircrafts.Mathematically the problem of coordinating and assigning tasks to a swarm of UAV can be modeled as a constraint satisfaction problem,and the cooperative search-track mission is a dynamic constrained Multi-objective Optimization Problems (DCMOPs).The objective functions and constraints are time-dependent and changing number. Unfortunately, most existing dynamic handling techniques can hardly be adapted to this type of dynamics. When solving dynamic constrained multiobjective optimization problems, an important issue is how to balance convergence, diversity, and feasibility simultaneously.In this paper, we report our attempt toward tackling the DCMOPs with a time-dependent and changing number objectives and constraints. We implement a dynamic two archives evolutionary with self-adaptive penalty algorithm which maintains two co-evolving populations simultaneously.

articleTitle: Unsupervised 3D Super-Resolution Imaging Based on Full Convolution Neural Network
abstract: Radar imaging based sparsity regularization has demonstrated superior performance in radar image quality. However, heavy computational burden and time-consuming iteration operation degrade the further development of radar imaging. This paper proposes an unsupervised three-dimension (3-D) super-resolution (SR) method based on full-convolution neural network (F-CNN). First, 3-D echo model of the given imaging geometry is presented and the expected SR image is derived based on point spread function. Second, the network architecture of F -CNN and unsupervised training framework are proposed in detail. Furthermore, the resolution characteristics of three different imaging methods are compared. Finally, simulation validates the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of image quality and imaging time.

articleTitle: Integrated Radar and Jammer Waveform Design Based on PNFM-NLFM
abstract: To achieve the integration of radar and jammer in the waveform, we proposed a pseudo-code noise and nonlinear frequency modulation (PNFM-NLFM) waveform. The PNFM-NLFM waveform is a combination of pseudo-random-codes noise frequency modulation (PNFM) and nonlinear frequency modulation (NLFM). The detection performance is evaluated by ambiguity function, and we study the interference performance through pulse compression(PC) processing. Finally, the simulation results show that compared with the existing noise-linear frequency modulation (Noise-LFM) signal, the PNFM-NLFM has low autocorrelation side lobe while keeping interference performance.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation for Multiple Target Tracking in Active and Passive Radar Network
abstract: A joint beam selection and power allocation (JBSPA) scheme is proposed for multiple target tracking (MTT) in active and passive radar network. The motivation of JBSPA is to exploit not only the degrees of freedom of power for active radars but also the degrees of freedom of receive beams for passive radars, thereby improving the overall tracking accuracy of multiple targets. The predictive Posterior Cramér-Rao lower bound is utilized to evaluate the impact of each allocation strategy on tracking performance, and then the JBSPA scheme is formulated as a mixed integer nonlinear program problem. To solve the formulation efficiently, an alternating direction method of multipliers is developed for an optimum. Numerical results demonstrate that the JBSPA scheme can achieve a significant improvement of the overall MTT accuracy, compared with conventional uniform allocation.

articleTitle: Ship Monitor Radar for Bridge Collision Avoidance
abstract: Bridge collision avoidance is increasingly urgent as the total bridge amount and marine traffic increase. Ship detection and tracking are vital techniques for bridge collision avoidance applications. This paper introduces a linear frequency modulation continuous wave radar (LFMCW) designed especially for the applications. The system design considerations and the associated signal processing algorithms are described. An experiment was conducted on a bridge over the Xiangjiang River. The radar can not only output backscattering amplitude image as a traditional marine radar, but also output trajectories of multiple ships. Bridge collision threat can be evaluated by using the ship length and velocity information from the trajectories. Experimental results show that the radar can satisfy the requirements for bridge collision early warning.

articleTitle: Radio Signal Smart Deception Based on Adversarial Learning
abstract: In recent years, electromagnetic spectrum becomes more and more congested and the task of spectrum sensing meets various challenges. On the other hand, there is also a counter-demand that the transmitted signal should not be detected, intercepted, or identified by the intelligent spectrum sensing equipment. In this paper, a smart deception method for radio signal using adversarial learning under the black-box assumption is investigated. By generating smart deception, the accuracy of the intelligent electromagnetic spectrum equipment to identify the radio signal decreasing more than 50.63%. The radio signal camouflage is achieved by smart deception, which will lower the interception and identification possibility of the transmitted signal.

articleTitle: Joint Optimization of Transmit and Receive Beamforming for MIMO Radar with One-Bit DACs
abstract: In this paper, we consider the joint optimization of transmit waveforms and receive filters for Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radar which deploys one-bit digital-to-analog converters (DACs). We aim to design the transmit signal by maximizing the output signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) in the presence of signal-dependent interference embedded in white Gaussian disturbance. To solve the non-convex problem, we devise an alternating direction multiplier method (ADMM) framework based on the sequential optimization algorithms. Furthermore, an auxiliary variable is introduced to relax the discrete one-bit constraint to continuous interval. Finally, we can obtain a high-quality one-bit transmit signal. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively achieve satisfactory performance.

articleTitle: Continuous Arm Motion Recognition Using Two-stream Spatial-Temporal Neural Network Based on Millimeter Wave Sensor
abstract: Radar-based continuous arm motion recognition has attracted increasing interests from research community due to its huge potential to interact with machine in a longer distance. Whereas, most existing arm motion recognition work have been conducted on individual motion or without caring for the preceding and subsequent motion information in the continuous data stream. Practical operation also requires that the system must continuously detect and recognize arm motions using untruncated input radar echo streams with unknown transitions between motions. In this paper, to address these challenges, a two-stream neural network accounting for the spatial-temporal information of the radar data stream is proposed for automatic continuous arm motion recognition with a Doppler radar sensor. One stream of the network combined 1-D CNN and Bi-LSTM in a sequential manner to extract the bi-direction long-term temporal dependencies of deep column-wise spatial features. The other stream used ResNet50 to extract the global spatial features. The two are then fused to output the final class label. The comparison with the state-of-art continuous motion recognition network, 1-D CNN-Bi-LSTM, shows that our proposed network structure achieves higher recognition accuracy. Furthermore, by applying a sliding window to the data stream, our approach can handle with random length arm motion echo stream with unconstrained transitions.

articleTitle: 2D high-resolution ISAR imaging by joint using matrix completion and compressed sensing
abstract: In practical stepped frequency radar imaging application, due to the change of environment and radar multi-mode, the missing number and position of sub-pulses usually randomly distributed in each pulse group. Although compressed sensing (CS) method can handle this 2D recovering model by matrix vectorization, the huge computational complexity makes it difficult to implement on a normal personal computer. In this paper, a new 2D high-resolution ISAR imaging approach by jointly using matrix completion (MC) and compressed sensing (CS) is proposed. Firstly, the MC method is used to estimate the randomly missing elements based on the low-rank property of echo data matrix. Second, we further use CS method to handle the 2D imaging task based on the recovered full data matrix directly. At last, a high-resolution ISAR image can be obtained. Compared with competing methods, it has an improved imaging performance under low sampling rate conditions, and can effectively elevate the recovery performance of anti-noise.

articleTitle: Resolution of Synthetic-Aperture Processing for Shipborne HF Hybrid Sky-surface Wave Radar
abstract: This paper analyses the ground resolution of the synthetic-aperture processing for the shipborne high frequency hybrid sky-surface wave radar (HFHSSWR). First, the system geometry of the moving target for the shipborne HFHSSWR is formulated. Then, the gradient method is utilized to derive the ground range and cross-range resolutions of this radar. Finally, the resolution results estimated by the simulated impulse response function verify the correctness of the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: A Transparent Liquid Antenna With Ultra-Wideband and High Gain for Ku-band Application
abstract: A novel fully transparent ultra-wideband and high gain liquid antenna has been investigated using ionic liquid and simple feeding structure for ku-band application. The antenna gain can be further improved by introducing surface-mounted horn. Numerical simulations are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the analytical prediction. The proposed antenna has frequency range from 12.33 GHz to 15.80 GHz(S<inf>11</inf><-10dB), high radiation efficiency(>85%) and a maximum gain is 10.73 dBi. Compared to existing similar liquid antenna, such antenna has segmental unique features, such as high transparency, high radiation efficiency, ultra-wideband, low profile and etc, which can be a prospective candidate for high integrated circuit and microwave devices in ku frequency band. More detailed work will be presented in the final paper.

articleTitle: An Efficient Sparse Imaging Method of TomoSAR Via Unfolded Deep Network
abstract: Tomography SAR (TomoSAR) can achieve three-dimensional imaging via multi-pass forming a large synthetic aperture in the tomographic direction. Compressive sensing has been widely utilized in TomoSAR 3D imaging, which can achieve high-quality focusing in tomographic direction. However, traditional CS-based imaging algorithms are limited to heavy computational cost and pre-define parameters that influences the quality of imaging results. In this paper, an efficient sparse 3D imaging method based on unfolded deep network is proposed. Alternation Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) reconstruction model and unfolded deep network are combined in the proposed method which solves the problems of large sidelobes in imaging results and heavy computational cost in the imaging process. In the scheme, with all the acquired rang-azimuth 2D SAR imaging results, the slant-range echo is used as the input of the network and the network outputs the reconstruct images directly. Simulation and experiment data are used to illustrate the effectiveness and performance of the proposed algorithm. The results demonstrate the method can obtain 3D imaging results with high quality while maintaining higher computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Optoelectronic Oscillators for High-Quality Microwave Signal Generation
abstract: Optoelectronic oscillators (OEOs) have been extensively investigated for the generation of microwave signals with ultra-low phase noise. In recent years, several major progresses have been made on OEOs. For example, the introduction of parity-time (PT) symmetry is proven to be an effective approach to solving the long-existing mode-selection problem, the Fourier-domain mode locking allows the generation of complex waveforms from an OEO, and the optical synthetic dimension allows the implementation of an OEO with great simplicity and stability. In this talk, OEOs with noval mode control and selection techniques will be discussed, including parity-time symmetry, Fourier domain mode locking and optical synthetic dimension, which enable OEOs with unprecedented performance and functionalities.

articleTitle: A New Method for Pointing Direction Recognition of Spacecraft Parabolic Antenna Payload Based on the Measured RCS Sequences
abstract: A pointing direction recognition approach for spacecraft parabolic antenna payload based on measured RCS sequences is presented in this paper. An electromagnetic simulation model is built for analyzing the RCS characteristic of spacecrafts who carry parabolic antenna payload. The simulated RCS shows that the step effect of RCS sequence measured by radar could be used as the criterion to recognize whether the line of sight (LOS) of earth radar is in the aperture of spacecraft parabolic antenna. Aiming at classifying whether the LOS of earth radar in the aperture of spacecraft parabolic antenna, this paper designed a hybrid-dimensional convolutional neural network (HCNN). Then the pointing direction recognition problem of spacecraft parabolic antenna payload is converted to a dichotomous problem where the RCS sequence is the input signal and the LOS of earth radar in the aperture of spacecraft parabolic antenna payload is the expected classified result. The proposed method was trained and validated on measured datasets. The results show that the proposed method yielded the classification accuracy as 90.5%. Moreover, it can tell that the proposed method has the limit of over fitting, which should be solved later in the engineering application.

articleTitle: SAR Target Enhancement Method via Prior Information Acquisition and Application
abstract: Compressed sensing synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging method can use the sparse prior information of the target in the scene to improve the imaging resolution. However, the actual target usually has more structural features, and it is difficult to reconstruct the target accurately if only the sparse prior of the target is used. This paper segmented the location and shape prior information of the target ROI region according to the historical imaging data. By selecting different weighting functions for the clutter region and the target ROI region, a weighting matrix was obtained, which could enhance the target region while suppressing clutter. At the same time, the TV regularization constraint is introduced into the optimization problem to enhance the structural characteristics of the target. Finally, the Augmented lagrange multiplier (ALM) method and Alternate direction multiplier (ADMM) method is used to solve the problem. Experimental results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A dual-mode navigation algorithm based on Infrared and SAR information fusion
abstract: Focused on revising the cumulative error of the SINS, a dual-mode navigation algorithm based on the infrared and SAR information fusion is studied in this paper. The SAR system can provide the SAR image and the information including the distance and the beam direction of the SAR antenna, the infrared system can provide the infrared image and the optical axis direction of the infrared lens. Under the premise of the same direction of the SAR and infrared beam, a navigation algorithm by associating the matching results of the SAR image and infrared image with the digital map is studied, which can be applied to amend the aberration of the SINS in the middle phase. At the same time, the common aperture characteristic and GPS error isolation method are used to isolate the error sub area. The simulation results reveal the validity of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Scattering Analysis for Typical Satellite in the Lower Terahertz Region
abstract: In order to meet the requirements of terahertz radar for space target detection, the radar cross sections (RCS) of typical satellite targets in terahertz low frequency region is studied. A typical satellite target with rough body is established by using half edge data structure. The RCS distributions at different heights, root-mean-square, correlation lengths and different frequencies are calculated by using the hybrid method of Physical Optics method (PO), Shooting and Bouncing Ray method (SBR) and Truncated-wedge Incremental-length Diffraction Coefficients (TWILDCs). Based on the principle of turntable imaging, the scattering center distribution of satellite target with different roughness at 220GHz and 0.05m imaging resolution is simulated and analyzed. The results show that RCS and image are more sensitive to the fluctuation of the target surface, the frequency and incident angle in terahertz band.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation for Underwater DOA Estimation based on Binary Measurements
abstract: Direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation is a core task for the sonar systems. Recently, an urgent need for estimating DOA from low precision measurements arises. This paper aims to evaluate the performance of DOA estimation based on the binary (1-bit) measurements in the underwater scenarios. Specifically, the synthetic data are generated from the underwater acoustic field model for the horizontal and vertical arrays, and then the data are quantized to be binary. The DOAs are estimated by the 1-bit conventional beamforming method and the 1-bit Compressive Sensing method. Compared with the un-quantized data, the simulation results show that in the specific situations the DOA can be well-estimated with binary measurements, and the performance is comparable with the unquantized case. Some experiences are summarized based on the simulational experiments, which can be useful in real applications.

articleTitle: Design of Low-Frequency Tightly Coupled Dipole Array With Transformer Balun
abstract: Tightly Coupled Dipole Array(TCDA) is a new type of radar antenna with UWB performance and low profile, but relevant designs focus on microwave frequency band. This article presents a TCPA working in 110-520MHz. Each array element is protected from the effect of the common mode resonance by the shorting posts, and excited by the co-designed integrated transformer Balun, which works as the wide-band impedance matching network and provides a balanced feeding. For wide-angle scanning, a printed Frequency Selected Surface(FSS) is used in place of the bulky dielectric superstrates. The final array achieves a low profile(<tex>$0.1 \lambda_{Low}$</tex>) and superior performance of 5:1 bandwidth with VSWR<2.5 when scanning ±50° in <tex>$E$</tex> plane and ±40° in <tex>$H$</tex> plane.

articleTitle: Single Channel CSAR Moving Target Detection Algorithm Based on Low-rank Sparse Decomposition
abstract: With the goal of detecting moving targets, this paper proposes a new single channel Circular Synthetic Aperture Radar (CSAR) moving targets detection algorithm based on Low-rank Sparse Decomposition (LRSD). This algorithm utilizes the correlation among overlap subaperture logarithmic amplitude image sequences, the static clutter is regarded as low-rank component and the moving targets is considered as sparse component. Then, the background image sequence (without moving target) and the foreground image sequence (moving targets) can be extracted by the LRSD. Considering the unknown foreground image distribution, this paper proposes a Local Dynamic Threshold based on Otsu (LDTO) method independent of image distribution to detect moving targets. Finally, the experiment on the X-band airborne Gotcha Data demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

Author Keywords: local dynamic threshold based on Otsu

articleTitle: Layered Media Inversion Network Applied in Ground Penetrating Radar
abstract: Ground-penetrating radar (GPR) is a mainstream detection tool for layered media inversion. However, due to the multiple reflections and complicated refraction effect, traditional inversion method can't achieve accurate parameter inversion. For the issue, a transformer-based layered media inversion network with GPR is proposed in the paper. The network utilizes velocity spectrum as the data set to enhance feature identification and utilizes transformer-based self-attention mechanism as the backbone to reallocate attention resources based on the degree of feature importance. It focuses more attention on reflected features adaptively and maps the velocity spectrum to the permittivity image. Extensive simulated results demonstrate that the proposed network has the superiority in reconstructing the underground structure and inversing the multilayered parameters.

articleTitle: Colocated MIMO Radar Waveform Design with Raised Cosine Filter
abstract: In colocated Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radars, phase coded waveform design is an important issue and in real applications, a raised cosine filter is typically used to avoid frequency-domain signal mutual interference, which however is rarely considered in existing waveform design algorithms. In this paper, we design MIMO radar transmit waveforms with optimized raised cosine filters to advance real application of MIMO radar waveforms. A waveform optimization criterion is formulated with the filter, which aims at suppressing auto and mutual correlation sidelobes and the mismatch to a desired transmit beampattern. Numerical results with transmit beampattern with two equal peaks are presented, indicating that waveforms with good sidelobes and close to the desired transmit beampattern can be achieved even with this filter. The Doppler sensitivity of this waveform is also studied.

articleTitle: Distributed ISAR spatial spectrum analysis and its influence on sparse recovery
abstract: The echo of distributed ISAR is modeled, and its spatial spectrum structure is analyzed under different array structures and different motion forms of target. Furthermore, when sparse recovery is used for cross-range imaging, the relationship between spatial spectrum structure and sparse recovery performance is discussed. Using the average coherence coefficient of the observation matrix as an index, the influence of accumulation time and sensor position is analyzed. These analyses are helpful to optimize the sparse recovery performance.

articleTitle: Compensation Imaging Algorithm for Arc Array SAR Based on DSFMT Vibration Parameter Estimation
abstract: When a helicopter platform equipped with an arc array SAR is hovering in the air, there is usually a simple harmonic vibration in the altitude direction, which causes errors in the imaging of the arc array SAR. Since the amplitude of the simple harmonic vibration is usually in the same order of magnitude as the wavelength of the arc array SAR, making arc array SAR imaging results very sensitive to vibration, it is particularly important to compensate vibration error in imaging processing. Aiming at the problem of vibration compensation, this paper first derives the slant distance with vibration error by constructing a geometric model and uses the BP imaging algorithm of the arc array SAR to obtain the imaging signal after filtering and projection, which contains only the sinusoidal frequency modulation phase generated by the vibration. Then the vibration compensation function is reconstructed by extracting the vibration phase of the signal and using DSFMT to estimate the vibration parameters. Finally, an accurate imaging algorithm of the arc array SAR under vibration is achieved. Simulation is used to verify the effectiveness and accuracy of the algorithm.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Single-polarized and Polarimetric SAR Images Applied on Unsupervised Classification
abstract: SAR image understanding is a significant but also challenging issue in practice. In order to detect the difference between single-polarized and polarimetric SAR (PolSAR) data and explore more information from the pre one, we use GF3 data for experiments and adopt the Deep Clustering with Convolutional Autoencoders (DCEC) algorithm for single-polarized SAR image unsupervised classification. Using both the Kappa coefficient and mutual information derived from the confusion matrix, the results of single-polarized SAR data and PolSAR data are compared. It shows that the classification results of single-polarized SAR data match with the polarimetric ones to some extent, and their results are comparable in some specific applications. This paper presents the potential of information mining from single-polarized SAR images, as well as gives some references for the selection and trade-off between single- and full-polarized SAR data.

articleTitle: Hand Gesture Recognition Method based on Dual-Channel Residual Neural Network
abstract: With the changes in the international situation, more stringent requirements have been put forward for counter-terrorism and stability maintenance tasks. Under invisible conditions such as night and shelter, the recognition of gestures becomes very important. The radar has the characteristics of all-weather and has a certain penetration ability. Therefore, radar has an irreplaceable role in solving this problem. Since wideband radar has higher range resolution than narrow-band radar, it can extract finer features of gestures, which has become the main sensing apparatus for gesture recognition. However, gestures are often in a complex background. Furthermore, gestures weak compared to the main body. Therefore, the classification and recognition of human micro-motion based on wideband radar is still a difficult problem. Inspired by the successful application of residual neural network in computer vision, this paper proposes a wideband radar gestures recognition method based on Pyramid Split Attention(PSA) dual-channel residual neural network, which takes the Range-Doppler (RD) map and High Resolution Range Profiles (HRRPs) of human micro-motion as inputs. The effectiveness of this method is verified by experimental data, after the information is convolved, the features are fused, and finally the purpose of classification is achieved. The target recognition rate of this method is 97.83%, which is higher than 95.83% without pyramid split attention, and much higher than 92.33% of the high-resolution range profile based recognition method and 90% of the range Doppler based recognition method, showing the superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Density-Based STAP for Detection of Range-Spread Targets
abstract: The detection performance of range-spread targets with the conventional space-time adaptive processing (STAP) may deteriorate due to the target self-nulling effect. To tackle this issue, in this paper, a new STAP detector for range-spread targets based on sample density, referred to as den-STAP, is proposed. In the new den-STAP, Capon spectrums are used to measure the distance between clutter samples and target samples. Then, two features of density and low-density distances are designed as the differentiation features of clutter samples and target samples. Finally, den-STAP selects the target-free samples to estimate the clutter covariance matrix and to reduce the target self-nulling effect. The detection stage is implemented via the adaptive matched filter. Simulation results show that the proposed den-STAP achieves superior detection performance on range-spread targets.

articleTitle: Squat Ellipsoidal Cylinder: Calibrators for Radar Cross Section Measurement
abstract: In order to overcome the radar cross section (RCS) sensitivity to elevation of squat circular cylinders, a set of squat ellipsoidal cylinder (SEC) calibrators are presented in this paper. In comparison to current widely used squat cylinders, the attractive advantages of the SEC calibrator are that its RCS is independent of frequency and insensitive to the elevation while also can be easily installed on the head of the metal pylon. Besides, the scattering mechanisms of SEC are studied using ultrawideband RCS data which are numerically calculated by the method of moments (MoM). In addition, the RCS deviation versus elevation angle demonstrates that the SEC is much less sensitive than conventional squat cylinder, especially at high frequencies.

articleTitle: SAS Doppler Estimation Based on Radon Transformation
abstract: Due to the motion errors, synthetic aperture sonar (SAS) maybe suffers from slight deviation of Doppler centroid. If the inaccurate Doppler centroid is used for imagery, the SAS image would be seriously affected. To some degree, there is no need to estimate the Doppler ambiguity, as the sidescan SAS system is mainly discussed in this paper. At this point, it is very important to estimate the Doppler centroid. In this paper, we mainly discuss the Doppler centroid estimation based on Radon transformation. Then, the real data is used to validate the presented method. The processing results show that the presented method can well estimate the Doppler centroid.

articleTitle: Fast Human Body Scan for Security Inspection Based on Multi-Mode Vortex Electromagnetic Wave
abstract: The current security inspection technology is mostly composed of imaging and recognition steps, in which high-pixel imaging corresponds to high accuracy but high computational burden. In this paper, we propose a fast end-to-end method to connect the original data to security check results directly, where the two-dimensional fast beamforming is achieved by a one-dimensional mode scanning of the vortex electromagnetic wave. Vortex electromagnetic wave achieves a helical wavefront through phase modulation related to azimuth Angle, which can cover two-dimensional space through one-dimensional scanning, and different modal vortex echoes contain information of different parts of the human body, but modal dimension signals do not have a clear corresponding relationship with the scene like the image. So the rapid detection of human body is realized by the combination of multi-modal vortex wave and feed-forward neural network. Through the training and simulation of the network, the feasibility of the proposed system and method is proved, and the high recognition rate can be obtained with very little computation.

articleTitle: Cost-reference Particle Filter Bank for Fast Instantaneous Estimation of Nonlinear FM Signal
abstract: Instantaneous frequency (IF) estimation of unknown nonlinear frequency modulated (FM) signal in complex background is an essential issue in radar. In this paper, a cost-reference particle filter (CRPF) based filter bank, i.e. CRPF bank is proposed for fast and accurate IF estimation. The proposed CRPF bank has entirely parallel structure, which consists of a large number of parallel CRPFs using different prior information. After filtering, the output of the CRPF with minimum cumulate cost is selected as the IF estimation of the CRPF bank. Experiments on IF estimation illustrates that, by comparing with the similar algorithms, the execution time of the proposed method is greatly minimized and also its estimate is improved.

articleTitle: A Novel Jamming Method of Combining Interrupted-sampling Repeater and Noise Convolution Modulation Assisted by Photon
abstract: For LFM pulse radar signal, this paper proposes a combined jamming pattern of interrupted-sampling repeater and noise modulation based on microwave photon technology. We use the active optical fiber ring pulse replicator to generate high-speed sampling pulse of light whose replication cycle is adjustable, when LFM pulse signal is modulated to the light pulse carrier, the intermittent sampling of the signal is realized, and then the random noise sequence is convoluted with the intermittent sampling pulse through the spatial light intensity modulator. Finally, it is transmitted by photodetectors and antennas to form jamming signal. In this paper, linear frequency modulation pulse signal can be sampled intermittently and forward quickly based on microwave photons, and the intermittent sampling rate can be adjusted freely through the delay line, therefore it will be able to implement different jamming effect. Electrical analog-to-digital conversion and digital radio frequency memory device will be ignored by this method, which avoids the storage for large amounts of data and the loss of processing time.

articleTitle: A clutter suppression method in single channel SAR image domain
abstract: Moving targets submerged in the stationary background clutter can be hardly indicated by a single channel synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system directly. In this paper, a symmetry Doppler pixel (SDP) method, which is performed on complex SAR image domain, is proposed to indicate targets for single channel SAR. Because the Doppler spectrum of clutter is symmetrically distributed in the complex SAR image domain whereas that of the targets are not, two symmetry images can be directly obtained by performing azimuth inverse Fourier transform on the positive and negative part of the Doppler spectrum of the original complex image data. In the two symmetry images, the clutter is coherent but the targets appear at different positions and have different intensities. Then, by stacking the pixels of these two symmetry images, the SDP filter is designed to minimize the clutter-pulse-noise component and keep the under test target component. Moreover, it provides more robust target indication performance when there exists pixels mis-registration between the two symmetry images.

articleTitle: An adaptive strong tracking Cubature Kalman filter based on noise estimation
abstract: This paper proposes to combine the noise estimation algorithm and the strong tracking cubature Kalman filter (STCKF)algorithm to establish an adaptive strong tracking cubature Kalman filter algorithm (ASTCKF). Using the idea of covariance matching, the adaptive adjustment of noise covariance in the state estimation process is realized. The simulation comparison with STCKF algorithm shows that the filtering algorithm proposed in this paper has better accuracy.

articleTitle: Target Detection in Sea Clutter with Transformer Neural Network
abstract: Target detection in sea clutter is a significant problem in marine surveillance. The difficulty of radar target detection lies in the low signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR) and insufficient feature extraction brought by handcrafted features. In recent years, with the great success of artificial intelligence in the field of computer vision, there is a trend that researchers start to apply convolutional neural networks to radar target detection. However, most methods based on convolutional neural networks need to convert one-dimensional signals into two-dimensional images for preprocessing, which not only increases the computational burden, but also reduces the accuracy of detection. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a Transformer-based sea clutter target detection method, which takes the collected one-dimensional signal as input directly after FFT preprocessing. And comparing with two-dimensional images, which can extremely reduces the computational cost. Most importantly, Transformer-based network has self-attention mechanism to strengthen target and suppress noise, thus improving the accuracy of target detection. The proposed algorithm is verified on the IPIX datasets, and the results show that the proposed algorithm attains excellent results compared to state-of-the-art convolutional networks while requiring substantially fewer computational resources to train and inference.

articleTitle: Design of A Wideband Low Sidelobe Waveguide Monopulse Antenna in Ka-Band
abstract: A wideband low sidelobe waveguide monopulse antenna for radar seeker working at Ka-band is proposed. A 752-elements circular waveguide antenna array is presented. The simulated bandwidth (return loss less than −10dB) of antenna array is 11.4% and the corresponding isolations between the sum and difference ports are better than 35 dB. The gain differences between the sum channel and difference channels are around 3.7 dB and the null depths are below −30 dB in both plane. The simulated realized gain is more than 34.8 dB and the antenna efficiency is more than 65%. The side-lobes for the sum pattern of the two planes are all less than −22 dB in the whole frequency band.

articleTitle: RFI Localization Using Joint Sparse Recovery in Synthetic Aperture Interferometric Radiometry
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new model combing the joint sparse recovery (JSR) with multiple snapshots data of the satellite named Soil Moisture and Ocean Salinity (SMOS) to get the geolocation of radio frequency interference (RFI) sources. The JSR method has been used to solve this model by exploiting the temporal redundancy of multiple snapshots data. Numerical simulation shows that the performance of the proposed model is much better than the conventional inversion algorithm based on single snapshot.

articleTitle: A Fast Learning Method for Optimal Jamming to Radar in Real-Time Environment
abstract: In real-time radar countermeasure environment where countermeasure time is limited, how the jammer can quickly find the optimal radar jamming policy is an urgent problem to be solved. Most of the existing reinforcement learning-based jamming methods are based on a multi-round training mechanism, such as Q-learning, which is difficult to achieve multi-round training in an actual countermeasure environment, and the convergence speed of such methods is slow and cannot be applied to a real-time countermeasure environment. In this paper, a fast learning method based on jamming bandits (JB) algorithm is proposed. On the basis of balanced exploration and exploitation, each round of optimization is based on the learning results of the previous round of countermeasure environment characteristics, and intelligently allocates more exploration opportunities to possible areas with higher countermeasure reward, so that the jamming policy optimization can converge faster. Simulation results show that under the condition of limited jamming time, the method in this paper has a faster jamming policy convergence speed and a higher average jamming reward than the previous methods in cross-eye jamming scenario.

articleTitle: An Azimuth Deramping Method for Spaceborne Sliding Spotlight SAR without Relying on Virtual Rotation Points
abstract: With the improvement of the azimuth width and azimuth resolution of the spaceborne SAR, the azimuth scan angle range of the antenna beam increases rapidly, and the beam center deviates significantly from the virtual rotation point under the control of uniform scanning, and the traditional virtual rotation point model becomes invalid. At this time, it is impossible to continue to use the virtual rotation point to perform azimuth deramping, and it is difficult to continue to apply the frequency domain imaging algorithm based on azimuth deramping. This paper proposes an improved azimuth deramping technology that does not rely on virtual rotation points. This technology can accurately remove Doppler aliasing caused by beam azimuth scanning and solve the problem of virtual rotation point model failure in sliding spotlight mode with large azimuth scanning angles.

articleTitle: Modified polar format algorithm (MPFA) for highly-squinted SAR
abstract: In the high-resolution highly-squinted (HRHS) synthetic aperture radar (SAR) processing, the residual errors of conventional polar format algorithm (PFA) brought by far-field assumption greatly deteriorate the reconstruction performance, which limits the allowable scene size. To address this problem, a modified PFA for HRHS SAR is presented with a new two-dimensional (2-D) interpolation function in this Letter. Different from the conventional PFA, the modified one has a larger focus depth and is insensitive to the target height. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the modified PFA.

articleTitle: Joint Detection and State Estimation of Doppler Radar
abstract: In order to improve the performance of Doppler echo signal's detection and parameter estimation under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), a joint detection and state estimation algorithm based on random finite set is proposed. Under the framework of formal Bernoulli filter, the target state model and observation model are designed at the Doppler echo signal level, which overcomes the problem that the traditional Detect-Before-track (DBT) method fails due to the loss of target information in the case of low SNR. The time update and observation update of state vector are realized by sequential Monte Carlo (SMC), and the joint detection and state parameter estimation of single target are realized. Simulation results show that the algorithm can effectively improve the performance of detection and state estimation.

articleTitle: Improving the SSMVEP Detection Performance by Introducing a Secondary Discriminant Mechanism
abstract: This study demonstrates that the detection performance of the steady-state motion visual evoked potential (SSMVEP) can be improved by introducing a secondary discriminant mechanism. An extended canonical correlation analysis (CCA)-based method was applied to the detection of SSMVEPs. The target corresponding to the maximum coefficient was not identified as the focused target after calculating the coefficients of the obtained electroencephalogram (EEG) at all stimulation frequencies and a maximum contrast fusion method was performed on the EEG data. A secondary analysis was performed on the fused signal. A radial contraction-expansion motion paradigm was used and 40 targets in the frequency range of 7-14.8 Hz were designed. The introduction of the secondary discriminant mechanism resulted in higher accuracy and information transfer rate (ITR) than the extended CCA-based method. The online accuracy increased by 5.17% and the online ITR increased by 10.41%, respectively. The experimental results showed that the second discriminant mechanism significantly improved the recognition accuracy when the extended CCA-based method was applied to detect the SSMVEPs with a single harmonic component.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Efficient Transmision of Optical Fiber Radar
abstract: Optical fiber is an efficient propagation passage for a light radar system in an adverse environment particularly in an explosion proof working place at which the electricity is not allowed and the fiber is needed to connect the data processing system to the measuring spot. But in the previous publications, the coupling between the fiber modes and light source and the matching between the fiber core diameter and the detector sensitive area are not studied, which is very important in the ranging distance. In this paper, a new light radar ranging model is presented, in which the efficient coupling between fiber modes and light source and the efficient matching between the fiber core diameter and the detector sensitive area are taken into account.

articleTitle: MIMO Array SAR Fast 3-D Imaging Based on Sparse Signal Gridless Recovery
abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) array synthetic aperture radar (SAR) can be used to directly obtain the 3-D imagery of the illuminated scene with a single track. Due to the length limitations of synthetic aperture and antenna array, the super-resolution algorithms within the framework of 2-D compressive sensing (CS) have been conceived to reconstruct the azimuth-cross-track plane image because of its spatial sparsity. Since the desired scatterers are presupposed to be distributed over a series of fixed grid points, the location accuracy of the existing 2-D CS algorithms is relatively low. To overcome this problem, a fast 2-D gridless recovery (GLR) algorithm for the 2-D imaging signal model established in the real domain is proposed in this paper. Extensive simulation results validate that the proposed 2-D real-valued gridless recovery approach can approximately improve the computational efficiency by a factor of ten in terms of CPU time when compared with that of the 2-D GLR algorithm in the complex domain.

articleTitle: RMDU-Net: 3-D MMW Imaging Via Range Migration Based Deep Unfolding Network
abstract: Limited by the Nyquist sampling rate, conventional matched filtering-based algorithms always confronts large-scale data dimension, causing difficulties in real-time processing. To address the issue, in this article, a 3-D millimeter-wave (MMW) radar imaging method via range migration (RM) based deep unfolding network is proposed, named as RMDU-Net, which utilizes the compressed sensing (CS) theory and unfolding networks to achieve high-resolution accurate reconstruction under a low sampling rate. The 512×512×6 large-scale imaging results can be obtained by RMDU-Net and the theoretical resolutions are up to 2.8mmx2.8mmx4cm. Besides, the proposed method is compared with traditional range migration algorithm (RMA), and the numerical evaluations are given. The practical experiments demonstrate this imaging approach is excellent in both imaging quality and computing efficiency compared with classical algorithms.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization in Communication and Radar Spectrum Sharing via Tchebycheff Algorithm
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the multiobjective optimization problem for array radar and multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communication spectrum sharing. The aim is to simultaneously implement the communication rates and the radar output signal-to-interference plus noise ratio (SINR) optimization. The multiobjective problem is converted into a singleobjective optimization problem by utilizing the weighted Tchebycheff method. We solve the resulting formulation via alternative iteration, whose convergence is guaranteed and the closed-form solutions can be derived. Finally, the numerical results are presented to show the merits of the proposed approach and validate the theoretical analyses.

articleTitle: Dual-Function MIMO Radar-Communications via Group Frequency Hopping Code Selection and PSK Modulation
abstract: The dual-function radar communication (DFRC) system is an important means to alleviate spectrum congestion. In this paper, we propose an information-embedding DFRC scheme through combining group frequency hopping (FH) code selection with phase-shift keying (PSK) modulation. Concretely, in each radar sub-pulse, first, all the FH codes are grouped and allocated to each antenna in turn. In order to make the distribution of FH codes in one antenna be more uniform, the allocation pattern between groups and transmit antennas performs cyclic shift from one sub-pulse to another. Second, each transmit antenna selects one active FH code from the allocated group according to the transmitted communication symbols. Third, given the FH code per antenna, the FH signal is further modulated by PSK to convey additional information. Moreover, a low-complexity two-stage method is presented to decode the FH code and PSK symbol separately. Simulation results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed information-embedding scheme.

articleTitle: Spaceborne SAR Target Recognition Method Based on Edge Computing
abstract: Aiming at the problems of the traditional satellite image processing system, such as the extension of the image pro-cessing task and high pressure of broadband data transmission between the satellite and the ground, this paper adopts the idea of edge computing to extend the SAR image processing site from the ground data processing center to the mobile edge processor on the satellite. Taking full account of the limited resources on the satellite, this paper uses channel pruning and knowledge distillation to compress the convolutional classification network. Under the condition of ensuring little accuracy degradation, the all-convolutional networks (A-convnets) is compressed by 14.66 times and the VGG16-LRN is compressed by 109.43 times. ASIC inference chip for edge computing with lower power consumption is used for deployment. Compared with GPU deployment, ASIC chip deployment can obtain more than twice the inference speed with 0.5 times the load power consumption.

articleTitle: Polarization characteristics of sea clutter and its application in target detection
abstract: In this paper, three categories of polarization features that represent the divergence between the small target and clutter are discussed and extracted from different views: (1) Since the scattering mechanism of sea clutter is random scattering in low glazing angle, while target has a specific shape, thus reducing the randomness of scattering, the mathematical expectation of the polarization entropy is extracted to reveal randomness of scattering mechanism in the echo; (2) In general, the scattering structure components such as the spherical, dihedral and helicoid scatters are different in the sea clutter and target echoes. Therefore, the power of the three scattering components in each echo is extracted based on Krogager polarization decomposition; (3) Due to the effectiveness of frequency-based and fractal-based features in sea-surface target detection, the average Tsallis entropy is extracted to represent the divergence between sea clutter and small target in full-polarization data. Based on the features in polarization views, localized one-class support vector machine (LOCSVM) is used as the detector because the target feature vector samples are insufficient. The experimental results on IPIX data under different sea conditions show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Joint Trajectory Design and Power Allocation for Target Tracking in Airborne Radar Network
abstract: In this paper, a performance driven joint trajectory design and power allocation (JTDPA) scheme is developed for target tracking application in airborne radar network (ARN). The key idea of this scheme is to collaboratively exploit the maneuverability of aircraft and the adaptable transmit power of radar network to maximize the target tracking performance. The practical constraints including the threat zone, as well as the aircraft's maneuverability and the total transmit power budget are considered. By building the JTDPA scheme as a mathematical optimization problem, we can utilize the heuristic algorithm to solve the problem. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed JTDPA scheme can greatly improve the target tracking performance.

articleTitle: A CNN-Based Direction-of-Arrival Estimation from Bistatic Scattering Pattern
abstract: The task of direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation is to identify the signal source direction. Previous studies demonstrated that the strength of speckle-noise could be related to the size of the resolution cell and other factors, including wind speed and frequencies. In this paper, we consider the effect of resolution cell size in DOA estimation. The advanced integral equation model (AIEM) is applied as the forward model to simulate the radar scattering from sea surface under various observation geometries. To simulate the speckle noise, we evaluate the number of equivalent scatterers per resolution area and generate K-distributed speckle statistics. A convolutional neural network (CNN) is then utilized to establish the relationship of radar measurements with their incident directions. The experimental results show that the CNN structure could be applied to DOA estimation with satisfactory accuracy for high-resolution radar measurement.

articleTitle: High-resolution Coastline Extraction in SAR Images via MISP-GGD Superpixel Segmentation
abstract: High accuracy coastline/shoreline extraction from SAR imagery is a crucial step in a number of maritime and coastal monitoring applications. We present a method based on image segmentation using the Generalised Gamma Mixture Model superpixel algorithm (MISP-GGD). MISP-GGD produces superpixels adhering with great accuracy to object edges in the image, such as the coastline. Unsupervised clustering of the generated superpixels according to textural and radiometric features allows for generation of a land/water mask from which a highly accurate coastline can be extracted. We present results of our proposed method on a number of SAR images of varying characteristics.

articleTitle: Advances in Integrated Microwave Photonic Signal Processors
abstract: Integrated microwave photonic signal processors have spurred substantial attention in recent years. Recent advances are presented with a focus on photonic-assisted frequency measurement, continuously tunable microwave photonic phase shifters, microwave photonic sensing and signal generation, and multipurpose and multitasking microwave photonic signal processing system.

articleTitle: Wheel-rail fatigue modeling and rail weld life evaluation for large aperture radio telescope
abstract: Due to the long-term reciprocation and cyclic stress, the structural fatigue of telescope track weld becomes increasingly prominent. In this paper, based on fatigue failure theory, a wheel-rail rolling contact model was established by using finite element method to complete the calculation of wheel-rail contact dynamic and static mechanics and rail weld fatigue life. It can provide a reference for fatigue life assessment of antenna track structure and on - line state detection, fault diagnosis and maintenance of welded structure.

articleTitle: Realization and Optimization of Inverse Algorithm of QR Decomposition of Arbitrary Order Signal Autocorrelation Matrix Based on HLS
abstract: The computation core of all kinds of adaptive beamforming algorithms lies in the inverse operation of signal autocorrelation function matrix. However, the design of all kinds of matrix inverse modules in FPGA development platform has some problems, such as difficulty in timing design, weak scalability and poor portability. This paper proposes a matrix inverse module of autocorrelation function of arbitrary order signal based on HLS (High Level Synthesis), completes the QR decomposition algorithm based on Housholder method, and encapsulates it into a large complex matrix inverse IP that meets the requirements of highspeed calculations, low resource consumption, and customizable configuration order. Finally, the synthesis results of RTL are analyzed from the aspects of timing delay, resource consumption, program configurability, etc. According to the synthesis results, the IP can improve the module speed to the magnitude of 2ms under the condition of 64 order complex matrix, and realize the advantages of configurable order, high data precision. It can well meet the high demand of real time in practical engineering and can be flexibly configured in various types of FPGA development platforms.

articleTitle: Micro-movement Parameters Estimation of Wind Turbine Multipath Echo
abstract: Wind turbine echo generated through multipath effect seriously affects the target detection effect of radar. Estimating the micro-movement parameters of the echo is one of the breakthroughs to suppress the wind turbine multipath echo. Therefore, a method to estimate the micro-movement parameters of the wind turbine multipath echo using whale optimization algorithm is proposed. Firstly, wind turbine echo model under the multipath effect influence is established based on scattering point integration algorithm and the micro-movement parameters to be estimated are determined. Secondly, a method to estimate the micro-movement parameters of the wind turbine multipath echo using whale optimization algorithm is proposed to obtain the wind turbine rotating state information, which provides the basis for multipath echo suppression. Finally, the practicability and feasibility of the method are verified by simulation.

articleTitle: A Space-Time Iterative Adaptive Method for Forward-Looking Radar Imaging
abstract: When the area to be imaging is in the forward-looking direction of airborne radar, existing imaging technology are incapable of imaging accurately, like synthetic aperture radar (SAR) and Doppler beam sharpening (DBS). To improve the poor azimuth resolution in airborne radar forward-looking imaging, a super-resolution algorithm based on space-time iterative adaptive method for airborne array radar is proposed in the paper. Compared with the conventional signal model, the new method considers both the spatial sampling obtained by multi-channel receiving technique and the temporal sampling obtained by coherent pulses to estimate the direction of arrival (DOA) of the ground scatterers, effectively utilizing space-time two-dimensional information. Then the iterative adaptive expressions based on the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) criterion are employed to process the space-time snapshots to generate the super-resolution image of the ground. As is verified by simulation results, the proposed algorithm has improved performance of reconstructing the forward-looking imaging scenario.

articleTitle: A Service-Environment-Oriented Shape Reconstruction Method of Vehicle-borne Active Phased Array Antenna
abstract: Modern electronic equipment has been moving towards large scale and increased complexity. Affected by such factors as complex working environments, the performance of a large number of structures in engineering is degraded or even destroyed. Therefore, structure shape estimation is of great significance. The complexity of the structure, however, makes it impossible for a single deformation evaluation algorithm to evaluate the structure comprehensively and accurately. In this paper, a modal-approximate curve (M-AC) method, using a small amount of strain data, is proposed for block shape estimation of structures. Three typical wind load experiments are carried out on the finite element model (FEM) of the vehicle-borne active phased array antenna, and the effectiveness of the algorithm is verified. Under the wind speed of 28 (m/s), the deformation of antenna front is 104.70 mm and the estimation accuracy of the M-AC method is 87.43%, which is 16.47% higher than that of the modal approach. The results indicate that the estimated displacement is consistent well with the simulation results of the finite element method.

articleTitle: A New Method to Evaluate the Quality of ISAR Image
abstract: Point spread function is commonly used for radar imaging evaluation. But in the measured ISAR (inverse synthetic aperture radar) image, it is hard to find an ideal scattering center with a standard point spread function. The phenomenon leads to a difficulty in evaluating the measured ISAR image. In this paper, we proposed a new method to accomplish this task. Firstly, a geometry of the target is established. Scattering database is obtained based electro-magnetic calculation. Then, the echo at the same posture with the measured ISAR image is obtained based on interpolation in the electro-magnetic scattering database. Lastly, the simulated ISAR image and the measured ISAR image are evaluation simultaneously. The same region in these two ISAR image are selected and evaluated with resolution. Despite the resolution of the selected region may deviate from the ideal value, the measured ISAR image can still be well evaluated based on whether the resolution of the measured ISAR image coincides with that of the simulated ISAR image. Experiments are carried out and the result show the proposed method has good performance.

articleTitle: SIDOND: Single-Input Dual-Output Network for Radar Target Detection in Complex Environment
abstract: The standard constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detectors often lose some detection performance under the situation of multiple targets, clutter edges, and high-speed targets. The existing single-input single-output network also cannot guarantee CFAR and high performance in complex environments. A single-input dual-output network for radar target detection (SIDOND) is proposed in this paper, which performs end-to-end detection tasks to solve the issue mentioned above. In SIDOND, a convolutional neural network based on a periodic activation function is utilized to extract features. Besides, two fully connected networks are used to detect and estimate background noise power, respectively. The detection threshold is adapted according to the estimated background noise power to achieve CFAR and maintain high performance. The experiment results have shown that SIDOND has target detection and CFAR advantages over traditional CFAR under complex scenes.

articleTitle: Polarization Scattering Matrix Analysis for Weak Target Detection in Sea Clutter
abstract: The polarization information involved in radar echoes could be used to effectively distinguish targets in clutter backgrounds. In this paper, a detection method is proposed based on the characteristics of polarization scattering matrix (PSM) for detecting of weak moving targets in sea clutter. The orientation angle and the amplitude of the maximum return are obtain by the eigenvalue decomposition of the PSM to separate target echo and sea clutter. Meanwhile, the fluctuation of the polarization scattering characteristics between adjacent pulses is also considered with the help of the CP decomposition of the tensor constructed by the PSMs. Based on the feature space which has effectively distinguished target echo and sea clutter, the support vector machine (SVM) is utilized to detect target within sea clutter. Experiments based on real sea clutter data in IPIX database show that the proposed detector could effectively improves the performance for weak targets detection in sea clutter.

articleTitle: Weighted Randomly Overlapped Phased Array Design via Two-Stage Convex Programming
abstract: The design of the overlapped sub array architecture has the potential to reduce the number of control components and the scanning sidelobe level. In this paper, a two-stage convex programming method is proposed. At the first stage, an iterative norm minimization method is applied to obtain the position of the subarray and the initial weighting. At the second stage, the weighting is optimized to minimize the sidelobe level base on the determined positions of the sub arrays. Through above-mentioned steps, lower sidelobe levels can be achieved with fewer subarrays. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated by numerical experiments.

articleTitle: Development of a high temperature resistant array type thin-walled unit radome
abstract: This paper describes the development process of a thin-walled radome for a ground-based high-mobility radar array unit, which is injection-molded with PEEK resin with high temperature resistance, excellent aging performance and good dielectric properties. The authors studied the dielectric properties of PEEK resin at different temperatures and the effect of different paint layer thicknesses on the dielectric properties of PEEK material from material selection, manufacturing process research and environmental test verification, respectively, and finally successfully developed a radar radome with performance indexes meeting the design requirements.

articleTitle: An Autofocus Algorithm of GCBP Image Based on Spectrum Compression for Curved Trajectory Spotlight SAR
abstract: The Back-projection (BP) algorithm has significant advantages for spotlight synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging with curved trajectory. However, when the motion measurement is not accurate enough, how to autofocus the defocused BP image is still a challenge. In this paper, aiming at the problem of motion error in the application of curved trajectory spotlight SAR, an autofocus algorithm of ground Cartesian BP (GCBP) image based on spectrum compression (SC) for curved trajectory spotlight SAR is proposed. Firstly, through the wavenumber analysis, we reveal the Fourier transform (FT) relationship between the image and the range-compression phase history data under the ground Cartesian coordinate system. Then, the two-step SC of the GCBP image is carried out. And by analyzing the image spectrum, it is found that the spectrum support regions of different targets are aligned and the phase errors of the alignment positions are consistent. Accordingly, efficient error estimation and compensation are carried out. Finally, the simulation experiment of curved trajectory spotlight SAR is given, which proves the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Weight Optimization Via Maximum Entropy Criterion for SPICE
abstract: Sparse iterative covariance-based estimation (SPICE) method is a popular sparse reconstruction approach with many advantages, such as, stable statistical property and hyper-parameter free. In this paper, we propose a maximum entropy method (MEM) to optimize the weight function which is the kernel of the SPICE algorithm. In the proposed MEM, the weight in SPICE is regarded as the inverse of the estimated energy spectrum. Thus, the beamforming technique is exploited. Using the optimized weight, sources with small interval can also be successfully resolved. Compared with existing SPICE algorithms, the proposed MEM has a better angular resolution capability. Numerical simulations verify the superiority of the proposed MEM.

articleTitle: Simulation and Detection Method of Tsunami
abstract: In recent years, simulation of tsunami and detection method have been the most meaningful and urgent task. Tsunami are generally caused by the earthquake. In addition, tsunami waves belong to the long wave and its empirical simulation method are the shallow water equations (SWEs). The existence of tsunami can be directly detected from the reverse direction of ocean radial surface velocity. The simulation result of single site radial surface velocity can demonstrate the existence of tsunami, while there might exist false alarm in the vortex circumstances. Dual site radar utilizes the unique flow velocity and direction of tsunami to detect the existence of tsunami without this problem. In addition, making a Fourier transformation in a certain direction is also a detection solution that liberates human eyes.

articleTitle: Application of VTK in ISAR imaging of Asteroids
abstract: In order to improve the quality of radar images and accurately obtain planetary surface features, this paper apply visualization toolkit (VTK) to inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging of asteroids. First, we obtain the scattered echoes of the asteroids through the high-frequency statistical algorithm, and generate the ISAR images of the asteroids. Then, we rearrange the ISAR imaging data points according to the original terrain grid positions of the asteroids. Based on the automatic interpolation and facet coloring function of VTK, we further convert the data into the classic format of VTK to form the topographic image with clear outlines. The results show that the application of VTK to ISAR imaging is very effective to obtain high-quality and clear radar images, which further supports the target detection and recognition of radar remote sensing.

articleTitle: Modulation Pattern Recognition of Underwater Acoustic Communication Signals
abstract: In this paper, the modulation pattern recognition of underwater acoustic communication signals is presented. The classification is evaluated. The experimental results show that the classification accuracy of the presented method is high.

articleTitle: An Optimized Resource Allocation Algorithm in Cognitive C-MIMO Radar for Multiple Maneuvering Target Tracking
abstract: In this paper, combined with the cognitive tracking technique and the C-MIMO radar system, an efficient resource optimal allocation scheme of the joint power and bandwidth allocation for multiple maneuvering target tracking is proposed. By establishing the system model of maneuvering target tracking and adopting the predicted conditional Cramer-Rao lower bound (PC-CRLB) as the tracking performance metric, the joint power and bandwidth allocation problem for maneuvering target tracking is converted as a non-convex optimal problem, which is solved by a three-step solution method combined with the semidefinite programing (SDP) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the effectiveness of the proposed optimal scheme in improving tracking accuracy.

articleTitle: Target Segmentation Based Adversarial Attack for SAR Images
abstract: With the increasing increments on the Deep Learning (DL) in these years, increasing attentions have been arose on the adversarial attack on DL models for Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) target recognition. However, most of the previous methods transfer exisiting adversarial attack methods from computer vision area which typically attack DL models by generating background-located perturbation of certain size. With respect to the physical realizability in SAR target recognition tasks, the perturbation is only feasibly generated in the target region. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a Target Segmentation based Adversarial Attack (TSAA) method for SAR images. The proposed TSAA method tends to only generate the perturbation on the target region by incorporating the target segmentation technique. Meanwhile, the TSAA approach reformulates the perturbation generation process to achieve an automatic perturbation region searching instead of manual design. Thus, the attack performance towards DL models and imperceptibility for visualization both present significantly better results than previous methods in extensive simulation results including white and black box experiments for eight popular DL models.

articleTitle: Bayesian LSTM Flight Trajectory Prediction
abstract: A novel method of Bayesian LSTM networks is presented for flight trajectory prediction. To solve model uncertain and incomplete, the parameters of normal LSTM networks are replaced by probability distributions. Then, a numerical solvable approach of characteristic estimation of the distribution is discussed and the experimental results prove the effectiveness of this approach.

articleTitle: Space-Time Adaptive Processing Using Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: Space-time adaptive processing (STAP) is a key technique of clutter suppression for airborne radar. However, clutter covariance matrix (CCM) cannot be estimated accurately suffering from the problem of the nonhomogeneous clutter environment, which leads to a significant degradation of clutter suppression performance. To address this issue, a super-resolution angle-Doppler spectrum estimation method for STAP based on deep learning is proposed in this paper. Our method directly learns a mapping between the low/super-resolution spectrum. The mapping is represented as a deep neural network that takes the low-resolution spectrum as the input and outputs the super-resolution one. In the test phase, the CCM can be calculated by the super-resolution spectrum obtained. Numerical experiments are conducted to exhibit the superior performance of the proposed method in terms of the estimation accuracy and computational complexity.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of the influence of electromagnetic Pulse Power on the performance degradation of CMOS Inverter
abstract: The strong electromagnetic pulses generated by nuclear explosions and electromagnetic pulse weapons can interfere radar system by damage the integrated circuit in the system. With the increasing of integrated circuit integration and the continuously reducing of the device feature size, the damage effect of electromagnetic pulse on the integrated circuit becomes more and more obvious. The electromagnetic pulse damage effect of integrated circuit is mainly reflected in the thermal field in the integrated circuit. Aiming at the electromagnetic pulse damage law of integrated circuits, CMOS inverter is researched. The device simulation software Sentaurus is then used to establish the inverter model. Then the effects of the power and pulse width of the injected electromagnetic pulse on the performance of the inverter are studied. The simulation results show that when the power is low, the performance of the inverter is only temporarily interfered, and its operation can resume normal when the EMP no longer acts. When the power reaches a certain threshold, the performance of the inverter will be permanently damaged. The larger the pulse width, the smaller the damage threshold of the inverter.

articleTitle: Rational Fitting with Weighted Iteration (RFWI) with Application to Band-Notched UWB Pyramidal Antenna
abstract: A novel approach, Rational Fitting with Weighted Iteration (RFWI), is presented in this paper. It has the ability to convert the concrete data in complex number field to an analytical rational function, for potential usage as a surrogate model. And an example of parameter extraction from a band-notched UWB pyramidal monopole antenna demonstrates that the RFWI approach is feasible and precise. Its flexible weighting factor can be adapted to a lot of harsh scenarios, even the precise recognition of a very narrow notched-band within an operating UWB spectrum, just as shown in this example.
