The surrogate model extracted through RFWI approach would be meaningful and necessary in the analysis required to further integrate the complicated antenna into a wireless communication system in the future.

articleTitle: Radar Multiple Targets Detection with Non-uniform Pulse Repetition Intervals
abstract: This paper deals with sidelobe pedestal suppression of the range-Doppler plane in the presence of multiple targets for radar with non-uniform pulse repetition interval (NUPRI). A novel algorithm for multiple targets estimation (MTE) is proposed to figure out the amplitude of targets in both range and Doppler dimension. Each dimension is implemented based on the gain constraint adaptive pulse compression (GCAPC) algorithm. Numerical simulations are provided to assess the capability of the proposed algorithm to NUPRI and its comparison with uniform PRI (UPRI). Results show the capability of MTE with lower sidelobe pedestal than the traditional matched filter and MTD (MF-MTD) method and unambiguity of NUPRI mode in Doppler dimension.

Author Keywords: gain constraint adaptive pulse compression algorithm

articleTitle: Estimation of Low-altitude Wind-shear Wind Speed based on DDD-EFA under Aircraft Yawing
abstract: When the airborne radar is affected by the aircraft yawing, the clutter suppression performance decreases and leads to the inaccurate estimation of the low altitude wind-shear velocity. This paper proposes a method for estimating the low-altitude wind-shear velocity based on Direct Data Domain-Extended Factored Approach (DDD-EFA), which can obtain effective estimation of wind speed even when the airborne radar is affected by the aircraft yawing. First, the wind-shear signal of the range bin is filtered out, and then estimate the clutter covariance matrix for multiple training samples obtains from the sliding window. Then, the multidimensional Doppler channel and space domain adaptive processing combined in the time domain are used to construct the dimensionality reduction matrix. Finally, the optimal weight vector of the dimensionality reduction processor is constructed according to the minimum variance criterion to realize clutter suppression and the wind speed estimation of low-altitude wind-shear. The simulation results show that the proposed method can obtain effective estimation of wind speed.

Author Keywords: Direct Data Domain Extended Factored Approach

articleTitle: Algorithm for Motion Compensation In An Airborne Mosaic Mode SAR System
abstract: Mosaic mode is a combination of spotlighting or sliding spotlighting mode and ScanSAR mode, which can improve the SAR image resolution through azimuth spotlighting and obtain a large imaging width through range scanning. This paper studies the problem of airborne SAR imaging with Mosaic mode. After performing the SAR imaging by using the polar format algorithm (PFA), the motion error in virtue of platform irregulation motion is modelled and compensated. The simulation results show the influences of the motion error on the Mosaic mode SAR imaging, and then the motion error compensation is performed, which provides a reference for the system design of the Mosaic mode SAR application on the airborne platform.

articleTitle: Maximin Joint Design of Transmit Waveform and Receive Filter Bank for MIMO-STAP Radar
abstract: This paper investigates the joint design of transmit waveform and receive filter bank for airborne multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar in the presence of uncertainties of target parameters. Assuming an unknown spatial angle and Doppler frequency for the target, the worst-case Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise-Ratio (SINR) at the output of the receive filter bank is considered as the figure of merit. The max-min joint design problem with constant-modulus constraint and similarity constraint on the transmit waveform is formulated. To solve this problem, a computational efficiently algorithm based on majorization-minimization (MM) technique is developed. Several numerical results are provided to demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of the devised method.

articleTitle: Analysis of Reflector Angle Errors for Two-Dimensional Mirrored Aperture Synthesis
abstract: Two-dimensional mirrored aperture synthesis (2D-MAS) was proposed to improve spatial resolution or reduce the number of antennas. The reflector errors exist only in the mirrored aperture synthesis, not in the conventional aperture synthesis. In this paper, reflector angle errors are analyzed. The influence of the errors on reconstructed images is alnalyzed through simulation. The experimental system of MAS at V Band (MAS- V) is used to verify the simulation result.

articleTitle: Non-coherent CFAR detector based on survival analysis
abstract: A non-coherent constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detector based on survival analysis (SA) using multiple observations is proposed for small targets in Rayleigh- and K-distributed background. This study is the first attempt to apply SA in field of target detection. The motivation of SA for target detection is introduced and the scheme of SA detector is established. The proposed detector is demonstrated to maintain CFAR property with respect to the Rayleigh parameter in Rayleigh-distributed background and the scale parameter in K-distributed background by simulations. Performance results show that the SA detector outperforms the traditional CFAR detector based on binary integration in both Rayleigh- and K-distributed backgrounds for the Marcum and Swerling II targets, indicating that the proposed detector is preferred for the detection of fast fluctuating targets in spiky background.

articleTitle: A PS points selection algorithm based on edge detection for GNSS-based InSAR system
abstract: Global navigation satellite system (GNSS)-based interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) can be considered as a distributed system. Traditional persistent scatterer (PS)-InSAR technique cannot be directly used due to the large point spread function (PSF) of GNSS-based InSAR. In this paper, a PS point selection algorithm based on edge detection and PSF comparison is proposed. First, the PSF of the strong points are extracted based on the edge detection. Then the coherence coefficient is calculated based on the theoretical PSF to obtain the PS candidate (PSC) points. Raw data is used to verify the effetiveness of the proposed algorithm in GNSS-based InSAR.

articleTitle: Topographic Phase Self-adaptive Compensation For Multi-satellite Formation Coherence Radar Systems
abstract: In multi-satellite formation synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems, terrain interferometric phase is a crucial factor that degrades the performance of multi-channels coherence processing. To address this issue, we developed a high-precision self-adaptive topographic phase compensation (TPC) method. It emphasizes minimizing the topographic phase estimation error based on an error feedback weighting correction structure. The self-adaptive weighting coefficient is constructed using image coherence, phase residual distribution, and fringe structural features. This ensures that the phase estimation error component will be corrected in an extremely heterogeneous observation scene. The experimental results of multi-satellite SAR image simulated data demonstrate that the proposed method can significantly improve the accuracy of the topographic phase compensation.

articleTitle: A New Evaluation Method of Similarity Between Two SAR Images
abstract: Evaluation method of similarity between two synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images plays a key role in the SAR raw data simulation and the analysis of SAR imaging quality. Although the similarity between two SAR images is intuitive, it still lacks objective and quantitative method to evaluate it. Thus, an evaluation method named Otsu-PHash is proposed in this paper from the perspective of image similarity to solve the problem. The key steps of the proposed Otsu-PHash method are threshold segmentation and similarity comparison. Finally, the numerical experiment verified that our proposed method can be applied to evaluate similarity of the two SAR images.

articleTitle: ESM and Detection Cooperated Jamming Strategy
abstract: In this paper, to improve the jamming efficiency of the existing jamming strategy, an ESM and detection cooperated jamming strategy is proposed. With the strategy, precise selective barrage jamming can be implemented to the emitters. In the strategy, the information sharing between different functions is considered to realize multi-function cooperation. Firstly, the jamming strategy is described and the influence of position accuracy on jamming efficiency is analyzed. Then, to quantitatively analyze the jamming efficiency, the probability models of ESM and detection are established. Finally, numerical results are provided to verify the validity of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: A Sub-aperture Partition Method for Airborne SAR Based on Particle Swarm Optimization
abstract: The airborne SAR platform is easily affected by the motion error, resulting in a serious decline in the quality of images processed by full-aperture echo data. In this paper, a new sub-aperture partition method based on particle swarm optimization is proposed, which can significantly improve the SAR image quality at a lower computational cost without motion compensation. Firstly, the echo matrix corresponding to the strong point targets in the SAR observation area is extracted from the original echo data. Then the position of the sub-aperture separation points are optimized by using the signal-to-noise ratio as the evaluation function. Finally, the data in each sub-aperture are imaged separately and the results are incoherently accumulated as the final image. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by point target simulation.

articleTitle: Classification of UAV and Ground Targets By Micro-Doppler Signatures Based on PD Surveillance Radar
abstract: As typical of low flying altitude, small size and slow flying speed (LSS) targets, the detection and recognition of mini-sized unmanned aerial vehicle (U A V) by surveillance radar is of great significance. However, it is difficult to realize classification of UA V and ground targets based on pulse Doppler (PD) surveillance radar because of low resolution and short dwell time. Based on the method of multiple micro-Doppler signatures (m-Ds) association, classification of UA V and non-UAV targets is considered and studied in this paper. We first focus on the micro-Doppler signature of UAV targets by PD radar, including the echo model and the micro-Doppler spectrum distribution. To verify the proposed method, we investigate UAVs, human and vehicle using the developed PD surveillance radar in a series of experiments. And seven key features are extracted from both frequency domain and time-frequency domain. The experiment results show that the classification accuracy is found to be more than 90%.

articleTitle: A Controllable Range Resolution Enhancement Method for Coherent FDA Radar
abstract: By introducing a frequency increment between the adjacent transmitting elements, the coherent frequency diverse array (FDA) radar realizes the large-scale airspace observation with coherent waveform. However, the beam scanning property of FDA radar leads to the degradation of its range resolution. In this paper, a controllable range resolution enhancement method called “controlled mainlobe expanding” (CME) method is proposed. Enlightened by the array pattern synthesis theory, the element-wise spatial phase encoding is employed to expand the mainlobe width of array pattern which prolongs the illumination time during the beam scanning. The proposed method is able to improve the range resolution to a desired value flexibly without sacrificing the full-spatial coverage and also makes a tradeoff between the high range resolution and the anti-interference performance. The experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Analysis of RCS Based on 3-D SAR Imaging
abstract: Radar Cross Section (RCS) is an important physical quantity that measures the ability of a target to scatter incident electromagnetic waves. The target RCS can be measured with high precision by using radar imaging technology, and the uncertainty analysis of RCS is helpful to evaluate the reliability of measurement results, However, the relevant research on the RCS uncertainty analysis of 3-D imaging has not been carried out. In this paper, combining with IEEE Standard 1502-2020: IEEE Recommended Practice for Radar Cross-Section Test Procedures, a reference standard for RCS uncertainty analysis based on 3-D synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging is provides. Firstly, analyze the sources of uncertainty factors in the RCS measurement mode of 3-D SAR imaging, and then analyze the generation process in detail. Through simulation analysis, its influence on RCS measurement results is obtained, finally the uncertainty estimation of each factor is given. Therefore, the uncertainty analysis proposed in this article can be effectively used as a reference standard for quantitative analysis of 3-D imaging RCS measurement results, which is conducive to improving the standardization of the RCS measurement process and the accuracy and reliability of the results.

articleTitle: A fully transparent broadband ionic liquid dielectric resonator antenna
abstract: This paper presents a fully transparent broadband ionic liquid dielectric resonator antenna. By replacing the metal conductor with a transparent nickel metal mesh film, and using the transparent ionic liquid trihexyl (tetradecyl) phosphine chloride with a relative dielectric constant of 3.2 as the medium, the antenna's extremely high light trans mittance characte ris tics can be realized. The antenna adopts coaxial feed, and the current path is changed by opening a U-shaped groove on the metal mesh film patch, which greatly improves the bandwidth of the antenna. The antenna proposed in this paper can achieve <tex>$\text{VSWR} < 2$</tex> (with a relative bandwidth of 14%) at 4.53∼5.21 GHz. The antenna radiation efficiency is 76%, and the antenna has a maximum gain of 6.63dBi at 4.87GHz.

articleTitle: Range-Velocity Tracking of Dynamic Finger Gestures Using 120GHz Radar With LFM-MFSK Waveform
abstract: Hand and finger gesture sensing with millimeter wave (MMW) radar is an emerging technology. In this paper, we propose a novel linear frequency modulation and multiple frequency shift key (LFM-MFSK) combined waveform to sense the finger gesture and a new 1D searching phase unwrapping algorithm for the unambiguous range estimation of the significant scatterers on the hand of interest. By utilizing the new waveform, the hand is resolved from other objects in the range domain, and the different fingers can be resolved in the Doppler domain with high Doppler resolution. Besides, the unambiguous high accurate range estimation of the fingers can be obtained from the phase differences of the returns via a 1D searching phase unwrapping algorithm based on the Chinese remainder theorem (CRT). The 120GHz millimeter wave radar with the LFM-MFSK waveform is designed, and the proposed method is verified with the returns of two common finger gestures.

articleTitle: Clutter Suppression Method of Inter-Pulse Frequency Agility Based on Zero Point Constraint
abstract: The inter-pulse frequency agility system is an effective way for radar to suppress the repeater jamming. But the non-stationarity of radar echo signal makes the traditional clutter suppression method invalid. Therefore, in order to improve the poor target detection ability of inter-pulse frequency agility radar, a novel clutter suppression method based on the zero point constraint is proposed. In this method, the zero point constrained clutter matrix is constructed based on the characteristics of clutter, and a clutter suppression filter is formed, which can suppress clutter and improve the performance of target detection. An experiment is designed under strong ground clutter to prove the target detection ability of this method. Comparing the coherent accumulation results between the traditional and this method, the result shows this method can effectively suppress clutter to achieve the goal of accurate target detection. And this method has high engineering feasibility, and has already implemented with the hardware, to promote the practicality of inter-pulse frequency agility radar.

articleTitle: Micro-Doppler Analysis of Target Based on the Clustering Prior to Solve the Block Sparse Forward and Backward TVAR Model
abstract: Micro-Doppler features generated by target micromotion are usually unique and can be used as an important basis for target recognition, which reflects the fine features of target. In this paper, we propose an algorithm based on cluster-structured prior to solve block sparse forward and backward time-varying autoregressive (TVAR) model to perform Micro-Doppler analysis of the target. Firstly, convert the time-varying coefficients into the form of time-invariant coefficients. Then, an improved algorithm based on extended block sparse Bayesian learning (EBSBL) is used to solve the time-invariant block sparse coefficients by adopting a cluster-structured prior. At the same time, the priori information with known boundary is applied. Finally, the electromagnetic simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has advantages in Micro-Doppler analysis, which can not only give a clearer TF diagram than traditional methods, but also has a strong anti-noise performance.

articleTitle: Geometric considerations of short-range multistatic SAR based on multi-rotor UAVs for improved spatial resolution
abstract: A method on the design of coherent multistatic synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system implemented by short-range radars onboard distributed multi-rotor unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) or drones for improved spatial resolution with a single transceiver and multiple bistatic receivers is presented. With high-resolution imaging application in mind, this method is used to derive the locations of all sensors in the system and the limitations of techniques such as this is explored. The theoretical results are confirmed via numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Closed-form two-dimensional DOA and polarization estimation of coexisted circular and noncircular signals
abstract: The polynomial rooting based closed-form two-dimensional direction-of-arrival and polarization estimation of coexisted circular and noncircular (NC) signals for parallel uniform linear arrays of diversely polarized antennas is studied in this paper. Noncircularity phase could also be estimated for the strictly NC signals. No pair matching is needed for the proposed closed-form multidimensional parameter estimation method. Simulation results are included to illustrate the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Joint DOD and DOA Estimation via Coupled CPD with Sparse MIMO Radar for IIoT
abstract: Coarray tensor-based joint direction-of-departure (DOD) and direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation with sparse multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar for industrial internet of things (IIoT) has been a heated topic, where the canonical polyadic decomposition (CPD) is utilized to retrieve angle information. However, the conventional CPD approach ignores the spatial relevance among the coarray tensors corresponding to the collocated transmitters and receivers of the sparse MIMO radar. In this paper, we propose a coupled CPD-based joint DOD and DOA estimation method for the sparse MIMO radar in IIoT. Firstly, multiple tensors are modeled to preserve the multi-dimensional signal structure of the sparse MIMO radar. Then, tensor-based spatially smoothed coarray statistics corresponding to augmented virtual transmit and receive arrays are derived. After that, a segmented coarray tensorization approach is proposed to formulate multiple coupled coarray tensors. To make full use of the relevance among these coarray tensors, they are jointly decomposed via coupled CPD for joint DOD and DOA estimation with a high accuracy and resolution. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by simulations.

articleTitle: Cognitive-Visual Fusion for Target Classification in Rapid SAR Image Series Visual Presentation
abstract: The ability of deep learning models in image classification tasks has already suppressed humans. However, The convolutional neural network (CNN) utilized in computer vision tends to focus on the local features of the images, which is different from human perception ability. In this paper, we aim to combine visual capabilities from the machine and cognitive capabilities from humans to perform image classification. In particular, we use the EEG data evoked by sparse Synthetic-aperture radar (SAR) target images presented in rapid series and the stimuli SAR image series to detect the SAR images containing targets. We propose a multimodal framework named Cognitive-Visual Fusion Network (CVF-Net) that employs both visual domain information and cognitive domain information. We demonstrate that the proposed network can effectively detect target images and show that multimodal information has significant improvement over single domain knowledge.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Network for Underground Dielectric Target Reconstruction
abstract: Ground penetrating radar (GPR) has been widely used in underground target detection. To meet the requirements of GPR echo data interpretation and achieve accurate retrieval of the position, shape and permittivity of the dielectric targets, this paper proposes a deep neural network-based target reconstruction method using the GPR full-wave inversion (FWI). By introducing Kirchhoff migration technique, the initial focusing and imaging space alignment of GPR data are achieved, and then an underground dielectric target reconstruction network (UDTR-Net) is constructed to substitute the iterative optimization process in the traditional GPR-FWI to achieve an accurate inversion. Finally, a simulation dataset containing multiple targets is constructed for training and testing the network. The test results show that the proposed method can achieve accurate reconstruction of targets - both the reconstruction accuracy and the generalization ability are improved.

articleTitle: A Range Ambiguity Resolution Method for High-Resolution and Wide-Swath SAR Imaging Based on Continuous Pulse Coding
abstract: In synthetic aperture radar (SAR), high-resolution and wide-swath (HRWS) imaging is a challenging problem due to the contradiction between azimuth Doppler ambiguity and range ambiguity. In order to break the limitation of the pulse repetition frequency (PRF) on the radar imaging width, a HRWS SAR imaging method based on continuous pulse coding (CPC) to solve the range ambiguity is proposed in this paper. CPC method requires the radar to transmit multi-pulse signals with varying high PRF in the original pulse repetition period. Because of the small distance between each pulse, the echo will be aliased and blocked. In order to recover the unambiguous echo, we first use the form of CPC signal and the swath width of the radar to construct a linear equation set to mathematically model the aliased echo signal of each receiving window. Next, the established linear equations are split according to the distribution law of the receiving window, and the range ambiguity of the echo is performed by solving the split sub-linear equations. Finally, imaging processing is performed on the decoded unambiguous echo to achieve HRWS SAR imaging. The experimental results have confirmed the effectiveness of the method proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Design of Constant Modulus Discrete Phase Sequence Set via IADPM Framework
abstract: This paper deals with constant modulus sequence set design for a cognitive radar with good correlation properties based on an Inexact Alternating Direction Penalty Method (IADPM) framework. The Weighted Integrated Sidelobe Level (WISL) of auto- and cross-correlation is minimized as a figure of metric in a finite alphabet phase case. In each iteration, the original problem is converted into two subproblems which are efficiently solved, while locally increasing the penalty factor involved in the IADPM framework. Finally, numerical examples highlight that the proposed algorithm shows a lowest WISL compared with some state-of-art methods.

articleTitle: Radar Maneuvering Target Motion Parameter Estimation Based on 2-D Region Centroid Tracking and Polynomial Chirplet Transform
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of estimating the motion parameters of a high-speed maneuvering target under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) environment. Based on the 2-D region centroid detection-tracking (RCDT) and the polynomial Chirplet transform (PCT), a novel parameter estimation method, named as RCDT-PCT, is proposed. Numerical investigations show that in terms of noise resistance capability, parameter estimation accuracy, and coherent integration performance, the RCDT-PCT is superior to some similar techniques for the motion parameter estimation. The results show that the RCDT-PCT can estimate the target's motion parameters accurately, and integrate the energy of radar returns along the target's moving trajectory, even the input SNR is low to −33 dB.

articleTitle: Application of High Silicon Aluminum Alloy in the Field of Microelectronic Packaging
abstract: The application status of high silicon aluminum alloy in the field of microelectronic packaging was reviewed. First of all, the developing status of high silicon aluminum alloy are introduced, and the various preparation methods are compared and analyzed, and the current development status of high silicon aluminum alloy in various countries is briefly introduced. Secondly, the application direction of high silicon aluminum alloy in the field of microelectronics is briefly introduced, and the application of high silicon aluminum alloy in the field of microelectronics packaging is introduced in detail. Finally, the performance of two typical grades of high silicon aluminum alloys used in the field of microelectronics packaging is compared. High silicon aluminum alloy has great development prospect by virtue of its own superior characteristics.

articleTitle: Foreground and attention guided Center Net for SAR Ship Detection
abstract: In recent years, with the vigorous improvement of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging technology, many deep learning-based methods are developed to detect ships in SAR images with higher accuracy under real-time applications. However, some challenges still exist: (1) Ship targets are difficult to distinguish from complicated background. (2) The densely distributed targets around the land area are prone to be missed. In this paper, we present a center-point based ship predictor, called FG-Att CenterNet for SAR ship detection under complex scenarios. First, the foreground information is extracted by foreground region proposal network to eliminate the complex inshore and inland interferences. This information serves for regression branch in detection framework. Then, for more accurate center point location, a coordinate attention module (CAM) is integrated to strengthen the feature maps for classification branch. The experimental results conducted on HRSID SAR ship dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our method. As an anchor free detector, the proposed detector can well detect targets under inshore and offshore scenario, which outperforms several mainstream detectors in speed and maintains high accuracy.

articleTitle: Velocity Estimation of SAR Moving Ship via CV-EstNet
abstract: Compared with the synthetic aperture radar (SAR) static target image, the moving target will produce additional Doppler center and Doppler modulation frequency change, which will cause the imaging result of the moving target to defocus and shift. Therefore, this paper proposes a complex-valued convolutional neural network (CV -CNN) architecture CV-EstNet. It adopts an end-to-end approach to complete the velocity estimation of SAR moving ship targets, and estimate the range velocity and azimuth velocity. Then, the proposed CV-EstN et is tested on the simulated target velocity estimation task of five-types SAR moving ships. The simulation shows that CV-EstN et can further reduce the velocity estimation error compared with the traditional real-valued CNN (RV-CNN) with the same degree of freedom.

articleTitle: A Novel High-resolution SAR Imaging Algorithm for Moving Targets Based on Tracking and Sub-aperture Imaging Technology in Low Azimuth Antenna degrees of Freedom
abstract: In this paper, an effective high-resolution imaging approach of moving targets is proposed for the space-borne multi-channel in azimuth high-resolution and wide-swath (HRWS) synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system, which is based on the multi-target tracking technique. Firstly, the echo of multi-channel in the azimuth multi-channel SAR system is utilized to deduce the sub-aperture focusing image of moving targets, where the sub-aperture division and imaging technology is involved. Then, the tracks of the moving targets in the sub-aperture focusing image can be obtained by using the multi-target tracking technology. After that, extract the corresponding data of each moving target in the sub-aperture focusing image, and stitch the data according to the tracks to obtain the secondary focus image of the moving target. Finally, some simulation experiments are implemented to validate the theoretical investigations and the proposed approach in this paper.

articleTitle: OFDM Chirp Waveform Design for Clutter Suppression
abstract: Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) chirp waveform has attracted much attention for its excellent characteristics such as large time-bandwidth product, high Doppler tolerance, low range-Doppler coupling and high degree of freedom in waveform design. To suppress clutter more effectively from the transmitter of radar system, a method of designing the OFDM chirp waveform based on the maximum output signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratio (SCNR) is proposed in this paper. First, the relationship between the optimal energy spectral density (ESD) corresponding to the maximum SCNR and the waveform parameters of OFDM chirp is analyzed. Then, the OFDM chirp waveform design with sub-bandwidths diversity is presented. Last, the designed waveform is analyzed and validated by numerical results. The simulation results demonstrate that the designed waveform has an output SCNR and ESD close to the optimal values so as to suppress clutter in frequency domain.

articleTitle: Fast Coherent Integration and Parameter Estimation Algorithm for Maneuvering Targets
abstract: The range migration (RM) and Doppler frequency migration (DFM) caused by the target motion would degrade the coherent integration performance significantly. To address this problem, a fast coherent integration and parameter estimation algorithm based on time reversing transform (TRT), dechrip process (DP) and Radon-Fourier transform (RFT), i.e., TRT-DP-RFT, is proposed. In this algorithm, TRT is firstly applied to remove the influence of RM. Then, DP is used to compensate the phase fluctuation induced by the target's acceleration and achieve coherent integration. The target's range and acceleration can be estimated by DP. Finally, RFT with estimated range and acceleration is performed to estimate the target's velocity. The proposed method has low computational complexity since it just need to search the velocity dimension. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of TRT-DP-RFT.

articleTitle: Baseline Optimization Design of Airborne Tomographic SAR System
abstract: Tomographic synthetic aperture radar (TomoSAR) imaging has shown great potential in the three dimensional SAR focusing in recent years. One practical challenge is that the spatial separation of the multi-pass system is always non-uniform and also the number of tracks is very limited, thus may leading to the focusing results deteriorate compared to the results with uniform baseline distribution. In practice, when the sampled signal does not meet Nyquist's law, the signal sidelobe obtained by non-uniform sampling in a certain range is lower than that obtained by uniform sampling. How to design the baseline distribution between flights to minimize the focused signal sidelobe to a certain extent is the primary consideration of the airborne system before data recording. In this paper, we proposes an iterative spatial disturbance - sequential quadratic programming (ISP-SQP) optimization method. We obtain the optimal baselines by using SQP as preliminary operation, and then add different disturbances to the center of the baseline sequence in space iteratively as the initial value of SQP until it converge to optimal value. The simulation data applied to this method demonstrate that the proposed method is more effective in obtaining lower sidelobe in TomoSAR focusing.

articleTitle: Clutter Suppression of Wind Farm for Airborne Radar Based on EFA
abstract: With the rapid development of wind power generation, the clutter generated by wind farms may lead to the problems such as decreased detection probability, increased false alarm rate, and target track divergence. Research on the wind farm clutter mitigation technology for airborne radar is vital. Considering the special problems of the wind farm clutter mitigation for airborne radar, such as the less prior information and the more complicated spectrum of the echoes, it is difficult to suppress the wind farm clutter with non-Gaussian and dynamic characteristics. In this paper, the extended factored approach (EFA) algorithm is used to suppress the wind farm clutter through space-time adaptive processing of airborne array radar echoes. The EFA algorithm does not need the prior information of wind farm clutter or a large number of training data and can adaptively form null with a certain width in the Doppler domain. The null is used to suppress the wind farm clutter, which can avoid the interference of the wind farm clutter on the detection of aircraft targets and improve the detection probability of airborne radar. The experiment results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Micro-motion Based Target Recognition Using Regularized DCNN
abstract: Micro-motion is an unique status of moving targets, playing an important role in detecting and recognizing space targets. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) has been widely applied for target recognition based on micro-motions, but the extracted features are still sensitive to environmental noise, thus it is of vital importance to improve CNNs' robustness to micro-motion targets under noisy environments. This paper takes ballistic missiles as an example, establishes and thus analyzes the echo signal model of cone warhead under three micro-motion conditions: rotation, coning and vibration. Based on the simulated radar echo signals under hypothetical war scenario, a dataset of time-frequency spectrums is established, consisting of twelve different types of ballistic targets which include warheads as well as decoys. This paper applys a regularization method to DCNNs, by minimizing feature variations caused by gaussian noise, notably improves the recognition accuracy of micro-motion targets as well as its robustness to gaussian noise, compared with conventional CNN methods.

articleTitle: Research and Realization of Adaptive Digital Beamforming Technology Based on Spatial Spectrum Estimation
abstract: Aiming at the super-resolution spectrum estimation and robust adaptive beamforming technology of digital array radar under non-ideal conditions (low snap, low SNR and strong correlation signals), a digital beamforming system architecture based on super-resolution spatial spectrum estimation is proposed in this paper to improve the performance of anti-main band interference and the angle measurement accuracy. The signal received by multiple sub-array channels is divided into sub-array and beam domain. The main lobe beam conformal method with multi-point constraints is used to ensure that the digital array radar can suppress the main lobe interference and improve the resolution and angle measurement accuracy of the target. The simulation proves that the system design has anti-main lobe interference, high-precision angle measurement performance and better robustness, which can be widely used in engineering.

articleTitle: DOA Estimation Using Nested EMVS Arrays Via Khatri-Rao Polarization Matrix Augmentation
abstract: In this paper, a new algorithm is proposed to estimate directions-of-arrival (DOAs) of multiple sources using a nested electromagnetic vector sensor (EMVS) array. Each EMVS consists of three mutually orthogonal electric dipoles and three mutually orthogonal magnetic loops, all collocated at a single point in space. By exploiting the additional polarization diversities embedded in the vector sensors, the proposed algorithm formulates a full rank augmented sample data matrix from the vectorization of array covariance matrix by Khatri-Rao polarization matrix augmentation (KR-PMA) to increase the degrees of freedom (DOFs). Unlike the widely used spatial smoothing technique, the KR-PMA does not reduce the efficient co-array aperture. For one-dimensional (1-D) DOA estimation, the KR-PMA is proved to offer up to 20 DOFs, which can be further multiplied by synthesizing with the spatial smoothing.

articleTitle: SAR Target Classification Based on Knowledge Distillation
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) classification methods based on deep learning usually rely on powerful computing resources and deep convolution neural networks. Although the large deep neural network has high accuracy, it needs a lot of computing and storage resources, which limits the application of SAR classification in mobile embedded devices. The small network has high efficiency but poor accuracy. To deal with the above problems, a ResNet8 network combined with knowledge distillation is proposed in this paper. ResNet18 and ResNet8 are selected as the teacher network and student network, respectively. The response-based knowledge of the ResNet18 network is used to guide the ResNet8 network learning via offline distillation. The experimental results based on the MSTAR real dataset demonstrate that the proposed method can obtain almost the same high accuracy as ResNet18. Compared with ResNet18, the model parameters of ResNet8 is about one-tenth of ResNet18, and it has higher classification efficiency while maintaining relatively high accuracy.

articleTitle: $L_{1/2}$-norm Regularization Based SAR Interferogram Generation
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar interferometry (InSAR) is a key technology developed in recent years. It extends two-dimensional synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging to a higher dimension by obtaining digital elevation model (DEM). It is known that high-quality DEM depends on the well processed interferogram. However, typical phase noise reduction technologies such as various filters will cause a decrease of image spatial resolution. To solve this problem, in this paper, an <tex>$L_{1/2}$</tex>-norm regularization based InSAR processing algorithm is proposed and introduced to generate the high-quality interferogram. In the proposed method, we first construct the model of interferogram generation procedure based on the relationship between two used images and discrete wavelet transform (DWT). Then the interferogram will be recovered by solving an <tex>$L_{1/2}$</tex>-norm regularization problem. Compared with typical matched filtering (MF) image based result, the interferogram reconstructed by the proposed method has better performance, especially less phase noise and reduced number of residue. Experimental results based on simulated and real data validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Multisensor Measurements Clustering Using Affinity Propagation
abstract: Motivated by multiple target track initialization in sensor network, this paper presents a multisensor measurements clustering algorithm based on affinity propagation with association constraint. Measurements from the same sensor cannot be grouped into the same cluster, referred as to association constraint, is considered. As a result, the affinity propagation based clustering algorithm is extended to clustering algorithm with association constraint. The max-sum belief propagation is utilized to produce neighborhood maximum clusters. The proposed method can automatically estimate the number of clusters and its complexity scales quadratically in the number of sensors and the number of measurements. The performance of the proposed method is verified by simulated data.

articleTitle: Compensation of THz Radar Signals for Atmospheric Effects Based on Range Profile Matching
abstract: the terahertz (THz) radar signal distorted by atmospheric propagation should be calibrated to suppress paired echoes in radar images. In this paper, to compensate THz radar signals for atmospheric effects, a procedure is proposed to estimate atmospheric condition based on range profile matching. The scattering centers in the range profile are identified via local maximum clustering to extract the distorted separable scattering centers. An atmospheric lookup table is generated to characterize typical atmospheric condition. The range profile of an arbitrary separable scattering center is simulated under different atmospheric condition to match with the extracted scattering center. The atmospheric condition achieving the highest correlation coefficient is used to compensate for atmospheric effects. To validate the proposed procedure, the THz radar echo composed of several scattering centers is simulated under random atmospheric condition, regarding as the distorted signal for calibration. The estimated atmospheric condition is slightly different from the set values, while the range profile distortion caused by paired echoes is noticeably suppressed using the proposed procedure.

articleTitle: Fusion of Spaceborne and Airborne SAR Images via Target Proposal and Polarization Information Exploitation for Vessel Detection
abstract: In this paper, we focus on the vessel detection via fusion of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images acquired from spaceborne-airborne collaborative observations, and propose a new method based on target proposal and polarization information exploitation (TPPIE). First, a new triple-state proposal matrix (TSPM) is generated by combing the normed gradient-based target proposal and the edge-based morphological candidate map. Second, we present a new polarization feature, named absolute polarization ratio (APR), to exploit the intensity information of dual-polarization SAR images. Third, the final fused image with enhanced targets and suppressed backgrounds, i.e., improved target-to-cluster ratio (TCR), is attained by the Hadamard product of the intersected TSPM from multi-sources and the composite map exploiting APR feature. Experimental results using Gaofen-3 satellite and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) SAR images show that the proposed TPPIE fusion method yields higher TCRs of fused images and better detection performance of vessel targets than the commonly used image fusion approaches.

articleTitle: Hypersonic Target Track Initiation Method Based on Interactive Multiple Gate
abstract: With regards to the problem that the near space hypersonic target flight speed and maneuverability, traditional methods can not initiate target track effectively, a kind of near space hypersonic target track initiation method based on interactive multiple gate (IMG) was proposed. Based on the near space hypersonic characteristics of target motion velocity and the set-up of the target's maneuver ability of the fan gate, oval gate and part of the annular gate, by using data processing method, the initial tracking of the target can be calculated through the input interaction, trace detection, weight updating and output interaction of the interactive computing of multiple gates. The simulation results show that, the new method can initiate near space hypersonic target track effectively and the correct track initiation probability is high with wide mobile coverage. This method has a certain applicability and adoptability.

articleTitle: Analysis and modeling of Internet user interest evolution
abstract: The number of users on the Internet is increasing day by day. In terms of the current development of Internet technology, Internet enterprises and companies do not have the ability and resources to make full use of users' information, but using only a small part of this huge data is enough to bring huge benefits to enterprises and companies. For example, user interest has always been the focus of the research of major Internet enterprises and groups. If we can fully understand the user's interest and the evolution of interest, enterprises can design products targeted and personalized to users, to attract more users to use products. This paper focuses on the analysis and modeling of user interest evolution. First, collect the data set from the Internet, then process the data set with numpy, construct various embedding vectors and user behavior sequences from the processed data, and input the user behavior into Gru cyclic neural network and auxiliary loss neural network, Finally, calculate the correlation between the implicit state of Gru's output and the embedded input attention mechanism of the target commodity, and weighted sum the hidden layer vectors. Finally, an attention value is obtained. The attention value and the hidden layer vector are continuously input into augru for learning. The final output result is the final predicted interest, take the interest as the vector and the vector of the target commodity, and various feature vectors are spliced and input into the MLP three-layer neural network to continuously learn the nonlinear relationship set of each vector, and calculate the cross entropy and accuracy. After multiple rounds of data training and testing of the model, the system can finally achieve the accuracy of predicting the evolution of user interest.

articleTitle: Computationally Efficient Ground Moving Target Focusing Method for Synthetic Aperture Radar
abstract: The unknown motions between synthetic aperture radar (SAR) and non-cooperative ground moving target will result in the range migration (RM) and Doppler frequency migration (DFM). The RM and DFM will make the energy of ground moving target defocused. In order to address these problems, a computationally efficient ground moving target focusing method for SAR is developed. Firstly, an operation based on slow-time reversal transform and scaled Fourier transform is initially introduced to estimate the second-order phase. Secondly, an operation based on improved slow-time reversal transform and scaled inverse Fourier transform is proposed to estimate the first-order phase. Finally, according to the estimated parameters, the focusing matched function is constructed to focus the moving target. The proposed method can effectively handle the RM and DFM, and the well-focused result can be obtained in the presence of Doppler ambiguity. The blind speed sidelobe can be further addressed. In addition, the developed approach is computationally efficient because the parameter-searching step is avoided. The processed results of both simulated and measured data are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of proposed method.

articleTitle: Gait Recognition of Millimeter Wave Radar Based on Local Texture Features
abstract: As a biological feature, the gait can be utilized to distinguish different individuals and different behaviors. Compared with other biological features, the gait has the characteristics of long distance and not easy to camouflage, which makes it a very promising biological feature. In this paper, human gait data collected from a millimeter wave radar is exploited to distinguish different behaviors. The micro-Doppler spectrogram of the corresponding gait is obtained via the Fast Fourier transform (FFT). In order to better characterize the gait features, the Local Binary Pattern (LBP) are exploited to represent the local texture features of the micro-Doppler spectrogram of different gaits, which can automatically extract micro-Doppler features and also reduces the amount of data required. In addition, Support Vector Machines (SVM) is employed for classification. The actual data from three gaits that include empty-handed walking, walking with a carton, and walking with one carry-on baggage by one hand and carrying a backpack, demonstrate that the classification accuracy rate of the proposed method can reach 92.59 %.

articleTitle: A New Frenquency-Domain Imaging for High-maneuverability Bistatic Forward-looking SAR
abstract: Bistatic forward-looking SAR is a synthetic aperture radar system with an independently moving transmitter and receiver breaks through the limitations of the conventional monostatic SAR on the forward-looking imaging. However, the existence of a double hyperbola in the bistatic range equation makes the severe two–Dimension (2-D) coupling. Based on the bistatic SAR space geometrical model and the point target spectrum form the series reversion, this paper deals with above problems with the Second-Keystone and the nonlinear chirp scaling (NCS) algorithm. The results of simulation verify the feasibility of the method.

articleTitle: Sensor Selection of Distributed MIMO Radar for Target Localization
abstract: This paper considers a sensor selection problem in the distribute MIMO radar networks. Sensor selection is considered as a constrained optimization problem, which is formulated to minimize the errors in estimating target position under the limit of the total number of transmitters and receiver. Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) is used as target localization performance metric. A suboptimal scheme is proposed for approximately solving this problem. The scheme is based on the reinforcement learning method, which is a branch of machine learning. Simulation results show that the proposed method provides satisfactory solution at a given antennas total number limit and is close to the optimal solution with exhaustive attack method.

articleTitle: A joint spatial-polarization adaptation method for DOA estimation under mainlobe jamming
abstract: Aiming at the DOA estimation problem under mainlobe jamming, a joint spatial-polarization adaptation method with polarization sensitive array is proposed in this paper. First, in order to suppress the mainlobe jamming, each row (or column) of array data is adaptively processed in spatial-polarization domain to obtain a column (or row) of adaptive channel data. Then, the maximum likelihood algorithm is used to estimate the elevation (or azimuth) of target. Numerical simulations are performed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Slow-time Randomly Missing Data Reconstruction for Skywave Over-the-horizon Radar
abstract: In skywave over-the-horizon radar (OTHR), the slow-time randomly missing data reconstruction is vital for the following signal processing where the data contaminated by lightning discharges or transient meteors are usually discarded and have to be reconstructed properly. The least-square auto-regressive (LS-AR) method is often used as a solver for the randomly missing problem. However, the derivations for the LS-AR method are not convincing and the performance of the LS-AR method would be degraded or even failed in some cases. In this paper, we are aimed at solving these two issues where two corresponding methods are proposed. The former method has a solid theoretical foundation and we will see that the LS-AR method could be considered as a simplified form of it. The latter method based on the LS-AR method behaves robustly for randomly missing positions compared with other types of methods by real data processing.

articleTitle: A Novel DEM Imaging Algorithm for Complex Terrain Based on GNSS-InBSAR System
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) based interferometric synthetic aperture radar(InSAR) can be considered as a distributed system. It is required to use digital elevation model (DEM) to obtain high-accuracy interferometric phase. However, using coarse DEM directly will make the edge of target's PSF distorted due to its low two-dimensional resolution. In this paper, a DEM imaging method that combines fitting and smoothing processing is proposed. The fitting processing is based on moving least square and the gaussian kernel with symmetrical transformation is used to realize the smooth effect. The experimental results show that the correlation coefficient of the associated points in imaging pairs has been improved, which proves the effectiveness of the algorithm.

Author Keywords: Global Navigation Satellite System based interferometric bistatic synthetic aperture radar(GNSS-InBSAR)

articleTitle: DEM Extraction of L-Band Repeat-Pass InSAR Based on BP Algorithm
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) technology is a high-precision earth observation technology. In recent years, the acquisition of high-precision ground digital elevation models (DEM) based on Interferometry SAR (InSAR) technology has attracted wide attention from researchers. In this paper, a DEM extraction method is proposed for the airborne L-band repeat-pass InSAR experimental data. First, the back projection algorithm (BP) is used to obtain the master and slave images. Then, we perform interference processing and to obtain interference phase of the imaging scene. Next, the coarse-precision DEM data is used to compensate the interference phase error. Finally, the DEM extraction result of the imaging scene is obtained. The processing results of simulation and experimental data verify the effectiveness and practicability of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Vehicle Classification via Multi-dimension Feature Extraction with Millimeter Wave Radar
abstract: Accurate vehicle classification is an important issue in autonomous driving and traffic monitoring technology. In order to improve the classification accuracy of road vehicles in passive traffic monitoring scenario with millimeter wave (MMW) radar, a vehicle classification algorithm based on multi-dimension feature extraction and support vector machine (SVM) is proposed in this paper. According to the scattering points distribution of the vehicle in range-doppler-angle domain, 9 statistical features are mined and extracted to obtain the feature vector, and then an SVM classifier is used to realize vehicle classification. The real data experimental results based on a 77GHz MMW radar verify the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method in road vehicle classification over the classification method based on point cloud feature and SVM.

articleTitle: High Performance Slotted Waveguide Array Antenna of mm-Wave Radar
abstract: This paper presents development of slotted waveguide array antenna applied in millimeter-wave FMCW radar detector device. This linear travelling wave array antenna which is excited by 50ohm glass insulator coaxial connector can integrated with the T/R module of the front-end systems compactly. The antenna has radiation beamwidth of E-plane 9deg, H-plane 108deg, and the side-lobe is less than - 13dB, the beam point is 22.5deg deviation of the normal vector. The gain is greater than 13.5dBi at the operating frequency of 37GHz. The SNR of the mm-wave IF output signal is larger than 15dB with this high performance antenna integrated.

articleTitle: Real sea surface electromagnetic scattering model with multi-physical fields based on satellite data
abstract: The characteristics of ocean electromagnetic scattering plays an important role in satellite remote sensing, radar detection and target recognition. The actual marine environment is complex and changeable. The traditional wind wave spectrum sea surface electromagnetic scattering model only considers wind speed and wind direction, which cannot accurately describe the difference of real sea clutter. In this paper, a robust method is proposed to analyze the characteristics of sea surface electromagnetic scattering. Based on the the ocean environment parameters data provided by the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), combined with the multi-physical field sea surface geometric model and the two-scale algorithm, the actual sea surface electromagnetic scattering model is built. The simulation results are consistent with the X-band measurements. This method can be used to build the multi-physical field sea surface electromagnetic characteristics database in different sea areas. In order to quickly realize the marine situation awareness, it has an important role in promoting the future development of electromagnetic space integration of the heaven and earth sea.

articleTitle: Target Amplitude Characteristic Analysis With Neighborhood Information Using C-band Circular SAR Data
abstract: The circular synthetic aperture radar (SAR) can observe the experimental scene from all angles. The backscatter intensity of the target in the scene can be obtained. Different targets in the imaging scene show different amplitude characteristics. For example, significant targets such as buildings and oil tanks show strong response characteristics at certain angles, and secondly, weak response characteristics for targets is shown such as grass and ground. In this article, the omnidirectional scattering intensity data of the target obtained from the radar is used to analyze the amplitude characteristics, and the model is established for different targets to obtain the final result. The fuzzy C-means (FCM) model combined with neighborhood information is used to analyze the target amplitude characteristics. The amplitude characteristics of the target are divided into two categories: strong response and weak response for analysis. The initial two types of cluster centers are set for iteration and finally the target amplitude characteristic reference values at different angles are obtained. C-band circular SAR data is used to validate our method. As a result, the amplitude characteristics of the whole scene using membership degree can be described.

articleTitle: Geophysical parameters retrieval from SMR measurements of HY-2B satellite
abstract: The Scanning Microwave Radiometer (SMR) onboard Chinese HY-2B satellite launched on 25 October 2018, is a multi-frequency conical-scanning microwave sensor, which operates on 6.925, 10.7, 18.7, 23.8 and 37 GHz. The SMR has the capability to measure accurate sea surface temperature, sea surface wind speed, total columnar water vapour and cloud liquid water simultaneously. In this paper, using an optimal estimation method, we retrieved these four geophysical parameters and compared the SMR retrievals with the WindSat products. The results show that the SMR performs well in the inversion of all the four physical parameters, which results in a good agreement with WindSat products.

articleTitle: Pulse Group Extraction of Multi-Function Radar
abstract: Multi-function radar signals account for a large proportion of radar reconnaissance datasets with a rapidly increasing amount of data. Automatic and accurate analysis of the pulse group of these radars is an important task to research and explain the working mode and behavior intention of radar system. In order to address this problem, this paper proposes an automatic analysis method of radar pulse group based on the joint extraction and extension of multi-parameter frequent items, including pulse repetition interval (PRI) and radio frequency (RF). The multi-parameter frequent items extracted from the pulse train are used to implement pulses extension and pulse segments extension. Finally, the pulse group of multi-function radar are obtained. The last part of this paper sets up several typical simulations to verify the feasibility and performance of the new method.

articleTitle: Deceptive Interference Suppression Method Based on Time Diversity Array
abstract: With the development of modern electronic technology, electronic interference has gradually become an important factor in target detection, and a variety of electronic interference has led to a sharp deterioration of the performance of the radar detection system. A model of deceptive interference of time diversity array is presented in this paper. Starting from the advantage of time diversity, it makes full use of the information carried by pulse time-varying, and separates the real target after signal processing effectively, so as to achieve the purpose of suppressing deceptive interference. The interference suppression performance of the proposed method is significantly better than MIMO radar. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Beamspace Dimension Reduction Technique With Application to DOA estimation in Low-angle Tracking
abstract: We develop a dimension reduction algorithm that against coherent signals with application to direction of arrival (DOA) estimation in low-angle tracking. The dimension reduction is done as a linear transformation which is commonly referred to as beamspace (BS). In this paper, the BS covariance matrix is reconstituted from several beams which can be applied to synthetic vector maximum likelihood (SVML) estimator. The proposed method is computationally less expensive to obtain similar DOA estimation performance as compared to the existing element space (ES) technique. Simulation results and field data sets validate the robustness of the developed algorithm, and they show its effectiveness and superiority to the ES SVML algorithm.

articleTitle: A New Bias Pseudo-Measurement Method for Distributed Sensor Bias Estimation
abstract: To deal with the problem of sensor registration in distributed sensors, a common method is to construct pseudo-measurements only related to the bias vector, and then estimate the bias through these pseudo-measurements. Consider the scene of limited communication, a new method to construct the bias pseudo-measurement only by operating the local tracks, covariances, and the equivalent bias measurement matrices is proposed in this paper. Compared with the existing methods, the proposed method can save about 36.4% of the communication cost with other performance unchanged in the system exemplified in this paper.

articleTitle: Vital Sign Detection of LFMCW Radar Based on Kernel Density Estimation
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of vital sign detection for the linear frequency-modulated continuous wave (LFMCW) radar system. We propose a heart rate estimation algorithm based on kernel density estimation to enhance the accuracy. Specifically, first, differences are calculated between the neighbor peaks and valleys of the heartbeat wave. Second, the kernel function is used to characterize the distribution of these differences. Then, based on this statistical characteristic, adaptive threshold values are selected to filter invalid peak-valley pairs. The number of valid peak-valley pairs is the basis to determine the area where we can obtain the final heartbeat estimation result. Finally, experimental data are used to prove the validity of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Novel Reconstruction Filter for the Azimuth Multi-Channel SAR
abstract: The compensation of channel imbalances plays a vital role in signal processing of the azimuth multi-channel (AMC) synthetic aperture radar (SAR). In the operational AMC SAR system, the channel imbalance is usually considered to be a constant in both the time and frequency domain for one image. However, since the antenna patterns of all channels cannot be strictly consistent, the channel imbalances may vary with the Doppler frequency. This paper establishes the signal model of AMC SAR with channel imbalances changing with Doppler frequency and proposes a novel compensation method during the reconstruction for the echo signals received by all channels. This method has been verified by simulations and real data acquired by Gaofen-3 (GF-3). The result shows that this method has excellent potential for improving the image quality for AMC SAR.

articleTitle: A Design of Push-Broom Reflector Antenna
abstract: This paper studies and analyzes the performance of an X-band offset ring reflector antenna system fed by a dense feed array. It is proposed to combine GA (genetic algorithm) and LTS (least squares method) to form a GA-LTS-based feed optimization algorithm to optimize the amplitude and phase of each unit in the dense feed array. The processing and testing of the antenna has realized that the main beam efficiency of the normal beam in the on-orbit and cross-orbit dimensions is greater than 95%, the sidelobe level is better than −24.5dB, and the antenna standing wave is less than 1.6.

articleTitle: Robust ISAR Target Classification Based on Attention Network
abstract: Target classification for inverse synthetic aperture radar images with unknown deformation is always an important and challenging task. This paper proposes an attention network for robust ISAR target classification. In the network, all the feature extraction and classification procedures are realized by attention mechanism. The stacked self-attention blocks are used to extract position independent feature maps. Then the feature maps are injected with position information and remapped by a transformer encoder. At last, a transformer decoder converts the process of target classification to attention calculation between the feature encoding and the learnable query vector. The proposed network shows high accuracy and robustness on the experiments of 4-satellite target classification.

articleTitle: An efficient parameter estimation approach before target detection for LFMCW radar using FFT
abstract: For a classical radar signal processing chain, target parameter estimation (TPE) is carried out after matched filtering (MF) and detection. Since target parameters are unknown when MF is implemented, data windows are generally adopted to reduce the side lobes of strong targets. However, the mismatch caused by data windows can result in significant performance loss. Sparse recovery (SR)-based detection method is a promising algorithm that can be used to reduce side lobes without adopting data windows. Nevertheless, grid mismatch problem is inevitable since target parameters are unknown as well. This paper proposes a novel estimate-before-detection (EBD) approach for LFMCW radar which can carry out TPE before MF and target detection. Firstly, based on the maximum likelihood (ML) principle and the first-order Taylor series, TPE is performed directly based on the received signal, and an analytical solution is obtained. Then, in order to reduce the compute complexity, a fast estimation method is proposed, which can carry out TPE using FFT. The proposed method makes it possible to perform “matched” signal processing with known target parameters.

articleTitle: Composite Sparsity-Driven SAR Parametric Imaging for Rectangular Plate
abstract: The traditional synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging technology is usually based on the point scatterers (PSs) model, which cannot preserve the structural characteristics of the distributed targets in SAR imaging. To solve this problem, in this paper, a parametric model of the rectangular plate scatterers (RPSs) is utilized to characterize the scattering features of the distributed target. Then, <tex>$\ell_{1}$</tex>-norm representing point sparsity and total variation (TV) norm representing edge sparsity is introduced, which can provide critical priors for signal recovery. Finally, the composite sparsity-driven parametric imaging algorithm based on the alternative direction method of multipliers (CSPI-ADMM) is proposed to solve the imaging problem of lack of structure. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm through simulation experiments.

Author Keywords: composite sparsity driven parametric imaging algorithm based on the alternative direction method of multipliers (CSPI-ADMM)

articleTitle: Active Self-Tuning Metasurface Radome for High-Power Microwave
abstract: In this paper a new-type active self-tuning metasurface radome with states of transmission and absorption in same band, that can add electromagnetic sensing module to communication when the state in low-power microwave and stealth when the state in high-power microwave, which comprise three layers and have simple structure, is proposed. By loading PIN diodes in the gap of the the top layer and bottom layer on the metasurface, the OFF/ON states of the PIN diodes can correspond to the transmission/absorption states of metasurface. In the frequency band of 5.7 GHz-7.6 GHz have admirable transmission upper 80%, when PIN diodes of the top and bottom layer are OFF, the band of 5.6 GHz-7.75 GHz have admirable absorption upper 90%, when PIN diodes of the top layer are ON and the bottom layer PIN diodes in the gap of g1 are OFF, and in the gap of g2 are ON. The proposed active self-tuning metasurface radome, which can through adding electromagnetic sensing module to realize the Self-tuning, have promising applications for high-power microwave. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Group Targets Splitting Algorithm for Ballistic Missile Penetration Applications
abstract: For missile defense systems, the sooner the group target split tracking of ballistic missile is completed, the more preparation time there will be. On the other hand, the group target split tracking too early may cause problems such as mixed tracking, wrong tracking and resources saturation during radar tracking process, which affect the combat performance of weapon systems. A group splitting algorithm for ballistic missile target tracking is proposed in this paper. First, the formation of group targets and the tracking strategy is analyzed, and the IMM-UKF filter framework is described. Then the mathematical model of the group splitting algorithm is established. The factors that affect the performance of the group splitting are discussed. Finally the multi-object optimization problem is solved by using Pareto method. Simulation and experimental results prove that the proposed algorithm can reach a balance between the instant splitting of group targets and the target association stability in a group.

articleTitle: Study on high stability of synthetic Aperture microwave radiometer
abstract: In order to solve the urgent high stability demand of synthetic aperture microwave radiometer, a high stability test method is proposed for the first time. Firstly, the factors affecting the stability of the system are analyzed, and then a high stability test system is established. Finally, the sensitivity and stability tests of each component are carried out, and the test results are processed by stability correction algorithm. The results showed that the stability test method and the correction model are feasible. It can effectively improve the system stability of the synthetic aperture microwave radiometer to 0.11K/3 days. This will lay a very important technical foundation for the final salinity detection.

articleTitle: Human Identification Based on Short-Time Radar Spectrograms Using Transformer Network
abstract: As an important topic in the field of public security, human identification is of great practical significance in a variety of tasks. Radar-based human identification has gained some attention in recent years, but recognizing people with short-time spectrograms remains an open problem. Since radar spectrograms with short durations contain limited micro-Doppler signatures, it is hard to extract discriminative personnel information for the recognition systems, resulting in poor identification performance. In this paper, a Transformer-based network is presented to solve this problem. The proposed model utilizes the self-attention mechanism to extract the inter-frame sequential features in the time domain, which act as a supplement to the lacking frequency information in the short-time spectrograms. A dataset with 15 subjects is constructed to verify the model, and the experimental results show that the proposed Transformer-based identification strategy achieves improved accuracy than existing methods when recognizing people with short-time spectrograms.

articleTitle: Frequency Analysis for Non-uniformly Data in a Smart Radar Warehouse
abstract: Numerous radar warehouses equipped with Internet of Things (IoT) sensors have recorded a large number of environmental monitoring data. These valuable data can be used to test decision systems and help to modify them. When the measured data are applied in real scenarios, weak components always appear to interfere irregular event surveillance Lots of missing samples, however, exist in IoT data, leading to a serious disturbance in frequency domain which may probably veil the weak components. Traditional algorithms obtain very limited effects when there exist quantities of missing samples. Based on this, a new weak components extraction algorithm is proposed in this paper for real temperature data acquired by IoT sensors installed in the radar warehouses. This algorithm suppresses missing samples disturbance by minimizing the mean squared error of inverse-transformed data and original data in available samples. Its effect is better than any other interpolation method, particularly when missing samples exist consecutively. Some experimental results verify the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Interference Suppression of Small Weak Scattering Targets in High-resolution SAR Image
abstract: SAR images play an important role in target detection. However, speckle noise, thermal noise and azimuth blur in SAR images can interfere with the small weak scattering targets detection. The denoising algorithm based on Doppler power spectrum can simultaneously remove the speckle noise, thermal noise and azimuth blur of SAR images at the expense of resolution. We draw on the ideas of sparse representation and image fusion, and propose image restoration fusion based on sparse representation (IRF), which makes it possible to keep the contours of inland waters clear while suppressing SAR image noise.

articleTitle: Effects of Measurement Model on Target Tracking Performance for Passive Bistatic Radar
abstract: In a complex electromagnetic environment, the measurements obtained by passive radar are usually uncertain due to the influence of many factors such as noise, interference and missed detection. The selection of the measurement model depends on the target state, which affects the implementation and performance of the tracking algorithm and may result in the trajectory tracking diverges under serious cases. Aiming at this problem, a measurement model based on passive bistatic radar is first established. Then the impact of the bistatic and cartesian measurement models on the tracking performance of different types of targets is investigated in combination with simulations. Finally, the performance of the two measurement models is confirmed via real data processing.

articleTitle: A 3D imaging method for future communication and imaging integrated terminal
abstract: The frequency band of 5G communication system has already reached the lower end of millimeter wave, and 6G may step into terahertz in the future. 3D tomography synthetic aperture imaging using manual intelligent terminal system may become a reality. However, 3D tomography is faced with the problem of sparse and non-uniform elevation sampling. This paper presents a 3D imaging method for near-field targets with sparse and non-uniform sampling. Firstly, echo model based on frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) is established, then the non-negligible errors caused by stop-and-go propagation assumption is compensated. The next step is 2D imaging of each baseline using frequency-domain BP. Finally, the tomography algorithm is performed on the 2D BP results pertaining the multiple baselines. For the sparse and non-uniform sampling situations and the unknowability of real scene, the Bayesian Compressed Sensing (BCS) algorithm is applied for reconstruction. The effectiveness of the method is verified by real data processing.

articleTitle: An Improved 2P-CFAR Method for Ship Detection in SAR Images
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) systems can be used for discovery and surveillance. According to the current requirements, accurate ship detection is becoming more and more important. However, the interference factors such as coherent speckle noise and strong target sidelobes will reduce the detection accuracy. In this paper, an improved two-parameter Constant False Alarm Rate (2P-CFAR) method is proposed to solve this problem. After using the non-local means (NLM) filtering method to suppress coherent speckle noise, the 2P-CFAR method is performed to obtain candidate targets, and an equal proportion segmentation procedure is carried out to optimize the aspect ratios of the candidate targets and weaken the sidelobes. Experimental results based on the SAR images acquired by the Gaofen-3 satellite verify the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Surface Grid Fast BP Method for Spaceborne SAR Imaging
abstract: In the previous spaceborne SAR imaging methods based on time domain algorithm, the imaging grids are usually arranged in a flat plane. However, for ultra-large width and ultra-high resolution imaging, the quadratic phase error caused by surface bending is large, which makes the images defocus. In this paper, the surface grid is arranged for accurate imaging, and a new two-step spectrum compression function is proposed to achieve sub-aperture images fusion.

articleTitle: Distributed Multi-Sensor Multi-View Fusion of PHD Filter for Maneuvering Targets
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of maneuvering multi-target tracking by a network of sensors having different and limited fields of view (FoV s). Each local sensor runs the Gaussian Mixture Probability Hypothetical Density (GMPHD) filter. Due to the target maneuver, based on a single motion model, severe tracking performance degradation can be observed. We propose to use multi-model (MM) method to realize the adaptation to motion characteristic so as to overcome maneuverability of targets. Then considering FoV s of sensors in the network are different and limited, the standard weighted arithmetic average (WAA) fusion is no longer applicable and leads to an underestimation of the target number. Therefore, we use state-dependent WAA (SD-WAA) fusion rule, which performs the WAA in a more robust way by calculating a set of state-related fusion weights. Numerical experiment is designed to demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Complex number domain SAR image fusion based on Laplacian pyramid
abstract: Aiming at the problem of low azimuth resolution due to the limited azimuth observation angle of a single synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image, a multi-view SAR image fusion method is proposed. According to the characteristics of complex number domain SAR images in the MSTAR dataset, this method uses complex image domain data for processing.
