First, the morphological opening and closing operations are used to suppress the background noise, and then the Canny operator is used to extract the target contour, and the target area is separated from the original image according to the contour. Then the angle information in the image data is used to complete the image registration, and finally the multiple targets are merged through the Laplacian pyramid, and the obtained image contains more information and has an improved resolution. The simulation and real data processing results show that the multi-view SAR image fusion algorithm can better reduce the influence of external errors and improve the resolution.

articleTitle: Changes in soil moisture and vegetation over the Tibetan Plateau during 2000–2019
abstract: The Tibetan Plateau (TP), known as the “Water Tower of Asia”, is an ecology-fragile region that is extremely sensitive to climate change. In this paper, the spatio-temporal trends of soil moisture (SM) and vegetation and their response to climatic factors (precipitation and air temperature) were explored by using remotely sensed ESA CCI SM and MODIS LAI data respectively in the growing season during 2000–2019 over the TP. Results show TP is generally wetting and significantly greening during the study period. The significant increasing trend of SM accounts for 21.80% of the TP, which is about twice of its significant decreasing trend (10.19%), while more than half of LAI (58.21 %) display a significant increasing trend. The precipitation is positively correlated with SM in most regions of TP and is the main driving factor of SM change. In contrast, temperature plays a more dominant role than precipitation in vegetation greening over the TP. The combined trend of SM and LAI indicates that TP mainly consists of wetting and greening regions, followed by drying and greening areas.

articleTitle: Characterization of Complex Corner Reflectors in Polarimetric Rotation Domain
abstract: The corner reflector can obtain a large effective radar cross section (RCS) with a small size, which has been widely used in the radar field. It is important to study the polarimetric scattering characteristics of the complex corner reflector. The polarimetric correlation pattern visual interpretation tool in rotation domain can effectively mine the hidden rich information between arbitrary two polarization channels along the radar line of sight. On this basis, the characteristics in polarimetric rotation domain of corner reflectors with different azimuth angles, frequencies and array intervals are analyzed. Experimental studies with electromagnetic computation datasets of octahedral and icosahedral corner reflectors are carried out. Experimental results show that the co-polarization correlation fluctuation <tex>$\vert \hat{\gamma}_{\text{HH}-\text{VV}}(\theta)\vert _{\text{std}}$</tex> can accurately characterize the characteristics in polarimetric rotation domain of the complex corner reflector. The two types of corner reflectors are roll-invariant in the large angle range. The research work provides important simulation basis and theoretical support for engineering application.

articleTitle: Dual-DDS based Microwave Photonic Coherent Radar System
abstract: With the pursuit of high detection accuracy, future radar systems are developing towards the direction of high working frequency and large bandwidth. With the advantages of wide working frequency range and large instantaneous bandwidth, the microwave photonic can generate and process high-frequency and large-bandwidth radar signals in the optical domain, which well meet the technology demand of high-resolution radar. To improve the multi-target detection ability of the radar with high resolution, a dual-DDS based microwave photonic radar is proposed in this paper. The radar prototype is developed. The microwave photonic radar signal generation and process are well studied. The prototype's instantaneous bandwidth can reach 4 GHz, which leads to a high resolution of 4.7 cm. More importantly, it demonstrates the ability to simultaneously multi-target detection.

articleTitle: Inflatable Eight-Octave Conformal Linearly Tapered Slot Antenna for Radar Application
abstract: A conformal linearly tapered slot balloon antenna operating at eight-octave band is presented in this letter. The antenna consists of circle, rectangular and taper slotline and is then attached to the surface of a cylindrical PDMS membrane balloon. Simulated results show that its operating bandwidth ranges from 7 to 57 GHz with the voltage standing wave ratio less than 2 and a good end-fire radiation pattern of 14.4 dBi maximum gain, which demonstrates potential of the proposed antenna in microwave and millimeter wave radar application.

articleTitle: Overview of ISAR maneuvering target imaging technology
abstract: Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) has been widely used in remote sensing because of its high-resolution imaging ability for moving targets in space, ground and sea. At present, the imaging technology for moving targets with uniform velocity has been mature and can get clearer images, but the imaging technology for maneuvering targets still needs to be improved. Firstly, this paper reviews the classical methods of ISAR full aperture maneuvering target imaging, and summarizes the algorithm innovation in recent years; Then, the development of ISAR sparse aperture maneuvering target imaging using compressed sensing technology is systematically introduced. Finally, the future development trend is prospected.

articleTitle: Incoherent Change Detection Method Based on Image Stack for UWB SAR Image
abstract: This paper presents a novel incoherent change detection method based on image stacks for the ultra-wideband synthetic aperture radar (UWB SAR) images. This method includes the image preprocess and change detection process. The image preprocess adopted the bilinear relative radiometric correction method for the radiometric correction. The change detection process firstly obtains the multiple difference images by subtracting a surveillance image with three reference images. And then, a Gaussian probability density function is used to model the distribution of the amplitude of the difference image. Finally, the generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT) is used for the change detection. Compared with existing change detection methods, the proposed method in this paper shows the better detection performance on the CARABAS-II dataset. Under a specific configuration, the proposed method achieves a detection probability of 97% with a false alarm rate of 0.16/km<sup>2</sup>.

articleTitle: FDA-3D-SAR imaging based on Bayesian compressed sensing
abstract: In view of the large amount of data to be processed by the Frequency Diversity Array three-dimensional Synthetic Aperture Radar (FDA-3D-SAR) system and the higher side lobes of traditional imaging algorithms, this paper proposes a FDA-3D-SAR imaging method based on Bayesian compressed sensing (BCS) reconstruction. This method combines the characteristics of the FDA to make three-dimensional sparse observation of the target. In the imaging part, the BCS algorithm is used to reconstruct the scattering coefficient of the space target. The experimental results show that the proposed method effectively suppresses the side lobes of the radar image and improves the imaging quality.

articleTitle: An X-band and Ku-band adjustable polarization insensitive AFSS reflector
abstract: In this paper, an adjustable active frequency selective surface (AFSS) with polarization insensitive properties is proposed. The designed structure comprises an active impedance layer, a dielectric layer, and a metal backplane layer. The active impedance layer contains “” - shaped structural unit, whose modulating properties are realized by controlling pin diodes. The switchable bandwidth of the proposed structure can achieve an adjustable effect of less than −15dB and covers a much wider frequency band (8.8-11.8GHz and 12.6GHz-18.6GHz) compared with previous adjustable AFSS reflector. Meanwhile, the structure is suitable for the two polarization states of TE and TM due to the symmetry of the unit structure. Finally, the CST simulation is carried out to demonstrate the validation of proposed structure.

articleTitle: Feasibility Analysis of Retrieving Sea Ice Surface and Bottom Roughness and Thickness from Polarimetric SAR
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) plays an important role in the refined inversion of sea ice surface, bottom roughness and sea ice thickness. At present, the research on SAR and sea ice morphology is not deep enough, and there is a lack of correlation research on the surface and bottom roughness of sea ice. In response to this problem, this paper uses the sea ice data provided by the Department of Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) and the RadarSat-2 data to analyze the correlation between SAR features and sea ice surface roughness, as well as sea ice surface and bottom roughness. The results show that there is a certain correlation between SAR features and sea ice surface roughness, and the maximum absolute value of the correlation coefficient is 0.764. The roughness of sea ice surface and bottom has a strong correlation, which provides a theoretical basis for inversion of sea ice bottom roughness by SAR. In addition, SAR has great potential in estimating the thickness of deformed ice.

articleTitle: Generalized Non-Iterative Time Delay Estimation Based on Taylor Interpolation Model
abstract: Time delay estimation (TDE) has been extensively studied in the past for off-grid cases since the time delay of the target does not fall on the sampling point (on-grid) usually. In this paper, two generalized non-iterative time delay estimation methods are proposed. The maximum range cell sampling point of signal powers after pulse compression is used as a rough estimate of the time delay, while multiple points around the peak location are employed to obtain the fine estimate. Based on the Taylor expansion model, the explicit generalized expressions of two methods for the fine estimate of the time delay are derived without the knowledge of the closed-form signal expression. The proposed methods can be applied in applications where the linear frequency modulation (LFM) signal and the nonlinear frequency modulation (NLFM) signal (without closed-form expression) are employed, and only the sampling values of several points around the peak location are required. Compared with existing methods, improved estimation performance can be achieved by both methods.

articleTitle: An Improved Earth-Based Radar High-Resolution Imaging Technology of the Moon Based on Polar Format Algorithm
abstract: The polar format algorithm (PFA) is a high-resolution imaging algorithm suitable for earth-based radar imaging of the moon. However, the earth-based radar imaging of moon has the problem of out-of-plane motion, which seriously deteriorates the imaging quality of the PFA. This paper first analyzes the basic principles of polar format algorithm based on the geometric model of the Earth-Moon motion. Then it quantitatively analyzes the influence of plane wavefront assumption and out-of-plane motion on imaging, and proposes an improved PFA high-resolution imaging algorithm. Based on the quantitative analysis of the spatial variance of the phase error, the proposed algorithm divides the whole imaging scene into multiple sub images. Then, the proposed algorithm compensates the phase error of the sub image successively and further obtain the well-focused imaging result of the whole scene by sub image stitching. Finally, the proposed algorithm is verified by the computer simulation.

articleTitle: Cross Sensor Transfer Learning for Unsupervised SAR Target Detection
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) target detection based on deep learning typically assume the training and test data drawn from the same distribution. However, when the radar sensors change, this assumption does not always hold and will cause to a performance degradation when encountering such distribution mismatch. Transfer learning shares a great idea to solve this issue by transferring knowledge from the labeled data of source sensor to the unlabeled data of target sensor. We proposed a cross sensor transfer learning method based on domain adaptation, which can improve the cross sensor robustness of SAR target detection with unlabeled target sensor (domain) data. Our method includes three stages: pixel domain diverse (PDD), multilevel feature alignment (MFA) and iterative self-training (IST). The PDD stage can alleviate the few training data of SAR target detection and enhance the generalization ability by generating transition domain. MFA can learn domain invariant features in a multi-layer feature space by using the idea of adversarial learning. To learn more discriminative features, we further proposed the IST that can generate and select high-quality pseudo labels for the SAR images of target sensor. The experimental results on miniSAR and FARADSAR datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Receive Filter Design for MIMO Radar with One-Bit Quantized Signals
abstract: In this paper, the problem of receive filter design for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar with one-bit quantized signals is investigated. Based on the Neyman-Pearson (NP) criterion, we formulate the optimization problem by maximizing the probability of detection with a fixed probability of false-alarm. To solve the resulting problem, we propose an approximation method. Moreover, the performance comparison between the one-bit and infinite-bit quantizations is investigated from a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) point of view, showing that there is about 1.96dB SNR loss of using one-bit quantization. Finally, simulations are presented to show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: The distributed imaging processing method of space-borne SAR based on embedded GPU
abstract: With the growth of space-borne SAR echo data, the pressure on satellite to ground data transmission is increasing. Therefore, real-time imaging processing of space-borne SAR on-orbit becomes an urgent need. A data processing method of distributed embedded GPU based on Chirp Scaling (CS) imaging algorithm is proposed in this paper. We use multiple embedded GPUs to process large-scale space-borne SAR data jointly. Unified Memory is used to allocate memory to reduce data transmission between the CPU and GPU, and the allocated memory is reused to solve the limited computing resources of a single embedded GPU. In addition, CUDA streams are used to overlap data transmission and data processing time to reduce communication delays between embedded GPUs. The distributed processing method proposed in this paper can effectively reduce a single satellite's computing and storage resources and improve the full-orbit utilization of a single satellite. Multiple NVIDIA Jetson Nanos are used to build the simulation system, and the system's feasibility was verified.

articleTitle: LRSNet: Lightweight and Real-time SAR Ship Detection with Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Object detection based on deep learning methods plays a significant role in usual tasks. These greatly universal detection algorithms can promote the intelligent interpretation of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images and help to get more accurate detection results. Different from the current methods directly used in SAR images, we creatively try to apply the semantic segmentation idea to SAR ship detection and complete detection and segmentation at the same time. We think SAR ship detection as a pixel-by-pixel binary classification problem rather than common general detection methods. By this way, the problem of multi-scale ships and small targets can be transformed into the unbalance of foreground and background in SAR images. In this paper, we propose a lightweight but efficient convolutional neural network (CNN) model named LRSNet. LRSNet has fewer parameters, higher efficiency and better detection and segmentation results. On HRSID dataset, the model can achieve 42.6% AP and 59.5% AR, which is better than the yolov4 detection algorithm, and the model size is only 8.4M.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Deformation Retrieval by Multi-Angle Processing in Distributed Geosynchronous SAR
abstract: This paper proposes distributed geosynchronous synthetic aperture radar (GEO SAR) for three-dimensional (3D) deformation retrieval. The system can provide sufficient observation angles, which can greatly improve the measurement accuracy. We firstly introduce the configuration of distributed GEO SAR. Then, we focus on the 3D deformation retrieval in distributed GEO SAR by multi-angle processing. An optimal multi-angle data selection method based on minimizing position dilution of precision (PDOP) is proposed to obtain optimal 3D deformation retrieval accuracy. Finally, the proposed methods and the theoretical analysis are verified by simulation experiments. 3D deformation retrieval accuracy of centimeter-level can be obtained by selecting optimal multi-angle data.

articleTitle: Multi-Sensor Control for Distributed Multi-Target Tracking with Limited Sensor Fields-of-view
abstract: This paper addresses the multi-sensor control problem for distributed multi-target tracking (DMTT) with limited sensor fields-of-view (FoVs). Existing control methods cannot be directly used when the FoVs of sensors are very limited. To solve this problem, we propose a new multi-sensor control strategy that contains two key points. One is to generate the FoV-based pseudo measurement set, which is also used to sift through control commands. The other one is to propose a new reward function composed of the Cauchy-Schwarz (CS) divergence between the fused predicted density and the fused posterior density and a penalty function related to the reduction of cardinality estimate. Based on it, the optimal control scheme is obtained by maximizing the reward function. Moreover, we employ the clustering algorithm generalized covariance intersection (CA-GCI) method to fuse the local densities for dealing with the different FoVs cases. Simulation results in a challenging multi-object tracking scenario with three radar-type sensors demonstrate effectiveness of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: Improved MOCO Approach Based on 2-D Taylor Expansion for Spatially-Variant Errors in High-Resolution Airborne SAR Imagery
abstract: Motion compensation (MOCO) is important for qualities of airborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image. However, in the case of high-resolution, the spatially-variant components of motion errors are significant and cannot be compensated by traditional MOCO algorithms. To address this problem, an improved compensation approach based on two dimensions (2-D) Taylor series expansion for high resolution airborne SAR imaging in the condition of large spatially-variant motion errors is proposed. First of all, an accurate slant range history is expressed in the geometric model, which is developed by the motion parameters measured by inertial navigation system (INS). Secondly, 2-D Taylor series expansion is performed to decouple the errors so that the spatially-variant components can be removed completely by means of the interpolation. Unlike previous MOCO methods, our approach can greatly decrease the spatially-variant effects on airborne SAR imaging in the condition of large motion errors. Finally, real data experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Spaceborne SAR Radiometric Calibration Scheme Using Power Transmission Towers
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) radiometric calibration is essential for quantitative application of SAR images. However, radiometric calibration using typical calibrators, such as transponders and corner reflectors, is quite expensive and requires installation of various ground equipment. To reduce the cost and simplify the calibration process, a spaceborne SAR radiometric calibration method is proposed, using power transmission towers (PTTs) as calibrators. PTTs are widely employed and distributed for electricity power transmission and have persistent scattering characteristics as metallic targets, which makes them ideal radiometric calibrators. For effective spaceborne SAR calibration, the required Radar Cross Section (RCS) information of PTTs can be measured by airborne SAR. Experiments are performed using the Gaofen-3 data for Zhenglanqi, Inner Mongolia. The calibration factor derived by the proposed method is compared with that provided in the original Gaofen-3 product, demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Nonconvex Approach for Line Spectral Estimation
abstract: As a significant problem in statistic signal processing, line spectral estimation has wide applications in radar, sonar and wireless communications. In this paper, we propose a novel nonconvex approach for estimating the frequency parameters of a superposition of complex sinusoids from noisy samples. By assuming that the number of frequencies is known, we formulate frequency estimation as a rank-constrained nonconvex optimization problem based on the double Hankel model that we proposed recently, and then resolve it using the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Numerical results are conducted that demonstrate the superior performance of our approach in improving the estimation accuracy compared with the existing method.

articleTitle: Human Movement Tracking and Fall Detection Using UWB Impulse Radar
abstract: Non-contact medical monitoring is an emerging challenging field. In this paper, based on the single chip radar development kit of XeThru X4 ultra wideband (UWB) modules, a small radar system is systematically designed for indoor human body tracking, and fall detection. The algorithms are compared, optimized, and integrated in the system. In signal processing, moving target indication (MTI) and clutter map methods are employed to cancel strong fixed clutter; wavelet analysis is used to denoise and reconstruct the echoes of human breathing and heart-movement; center-of-gravity ranging method is used to detect the presence of human targets and to measure the human range. In data processing, using only the range dimensional measurement, the algorithms for single human target track initialization, track filtering, data association, and track management are designed in a systematic way. Since a normal human body is usually stationary or moving uniformly, a constant-velocity (CV) model is adequately to estimate the human state, and the normalized innovation squared (NIS) is sliding averaged to implement fall judgment. The field data show that the system can effectively detect and track a human body, make timely judgments of human falling and drastic moving changes of state, and extract other vital features.

articleTitle: Multi-target Direction-of-Arrival Estimation Method Based on Graph Signal Processing
abstract: Direction of Arrival Estimation (DoA) is one of the important research directions in array signal processing. Recently, DoA based on graph signal processing provides new ideas and methods for the direction of arrival estimation application. In this paper, by improving the structure of the non-fully connected graph, a multi-target DoA method based on the graph signal of a fully connected graph is proposed. By constructing a fully connected graph related to the phase information of the linear array radar elements and performing the Fourier transform of the graph. Then use the full phase difference information between the array elements to improve the DoA estimation results, which can realize the array multi-target azimuth DoA. The simulation results show that the proposed method is more accurate than the traditional classical DoA estimation method, and it is more suitable for parallel computing.

articleTitle: The Influence Mechanism of UAV Cluster Electronic Countermeasures on Radar Parameter Measurement
abstract: As a new radar jamming strategy, UAV cluster electronic countermeasures need to study its influence mechanism on radar detection. Based on the principle of radar detection, this paper has discussed the influence of drone cluster body, cluster suppression interference, cluster forwarding interference, cluster coherent interference on radar parameter measurement; and has analyzed influencing factors such as SNR, JSR, drone density, the amplitude ratio between target echo and UAV body echo. The body of UAV cluster has a poor interference effect on the radar. The main reason is that the body of UAV is small in size and the corresponding radar echo power is low. The three interference methods, suppression interference, forwarding interference and coherent interference, have good interference effects when used in cluster interference. Through the above analysis, the influence mechanism of UAV cluster on radar parameter measurement in electronic countermeasures is summarized.

articleTitle: A Multi-band and Multi-functional Conformal Array Antenna
abstract: According to the requirements of electronic information system and platform for multi-functional integration of radar, communication and navigation, the methods and technologies to expand the working bandwidth of antenna are studied. An ultra-wideband conformal element and array antenna with operating frequencies across Band P, L, S, C and X are designed and realized by comprehensively using coplanar waveguide feeding, loading matching branches, edge deformation of radiation structure, metamaterial loading and microwave holographic control. The measured data are in good agreement with the simulation results, which provides a potential antenna for multi mission integrated electromagnetic radiation and reception.

articleTitle: An Ultra-wide Band Inclined Oblique-cone Antenna for High Power Pulse Application
abstract: Cone antenna is widely used in UWB(ultra-wide band) radar.In this paper, An oblique-cone antenna is designed based on mono-cone antenna.The simulation results show that the antenna has good directivity and UWB characteristics. The oblique-cone antenna is operating from 10MHz to 1.35GHz,and the directivity in the max main lobe mangnitude is increased by 5.95dBi compared with the mono-cone antenna. At the same time, the antenna has good pulse fidelity for high power pulse.

articleTitle: Dealing with Doppler Migration for Passive Radar Based on Airborne High Speed Platform
abstract: The passive radar usually receives very weak target scattered waves, and long-term coherent accumulation is required to increase the receiving gain. However, for high-speed moving platforms, long-term accumulation will cause serious Doppler migration, which affects the energy concentration of the signal and further affects the target detection performance. This paper analyzes the reasons for the broadening and refers to ISAR imaging technology, and proposes a solution algorithm based on LVD transformation. This method transforms the broadened Doppler frequency into a two-dimensional frequency domain to form a peak with a high concentration of capabilities. The Doppler migration parameter completes the compensation for the Doppler expansion The method mainly uses FFT, complex multiplication and other operations in the realization process. and the realization process is simple and the calculation is less. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively solve the Doppler migration problem, improve the target signal-to-noise ratio, and the computational complexity is lower than other algorithms.

articleTitle: Dilated Fractal Nested Array on Moving Platform
abstract: A novel dilated fractal nested array is proposed to improve the degrees of freedom on moving platform by combining the sparse fractal array and the dilated nested array. The proposed array can be used in the scenario of large array aperture. The closed-form expression of the sensor positions of the proposed array is presented. The translation factor is given and proved to obtain a fully filled difference coarray of the synthetic array. It is shown that the degree of freedom of the proposed array is greatly enhanced. Meanwhile, the proposed array has large aperture with less mutual coupling.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of Subaperture Correlation Method Based on Height Projection
abstract: This paper analyzes the method of extracting the elevation of the target area through the chain correlation method in the Circular Synthetic Aperture Radar (CSAR) mode. By dividing the 360° CSAR platform trajectory circle into multiple sub-apertures, the sub-apertures are projected to the height layers, and the similarity of the adjacent sub-apertures corresponding to the height layer projection images is used for chain correlation to obtain the height information of the ground scene. the applicability of the method based on the division of heights is analyzed in this paper through the measured data of different types of observation scenarios.

articleTitle: Rip currents detection based on Sentinel-1 dual-polarization SAR data
abstract: In recent years, there has been an increasing interest in rip currents as an emerging public health issue for researchers. This study aims to detect and identify breaking waves region and surf zone from Sentinel-1 images, and extract the rip currents on the Portuguese coast beach. From Sentienl-1 GRD data of two scenes, it shows bright features and dark features as a “jig-saw tooth” appearance, respectively. In this paper, polarization difference of VV-polarization and VH-polarization supports to enhance the contrast between rip currents and background, and the edge detection operator is applied to identify wave breaking area and surf area shown promising result. The area, extension length and flow direction of rip currents are extracted from the image well.

articleTitle: A Novel Working Model for Distributed Space-Based Early Warning Radar
abstract: The constellation composed of distributed small satellites can perform the moving target detection function. Space-based early warning radar (SBEWR) needs an ultra-large aperture antenna to obtain the ideal performance of moving target detection, and distributed SBEWR is used to solve the problem that ultra-large antenna cannot be realized. The sparse array can use multiple small aperture antennas to achieve the minimum detectable velocity (MDV) performance of the large aperture antenna. A novel working model for distributed SBEWR is proposed, the signal processing method based on this model is theoretically deduced, and the performance of this model is verified by simulation experiments.

articleTitle: The Calibration Procedure for ACMIR
abstract: ACMIR (an airborne C-band one-dimensional microwave interferometric radiometer) is proposed for area sea surface temperature (SST) measurement with high resolution and high accuracy. A good calibration of ACMIR is needed to provide accurate values of visibility, which is used to get the brightness temperature. In this paper, the calibration procedure of ACMIR is presented. The modeling of temperature compensation and loss correction is given to improve the calibration accuracy.

articleTitle: Fast Implementation of Signal Reconstruction based on Sparse Bayesian Learning with Fourier Dictionary
abstract: Sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) is a robust algorithm for sparse signal reconstruction (SSR) and widely applied in many fields. Unfortunately, the conventional SBL algorithm suffers from heavy computational complexity due to the matrix inversion involved in each iteration, which is proportional to the cube of the observed data length and thus prevents it solving large-scale data. In this paper, based on the Fourier Dictionary (FD)-based SBL, abbreviated as FD-SBL, we propose an efficient FD-SBL method to implement SSR for uniformly sampled one-dimensional (1D) case. By utilizing the property that the matrix to be inverted is a Toeplitz matrix, we can exploit the Gohberg-Semencul (G-S)-type factorization to reduce the computational complexity of the FD-SBL algorithm. To be noted, there is no approximation in our proposed method, and the computational cost is reduced by several orders of magnitude compared with the conventional SBL algorithm. Finally, the experimental results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Fast Near-field Computational Imaging with Deep Neural Networks
abstract: With the capability to sculpt complex radiative wavefronts and couple energy from the reference wave to the desired radiation pattern, metasurface antennas have gained tremendous progress in recent years. The flexibility in antenna design gives rise to a bunch of metasurface antennas, while there is still a comprise between the needed operation band and radiation field pattern coherence. Furthermore, the relatively low sampling ratio and overlap between frequency measurement modes would inevitably pose a great challenge for matched filter and other advanced sparsity-driven post-processing imaging algorithms. In this paper, we design a deep neural network to achieve fast scene image reconstruction. The trained network could fastly reconstruct the imaged object in both low scene compressed ratio and high coherence of the measurement modes. The imaging experiments with measured radiation field data are conducted to verify the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: GPU-Based Fast Imaging Scheme for GB-MIMO Radar
abstract: GB-MIMO (Ground-Based Multiple Input Multiple Output) radar plays an important role in landslide disaster prevention. Common MIMO radar imaging based on BP (Back Projection) algorithm is slow, and severely affects the real-time performance of deformation measurement. In this paper, a fast imaging scheme applied for GB-MIMO radar is proposed based on a heterogeneous system consisting of CPU (Center Processing Unit) and GPU (Graphic Processing Unit). The signal processing architecture is firstly designed according to the radar imaging principle and algorithm analysis. Then the acceleration technology of GPU is studied with CUDA technology. The results show that the computing speed achieves 30∼35 times in three different echo sizes less than conventional schemes, which proves that the method can meet the requirement of real-time well.

articleTitle: Forecasting the Spread of COVID-19 Based on Differential Transfer Graph Neural Network
abstract: The pandemic outbreak of the 2019 Coronavirus disease (COVID-19) has a significant effect on the health and lives of people around the world. Accurately predicting the spread of the disease is vital for fighting the disease during a pandemic. This paper presents a prediction model named Differential Transfer Graph Neural Network (DTGNN). The proposed model takes the differential information of time series into account, which includes the important trend of disease evolution. Since the limited training data may cause the phenomenon of underfitting, we employ transfer learning method to train the model. We first learn the model for countries with disease widespread, and then transfer it to the target country where disease is in the early stages. Compared with the baseline models, the proposed model performs better in mid- and long-term predictions.

articleTitle: Intelligent Reflection Surface Aided MIMO Radar System
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of radar signal path weakness, where intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) is exploited to provide indirect radar detection path. The radar beampattern and phase shift matrix of IRS are jointly designed to maximize the signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) of the radar system, while the transmit power budget of radar and a non-convex unit modulus constraint imposed on the phase shifters are guaranteed. To tackle this problem, we propose a semidefinite programming (SDP)-based iterative algorithm and a closed-form-based iterative algorithm. Simulation results show that the IRS can help improve the performance of colocated multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar system.

articleTitle: A Radar Target Multi-scale Transformation Method Based on Subband Decomposition
abstract: The resolution of high-performance wideband radar is accurate enough to distinguish each strong scattering center of the target, which provides more information about the electromagnetic characteristics of the target and improves the accuracy of target recognition. However, the increased resolution will reduce the coherence of the range unit within the target range and increase the fluctuation of the target. These characteristics will deteriorate the target detection performance. In this paper, a flexible radar target multi-scale transformation method is proposed. Enlightened by the multi-rate filter bank technology, a special combination of analysis filter bank and synthesis filter bank is used to achieve any scale transformation of the original radar signal. This method can transform the radar target signal to the most suitable scale for detection according to the different early warning tasks. After the detection link, the original target signal can be accurately reconstructed without affecting the performance of the radar system. The proposed method is able to improve the performance of modern radar systems by balancing the conflict of resolution requirements between detection and other links of radar system.

articleTitle: On-orbit calibration of the scatterometer on HY-2 using Active Radar Calibration
abstract: The Active Radar Calibration(ARC) is an important on-orbit calibration device of scatterometer., which can both receive and retransmit the signal of the scatterometer. The ARC purpose is to prove the precision of Radar Cross Section(RCS) and to measure very accurately the radar pulse timing., frequency and the antenna pattern in order to monitor independently the scatterometer on HY-2 over the mission. We use the output data of the ARC to estimate the key parameters and on-orbit antenna pattern of scatterometer. Result is presented in this paper which show the ability to measure scatterometer pulse timing to microsecond detail and the precision of the antenna beamwidth to better than 0.1degrees.

articleTitle: Precise Instance Segmentation Network for High-Resolution SAR Images
abstract: With the development of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system technology and the wide application of deep learning technology, ship detection on SAR images has rapidly developed. Benefit from the strong generalization ability and end-to-end training capabilities, convolution neural network (CNN) based ship detection methods have the proprietary advantage in high-performance SAR ship detection. However, relevant SAR ship detection methods adopt rectangular bounding boxes to locate the ships which are unable to extract the contours feature of the ships. To solve this problem, we proposed a precise instance segmentation network for high-resolution SAR images. The method combines the bottom-up path augmentation module, global context module, and soft non-maximum suppression to improve Mask R-CNN for segmenting high-resolution SAR ships in pixel-wise. The network is trained and tested on the high-resolution SAR images dataset (HRSID), and the ablation experiments are conducted with Microsoft Common Objects in Context (MS COCO) evaluation metrics to verify the effects of each module. Quantitatively, the experimental results show that the method exceeds vanilla Mask R-CNN 2% AP in instance segmentation of high-resolution SAR images. Meanwhile, the visualized instance segmentation results indicate that our method fits the practical application, and it possesses the ability to extract the contour of the ship, which is more conducive to the instance segmentation of SAR images.

articleTitle: Microwave photonic radar Backscatter Simulation for 3D model based on LCIM algorithm and NVAF
abstract: Microwave photonics radar generates signals with large bandwidth and cross-spectrum. It has the capability of ultra-high resolution of Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar(ISAR) image and more electromagnetic information. The large-bandwidth signal simulated by the scattering point model cannot accurately characterize the electromagnetic scattering of a target, and the imaging results are not realistic enough according to the acquired images. This paper proposes a method for electromagnetic scattering calculation based on the Local Coordinate Improved Moller (LCIM) algorithm to solve this problem. Our algorithm adaptively processes the facets in the local coordinate, which makes the redundant tube eliminated. And the LCIM algorithm simplifies the solution formula so that the intersection can be calculated in parallel through the matrix. Because of the difference between the acquired images and the simulation results of the simplified model, the normal vector adjustment factor (NVAF) is introduced to make the imaging results of the fully polarized backscatter more realistic. The results of the satellite model with the condition of the large band and wide-angle demonstrate the feasibility of our method.

articleTitle: Accurate Millimeter-Wave Imaging of Concave Objects Under Multistatic Array Configurations
abstract: The accurate imaging of a target with complex shape, especially concave surfaces, has always been a trouble. Since concave surfaces often exhibit strong high-order scattering during forward propagation, which is often misinterpreted as artifacts or phantom targets during imaging. In this work, a bistatic imaging method for reducing artifacts caused by high-order scattering from concave objects under cylindrical millimeter-wave scanning geometry is proposed. The effects of multiple reflections within concave structures are firstly analyzed by using ray-tracing techniques. It is observed that these troublesome multiple reflection echoes often exhibit in uncertain positions with varying of observation angles. Based on this analysis, a multistatic cylindrical aperture synthesis technique is proposed to obtain accurate images of concave object despite strong high-order scattering. To verify this method, simulation and measurement imaging results under multistatic array configurations are presented. Finally, the effectiveness of artifact reduction of complex metallic targets with concave outlines is confirmed.

articleTitle: Analysis on ISAR image displacement of Plasma-Sheath-Enveloped Reentry Vehicle
abstract: The plasma sheath enveloping the surface of reentry vehicle can cause parasitic modulation on electromagnetic waves in amplitude and phase. When performing ISAR imaging on reentry vehicle, the radar echoes will also be affected. Due to its high-speed and fluid characteristics, the plasma has non-uniform velocity distribution. High-velocity scattering points in plasma sheath will induce mismatching of radar echoes' pulse compression, resulting in not only peak position offset in one-dimensional range profile, but also ISAR image displacement on range dimension. In this paper, through analyzing the distributions of electron density and flow velocity of the plasma sheath, we deduce the echo model of plasma-sheath-enveloped reentry vehicle. By calculating the relationship between the peak position offset in one-dimension range profile and the flow velocity of scattering point with different radar parameters, we reveal the mechanism of ISAR image displacement on range dimension. Simulations results suggest that the phenomenon of ISAR image displacement can be significantly alleviated by either minimizing the carrier frequency and pulse width or increasing the bandwidth and the echo delay or both.

articleTitle: K-means without K in multi-view SAR clustering
abstract: K-means algorithm realizes clustering through the correlation between data, which is a typical unsupervised algorithm. But the K-means algorithm needs to set the corresponding number of clusters K first, and the accuracy of K greatly affects the performance of the algorithm. In multi-view SAR images, the similarity value of adjacent azimuth images of the same category is higher than the similarity of adjacent azimuth images of the different category. Therefore, the K can be estimated through the relationship between the azimuth angles, and the negative impact of clustering caused by the inaccurate setting of K can be avoided. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a method for estimating the number of clusters K in SAR images based on the similarity relationship of multi-view SAR images. This method simplifies the use of K-means in multi-view SAR images.

articleTitle: Sensitivity analysis for stereo SAR based on the range-Doppler equations
abstract: Stereo synthetic aperture radar (SAR) technique can retrieve the target's high-precision three-dimensional coordinates, which is a promising solution for creating the ground control points. In order to better study the stereo SAR performance influencing factors, a sensitivity analysis method is proposed in this paper. Considering multiple SAR observations are often used in the stereo SAR to improve the localization accuracy, a least square based method is adopted to solve the overdetermined sensitivity equations. Then the stereo SAR localization accuracy sensitivity in terms of the measured error of the range between the radar and the target, the satellite's location and velocity are derived. Furthermore, the impacts of the baseline length and the observation times on the localization accuracy are analyzed based on the proposed sensitivity equations. Finally, some numerical experiments are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Fast ISAR Image Prediction for Targets with Coating Defects Through Deep Learning
abstract: The radar absorbing material (RAM) coating defects existing on the surface of stealth aircraft have important effects on their electromagnetic (EM) scattering characteristics. Considering the complexity and randomness of defects and the large electrical dimension of the platform, it is necessary to analyze their scattering characteristics through a series of complex and time-consuming processes including geometric modeling, meshing, EM simulation, and ISAR imaging, thus cannot meet the requirement of real-time analysis. To address this issue, this paper proposed a novel end-to-end deep neural network (DNN) based on residual U-net, which can perform time-efficient ISAR image prediction of a target with random coating defects from the input 2D geometric map of it. Compared to the method of shooting and bouncing ray (SBR) simulation and range-Doppler (R-D) ISAR imaging, the proposed DNN can accelerate the speed by three orders while ensuring a relative error lower than 1%. Numerical results are exhibited to verify the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Multi-Targets Tracking Association Based on Online Sequential ELM
abstract: With the clutter and dense routes of maneuvering targets such as airplanes, their trajectories are difficult to track and are easily disconnected. In this paper, we propose a method for identifying disconnected trajectories based on Multiple Model Nonlinear Smoothing Gaussian Probability Filtering algorithm (MM-SGM-PHD) and Online Sequential Extreme Learning Machine (OS-ELM), which is fast, accurate, and effectively avoids identifying false tracks as target tracks. First, the MM-SGM-PHD method is proposed to suppress clutter and track multiple targets. Then, based on the Kullback-Leibler divergence, a representative track feature is selected to estimate the disconnected track. Finally, the OS-ELM is employed to train and test the average speed of the track, the average acceleration on the <tex>$x$</tex> and <tex>$y$</tex>-axis, and the distance difference of each segment to determine whether the track segments are the same. Simulation experiments are given to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. Moreover, the proposed method is more suitable for track association engineering applications than traditional tracking and association methods.

articleTitle: An adaptive Enhanced Imaging Method for Multi-aspect SAR
abstract: Compared with traditional SAR working modes, multi-aspect SAR can provide images with higher resolution and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) due to its larger synthetic aperture. However, the SNR does not increase with the increase of the aperture length. This is because the scattering is no longer isotropic as traditional SAR when the viewing angle is large. In this paper, an adaptive enhanced imaging method for multi-aspect SAR is proposed. The resolution and the SNR are maximized by scattering analysis performed simultaneously with imaging. In the process of image generation, the scattering characteristic is analyzed and all targets are divided into two categories: isotropic and anisotropic. Then different image formation strategies are used for isotropic and anisotropic target. A C-band circular SAR data is used to validate our method.

articleTitle: Unimodular Waveform Design With Precise Spectrum Control and Good Correlation Properties
abstract: In this paper, to realize the dynamic spectrum allocation in radar communications coexistence (RCC) system, we focus on the high-quality unimodular waveform design with precise spectrum control and good correlation properties. Our waveform design aims to simultaneously achieve non-conflicting spectrum sharing with ideal power spectral density (PSD) shape and satisfactory auto-correlation level. To achieve this, the difference between actual spectrum shape and ideal template is derived in a weighted least squares (WLS) manner, which is collaboratively optimized with the weighted integrated sidelobe level (WISL) of waveform. A Pareto coefficient of user choice is introduced to make a tradeoff of two objectives. We reformulate the unimodular waveform design into a nonconvex quartic optimization problem in frequency domain. We develop an efficient algorithm by applying the majorization-minimization (MM) twice to derive a closed solution in each iteration. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of our design.

articleTitle: High-Purity Dual-Polarized Leaky-Wave Antenna Based on Complementary Magneto- and Electric-Couplings
abstract: In this paper, complementary magneto- (M-couplings) and electric-couplings (E-couplings) are utilized to design a leaky-wave antenna (LWA) with high-purity dual-linearly polarized radiation. In detail, different excitations are used to effectively distinguish the E-couplings and M-couplings between symmetrical spoof surface plasmon polariton (S-SSPP) transmission lines and the square patch array. During the excitation of the common mode, the M-couplings between the square patch array and the S-SSPP transmission lines superpose each other. However, the cross-polarized radiation generated by the E-couplings cancels each other out. In this case, only the TM<inf>01</inf> mode of the square patch is excited, and the square patch array generates horizontally-polarized (H-pol) waves. Otherwise, when the differential-mode excitation implements, the E-couplings works, and only the TM<inf>10</inf> mode is excited, which make the square patch array radiate vertically-polarized (V-pol) waves. In addition, the cross polarization levels for each polarization state are suppressed at the same time. Simulated results show that the LWA generates H-pol waves with the common mode excitation. In 11.0∽14.8 GHz band, the main beams scan from -34° to +33° with cross polarization levels lower than -45 dB. The maximum gain is 15.2 dBi. When the differential mode excitation works, the scanning range of the V-pol LWA is -51°∽+17° in 10.2∽13.8 GHz band. The maximum gain and cross polarization level are 13.9 dBi and -45 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: The Design of P-L band Digital Antenna Array
abstract: The digital antenna array designed in this paper realized direct generation and sampling of five-octave RF signals based on high speed sampling and multi-channel synchronization. This system uses standard protocol to realize realtime control of array element level parameters, including transmitting power, receiving gain, frequency, waveform and so on. The main features of this array include: supporting direct generation and sampling of RF signals, 64 channels synchronization accuracy less than 20 ps, supporting the parameterized definition of a variety of waveforms, and supporting the parameterized formation of a variety of polarization modes.

Author Keywords: direct generation and sampling of RF signals

articleTitle: A Method for 3-D Imaging of Group Rotating Targets
abstract: In broadband inverse synthetic aperture radar imaging, the rapidly spinning motion introduces intense range cell migration, which can significantly affect the imaging quality. In this paper, we have combined the advantages of particle swarm optimization and matched-filter-bank to achieve high resolution imaging of space debris. For the proposed method, particle swarm optimization is used to perform efficiently parametric search and the matched-filter-bank is used to achieve accurately parameter estimation. The simulation results demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed method under complex conditions.

articleTitle: Weighted Iterative Adaptive Approach for Scanning Radar Imaging
abstract: Iterative adaptive approach (IAA) has been applied to scanning radar imaging to improve the azimuth resolution. However, IAA method suffers from limited resolution improvement in low signal to noise ratio (SNR). In this paper, a weighted IAA method is proposed to enhance the azimuth resolution in low SNR by adjusting the weight of scattering point power. Simulation result illustrates the superior performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Scene-Aware Data Augmentation Method for SAR Ship Detection
abstract: This article presents a scene-aware data augmentation method, known as SADA, for ship detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images. SADA can be aware of ship scenes, and conduct data augmentation selectively. It mainly adopts a classification convolutional neural network (CNN) to discriminate inshore ship scenes and offshore ones. Then, the hard-detected inshore scene samples are augmented, rather than the whole training samples. It is rather useful to improve the detection accuracy of inshore ships. We conduct experiments on the open SSDD dataset, and the results show SADA's effectiveness. SADA is a simple but rather high-beneficial method.

articleTitle: Multiple weak targets detection and tracking integrated processing with time diversity array radar
abstract: In order to solve the problem of detection and tracking of small and weak targets, this paper firstly uses pulse compression and Angle search technology to establish the echo model of time-diversity array radar to multiple targets. Secondly, the target can be detected by setting a high detection threshold with the condition of low SNR. Finally, the Gaussian mixture cardinality balance probability hypothesis density filter is introduced to eliminate the false alarm target, and the accurate position information of the multi-target is obtained. Simulation experiments verify the performance of the proposed method in multi-target detection and tracking under the condition of low SNR.

Author Keywords: cardinality balance prob-ability hypothesis density filter

articleTitle: Range and Velocity Estimation for Multi-symbol OFDM-based Integrated Radar and Communications Systems
abstract: In the integrated radar and communications (IRC) systems, accurate range and velocity estimation results can improve radar detection performance and reduce communication bit error rate. In order to better fit the integrated echo signal based on orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), it is necessary to approximate the terms in the receiving signal as little as possible. This paper first establishes a receiving model of the IRC echo signal, including all terms. Using this model, we propose a least square weighted (LSW) method for range and velocity estimation separately. The proposed method takes the partial derivative of the LSW estimation error with respect to the range term and replaces it. The estimated velocities are substituted into the error to estimate the ranges of the targets. The search space is greatly reduced compared with that in the range-velocity dimension because the spectral peaks are searched in the velocity and range dimensions. Theoretical analysis and simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Multi-frame Sea Clutter Filtering Method based on Image Processing
abstract: Sea clutter filtering plays an import role in weak target detection under sea clutter background. It is difficult to distinguish sea clutter from targets in a single radar frame due to the limited information. Considering the motion of targets, the traditional multi-frame sea clutter filtering methods are complex. Here, a multi-frame filtering method based on image processing is proposed. The image is set up on a single radar frame, and the pixel value is set according to echo features. With image processing, the criterion for sea clutter filtering is proposed. This method is efficient and has a low computational complexity. The simulation and real data analysis results confirm the validity of this method, and its good performance for sea clutter filtering.

articleTitle: TWIST-SBRIM: A Novel Efficient and Robust Approach for Compressive Sensing with Application to SAR Tomography
abstract: Tomography synthetic aperture radar (TomoSAR) realizes 3D imaging by using multi-baseline acquisitions in the elevation direction. And the elevation resolution depends on the elevation aperture. However, in practice, due to the limited track number or non-uniform distribution of the spatial baseline, the elevation resolution of the traditional methods, such as Fourier transform, the back-projection algorithm and spectral estimation is lower. Compressive sensing (CS) methods can achieve high elevation resolution, while often can't guarantee computation efficiency. To address these difficulties, a novel efficient and robust CS algorithm named TWIST-SBRIM is proposed and used for TomoSAR 3D imaging. In this paper, we firstly establish a TomoSAR linear measurement model. Then the TWIST-SBRIM algorithm is used to realize the TomoSAR 3D inversion. Both simulated data and measured data of TerraSAR-X system are used. 3D image reconstruction results show that the proposed method outperforms traditional methods regarding efficiency and accuracy under the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) condition, which proves the validity and practicality of the proposed method.

articleTitle: G-SM-CAM: A Fast Visual Understanding of CNNs in SAR Images Interpretation
abstract: Numerous automatic recognition methods based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) can achieve high calcu-lation efficiency owing to its end-to-end structure. However, the internal mechanism of CNNs is intransparent which is limiting or even disqualifying in SAR image interpretation. To provide a visual understanding of CNNs' mechanism, we propose a Group-Self-Matching class activation mapping (G-SM-CAM) inspired by the split strategy and Self-Matching CAM. In specific, feature maps are firstly “self-matched” with the input image as the renewed feature maps. Then these renewed feature maps are split into several groups. Finally the saliency map can be generated by these sub-feature maps. G-SM-CAM is efficient and effective on SAR images, which runs dramatically faster than Self-Matching CAM at minor cost of saliency map quality. Numerous experimental results demonstrate the validity and efficiency of G-SM-CAM based on a benchmark dataset MSTAR.

articleTitle: Design of a new compact $4\times 4$ Butler matrix for UWB applications
abstract: In this paper, a design of a new compact <tex>$4\times 4$</tex> Butler matrix for UWB applications is presented. The multilayer structure is used to design a drip-shaped coupler, which offers coupling in the range of <tex>$3\pm 1$</tex> dB over an ultra-wide frequency band from 2 to 7 GHz. Based on this, the Butler matrix has good performance in the frequency band from 2 to 7 GHz, the return loss and isolation of each port are greater than 10dB, the transmission coefficient is between −5.5 dB and −8.8 dB, and the phase fluctuation of the output ports is <tex>$\pm 13^{\circ}$</tex>. The structure of this Butler matrix is compact and occupies an area of <tex>$\boldsymbol{90}\ \mathbf{mm} \times \boldsymbol{70}$</tex> mm.

articleTitle: A Method for Estimating Structure parameters of Space Cone Targets based on HRRP sequence
abstract: The difference in structure parameters can be utilized to distinguish different space cone targets effectively. Due to the fact that the high resolution range profile (HRRP) sequence contains the structure and shape information of the observed target, an inversion method for geometrical structure parameters of space cone targets based on the HRRP sequence was proposed in this paper. Firstly, the projected length of the target under different radar line of sight conditions was analyzed. Then, aiming at the problem of a relatively large error of the projected length extracted by the traditional threshold method under the strong noise condition in the actual measurement, a method to estimate the projected length was proposed after extraction of the optimum path by the improved ant colony algorithm. Finally, the generatrix length and the half cone angle were estimated by the triangular fitting. By comparison of the traditional method through simulation, it was demonstrated that the proposed method could still obtain relatively high estimation accuracy of structure parameters under the condition of a comparatively low signal-to-noise ratio.

articleTitle: Cooperative Node Selection and Dwell Time Allocation for Multi-Target Tracking in Multiple Radar Networks with Imperfect Detection Performance
abstract: Current researches on resource management for multi-target tracking (MTT) are mostly studied under an ideal detection environment (IDE). However, since the signal radiation attenuation and random fluctuating of target amplitudes affect target detection, the existing works under IDE are hard to be accomplished. In this paper, a cooperative node selection and dwell time allocation (CNS-DTA) strategy for MTT in multiple radar networks (MRN) with imperfect detection performance is proposed, whose purpose is to effectively minimize the total dwell time while meeting the predetermined MTT accuracy and several system resource budgets. The Bayesian Cramer-Rao lower bound (BCRLB) with imperfect detection performance is derived and used as the performance metric for MTT. Since the CNS-DTA strategy optimization problem is non-convex, a two-step methodology is proposed to solve the formulated optimization problem. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively reduce the total dwell time consumption of MRN with different probabilities of detection.

Author Keywords: cooperative node selection and dwell time allocation (CNS-DTA)

articleTitle: Research On Sliding Spotlight And TOPS SAR Variable PRF Imaging Technology
abstract: Because the traditional single-based spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) cannot receive signals while transmitting signals, there is a defect that high azimuth resolution and wide swath imaging cannot be achieved at the same time. In response to this problem, researchers have proposed the use of variable pulse repetition frequency (PRF) technology to achieve high-resolution wide swath imaging. However, the echo data of the variable PRF SAR will have the problem of sampling at different intervals in the azimuth direction. Using traditional frequency domain algorithms to process the data will cause serious deterioration of the imaging quality, or even imaging; the time domain algorithm can directly focus on the data of the variable PRF, but the amount of calculation is huge. In this paper, we deduced the change rule of PRF and proposed a variable PRF imaging algorithm based on time-frequency scale scaling. A new interpolation method is used to perform uniform sampling of the unambiguous signal in the time domain. Then use the Omega-K algorithm to achieve range cell migration correction (RCMC), and finally focuses the signal in the azimuth frequency domain. The proposed SAR working system with variable PRF is verified by simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Water-based broadband bidirectional metamaterial absorber
abstract: In this paper, a flower-shaped cross water-based broadband bidirectional metamaterial absorber is designed. Simulation result indicates that the absorber achieves electromagnetic absorption of over 90% in the frequency range of 6-28.1GHz, and the relative bandwidth is 129.6%. Additionally, the absorber has the characteristics of polarization insensitivity and wide incident angle. It also has excellent thermal stability, and the absorption efficiency hardly changes in the range of 0-40°C.

articleTitle: Robust Capon Beamforming via Refining Steering Vector Based on Fractional Semidefinite Relaxation
abstract: Robust adaptive beamforming is a very important technique in array processing applications. In this paper, we propose a new design of robust Capon beamformer via refining the signal steering vector. Specifically, with an approximate range of the direction of the signal of interest (SOI) and the norm bound of allowable error on the presumed steering vector, we formulate a novel objective function in the form of quadratic fractional programming. This objective function aims at maximizing the output power of the beamformer and simultaneously focusing the SOI power at the array output as much as possible. Such an objective promotes the estimated steering vector approaching the true one and prevents the estimate converging to the interference subspace. It turns out that the proposed design is a non-convex fractional quadratically constrained quadratic programming problem, which is NP-hard and difficult to solve. We efficiently and exactly solve the problem with the aid of fractional semidefinite relaxation technique. Finally, numerical examples are provided to demonstrate the superiority of the derived beamformer over several existing state-art-of robust adaptive beamformers.

articleTitle: The design and implementation of cooperative surveillance task planning software for regional radar chain
abstract: Aiming at the problem of how regional radar chains can surveil multiple space targets simultaneously in real combat scenarios, this paper brings out an optimized mission planning solution for multi-target tracking with radar resource constraints, and develops regional radar chain collaborative surveillance mission planning software, which integrates functions such as task parameters configuration, planning result output and scene demonstration in the task planning process. Firstly, this paper carries out a secondary development of system tool kit (STK), realizing the call of STK scene simulation and analysis function in the task planning software, and realizes the input of scenario configuration parameters and the output and display of simulation results. Next this paper discussed the task mode and task flow of radar chain cooperative monitoring when the actual combat target is single target or multi-target, carries out 0–1 integer programming modeling for the latter, and automatically finds the optimal solution of the task by using MATLAB intlinprog toolkit. On this basis, the internal information interaction method of the system software is designed, which realizes the process of inputting the scene configuration from the user and generating the scenario configuration file, reading the scenario configuration file by calling STK and performing access analysis to generate the access report file, and inputting the all above files into the MATLAB task planning algorithm, and the process of outputting the planning scheme chart and calling STK for scenario demonstration. Finally, an example of the radar chain monitoring “StarLink” satellites is given to demonstrate the rationality of the result of regional radar chain cooperative surveillance task planning software.

articleTitle: Manmade Target Scattering Structure Null-Pol Recognition and Application
abstract: Target's optimal polarization is the fundamental theory of radar polarization. Null-Pol, also called Co-Pol Null, is one of the significant polarization states, through which other optimal polarization states can be derived. Null-Pol theory is widely applied in polarization reception match, contrast enhancement and so on. This paper revealed the advantage of Null-Pol theory in manmade target scattering structure recognition for the first time. The complex polarization ratio plane and polarization response characteristics were combined and the Null-Pol 3D response patterns were represented, which can reveal the difference of canonical scattering structures. Then, the Null-Pol scattering structure recognition method of manmade targets is proposed. The scattering centers are extracted from radar images. The scattering structure type can be identified by matching the Null-Pol response characteristic vectors with canonical scatters. Through the analysis of electromagnetic computation data of manmade targets, the proposed Null-Pol scattering structure recognition method can identify the scattering structure types of manmade targets. Especially, the results of symmetric targets have better performance than Cameron decomposition, which is more consistent with target's actual scattering structure types.

articleTitle: Target Tracking Based on Separate Modeling of Trajectory Shape and Dynamic Characteristics
abstract: This paper proposes a novel on-road target tracking algorithm based on the separate modeling of target trajectory shape and dynamic characteristics. A description of the target maneuvering behavior in one-dimensional mileage coordinates is given by a mean-adaptive acceleration model. In the absence of prior information about the road, the unknown target trajectory over a sliding window is modeled by third -degree polynomials. The algorithm presented here for on-road maneuvering target tracking based on the separate modeling has been verified through an experiment. Simulation results show that the pro-posed algorithm provides sufficient accuracy compared with existing algorithms with coupled modeling.

articleTitle: Multi-layer Multi-head Self-attention Model for Radar HRRP Target Recognition
abstract: Radar automatic target recognition (RATR) based on high-resolution range profile (HRRP) has attracted much attention in recent years. We present a Multi-head Attention model to characterizes the long-term temporary dependency across the range cells of HRRP, which utilizes stacked attention modules to aggregate features with weights obtained by aligning range cells in a single HRRP, resulting in more discriminative latent representations. We further develop two efficient pooling strategies to obtain the final HRRP representations for the downstream tasks. Experiments on measured data show that the proposed method brings better performance over the corresponding models.

articleTitle: Markov Random Field Model-Based Label Classification Method for High-Resolution SAR Image Recovery
abstract: In the research of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging technology, there is an increasing interest in effectively using prior knowledge to achieve high-resolution images under downsampling conditions. In order to distinguish the target from the background clutter using prior conditions such as target continuity, this paper reconstructs the SAR image based on the Bayesian maximum posterior method. We construct three hidden variables of the scattering point: intensity, label type and distribution parameters, and then estimate the values of the variables. Among them, we assign a Markov prior to the distribution of label type, and design the energy function of the Markov model to encourage the continuity of labels and distinguish the influence of different neighbors. Simulations validate the proposed method, and the results show that the method can effectively correct the discontinuity of the prior label distribution and eventually iterate to recover a continuous target.

articleTitle: Microwave system of phased array radar based on multi-level blind matching technology
abstract: With the development of semiconductor technology, microwave technology, computer technology and considering the complex electromagnetic environment during RF operation of the phased array radar system, the microwave system is facing new opportunities and challenges. A microwave system based on multi-level blind matching technology is proposed in this paper. It has the advantages and characteristics of high integration, small size, light weight and high reliability. It can be widely used in small phased array radar system.

articleTitle: Research on Embedded SAR Target Recognition for Remote Sensing Application
abstract: With rapid development and wide application of high-resolution SAR (synthetic aperture radar) for commercial remote sensing, the on-board intelligent target recognition is expected. In this paper, the embedded AI module is designed, which has the advantages of small size, low power consumption, light weight and convenient connection. Then the YOLOv3-Spp deep neural network model is proposed and transplanted to the module, which has high detection accuracy and strong generalization ability. The experimental results show that the method is effective for remote sensing applications.

articleTitle: Design of an Ultra-Wide-Band Polarization Selective Reflectarray
abstract: A novel ultra-wide-band polarization selective reflectarray by using true-time delay is presented in this paper. Tightly coupled elements and the method of true-time-delay are used to broaden the bandwidth of the reflectarray. The reflectarray has the advantages of large bandwidth, polarization selective, and reduced complexity and fabrication cost. A reflectarray with the elements arranged in a <tex>$41\times 41$</tex> grid is designed and simulated operating from 6 to 32GHz. The measured results show that the reflectarray has stable radiation patterns from 6 to 32GHz, over 5:1 frequency range and has a low loss and high efficiency over 60 %, it also has the low cross polarization below −28dB across the entire band and has the function of polarization selectivity.

articleTitle: A Novel Image Domain Method of Suppressing Moving Target Interference for the Azimuth Multi-Channel SAR
abstract: Combined with digital beamforming technology, azimuth multi-channel SAR can be used to achieve high-resolution wide-range imaging. However, the moving target in the imaging scene cannot be reconstructed well to obtain its unambiguous azimuth spectrum. Therefore, in the final imaging result, the moving target is defocused and there are multiple ambiguity points along the azimuth, which affects the original ground scene. Target. Using traditional space-time adaptive processing methods to suppress moving targets in images, the degree of spatial freedom is often difficult to satisfy in actual operations. In order to solve this problem, this paper proposes a moving target suppression method based on the multi-channel SAR image domain. Since the moving target is partially focused in the SAR image, different steering vectors can be used at different moving target positions. Reduce the need for space freedom. Finally, simulations verify the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Noise suppression of ISAR micro cluster targets based on Generated Adversarial Network
abstract: When the inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) is used to detect micro cluster target in the air, the noise in the detection process will seriously affect the range profile resolution of the cluster target. Especially when each target in the cluster target is close to each other, the noise will cause the signal of the cluster target to be difficult to identify, and the imaging quality will be greatly reduced. Therefore, it is very necessary to design an algorithm to improve the signal-to-noise ratio of the cluster target signal. This paper combines the generative adversarial network to suppress the noise of the micro cluster target detected by ISAR, and the measured data after pulse compression are added to the optimization process of neural network. The simulation method will be used to generate training data. This method improves the targets' range profile resolution to a certain extent by processing the measured data and effectively suppresses the background noise.

articleTitle: Fast Space-Time Adaptive Processing for Clutter Suppression in Airborne Radar with Coprime Arrays under Gain and Phase Errors
abstract: The clutter suppression problem with space-time adaptive processing (STAP) for coprime arrays in presence of gain and phase (GP) errors is considered. More precisely, the proposed algorithm firstly formulates the virtual space-time signal model for the signal observed by the coprime arrays with GP errors. Then, the clutter spectrum and array GP errors estimation are formulated as a joint optimization problem based on the clutter sparsity and a fast method is derived to solve the resultant optimization problem based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Finally, the virtual covariance matrix can be estimated using the clutter spectrum and GP errors estimates and the conventional STAP filters can be directly applied. Simulation examples are provided to demonstrate its effectiveness and show low complexity than existing sparsity-based STAP algorithms for coprime arrays.

articleTitle: Baseline design for GEO SAR tomography in the presence of squint
abstract: GEO SAR (Geosynchronous Synthetic Aperture Radar) has great potential for SAR tomography applications because it can obtain large amounts of data from the same scene due to the advantage of one-day revisit time. In this paper, we analyze the performance index of GEO SAR tomography in squint mode, and design the orbital elements of satellites at different inclination angles according to the performance requirements. The results show that the squint mode does not affect the perpendicular baseline of GEO SAR, but it can lead to the decrease of ambiguous height. GEO SAR tomography can be realized by adjusting the semi-major axis. The higher the inclination, the greater the adjustment amount of the semi-major axis.

articleTitle: Real Data Imaging Approach Design for Automotive SAR Experiments
abstract: In this paper, the potential of applying synthetic aperture radar (SAR) in automotive filed has been demonstrated by using a vehicle-mounted 77GHz Frequency Modulation Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar. An improved Range Doppler Algorithm (RDA), which is ideal for focusing serious range curvatures of targets at short ranges, has been presented in this work to produce high-resolution SAR images of automotive scenarios. The first part of this paper gives a detailed model of vehicle-mounted SAR system and the problems caused by the unique characteristics of model has been analyzed.
