In the latter part, the processing flow of the proposed novel RD algorithm based on range partition is presented, which, compared to the traditional RD algorithm, performs well in automotive SAR imaging. The imaging result of real scene is presented to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design Method of Radar Human-Computer Interaction Software Based on MBSE
abstract: Aiming at the shortcomings of the traditional development mode of radar human-computer interaction (HCI) software in terms of design efficiency and design quality, through the study of model-based systems engineering (MBSE), a model-based radar HCI software development mode is proposed. Discusses the purpose and importance of introducing prototype design into MBSE, gives the method of encapsulating various interactive elements required in the process of prototype design into radar HCI domain model library to realize rapid reuse, and the method associated with MBSE's requirements management tool DOORS, and also gives the method of automatically generating code based on prototype, combined with examples, the process of integrating the model to construct a HCI virtual prototype is given. Practice has shown that the design method of radar HCI software based on MBSE can effectively improve the work efficiency and work quality of designers, and is of great significance to improving the professionalism, standardization and advancement of radar HCI design.

articleTitle: Ground Moving Targets Velocity Estimation based on Shadow and Target Detection
abstract: THz radar has the advantages of short synthetic aperture time and fast imaging velocity, and performs realtime imaging of ground moving targets. Therefore, it is possible to use the shadow and target information in SAR images to estimate the velocity of ground moving targets. In this paper, shadow detection and target detection are introduced to estimate the moving targets velocity respectively, and the results are compared between the two methods. In the experiments, the measured data of THz radar is applied to estimate the velocity of moving targets. The results show that the estimation method based on shadow detection is robust, and the method based on target detection has high estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: The application of Triangle Wave Signal in UAV SAR imaging
abstract: In the field of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) synthetic aperture radar (SAR), frequency modulation continuous wave (FMCW) signal is commonly used. Compared with sawtooth wave, symmetric triangular modulation wave offers a unique opportunity to focus image for each pulse cycle, which includes up-ramp chirp and down-ramp chirp. However, when the observed scene is stationary, the radial motion of platform during the beam round trip time will also result in a Doppler effect. By extracting this Doppler frequency shift during up chirp and down chirp periods, both the range and velocity of antenna phase center (APC) can be determined. Based on this characteristic, this paper describes a new application of symmetric triangular linear FMCW in motion estimation for SAR imagery. Simulation results validate the proposed method.

Author Keywords: symmetric triangular linear frequency modulation continuous wave

articleTitle: Transmitters Selection in Distributed MIMO Radar Network with Partially Correlated Signals
abstract: In this paper, we consider a problem of transmitters selection for parameter estimation in a distributed multi-input multi-output (MIMO) radar network. Waveforms of the transmitters in the radar network are assumed to be partially correlated. The estimation performance is characterized by the inverse of Fisher information matrix (FIM) as Cramér Rao lower bound. Different from those transmitters with orthogonal waveforms, the non-orthogonality of probing signals leads to the non-diagonal structure of the FIM. Owing to this fact, the seeking of optimal subset of transmitters is formulated as a sensor selection problem with correlated measurement noise. To efficiently address nonconvex integer programming problem, we propose and verify a novel equivalent relaxation. Using the bi-convexity of proposed surrogate problem, the suboptimal solution is numerically calculated by a algorithm based on nonlinear alternating direction method of multipliers. Simulation results are presented to assess the effectiveness and reveal the superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Robust Nonlinear Filter for Doppler Radar Target Tracking
abstract: The smooth variable structure filter (SVSF) offers robust state estimation in the presence of model uncertainty but requires a linear measurement model and a full-rank measurement matrix. Doppler radar reports target position and range rate in the polar or spherical coordinates without tangential velocity, leading to a nonlinear and underdetermined measurement model in Cartesian coordinates and thus precluding the use of the standard SVSF. In this paper, a novel robust estimator, referred to as the sequential smooth variable structure filter (SSVSF), is proposed for Doppler radar target tracking. The Doppler radar measurement vector is partitioned into two parts, i.e., the position (containing range, azimuth, and elevation) and the range rate, and is used for a two-stage sequential processor. In the first stage, the target position measurement is transformed into Cartesian coordinates via the unbiased converted measurement (UCM) strategy, so that a generalized SVSF is implemented for robust target state estimation with a linear measurement model. In the second stage, a pseudo measurement is constructed from the product of range and range rate, and accordingly, an approximate linear minimum mean square error (LMMSE) estimator is developed to update the first-stage estimation. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in Doppler radar tracking, and superior robustness to the conventional nonlinear Bayesian filter in the case of target motion uncertainty.

articleTitle: Target Detection based on Two-dimensional Fractal Property under Sea Clutter Background
abstract: To overcome the shortages of the traditional target detection method based on a statistical model, this paper concentrate on the fractal property of sea clutter and its application on target detection. Since the complex properties of sea clutter, it is hard to detect targets based on a single fractal parameter. Therefore, this paper analyzed the two-dimensional fractal properties of sea clutter, where the box-counting dimension and fractal model fit error of autoregressive (AR) spectrum are treated as the feature inputs for target detector. Then, real measured S-band sea clutter datasets are taken to analyze the two-dimensional property of sea clutter and several datasets are taken to test the performance of the detection method. Finally, from the analysis of real sea clutter datasets, the proposed method based on two-dimensional fractal property has a better detection performance than the traditional CFAR method and existing fractal methods.

articleTitle: A Spread Sea Clutter Suppression Method Based on Prior Knowledge for HF Hybrid Sky-Surface Wave Radar
abstract: In this paper, a spread sea clutter suppression method based on prior knowledge & joint domain localized (JDL) algorithm is proposed. Firstly, the internal mechanism and characteristics of the broadening sea clutter based on the detection principle of HF hybrid sky-surface wave radar are studied deeply and carefully in this paper. Secondly, the broadening first-order sea clutter model for HF hybrid sky-surface wave radar is established. Eventually, based on the preceding established broadening sea clutter model and characteristics, the techniques to suppress the broadening sea clutter are studied. The research in this paper will provide the theory and technology foundation to detect the target over the horizon under the broadening sea clutter in HF hybrid sky-surface wave radar.

articleTitle: GAF-MN: A New HRRP Target Recognition Method Based on Gramian Angular Field and Matching Networks in Few-Shot Condition
abstract: Radar high resolution range profiles(HRRP) can provide lots of useful information for radar automatic target recognition(RATR). Recently HRRP based RATR methods adopting deep neural networks have achieved promising performance because of their strong generalization ability. However, these deep models usually need lots of training samples to optimize the parameters, otherwise they would possibly encounter serious overfitting problem in few-shot condition. In this paper, a novel HRRP few-shot recognition method named gramian angular field matching networks(GAF-MN) is proposed to solve the above problems. In the proposed method, a gramian angular field(GAF) technique is adopted to transform the one-dimensional HRRPs to two-dimensional GAF images without any information lost. Further more, the single-channel matching networks is designed to fit the one-dimensional statistical HRRP data. The experimental results demonstrated that the proposed method improved the recognition accuracy and generalization performance in few-shot condition. The proposed method achieved improved performance on an airplane electromagnetic calculation dataset compared with traditional deep learning methods.

articleTitle: SAR Image Low Scattering Region Extraction Based on Multi-module Fusion Network
abstract: This paper presents a multi-module fusion network (MMFNet) for the extraction of low scattering regions such as shadows, waters, and roads in SAR images. MMFNet consists of high-resolution backbone network module, spatial pyramid pooling convolution module, and channel attention module. Specifically, the high-resolution backbone network maintains high resolution of feature maps and reduces spatial accuracy loss, which is conducive to the extraction of edge information. Spatial pyramid pooling convolutional module performs multi-scale feature fusion, extracts target areas with different sizes and improves network accuracy. Channel attention module is able to enhance network expression of category information, thus further improve network performance. Our experimental analysis using real SAR data shows that MMFNet achieves state-of-the-art low scattering region extraction, with mean IoU (MIoU) reaching 82.49%.

articleTitle: A spaceborne SAR echo simulation and imaging method based on fixed range delay
abstract: Spaceborne SAR payload test on the ground is an important method to evaluate the On-orbit performance of the satellite, with the massive increase of the sampling data of the geosynchronous orbit SAR, the demand for the efficiency and simplify the test system is gradually growing. In this paper, a novel method for the echo simulation and imaging for the SAR payload test on the ground with a fixed delay echo signal is proposed, which can greatly shorten the test time and improve the test efficiency. The experimental results show that this method can realize the evaluation of point target imaging results for the real echo of GEO SAR with a fixed delay test system. It has high practical value for the SAR payload test.

articleTitle: Measurement of surface traveling wave attenuation characteristics for absorbing materials under high temperatures
abstract: Measurement and processing techniques for testing the attenuation performance of absorbing materials under high temperatures are proposed in this work. Based on the principles of near-field test of target radar cross section (RCS), a high temperature test facility with low scattering clutter is constructed. Time-domain gating through software processing is applied to further eliminate the possible clutter resulting from the high temperature test environment. The measurement uncertainty of surface traveling wave attenuation is improved using the near-field-to-far-field transformation (NFFFT) method that transforms the near-field RCS data into far-field counterpart. Both calibration spheres and different absorbing materials are tested using the constructed high temperature test facility with high accuracy, demonstrating the validity and usefulness of the proposed techniques.

articleTitle: Ground stationary target detection method for airborne wide-band radar based on statistical characteristics
abstract: Effective ground stationary operational target detection is the precondition of subsequent target identification for helicopter-borne fire-controlled radar. More abundant target information could be obtained when adopting wide-band radar than traditional narrow-band one. While there exit such problem of high false alarm and poor adaptability when applying traditional detection methods. Thus, a novel ground stationary target detection method for airborne wide-band radar based on statistical characteristic is presented in this paper. By considering statistical distribution property in both range and azimuth directions, this method could distinguish the target from strong ground clutter background adaptively and effectively. Experiment results show that our algorithm not only can improve detection performance significantly but also could enhance processing efficiency.

articleTitle: Parameter Estimation of Layered Media Based on GPR Time-Frequency Spectrum Inversion
abstract: Conventional ground-penetrating radar (GPR) has limitations in estimating the dielectric properties of individual layers of multi-layer media. In this work, we propose a new inversion method based on the time-frequency spectrum to address this problem. First, the time-domain reflected signal is reconstructed using the generalized reflection coefficient. Then, the actual reflected signal is analyzed in the time-frequency domain by using the wavelet transform, and the reflection time delays of the layered interfaces are determined. Finally, an improved cost function is optimized by using the genetic algorithm (GA) to obtain the inversion parameters. The accuracy and anti-noise capability of the method is validated by the simulation data generated using gprMax software.

articleTitle: Mainlobe Interference Suppression Method Based on Coprime Array
abstract: When combating multiple mainlobe interferences in space, the traditional interference suppression methods based on eigen-projection have the problems of model mismatch and mainlobe distortion. In order to solve the above problems, a mainlobe interference suppression method based on coprime array is proposed. In the proved method, the signal covariance matrix of the virtual uniform array is constructed according to the observation vector, and the angles and powers of all incident signals are estimated by Capon spectrum. Then, the reconstructed interference plus noise covariance matrix is used to construct the corresponding subspace, and the component of mainlobe interferences is suppressed by eigen-projection. Finally, the reconstructed sidelobe interference plus noise covariance matrix is used to calculate the adaptive weight vector to form an ideal beam pattern. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Oriented Ship Target Detection Based on Improved CenterNet in Synthetic Aperture Radar Images
abstract: Deep learning has a wide application prospects in the field of the ship target detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images. The existing researches mainly use anchor-based target detection method, but this kind of methods is not suitable for the ship SAR image with the sparse ship targets. It requires additional computational resources to filter out a large number of overlapped candidate prediction boxes, which tends to result in the inaccurate target position and low detection efficiency. At the same time, most of existing methods use the horizontal box to detect the ship targets, which are not suitable for detecting the large aspect ratio ship targets and densely arranged ship targets. Aiming at the problem of the insufficient data, a data augmentation strategy for the ship SAR images is proposed, which effectively alleviates the problem of over-fitting during training, improves the detection performance and stability of the model. Then, an oriented ship target detection method is presented for the SAR images, which extends the CenterNet to the field of the rotating target detection. Compared with the existing ship detection method of the SAR images based on the deep learning, this method is very easy to implement, has the high detection precision and positioning accuracy, which has been conducive to the ship detection in practice.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional DOA Estimation Based on Reweighted Decoupled Atomic Norm Minimization
abstract: In this paper, the reweighting strategy is introduced into the decoupled atomic norm minimization(DANM) algorithm to obtain the reweighted decoupled atomic norm minimization(RDANM) algorithm. The algorithm can automatically obtain the order of the model on the basis of maintaining the excellent characteristics of the original algorithm, and improve the resolution of the angle estimation. Therefore, applying it to two-dimensional direction of arrival(DOA) estimation can not only obtain efficient calculation efficiency, but also have higher angle estimation resolution without the model order as a priori information.

articleTitle: Feature Selection and Recognition Based on SAR Image
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image feature selecting can effectively reduce the data dimension of subsequent processing through feature extraction and selection based on a small number of sample images, thereby reduce the complexity of subsequent processing and the workload in the process of feature extraction for a large number of images. In this paper, a method composed of feature difference analysis and Relief algorithm is proposed to select the features. The proposed method is called D-Relief method. Then support vector machine (SVM) is utilized to verify the influence of different feature selection methods on the classification results. The experimental results show that the proposed D-Relief method can further reduce the dimension of feature vector and ensure the performance of classifier.

articleTitle: Process Noise Adaptive Kalman Filtering with Stein Variational Gradient Descent
abstract: Adaptive Kalman filtering has become a widely used state estimation method when the system noise statistics are not available a priori. In this article, we consider the application of Stein variational gradient descent (SVGD) in adaptive Kalman filtering for the linear Gaussian state-space model with inaccurate process noise statistics. The proposed algorithm separately estimates the system state and noise parameters with the Kalman filter and SVGD online inference. Compared to the existing state-of-the-art adaptive Kalman filters, the proposed method can approximate the noise statistics better and thus provides higher state estimation accuracy, which is confirmed by the simulation results on a target tracking example.

articleTitle: A Long Synthetic Aperture Passive Localization Method Using Two Planes
abstract: A long synthetic aperture passive localization algorithm is proposed in this paper. First of all, the Doppler change rate of signal can be measured by the image contrast and then, grid points are divided within the maximum possible latitude and longitude of the emitter location, the Doppler change rate at each grid point can be calculated by using known position and velocity of the receiver. The grid points at which the calculated Doppler change rate is equal to the value measured by the received signal form an isoline. Two receivers can draw two isolines on the ground and the intersection of the isolines gives estimate of the emitter location.

articleTitle: Cognitive Transmit Nulling Beamforming via Manifold Optimization Approach
abstract: In this paper, we deal with the design of the constant modulus weight vector in an effort to achieving a desired transmit beampattern with the nulling in the spatial of interest. The design model is formulated accounting for maximizing the ratio of the mainlobe level to the weighted integrated sidelobe level in the presence of the constant modulus restriction. To handle the resulting non-convex (in general NP-hard) problem, an iterative approach resorting to the complex circle manifold is proposed. By deriving Riemannian gradient and retraction operator, each iteration of the proposed algorithm invokes the Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (BFGS) in complex circle manifold instead of Euclidean space to ensure the monotonic increase of the objective function. Finally, numerical examples are provided to verify the capability of manifold optimization approach over some counterparts.

articleTitle: Novel Interferometric Radar for Railway Overhead Catenary Dynamic Telemetry
abstract: The overhead catenary is a vital subsystem of a high-speed train. We proposed an Interferometric radar-based catenary non-contact offline measurement technique. The Interferometric radar adopts the linear frequency modulation continuous wave technique, a dechirp receiver, the pulse compression technique, and the time differential displacement measuring technique. We design a dynamic catenary parameter measuring method with one radar according to geometry and radar backscattering property of overhead catenary. A real catenary measuring experiment was conducted on the Jing-Guang railway line in Changsha. The dynamic wire lift can be directly measured from the displacement curve. The bearing force can be calculated from the fundamental frequency which is obtained by the Fourier transform of the displacement curve. The two parameters are required catenary parameters in railway technique regulation. Experiment results demonstrate that the proposed remote non-contact measuring method is accurate, efficient, and easy to operate and deploy.

Author Keywords: linear frequency modulation continuous wave radar

articleTitle: Radar HRRP Target Recognition Based on an ADAM-CNN with Side-Information
abstract: High-resolution range profile (HRRP) holds great potential for radar automatic target recognition (RATR) owing to its capability of providing target structure information and spatial scattering information. In recent years, an increasing number of deep learning methods are proposed to improve recognition performance of HRRP. However, these data-driven models still cannot solve some fundamental problems in RATR, such as small sample problem and low SNR problem. Inspired by the idea of knowledge-driven model, a new model combining adaptive domain knowledge and attention mechanism based on convolutional neural network (ADAM-CNN) is proposed in this work. In the proposed model, domain knowledge is introduced to the convolutional module as side-information (SI) to guide the mode make full use of the prior information of the target introduced by domain knowledge, and construct data distribution mapping between training and testing phase to overcome small sample problem and low SNR problem. Then, Attention mechanism is introduced by convolutional block attention module (CBAM) to guide the model focus on the range cells with more target scattering information by capturing global information of HRRP, so as to further reduce the dependence of the proposed model on the number of training samples. Experimental results prove that ADAM-CNN model has a good ability to prevent overfitting in small sample and has a good noise-resisted performance.

articleTitle: Preliminary Analysis of PolInSAR Scattering Mechanism in Urban Areas through UAV-borne PolInSAR System
abstract: Polarimetric Interferometric SAR (PolInSAR) can improve the coherence of images and it plays an important role in urban remote sensing. The explanation of its scattering mechanism is concerned by many researchers. It is always explained from the aspect of different polarization decompositions but seldom from the height of scattering centers. In this paper, a Ku-band UAV-borne PolInSAR system is used to compare the relationship of scattering centers between PolInSAR and Pauli decomposition on different artificial targets. The physical meaning of PolInSAR is preliminary analyzed and our conclusion is also verified through a C-band manned airborne PolInSAR system.

articleTitle: Polarimetric ISAR Image Interpretation Based on Polarimetric Correlation Pattern
abstract: Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) plays an important role in man-made target observation, especially in space surveillance. Polarimetric ISAR can acquire full polarimetric information of radar targets, which receives great attention. In this paper, the hidden information in polarimetric rotation domain along the radar's line of sight has been explored by the means of polarimetric correlation pattern. The core idea is to expand the correlation value of two channels acquired at a fixed angle to the rotation domain along the radar's line of sight. Totally four independent polarimetric correlation patterns are derived. Theoretical analysis indicates that the polarimetric correlation pattern various a lot for different canonical structures. Experimental studies with simulated data reveal the potential of polarimetric correlation pattern on man-made target interpretation.

articleTitle: Human Respiration Signal Extraction Based on Multi-singular-spectrum-analysis
abstract: Non-contact human life signal extraction is widely used in civil and military applications. In this paper, a method based on multi-singular-spectrum-analysis (MSSA) is proposed to extract human respiration signal from random body movement. Firstly, the human respiration and random body movement model is established. Then, the procedures of separating respiration movement and random body movement based on MSSA is introduced. Finally, the proposed method is validated by experimental results.

articleTitle: Sea Clutter Modeling and Spectrum Analysis for Airframe Conformal Array
abstract: Conformal array has advantages of small aircraft load, small air friction and large effective aperture. When the airborne radar observes the land or sea, the echoes will be induced to influence the moving target detection. In view of the advantages of the conformal array, the sea clutter model and suppression for airframe conformal radar are first studied in this paper. The spatial steer vector of conformal array and sea clutter decorrelation matrix are used to model the conformal array sea clutter echoes. The eigen spectrum and space-time spectrum under different sea states show that conformal array non-linear structure has a large influence on the clutter spectrum. At the same time, an effective gain weight is proposed to decrease the broadening of the sea clutter spectrum to improve the moving target detection performance. The simulation results demonstrate the good sea clutter suppression performance for airframe conformal array.

articleTitle: Signal structure information-based data association for maneuvering targets with a convolutional Siamese network
abstract: Traditional data association methods usually suffer performance degradation caused by model mismatch when target maneuvers occur. In addition, the signal structure information (SSI) available from the employed signal processing techniques is rarely used in data association due to the lack of appropriate tools. To overcome the model mismatch problem brought by the target maneuvers, we resort to a data driven method to design the data association algorithm. To make full use of the SSI, a convolutional neural network is used to transform the SSI into a feature space, where the similarity of the SSI between two observations can be calculated using the Euclidean distance. The resulting structure is the convolutional Siamese network (CSN). By comparing the similarity with a predetermined margin parameter, the decision about association can be made. Simulation results are presented to show that the use of SSI in the designed CSN can improve the association probability of maneuvering targets.

articleTitle: The Low Cost DOA estimation Method for LSS-Target via Intelligent Reflecting Surface System and Deep Neural Network
abstract: Detection and localization LSS (Low altitude, Slow speed and Small) targets, having become a cosmopolitan difficult problem and studying hotspot. To address this challenge, a direction of arrival (DOA) estimation method in intelligent reflecting surface(IRS) with low-cost ADC is first investigated in this paper. We propose a deep neural network (DNN) as recovery method for the low-resolution sampled signal, which can estimates the quantization noise caused by the ADC accurately. Then, the denoised signal is utilized to improve the DOA estimation, and the recovery performance for the quantized signal is evaluated by DOA estimation. Simulation results show that, the better reconstruction performance is achieved by the proposed network than existing denoising method under the same training conditions. Through comparison with state-of-the-art methods, DNN shows a better denoising effect. Combined with DNN denoising, the performance of the DOA estimation with 1-bit ADC outperforms existing 2-bit ADC systems.

articleTitle: Waveform Design for MIMO Radar with Consistent Correlation Phase
abstract: Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) radar provides additional degrees of freedom (DOFs) by emitting orthogonal waveforms at transmit channels compared to the phase array radar. Therefore, ideal orthogonal waveforms ensure the performance of transmit channels diversity which directly affects the parameter estimation performance of MIMO radar system. In this paper, the mechanism of existing non-ideal orthogonal waveforms affecting MIMO radar target estimation is described. Furthermore, we propose an consistent correlation phase criterion that make the phase sequences of correlation function between different waveforms basically consistent. The orthogonal waveforms with consistent correlation phase cause lower sidelobe in transmit spatial frequency domain during spectrum estimating of target.

articleTitle: Shelter effect analysis of wind barrier on large radio telescope
abstract: With the development of radio telescopes to large aperture, high frequency and high precision, the fitting accuracy of the reflector can be deteriorated by the time-varying wind load, leading to the reduction of the telescope performance. Therefore, wind load is an unneglectable environmental factor affecting the telescope. In this paper, the feasibility of designing a wind barrier in front of the telescope to reduce the wind disturbance on the telescope is discussed, and the effect of wind barrier size parameters on reducing the wind disturbance is analyzed through orthogonal experiments. The numerical simulation indicates that the wind barrier can effectively reduce the wind pressure on the reflector surface. Orthogonal experiments suggest that the height of the wind barrier is the most significant factor affecting the shelter effect, while the width of the wind barrier ranks the second, and the length of the wind barrier has the least effect.

articleTitle: Aircraft Detection by a Ground-based Passive Interferometric Microwave Sensor (PIMS)
abstract: The critical advantage of passive microwave imaging is that it can be used in all-day and in low visibility conditions, such as haze, fog, clouds, smoke, and sandstorms. In this paper, the ground-based passive interferometric microwave sensor (PIMS) is proposed to detect the aircraft, especially in low visibility conditions. The brightness temperature (TB) model of the aircraft detected by PIMS is analyzed and established using the ray-tracing method. A detection algorithm is proposed for the aircraft detected by PIMS. Experiments are performed to verify the craft detection algorithm and demonstrate the feasibility of the aircraft detected by PIMS. Experimental results have demonstrated the feasibility of the aricraft can be effectively detected by the ground-based PIMS.

articleTitle: SE-Based Optimal Power Allocation Strategy for Cognitive MIMO Radar Against Jammer Interference
abstract: Cognitive radar system capable of complex and volatile external environment by sensing and adaptive adjustment transponder system to adapt to the current environment. In this paper, the cognitive MIMO radar power allocation strategy is considered with a smart jammer present. Radar strives to improve detection efficiency, while jammer maximizes its jamming effect. Hence Stackelberg Game is modeled to solve the countermeasures using MMSE as the utility function. The proposed SE-PSO algorithm obtain the optimal power allocation strategy at Stackelberg equilibrium. Simulation result prove the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Domain Adaptation Based Multi-Source Data Fusion for Pattern Classification
abstract: Multi-source Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (MUDA) is an important and challenging research topic for target classification with the assistance of labeled data in source domains. When we have several labeled source domains, it is hard to map all source domains and target domain into a common feature space for well classifying the targets. A new Progressive Multi-Source Domain Adaptation Network (PMSDAN) is proposed to further improve the classification performance. PMSDAN mainly consists of two steps for distribution alignment. Firstly, the multiple source domains are integrated as one auxiliary domain to match the distribution with the target domain. In order to mine as much as possible assistance knowledge from each source domain, the distribution of the target domain will be separately aligned with that of each source domain. Finally, a weighted fusion method is employed to combine the multiple classification results for making the final classification decision. In the optimization of domain adaption, Weighted Hybrid Maximum Mean Discrepancy (WHMMD) is proposed, and it considers both the inter-class and intra-class Discrepancy. The experiments show that the proposed method can obtain remarkable results for MUDA on public benchmark dataset compared to some state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Cluster Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Electromagnetic Calculations and Applications
abstract: The paper analyses the electromagnetic scattering calculation of a typical fixed-wing UAV target “Gremlin” from the perspective of aerial target detection and tracking, using the Multilevel Fast Multi-pole Method for the calculation of electro-magnetic scattering of “Gremlin” in single and cluster situations, and the calculation results are verified by an inverse synthetic aperture radar imaging method. Through the above research and analysis, the electromagnetic scattering characteristics and imaging laws of the relevant targets are summarised, so that the detection and tracking effects of radar on such UAV targets can be more realistically simulated.

articleTitle: A Spatial Variant Phase Compensation Algorithm for Bistatic ISAR Imaging of Maneuvering Targets Based on Optimal Parameter Estimation
abstract: When imaging a maneuvering target with complex three-dimensional (3-D) non-uniform rotational motion, the traditional range Doppler (RD) algorithm for bistatic inverse synthetic aperture radar (Bi-ISAR) will fail due to the presence of phase errors. Moreover, due to the time-varying property of the imaging projection plane (IPP), the phase errors are two-dimensional (2-D) spatial variant. In order to deal with these problems, we propose a spatial variant phase compensation (SVPC) method based on parametric minimun entropy optimization to compensate for the 2-D spatial variant phase errors. The main contribution of the proposed method is to give an accurate expression of the 2-D spatial variant model and optimally compensate the 2-D spatial variant phase errors in the Bi-ISAR configuration. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Recognition of Space Target Based on GNN under the Condition of Small Samples for ISAR Image
abstract: With the development of space science and technology and the increasing demand for space monitoring, high-precision recognition technology of space targets has become more and more important. Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) is an effective means of space detection, with the advantages of all-weather and high resolution. In recent years, there have been more and more techniques for applying deep learning methods to ISAR image recognition. However, for non-cooperative space targets, the lateral resolution of ISAR images is difficult to determine, and due to factors such as speckle noise and interference fringes, the quality of ISAR images will decrease to varying degrees. Therefore, the number of effective ISAR images obtained for the target is very small. This paper uses graph neural network (GNN) to find the deep relationship between similar samples by calculating the adjacency matrix between graph data nodes to realize small-sample recognition. Experimental results show that under the same conditions, the recognition rate of this method is about 10% higher than that of the CNN method with 20 times the sample size, which proves that this method can improve the reliability of spatial target recognition and has practical value.

articleTitle: RFI Extraction for Synthetic Aperture Radar in 2D Domain Based on Low Rank and Sparsity Property
abstract: Radio frequency interference (RFI) is a core issue of synthetic aperture radar (SAR), which significantly reduces the signal-to-noise ratio of SAR echo and image interpretation accuracy. Therefore, RFI mitigation plays an important role in the SAR imaging. Based on the azimuth echo analysis, some methods based on low rank characteristic or sparsity are introduced to reconstruct RFI and recover target echo signal. However, the property of RFI described in these models is not accurate enough, and there is a large signal loss problem. In this paper, an interference extracted algorithm is introduced for SAR data based on low rank and sparsity property. Via the measured SAR data analysis, a separation optimization model is established joint the low rank characteristic for RFI and sparsity assumption for the target echo signal. And the optimization problem can be solved iteratively by bilateral random projection and soft threshold mapping. Meanwhile, the mask procession is used to constrain the location of RFI in 2-dimensional domain to improve the reconstruction accuracy. Finally, the RFI mitigation experiments of the measured SAR data verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Landslide Detection using Interferometric Coherence of Different Polarization Configurations
abstract: With the continuous development of Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) technology, its application in landslide detection has become more and more extensive. Due to the occurrence of landslides, the diffusion of landslide soil often buries and destroys the original landform, changing the surface scattering mechanism in the disaster area; the displacement of landslide soil often causes changes in ground elevation. These changes will reduce the coherence of the landslide area. This paper focuses on landslide detection using interferometric coherence of different polarization-configuration images of a full-polarization Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR). The coherence maps of the two study sites are obtained by the pre-and post-landslide images of ALOS-2/PALSAR and then the landslides' decoherence of different polarization configurations (HH, HV/VH, and VV) is discussed. As a result, the HH and VV coherence maps could better reflect the changes of landslides than that of HV/VH, and VV coherence map offers the best description of the landslide area compared with the other two polarization configurations.

articleTitle: A Moving Target Detection Method for Airborne Multichannel Circular SAR Based on Post-Doppler STAP
abstract: As a new observation mode, circular synthetic aperture radar (CSAR) overcomes the limitation of traditional linear SAR. It can observe the fixed area for a long time and achieve moving target tracking. In 2021, The Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences (AIRCAS) carried out the airborne digital array SAR experiment. In this paper, the system is briefly introduced and the sub-aperture post-Doppler space-time adaptive processing (PD-STAP) is adopted to process the data. The training data play an important role in the applications of the PD-STAP. Herein, the generalized inner product (GIP) test is utilized in the space-Doppler domain to eliminate the inappropriate training data. Moreover, considering the partially homogeneous environment, a segmented estimation method of clutter covariance matrix (CCM) along the range direction is proposed, which improves the accuracy of the CCM, and a multi-thread PD-STAP implementation based on Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) parallelization is designed. These have improved the performance of PD-STAP in the real applications. Experimental results show that the method can increase the signal-to-clutter plus noise ratio (SCNR) by about 10 dB and achieve 20x speedup for target detection.

articleTitle: Velocity Estimation of Moving Targets in Multichannel SAR Images via Optimally-Weighted Velocity Averaging Based on MUSIC Algorithm
abstract: This paper described a scheme to estimate moving targets' radial velocities in complex images obtained from multi-channel synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems. A moving target in SAR images is made of multiple pixels. At each pixel, the data along the spatial direction can be treated as one observation of the moving target. The spectrum analysis, such as the multiple signal classification (MUSIC), helps to acquire the radial-velocity estimate of this pixel. The radial velocity of the moving target can be achieved through all the radial-velocity estimates of the multiple pixels via an optimally-weighted averaging scheme. The corresponding weight of each pixel is extracted during the MUSIC analysis, which is supposed to be the signal intensity of the moving target. The proposed scheme is more accurate than that based on the interferometry because it is more robust against the clutter. Experimental results of simulated SAR data demonstrate the accuracy and the utility of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Clutter Environment Perception via Residual Network Equipped with Pyramid Split Attention
abstract: With the increasing complexity of the radar working environment, the traditional radar working mode has been unable to allocate its own resources reasonably, which severely limits the performance of the radar. Perception and understanding of the target environment can provide prior knowledge for radar data processing, which is the key to improving radar performance. In order to make full use of the amplitude and phase characteristics of clutter complex data, a dual-channel network architecture is used in this article. In order to obtain better recognition performance, we combine the residual network with Pyramid Split Attention (PSA). Experiments based on measured data show that the method proposed in this paper has excellent recognition performance for typical clutter environments, and is of great significance to the intelligent development of radar.

articleTitle: Deep Unfolding Network for Near-Field Source Localization via Symmetric Nested Array
abstract: We exploit the deep unfolding networks (DUN) to achieve localization of near-field (NF) sources via symmetric nested array (SNA). Firstly, we calculate the vectorization of fourth-order cumulant (FOC) matrix which is only related to direction of arrival (DOA). Then, the vectorization of FOC matrix is considered as the input of DUN to obtain DOA spatial spectrum. Next, we calculate the range vector with the estimated DOA. Finally, the range vector is considered as the input of DUN to estimate the range parameter of NF sources. Simulation demonstrate that the DUN is robust to off-grid parameter estimation and can improve the resolution of DOA spatial spectrum. Moreover, the DUN has faster convergence speed and higher estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: Highly Integrated 64-element Transmitting Sub-array for Ku-band Phased Array Antenna
abstract: This paper proposed a highly integrated 64-element transmitting sub-array for Ku-band active phased array antenna. This sub-array integrates 64-channel tile-type transmitting module, 64-element antenna and 1-to-64 feed network in high density, which is convenient for flexible expansion of antenna array scale. Multi-function microwave monolithic integrated circuit (MMIC) is used to realize the miniaturization and high integration of RF channel. Microwave multilayer PCB and vertical interconnection technology are adopted to realize the integration of feed network and RF front end. The dual-polarized multilayer microstrip antenna is used to achieve wide bandwidth and the low profile of the antenna. The test result shows that EIRP of 25.5 dBW is obtained, with size within <tex>$83.8\text{mm}\times 83.8\text{mm}\times 12.3\text{mm}$</tex> and weight less than 200g.

articleTitle: A Low-Complexity Migration Compensation Method Based on Long-Term Integration
abstract: Long-term integration is an effective method for detection and estimation. However, as the integration time increases, the problem of range and Doppler frequency migrations caused by high-dynamic motions spoil the overall detection performance. A low-complexity migration compensation method for a hybrid long-term integration consisting of intra-segment coherent integration and inter-segment non-coherent integration, which is easy-to-implement, is proposed, where the compensation is performed across non-coherent integration segments rather than within coherent integration, leading to significantly reduced complexity while the detection performance is still affordable. The proposed solution is more convenient for real-time implementation, especially for resource-limited platforms.

articleTitle: Spatial Registration Based on Weighted Fusion of Multiple Significant Targets
abstract: Spatial registration algorithm deeply relies on the significant target. During the whole process of spatial registration, most registration algorithm only select one significant target and the sensor bias remains constant. However, in actual scene, the single significant target cannot be stably detected by all sensors, and the sensor bias will drift over time. Therefore, in order to accurately estimate the sensor bias in real-time, this paper proposes a registration method based on the weighted fusion of multiple significant targets. By fusing the spatial registration results of multiple significant targets, the robustness and accuracy of the registration algorithm are enhanced. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Design of a New Sensor Integrating Scatterometer and SAR to Observe Sea Surface Wind Field
abstract: The sea surface wind vectors in different sea areas such as the general waters and offshore waters, change in different spatial scales and requires different resolutions. Due to different retrieving mechanisms, the scatterometer is suitable for observing wind fields with low resolution in general waters, while the SAR can be applied to obtain wind fields with higher resolution in offshore waters. In order to retrieve wind fields in all kinds of sea areas, this paper proposes a new sensor integrating scatterometer and SAR, which adopts a single digital array antenna, but functions as a SAR and a scatterometer simultaneously through multiple beamforming Besides, this paper designs the operating mode, together with the joint time sequence of the transceiver for two modes to work simultaneously. This proposed concept can benefit the system development in simpler architecture, lighter weight, and lower cost. Moreover, the multiple observation modes working synchronously can improve the retrieving accuracy, and may give birth to some new applications.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Broadband Phased Array Antenna with Wide-Scanning Range
abstract: A wideband and wide-angle scanning patch array antenna with the height of only 4.2mm is presented. The antenna element operates on the aperture-coupling mechanism with a stacked patches architecture. The structure formed by the foam-filled substrates and the periodical metallic vias with a four-leaf clover (FLC) shape affords a broadband matching with a large field of view. The measured results of the prototype array with <tex>$15\times 15$</tex> elements exhibit a broadside bandwidth of 55% (active <tex>$\text{VSWR} <2$</tex>) and an off-broadside scanning bandwidth over 50% with the angle of 60° (active <tex>$\text{VSWR}< 2.5$</tex>).

articleTitle: Few-shot Human Activity Recognition with Radar Micro-Doppler Spectrograms
abstract: With the application of deep learning (DL) techniques, radar-based human activity recognition (HAR) attracts increasing attention for its high accuracy and good privacy. However, training a DL model requires a large volume of data, and the trained model cannot be easily adapted to a new environment. To deal with these challenges, in this paper, we propose a few-shot human activity recognition method with limited radar training data collected from a new application scenario. The proposed method adopts the domain adaptation method to learn a common feature space between a pre-existing radar dataset and the newly acquired training data. A multi-class discriminator network is also proposed to integrate the category classifier and the domain discriminator. As a result, the proposed FS-ADA can be both domain-invariant and category-discriminative. An improved generative adversarial training mechanism is then employed to optimize FS-ADA. Experimental results show that the proposed FS-ADA method is effective and outperforms state-of - the-art methods.

articleTitle: ISAR Imaging of Multi-Target Based on Edge Detection of Range Profiles and Particle Swarm Optimization
abstract: For inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging of multi-target, due to the coupling of the range profiles of different targets, conventional ISAR imaging method for single target is no longer applicable. In this paper, a novel multi-target ISAR imaging algorithm based on edge detection of range profiles (EDRP) and particle swarm optimization (PSO) is proposed. PSO is applied to estimate translational motion parameters and EDRP is utilized to determine whether the range profile of a certain target has been aligned. Through stepwise translational motion compensation and CLEAN-based image extraction, clear ISAR image of each target can be obtained in turn. Several simulations are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Periodicity Estimation Method for RCS Sequence based on Convolution Self-Attention Network
abstract: The RCS (Radar cross section) sequence usually contains the periodicity of the motion of the space target because of their stable or rolling attitude. However, the measured data are inevitably disturbed by various reasons. Most traditional period estimation methods require high data quality. In this paper, we propose a periodicity estimation method for RCS sequence using convolution self-attention networks. First, calculate the normalized RCS sequence. Then, highlight periodicity smooth local texture cased by noise, interference, or other movement using gamma correction. Finally, intercept fixed duration RCS sequence as the input of convolution self-attention networks to estimate the period. A certain amount of training data can ensure the performance of the proposed method. Experimental results show that the proposed method could obtain the comparatively accurate results and perform stably and reliably.

articleTitle: Experimental research on UWB channel and DF algorithm based on EKF
abstract: This paper carried out a series of experiments in both the LOS and NLOS scenes, which was based on an unmanned mobile platform, UWB and INS. Throughout experiments, this paper analyzes the ranging error from UWB, verifying that it obeys rice distribution in LOS and lognormal distribution in NLOS respectively; By using TOA combined with GN algorithm, the impact of the number of NLOS links on the positioning error is summarized; Taking the correlation between Links into consideration, their degradation processes was studied; To the end, this paper proposes a DF algorithm based on EKF, whose the positioning error of RMSE is proved to be lower than traditional algorithm.

articleTitle: Assumption and Discussion of Volume Scanning Strategy of New Generation Weather Radar in China I
abstract: The new generation weather radar plays an important role in the monitoring and early warning of severe convective disastrous weather. The current radar scanning mode in China is VCP21 mode, which completes an individual scanning time of 6 minutes and scans 9 elevation angles. The low temporal and spatial resolution is difficult to capture the vertical and horizontal structures of rapidly evolving weather phenomena in different stages, which can not meet the operational needs of forecasters. Based on the existing new generation weather radar observation network in China, by increasing the low-level scanning elevation, improving the radar scanning speed, improving the radar product algorithm, and improving the current business radar scanning strategy, we can further improve the radar data quality, realize the intellectualization of radar observation, refinement of temporal and spatial resolution, and improve the monitoring and early warning ability of small and medium-scale weather systems.to make the radar system play a greater role in the early warning of short-term strong convection and severe weather.

articleTitle: Dual-Use Signal Design for Radar and Communication via Pseudorandom Position and Phase Modulation
abstract: This paper proposes a new information modulation resorting to the pseudorandom position of communication sub-pulses and their phase in a designed unimodular signal for dual-function radar communication (DFRC) systems. Pseudorandom position modulation exploits the time randomness in the form of index modulation. Besides, the special phase of communication subpulses is utilized to decode the pseudorandom position and convey extral information simultaneously. In order to promise the radar detection ability, the peak sidelobe level (PSL) is considered as a figure of merit to minimize. At the same time, unimodular and radar subpulses phase constraints to comply with the current hardware technique and decode demand, are forced, respectively. This therefore yields a non-convex and NP-hard optimization problem with multiple constraints. Herein, a improved majorization-minimization frequency domain (MM-FD) method leads a way to find converged solution. Numerical results demonstrate the proposed pseudorandom position and phase modulation (P3M) and MM-FD method are capable of realizing high speed communication under the premise of ensuring acceptable radar performance.

articleTitle: Adaptive Dense main lobe Jamming Suppression Method Based on Multiple Measurement Sparse Recovery for Frequency Agile Radar
abstract: Frequency agile radar (FAR) can improve the coherent integration performance due to the spectrum sharing potential in electromagnetic countermeasure environments. However, the coherent integration performance of FAR would severely degrade in dense main lobe jamming environment. In order to solve this problem, an adaptive dense repeated jamming suppression method based on multiple measurement sparse recovery is proposed for frequency agile radar. In the proposed method, the target steering vector in the sparse recovery dictionary can be estimated by the multiple measurement vectors orthogonal matching pursuit (MMV-OMP) from the pulses without jamming cover, and then based on the maximum signal to interference-plus-noise ratio (MSINR) principle, the adaptive weight vector is obtained to suppress the jamming in the pulses of each coherent processing interval (CPI). Because of the MMV-OMP, the target steering vector can be estimated with less iterations, and the jamming in different pulses can be effectively suppressed by the adaptive weight vector, thus the output SNR can be improved. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by the simulated FAR data.

articleTitle: An Ultra Wideband Optical Transparent Seawater Patch Antenna
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-wideband optically transparent seawater patch antenna. Both the patch and the ground are realized by wrapping seawater in transparent organic glass, and no metal is needed to connect to the ground. Therefore, the entire antenna is almost 100 % optically transparent, and the only opaque part is the central metal feeding part. The antenna can achieve 67 % relative bandwidth for <tex>$\vert\mathrm{S}11\vert < -10\ \text{dB}$</tex> in the range of 10–20 GHz, and the radiation efficiency is above 85 %. The proposed transparent seawater patch antenna has the advantages of ultra-wideband, high radiation efficiency, optical transparency and low cost.

articleTitle: Dimension Reduction for Grid-Based 2D DOA Estimation with Arbitrary Planar Arrays
abstract: Grid-based methods are powerful in direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation with irregular arrays, whereas the fast implementation in 2D case is an important but challenging work. In this paper, we propose a modified version of continuous approximation based dimension-reduced estimator (M-CADRE), which is available for arbitrary planar arrays. The decoupled model is established by replacing the normal steering vector with an approximate basis matrix of the azimuth-defined vector space. Thus the azimuth and elevation angle can be estimated sequentially without 2D angle pairing. Both grid-searching-based estimators and block-sparse-based ones are allowed. Simulation results verify the superiority of M-CADRE in both performance and computational complexity.

articleTitle: An Efficient Continuous Imaging Framework for Bistatic SAR in Strip-map Mode
abstract: Fast factorized back-projection (FFBP) is a clas-sic fast time-domain algorithm (FTDA) for bistatic synthetic aperture radar (BiSAR) in spotlight mode. However, when conventional FFBP is employed for BiSAR in strip-map mode, the processing efficiency for continuous imaging of multiple full-apertures will be decreased significantly. In this paper, an efficient continous imaging framework is developed for BiSAR in strip-map mode. In the proposed framework, echo data are divided into several full-apertures data blocks then processed separately by FFBP to reduce redundant BP operations, so that the new continuos imaging framework has the higher efficiency than conventional FFBP. Promising results from both simulation and raw data experiments are provided and analyzed to validate the high performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Widening Circular Polarized Beam of An X-Band Feed Horn
abstract: This paper presents a design method of widening the circular polarized beam of feed horn by using a corrugated structure. Under the premise of no other circuit structure changes, the circular polarization beam width of 3 dB axial ratio is broadened from 25°x29° to 98.2°x99.5°, by replacing the conical horn in the X-band circular polarization feed horn with a corrugated horn. There is no obvious deterioration in return loss and directivity pattern of the improved feed horn.

articleTitle: Optimization of a Sparse Uniform Linear Array for Cylindrical Wave Synthesis
abstract: For the outdoor measurements of large-sized targets and phased arrays at high frequencies, an extremely long distance is required to satisfy the far-field criterion, which is impractical in many applications. As a replacement, near-field tests followed by a near-field to far-field transform (NFFFT) are usually considered. In this paper, an optimized sparse uniform linear array design is proposed for the synthesis of quasi-cylindrical wave in the test zone. To this end, the performance of synthetic wavefront and system complexity are considered systematically. The genetic algorithm (GA) is exploited to optimize the excitation amplitudes and phases. Both uniformity and gain of the electric field (E-field) are considered for wideband measurement while the corresponding optimizing strategy is constructed. Besides, the impacts of uncertainties in practical implementation are discussed. Simulation results for an X-band array are presented, demonstrating that the optimized array produces cylindrical wavefront with specified metrics of performance.

articleTitle: A Spatially Variant Relax Algorithm for Scattering Center Extraction from MIMO Radar Images
abstract: In high frequency region, the scattering response of an extended target can be well approximated as a sum of responses from individual scattering centers. The spatially variant point spread function (PSF) of MIMO radar near-field imaging system makes it difficult to extract scattering centers. Based on the spatial wavenumber support domain of the MIMO radar, this paper proposes a spatially variant Relax (SV-Relax) algorithm for its scattering center extraction. The spatial wavenumber support domain of the MIMO radar is firstly analyzed. Then the process of the SV-Relax algorithm is discussed in detail. Finally, both numerical and measured data are processed to demonstrate the validity of proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Using Phase Symmetry to Detect the Hyperbolic Region In GPR Images
abstract: Hyperbolic detection is an important task in the Ground-Penetrating Radar (GPR) images due to the buried targets display the form of hyperbolic and has been researched all the time. The detection of hyperbolic is beneficial to the buried threat detection, classification and environment change detection of GPR images. In this letter, a robust hyperbola detection method for GPR images is presented. A model based on image phase and symmetry information is developed as a detector. The detector solves the problem of hyperbola extraction from GPR images with low physical resolution. As far as we know, the phase symmetry (PS) model is used in this task for the first time and the experimental results show that the effectiveness of the proposed method is better than other methods used in recent researches.

articleTitle: A Density Based Unsupervised Learning Method for Radar Target Route Estimation
abstract: Tracking radar targets generally relies on kinematic characteristics from signal processing, since there is no specific priori knowledge of routes information in an area. However, it is a passive way that only using kinematic characteristics to tracking targets, and cannot further predict and analyze the target motivation in advance, losing important information. In practice, targets moving in the sea/air are following assigned routes due to the constraints of fuel, weather and expense. Aim at this problem, in this paper, we propose a method Density Based Route Extraction (DBRE) to extract routes from accumulated data without any information in advance. It finds hot regions where targets usually appears, labels noise data, and then extracts routes. Through comprehensive and comparative experiments, the performance of DBRE on route extraction is validated, especially in the aspects of route coverage and correctness, proving that our method provides an effective way to construct route network in an area when no extra information is available.

articleTitle: Low-Cost High-Resolution SAR Imaging on Drone
abstract: This paper presents a novel, small, and compact K-band synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system – based in an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) – together with the first drone-based experiment results. The article also describes the system architecture and the implemented SAR imaging algorithm. The system uses a GPS position sensor, and inertial measurement unit (IMU) aided with SAR autofocus algorithm for trajectory estimation required for high-resolution radar image creation.

articleTitle: Radar Waveform Covariance Design for Extended Targets Based on Two-Person Zero Sum Game
abstract: This paper studies the Two-Person Zero Sum (TPZS) game between the radar and the extended target with the output Signal-to-Interference-pulse-Noise Ratio (SINR) being the payoff function. The radar player wants to maximize SINR by adjusting its transmit waveform under Peak to Average power Ratio (PAR) constraint. Conversely, the target player is intelligent to avoid being detected by controlling its Target Impulse Response (TIR) over a spherical set. It is proved theoretically that the Nash equilibrium exists for the Semi-Definite Relaxation (SDR) form of the TPZS game. Moreover, a first order iterative algorithm is introduced to find the equilibrium strategy. Numerical results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm as well as the designed waveform covariance.

articleTitle: Photonics-based MIMO Radar for High-resolution 2D and 3D Imaging
abstract: Photonics-based broadband radar has attracted lots of attention because it enables ultra-high range resolution detection. As the photonics-based monostatic radar has been investigated intensively, photonics-based array radars are highly desirable to further improve the angular or azimuth resolution. In this paper, we introduce our recent research progress on photonics-based multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) radar. Each broadband radar transceiver is built by photonics frequency multiplication and frequency mixing. By frequency division multiplexing or time division multiplexing, photonics-based broadband MIMO radar can be constructed. Based on the established photonics-based MIMO radar, high-resolution 2D and 3D imaging are demonstrated.

articleTitle: A Robust Coprime Array Interpolation Method for DOA Estimation in Unknown Nonuniform Noise
abstract: The most existing coprime array interpolation-based algorithms have the potential to increase the degree of freedom for direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation. However, these algorithms are modeled on the Gaussian white noise and do not consider the possibility of nonuniform noise. To eliminate the unknown nonuniform noise, we propose a robust coprime array interpolation method in this paper. First, the vectorization is performed on the covariance matrix to obtain the difference co-array with overlapping sensors. Next, we develop a robust interpolation technique to optimize the signal model of the nonuniform virtual array and fill in the holes to convert it into a contiguous virtual uniform linear array (ULA). We then divide the virtual ULA into overlapping subarrays and reconstruct the Toeplitz covariance matrix through the denoising constraint. This constraint can alleviate the impact of nonuniform noise to ensure the robustness of the reconstruction. Finally, the DOA estimation is resolved through the MUSIC algorithm. Numerical experiments validate the superiority of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Online Beam Scheduling for Multi-Target Tracking in Linear Wireless Array Radar
abstract: In this paper, an effective online beam scheduling (OBS) is proposed for multi-target tracking (MTT) in linear wireless array radar (LWAR). The proposed OBS strategy is performed by selecting antenna elements in LWAR subject to one-to-one constraint between beam and target to achieve better beampattern and MTT performance. Firstly, the relationship between the subset of selected antenna elements and the radiation performance of beampattern is established to derive the Bayesian Cramér-Rae lower bound (BCRLB). Then, the quality of service (QoS) based global MTT performance metric is applied to form the optimization problem. To solve the non-convex problem, the ant colony optimization (ACO) is applied by using the QoS-based metric as the desirability parameter. Compared with the traditional fixed strategy, simulation results demonstrate that our proposed strategy has the ability to coordinate antenna elements in LWAR and improve MTT global accuracy.

articleTitle: 3D Point Cloud Reconstruction of Vehicle using Inversely Mapping and Voting from CSAR Images
abstract: 3D reconstruction of object has raised much interest in the field of SAR. The feature of target at multi aspect angles can be obtained from sub-aperture images provided by circular SAR(CSAR), which is conducive to 3D reconstruction. Radargrammetric method is a conventional way to extract DEM while its performance for 3D reconstruction is limited by the image registration. It is difficult to find corresponding points in different sub-aperture images. In this paper, we proposed a method for 3D reconstruction of vehicle based on projections in sub-aperture images. According to the imaging mechanism of CSAR, different targets located on the same iso-range line in the zero doppler plane fall into the same cell. For a projection point, given a series of offsets, the projection point will be mapped inversely to the 3D mesh along the iso-range line. We can obtain candidates of the target. The intersection of iso-range lines can be regarded as voting process. For a candidate, the more times of intersection, the higher the number of votes, and the candidate point will be reserved. This fully excavates the information contained in the angle dimension of CSAR. The proposed approach is verified by the Gotcha Volumetric SAR Data Set.

articleTitle: SAR Image Segmentation Based on Fast Superpixel Clustering
abstract: Accurate segmentation on synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images is a challenging task. In this paper, we propose a SAR image segmentation method based on the fast superpixel clustering algorithm. First, our proposed multi-scale superpixel generation method is used to generate a superpixel map with high quality. Second, the edge-aware superpixel smoothing is performed on the superpixels to alleviate the effect of speckle noise, which facilitates improving segmentation accuracy. Finally, the fuzzy C-means (FCM) clustering is implemented on the superpixels to obtain the final segmentation result. Experimental results on two Sentinel-1 C band SAR images demonstrate that the proposed method exceeds the comparing methods both quantitatively and qualitatively, confirming its advantages in SAR image segmentation.

articleTitle: On Compressive Toeplitz Covariance Sketching
abstract: This paper studies the problem of estimating Toeplitz covariance matrices from compressive temporal sketches. In contrast to most existing works on Toeplitz covariance estimation, we simultaneously look at the spatial and temporal sample complexities. To fully exploit the Toeplitz structure, we rely on the sparse-array idea to design the spatial samplers. Then we compare the performances of common unbiased estimators, and derive the conditions in terms of the sampler design under which the estimators yield the same MSE. As for the temporal complexity, for the first time in literature, we provide the non-asymptotic guarantee on entry-wise convergence as a function of the MSE, which reveals the trade-off between spatial and temporal complexities. The theoretical claims are demonstrated by the numerical experiments.

articleTitle: Multiobjective optimal waveform design for TDS-OFDM integrated radar and communication systems
abstract: The integrated radar and communication waveform is one of solutions to alleviate the problem of frequency spectrum shortage, which plays an importance role in the development of multifunctional electronic information systems. To deal with the difficulties of waveform design for the integrated radar and communication systems, a multiobjective optimal waveform design for integrated radar and communication systems of Time-Domain-Synchronization Orthogonal-Frequency-Division-Multiplexing (TDS-OFDM) is proposed. At first, a multiobjective optimal function is built to design the transmitting waveforms with the radar sensing performance, the Communications Channel Capacity (CCC), and the Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR). To simply the global optimization process, the multiobjective optimal function decomposes into a cascade of independent objective optimal functions as an approximation. Then, a proper waveform is obtained by solving the independent objective optimal functions. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate the advantages of the method.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Control Strategy for Radar Servo System
abstract: A hybrid control strategy composed of a classical proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller and an expert PID controller is presented for the radar servo system in this paper. Based on the presented mathematic detailed model with current loop, the velocity loop and position loop are studied and discussed. And then, its responses with different proportion coefficient and integration time in PID controls are investigated, which shows that there is a large overshoot in the current loop, resulting in excessive motor current in practice. Based on the expert PID control strategy introduced in the current loop, a hybrid control strategy is introduced for the radar servo position tracing. The simulation results show that the presented hybrid control strategy with the classical PID and expert PID controllers can not only quickly trace the angle position with the smooth speed, but also can prevent excessive current.

articleTitle: Requirement Analysis of Airborne Multi-platform Distributed Coherent Radar
abstract: In this paper, the resource requirements of airborne multi-platform distributed coherent radar system is studied. First, the coherent principle is analyzed for airborne multi-platform distributed radar. Then, the coherent influence factors of airborne multi-platform distributed radar are introduced and the influence of each factor on the coherent performance is analyzed. According to the analysis, the requirements of airborne multi-platform distributed coherent radar system are given. Finally, numerical results are provided to verify our analysis.

articleTitle: A Three-Dimension Polarimetric Correlation Pattern Interpretation Tool and Its Application
abstract: A new three-dimension polarimetric correlation pattern (3-D PCP) is developed in this paper by extending the polarimetric correlation pattern along the polarimetric ellipti-city angle. Three representative 3-D correlation patterns can be thus derived. Then, the periodicity and extreme points distribution are analyzed for four canonical scatterers in detail. Signifi-cant differences can be observed in their manifold pattern structures and several physical meaningful features including the Gaussian curvature in differential geometry are extracted to an-alyze the polarimetric response with the change of polarimetric rotation angle and polarimetric ellipse angle. On this basis, the ship and sea pixels of the Radarsat-2 PolSAR data are analyzed by using the three-dimensional polarimetric correlation pattern of HH and HV channels. The ship region can be well extracted utilizing the Gaussian curvature feature, which shows the poten-tial in ship detection. The results prove that the three-dimensional polarimetric correlation pattern and the extracted features have the ability to distinguish different scattering mecha-nisms.

articleTitle: Design of Low-Frequency Tightly Coupled Dipole Array with Integrated Balun
abstract: Tightly Coupled Dipole Array(TCDA) is a new type of radar antenna with UWB performance and low profile, but relevant designs are rare in low frequency band. This article presents a TCPA working in low frequency band (110-520MHz). Each array element is divided into 2 dipoles to avoid common mode resonance. The TCDA is excited by the co-designed integrated Marchand Balun, which works as the wide-band impedance matching network and provides a balanced feeding. A printed Frequency Selected Surface(FSS) is used for wide-angle scanning in place of the bulky dielectric superstrates. The final array achieves a low profile <tex>$(0.1\lambda_{Low})$</tex> and superior performance of 5:1 bandwidth with <tex>$\textbf{VSWR} \bm{< 2.5}$</tex> when scanning ±50° in E plane and <tex>$\textbf{VSWR}\bm{ < 3.0}$</tex> when scanning ±40° in H plane.

articleTitle: Modified 3D Metamaterial Aperture Imaging Method Based on Back Projection Algorithm
abstract: In recent research trends of millimeter wave imaging, metamaterial aperture imaging systems are getting increasing popularity. By employing the spatially variant radiation pattern, a metamaterial aperture antenna (MAA) with the linear structure could obtain the information of the two-dimensional scenes. In principle, the three-dimensional (3D) scene images can be obtained by moving the MAA in the cross direction. In this paper, we proposed a 3D decoupling imaging method based on the back projection algorithm. This method could decompose the scenario into a number of slices and reconstruct extract slices containing targets in parallel way. Simulation results verify the effectivity of proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Single-photon Passive Direction Finding Method
abstract: The rapid development of quantum radar brings subversive challenges to radar countermeasures, the difficulty is reconnaissance. Aiming at the problems of quantum radar signal reception and passive direction finding at the present stage, this paper carried out research on quantum radar reconnaissance technology based on single photon measurement, proposed a passive direction finding method for quantum radar signal at the present stage, and verified the feasibility of the method through experiments and simulation calculation. This method solves the problem that the traditional passive direction finding technology is difficult to detect the quantum target signal, and can be effectively used for the detection and alarm of the quantum radar radiation source at this stage, which is of great significance in the fields of electronic countermeasures, environmental monitoring and space exploration.

articleTitle: Application of Feature Selective Auto-encoder in Aero Target Recognition
abstract: Rader aero target recognition has important application value on modern war field. In this paper, a feature selection auto-encoder based radar aero target classification method is proposed. The proposed method can automatically select manual features and further extract high-level features for classification of helicopter, propeller and jet. In experiments, real application data is used for the classification. Experimental results indicate the efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A New Ship Detection Method With Limited Labeled Data In SAR Imagery
abstract: The ship detection from synthetic aperture radar remains a challenging problem for maritime surveillance applications. In the fully-supervised object detection methods, a lot of labeled bounding boxes (training data) are required, but the exact instance-level annotations are difficult to obtain. The classical approaches that are based on statistical characteristics and polarization characteristics do not require any annotation, but the statistical distribution model cannot match the data perfectly, which often leads to high false alarm rates. In order to solve this problem, a dynamic data augmentation method (DDAM) is proposed for dealing with missing labels and lacking annotations for ship detection.
