In DDAM, we just annotate a small number of ship targets in training data before training, then the proposed learning framework can dynamically update training data with pseudo-annotated data in iterations. The detection performances are evaluated by mean Average Precision (mAP). Extensive experiments on the Sentinel-1A SAR data show the effectiveness of this new method.

articleTitle: Sar Anti-Jamming Method Based on Optimization of Phase-Jittered LFM Signal
abstract: In view of the false target deception jamming based on digital radio frequency storage technology, mutually orthogonal waveforms between pulses can be used to suppress the jamming. This paper proposes a phase jitter optimization model based on the linear frequency modulation(LFM) signal. Theoretically, the phase jitter of the signal can be optimized from three degrees of freedom. This paper focuses on the simulation and verification of the disturbance amplitude factor. Firstly, the anti-jamming strategy and feasibility under certain conditions are discriminated. Then gives the form of the phase-jittered LFM signal and its optimization model. Finally, the simulation verifies the anti-jamming effect and imaging performance. The simulation results show that the imaging performance of the optimized phase-jittered LFM signal is significantly improved, and the active deception jamming can be suppressed.

articleTitle: DOA Estimation of Uniform Linear Array Based on Improved Whitening and RobustICA
abstract: Aiming at the problem about DOA estimation of a far-field uniform linear array (ULA) under the framework of blind source separation (BSS), this paper proposes a method based on improved whitening and robust independent component analysis (RobustICA). The approach first adopts improved whitening preprocessing to reduce the noise of the received signals. Then, according to prior knowledge such as the independence of the signals, RobustICA is utilized to obtain the estimation of the steering vector matrix. Finally, combined with the matrix structure of ULA, the analytical solution is directly calculated to obtain the results. Simulation results demonstrate that compared with ESPRIT and MUSIC, the proposed method can still obtain high-precision estimation while the number of antenna elements is small, the SNR is low, and the incident angles of sources are closely spaced. Furthermore, under the premise that the number of elements is equal to that of sources, the proposed approach can also successfully estimate the angles, in which case, MUSIC and ESPRIT become invalid.

articleTitle: Waveform design for random stepped frequency radars to achieve the ultra-low side-lobes in high resolution range profile
abstract: In this paper, a waveform design method for random stepped frequency radars (RSFR) to achieve the ultra-low side-lobes in its high resolution range profile (HRRP) is proposed. The randomly distributed modulated frequencies of RSFR make it possible to synthesize the wide-band to generate the HRRP. Meanwhile, the HRRP side-lobes can be significantly suppressed by arranging the modulated frequency with the window type distribution. Simulations show that the proposed method can achieve similar side-lobe level as the windowed linear stepped frequency radar, but without causing the output signal power loss. This is beneficial to improve the probability of target detection.

articleTitle: DOA Estimation Method Based on Maximum Likelihood for Nest Array Via Sparse Representation
abstract: The performance of the direction of arrival (DOA) estimation method based on sparse representation can be degraded by the grid error. A new DOA estimation method based on maximum likelihood for nest array is proposed in this paper. By the vectorization operator and the denoising processing, we build a new sparse model which has a wider aperture and can obtain better performance. The grids near the true DOAs are roughly obtained by the estimation of spatial power spectrum estimation, then it is refined by one-dimension searching method. Simulation results indicate the proposed method outperforms the existing methods with a higher accuracy and detection possibility, especially in lower signal-to-noise (SNR).

articleTitle: Radar High Range Resolution Rrofile Attitude Estimation Based on Neural Network
abstract: The sensitivity of attitude is core problem of radar high range resolution profile (HRRP) target recognition, if the orientation of targets can be approximately confirmed, we can narrow the search area of template library in recognition. Then the real time of recognition results can be guaranteed, and the recognition performance can be improved too. In this paper, we propose a radar high range resolution profile attitude estimation method based on neural network, the data argumentation and regularization technique improve the generalization ability of model, and they make the model have some noise robustness.

articleTitle: Terahertz ISAR Imaging Experiment Based on Near-field BP Algorithm
abstract: The inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging technique is widely used in remote sensing and target detection areas, and the back projection (BP) algorithm is a fundamental method to obtain the target's images. Large signal bandwidth and high frequency of the Terahertz ISAR can lead to a relative high resolution. But the ISAR images are vulnerable to the signal errors at the same time. Both the signal nonlinearity and the imaging parameters errors will make the imaging result defocusing and consisting of distortion. The imaging parameters mainly consist the deviation of the turntable center• and the distance between the scattering point and the antenna. This paper analyses the influences of the signal nonlinearity and the deviation of the target center, and proposes an improved near-field BP algorithm to eliminate the defocusing and distortion in a 330GHz Terahertz ISAR imaging experiment of a metal cylinder model.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional DOA Estimation by Using Two Parallel Coprime-Nested Arrays
abstract: In this paper, we address the problem of two-dimensional (2-D) direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation for two parallel coprime-nested arrays (TPCNAs), which can be divided into two parallel sparse nested arrays (TPSNAs). By vectorizing the covariance and cross-covariance matrices and Toeplitz matrix reconstruction, a two parallel sparse uniform linear array with longer aperture is formed for each TPSNA. Subsequently, the root multiple signals classification is applied to each virtual array to reduce the complexity. According to the coprime property, the final estimates can be uniquely determined by the two virtual arrays. Simulations results are also provided to verify the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Maneuvering Target Tracking Performance Online Monitoring Based on Fréchet Distance
abstract: In the application of maneuvering target tracking, online performance monitoring helps to optimize the way of radar resource allocation and improve tracking accuracy. To solve the problem of very high computation cost in the existing online monitoring methods based on information geometry, we propose an online monitoring method for tracking performance based on the Frèchet distance in this paper. The Frèchet distance under the multivariate Gaussian distribution takes into account the mean and covariance in the filtering, which can get a more reasonable error measurement. The advantage of the method is high computational efficiency, which is conducive to online evaluation. Simulation results show that the performance monitoring results of this method for maneuvering targets are equivalent to the shooting algorithm based on information geometry, but the computation cost is significantly lower than that of the shooting algorithm.

articleTitle: A Potential Human Activity Detection Method Based on Multi-polarization InSAR
abstract: Human activity detection refers to detect, locate and extract potential activities from the observation scene, which employs the coherent change detection (CCD) method to detect the subtle change between two data acquisitions. The polarization information of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) system can represent the scattering characteristics of the target more comprehensively. This paper adopts a coherent change detection method based on multi-polarization interferometric coherence to detect potential human activity in the scene. The effectiveness of the method is further validated by the actual airborne repeat-pass C-band Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) data that acquired by the Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences (AIRCAS). Moreover, the results are compared with the coherent change detection method based on single-polarization InSAR. The results show that the method proposed in this paper has better detection performance than the traditional coherent change detection method based on single-polarization.

articleTitle: A Measurement Matrix-Based Deceptive Jamming Suppression Method for Compressive Sensing Radar
abstract: The problem of detection performance degradation caused by digital radio frequency memory(DRFM) repeat-back jamming in compressive sensing radar(CSR) is investigated in this paper. Then we present a deceptive jamming suppression method based on a structured measurement matrix. Specific initial phases are added in each transmitted pulse to make the CSR be able to distinguish the jamming pulses firstly. Then a structured measurement matrix is devised to demodulate the additive initial phase of each received pulse and accumulate the target's echo without integrating the deceptive jamming. Compared with the existed typical target detection methods in CSR, the proposed method achieve more accurate targets estimation by suppressing the false target caused by deceptive jamming. Numerical results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed deceptive jamming suppression method.

articleTitle: A Quadtree Beam-Segmenting Fast Backprojection Algorithm
abstract: The computation of the backprojection (BP) algorithm for spotlight synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is expensive since the reflectivity reconstruction is based on pixel-by-pixel interpolation operation. Based on dechirp, a quadtree beam-segmenting fast BP algorithm for spotlight SAR is proposed. This fast BP algorithm is to generate multiple sub-beam down-sampled raw data by using dechirp imaging algorithm to filter the whole beam data, and the filtering process is recursively implemented like a quadtree. For any narrow sub-beam, the corresponding sub-image can be reconstructed by a regular backprojection. The pixel numbers of each sub-image is small and the down-sampled sub-beam raw data is small, so it can significantly accelerate the regular BP algorithm. The processing flows are derived in detail and the algorithm is validated by simulated data.

articleTitle: A New Attitude Estimation Method of Space Target Utilizing ISAR Image Sequence Under Low SNR
abstract: Given the prior geometry model, the attitude of a space target can be estimated by evaluating the target contour similarity between the practical inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) image sequence and the theoretical projection images. However, the target will be submerged in the noise under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), resulting in inaccurate target contour extraction and attitude estimation. In view of this, a new attitude estimation method is proposed by optimizing the projection area energy accumulation value along the ISAR image sequence. The projection area energy accumulation (PAEA) value will reach the maximum when the attitude candidate of the prior geometry model corresponds to the true one. Particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is utilized to improve the search efficiency. The proposed method is more robust to the noise because of the utilization of target energy instead of the target contour. Experimental results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Wideband Radar System Distortion Compensation Based on Coherent Integration
abstract: The system distortion in an ISAR system can severely distort the high-resolution range profile and then defocus the final IASR image. Hence, the compensation for the system distortion is important for generating high-quality ISAR image. In this paper, we will present a novel method based on coherent integration to compensate the system distortion under a low SNR condition. First, we will analysis the model of the received spherical satellite signal and then introduce the idea of coherent integration. Then, we will illustrate the process of the proposed method. After the process, we can achieve coherent integration of the received echoes and then the SNR of the signal can be significantly increased. Therefore, the amplitude and phase distortion characteristics can be effectively calculated by the coherently integrated data. Furthermore, the target echoes received by the radar can be conveniently compensated via this method. Finally, the results of the real data experiment demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: UCCN: A Fast and Efficient Complex Convolution Network for SAR Data
abstract: Because the volume of labeled datasets is very limited and the datasets are complex-valued, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image classification has always been a difficult problem. In addition, the phase error of the data caused by the non-systematic motion of SAR makes image classification more difficult. The existing complex cross-convolution neural network (CCNN) is a down sampling structure, in which the methods of SAR image processing cannot be used in the network. In this work, a U-shaped complex cross-convolution network (UCCN) is proposed, which normalizes the output dimension through the U-shaped structure, so that the regularization of image entropy norm can be applied. Specifically, image entropy norm regularization and cross entropy regularization are jointly applied to UCCN to improve the accuracy and convergence of classification. Experiments show that UCCN has better classification performance in terms of accuracy than other networks for SAR datasets. Through further experiments, it is concluded that UCCN has faster convergence speed and higher classification accuracy, and UCCN with image entropy norm regularization has better generalization ability for larger phase error data.

articleTitle: Ground Background Clutter Recognition Based on Fully Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: Accurate and robust recognition of background clutter is essential for radar target detection. Aiming at the problems that existing clutter recognition methods have low accuracy and poor robustness, a background clutter recognition method based on novel Fully Convolutional Neural Network (FCNN) is proposed. FCNN is trained and tested based on the simulated ground clutter Range-Doppler (R-D) spectra. Experimental results demonstrate that FCNN is significantly superior to the existing background clutter recognition models in terms of clutter classification accuracy or time complexity. In addition, FCNN can better adapt to clutter recognition under low clutter-to-noise ratio (CNR) scenarios. Finally, we verify the effectiveness of the CFAR detector based on clutter recognition.

articleTitle: A Fast Super-resolution Imaging Method Based On Vortex Electromagnetic Wave Radar
abstract: Vortex electromagnetic wave radar forms different modes by modulating the wavefront phase, and realizes two-dimensional imaging of radar targets by fast Fourier transform (FFT) or back projection (BP). However, the resolution of the conventional vortex imaging methods limit by the number of modes that can irradiate the target. In this paper, based on the uniform circular array (UCA) and multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm, the two-dimensional imaging model of echo signal in azimuth domain and pitch domain is constructed, and the two-dimensional imaging of target in spherical coordinates is achieved. Simultaneously, the real value minimum norm algorithm (RV-MNM) is proposed, which can realize the two-dimensional imaging of the target when the scatterer number of targets is unknown, and the operation efficiency is increased by about 30% compared with the traditional MUSIC algorithm.

articleTitle: Facial Expression Recognition based on a Dual Graph Convolutional Network
abstract: The facial expression recognition on non-laboratory database is difficult and challenging. To improve the recognition performance, we propose a dual graph convolutional network, based on which two feature extractors are employed to facial images. The experimental results on RAF-DB and SFEW database show that our proposed method improves the accuracy of facial expression recognition on non-laboratory datasets.

articleTitle: Human Echo Signal Preprocessing for Through-The-Wall Radar Based on Improved PCA and MTI Fusion Algorithm
abstract: Accurate and loss-free extraction of human echo signals from the hidden environment is of great importance in military, disaster relief and medical fields, and is also a hot spot for research in the related field of radar through walls. When detecting human targets through walls, noise and hidden environment objects such as walls tend to attenuate electro-magnetic waves to a large extent, which leads to the inability of radar to detect human targets accurately. In this paper, in order to remove the interference of wall echo and environmental noise from the echo signal, a pre-processing method of human echo signal of through-wall radar with improved PCA and MTI fusion algorithm is proposed. Firstly, SVD is used to pre-process the simulated noise-plus-interference echo signal, and then it is verified by the actual collected data, and the simulation results are more satisfactory, but the interference from the wall cannot be completely removed in practical application. In response to the above problem, the improved PCA and MTI fusion algorithm was used for pre-processing, and the simulation results and actual data showed that the ambient noise was suppressed and the wall interference was also removed.

articleTitle: A New Position Error Calibration Approach to DOA Estimation for Quasi-Stationary Signals
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of direction of arrival (DOA) for quasi-stationary signals(QSS) in an uniform linear array (ULA) where partial sensor position errors exist. Inspired by the instrumental sensor method (ISM) and based on the Khatri-Rao (KR) subspace technique, we devise a computational efficient method to determine the DOAs. The proposed method can calculate the DOAs with no need of spectrum searching. Moreover, by exploiting the characteristic of long-term time-variation in QSS, it can estimate more signals than the number of well-calibrated signals. Based on the estimated DOAs, we propose a new sensor position error calibration method which can calculate sensor position errors one by one only if two elements have been well-calibrated in advance. Simulation results verify the effectiveness and the superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Video SAR Image Fusion Using the Effective Reflection Coefficient
abstract: The video synthetic aperture radar (ViSAR), as a mode for sensing in an ever-wider synthetic aperture by sequentially forming SAR images on a series of contiguous or overlapping sub-apertures, has the promising capability to capture wide-angle scattering behavior of objects. In this paper, a novel method for ViSAR image fusion is proposed. First, the ViSAR imaging mode is analyzed and modeled. Based on this model, the reflection coefficient (RC) is then estimated and the significant RC is detected in each sub-aperture image. These detection results are then fused across sub-aperture images to detect scatterers in the area of interest. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated using a simulated scenario and compared with that of the conventional ViSAR image fusion method based on the generalized likelihood ratio test. Numerical results demonstrate the advantages of the proposed method in capturing the aspect-dependent scattering characteristics as well as the spatial structure of objects.

articleTitle: Tropical Cyclone Wind Speed Retrieval from SAR Imagery Using A Neural Network
abstract: Tropical Cyclone (TC) wind speed retrieval from spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) cross-polarization acquisitions is a hotspot in SAR remote sensing application. In this paper, we collected 12 Interferometric Wide swath (IW) mode VH-polarization images observed by the European Space Agency Sentinel-1 satellites and the collocated Stepped Frequency Microwave Radiometer and Soil Moisture Active Passive radiometer wind speed observations up to 74 m/s under TC conditions. Matching samples were divided into two datasets. Dataset 1 contained 3851 samples and was used to develop a new geophysical model function (GMF). Dataset 2 contained 1282 samples and was used for validation. Each dataset included the parameters of VH-polarized normalized radar cross section (VH NRCS), wind speed and radar incident angle. A two-layer feed-forward network was utilized to generate a GMF named as the Sentinel-1 IW mode Wind Retrieval Model Based on Neural Network (S1IW.NN). VH NRCS and incident angle were inputs. Wind speed was output. The network outputs' related coefficient with respect to targets was 0.94 for Dataset 1. In order to validate the S1IW.NN model, we compared the S1IW.NN model's retrievals and those from a traditional empirical GMF S1IW.NR, based on the wind speed observations in Dataset 2. For the S1IW.NN model, the overall bias, correlation coefficient (Cor) and root mean squared error (RMSE) were −0.03 m/s, 0.93 and 3.72 m/s, respectively. For the S1IW.NR model, the overall bias, Cor and RMSE were −0.17 m/s, 0.92 and 4.61 m/s, respectively. In addition, we carried out a case study of the Hurricane Dorian for evaluating the proposed GMF visually and statistically. Results showed that the proposed GMF has a higher accuracy than the traditional model. Last but not least, the S1IW.NN model was able to retrieve the wind speeds at the sub-swaths' inner boundaries more smoothly, indicating the neural network's good performance in application to GMF regression.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of Targets Based on Adaptive Complex ℓ1 Reweighted Minimization via Homotopy
abstract: The stepped frequency (SF) signal plays an important role in the high-resolution radar system. In a complex radar environment, some echo pulses may be lost or be interfered with. Directly apply a conventional reconstructive algorithm to obtain high-resolution range profile (HRRP) will lead to high sidelobes in this case. In this paper, the adaptive complex <tex>$\ell_{1}$</tex> reweighted minimization via homotopy (ACRW-H) is applied to deal with the problem above. The algorithm adaptively selects accurate regularization parameters (RPs) while updating the estimation to reconstruct HRRP when echo pulses are incomplete. Both simulation and real data experiments are presented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. It is shown that this algorithm gives better accuracy than some existing algorithms like OMP and <tex>$\ell_{1}$</tex> minimization. The robustness to noise of the proposed method is also investigated.

articleTitle: Anomalous Reflection and RCS Reduction Based Ultra-wideband Polarization Conversion Metasurface
abstract: In this paper, a new metasurface (MS) reflection polarization converter was came up for combining with Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) phase theory in realizing anomalous reflection and Radar Cross-Section (RCS) reduction. The basic unit of the polarization converter was composed of a dielectric substrate, a metal patch and a metal backplane, which enabled the linearly polarized incident waves to cross-polarized wave with relative bandwidth of 43.1%, polarization conversion rate (PCR) of almost 100% from 9.8GHz to 19.9GHz by simulation. Furthermore, a phase gradient (GM) MS was designed to react on anisotropic reflection and satisfy the generalized Snell's law based on the PB phase principle. Finally, we designed two arrangement structure to verify the RCS reduction. The structure plays an important role in electromagnetic stealth and antenna designs.

articleTitle: Convolution Neural Network Enhanced MIMO Array Radar Imaging Based on Back Projection Algorithm
abstract: The multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) array radar has plentiful application scenarios in the modern intelligent life. The back projection (BP) algorithm is widely used in MIMO array radar imaging for the superior imaging accuracy and generality of measurement configurations. However, the BP algorithm also bring the two-dimensional spatial distortion and background noise. To solve these problems, the U-Net network is introduced in MIMO array radar enhanced imaging in this paper. The experimental results of both random and fixed scatters show that the scatters are accurately reconstructed and positioned, the two-dimensional spatial distortion is corrected and the background noise is eliminated with the proposed method.

articleTitle: Power Control Game Between a Dual-Function Radar-Communication System and a Jammer
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of power allocation for a dual-function radar-communication system in the presence of an intelligent jammer. The primary objective of the system is to minimize the total transmit power while guaranteeing a specified signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) for target detection and a predetermined data information rate (DIR) for data communication, whereas the jammer can observe the transmit power of the system and consequently choose its optimal jamming power to maximize the interference to the system. In this context, a Stackelberg game is proposed to capture the interactions between the system and the jammer. Furthermore, the Stackelberg equilibrium (SE) of the game is analytically derived with Lagrange multipliers. Finally, simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy. In particular, the SE strategy is superior to the strategy based on Nash equilibrium in terms of the total power consumption.

articleTitle: Channel Attention-Driven Recurrent Feedback Neural Network for Ship Detection in SAR Images
abstract: In recent years, deep learning has presented great advantages for ship detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images. However, the existing deep learning methods have the problems of high computational and storage complexity, and have been prone to false alarm for the detection of coastal and small-scale ship targets. As such, in this paper, by introducing the brain-like recurrent feedback mechanism into SAR ship detection, a novel recurrent feedback channel attention-based convolutional block (i.e., RFCACB) is designed to improve the feature extraction ability, and suppress the noise interference. And then, based on the YOLOv3, a channel attention-driven recurrent feedback neural network (CARFNN) is proposed for ship detection. Experimental results on a widely-used SAR ship detection data set (i.e., SAR Ship Detection Dataset, SSDD) illustrate that the proposed CARFNN model can be superior to the YOLOv3 model, resulting in better detection accuracy.

articleTitle: A New Adversarial Hierarchy for SAR Clutter Generation
abstract: Clutter simulation plays an important role in SAR image interpretation. The preceding works usually generate the clutter by the amplitude of measured data. They ignore the phase information. In addition, it is difficult to describe the ground clutter accurately with a certain statistical distribution model, due to the complex and mutable scenes. To address these problems, this paper presents a new adversarial hierarchy for SAR clutter generation. Different from the preceding works, we jointly consider the real and the imaginary components into a unified framework. They are used to generate the complex clutter data. It is therefore no need to tune the model parameters manually. On the other hand, a new measurement, Jensen-Shannon divergence is developed to quantify the similarity between the generated data and the real clutter data. Multiple comparative studies are made to demonstrate the advantages of the proposed framework and the effectiveness of the measurement.

articleTitle: Automatic target recognition of SAR images based on Transformer
abstract: In order to solve the overfitting problem of synthetic aperture radar automatic target recognition (SAR-ATR) at small samples scenarios, this paper proposes a non-subsampling laplace pyramid decomposition (NSLP) based vision transformer (VIT) model, namely NSLP-VIT, for SAR-ATR task. First, the SAR images are preprocessed by feature decomposition via NSLP; Second, a three-channel image is merged as the input of the network using three feature sub-maps; Finally, the preprocessed SAR images are as inputs for VIT network training. The experimental results on Moving and Stationary Target Acquisition and Recognition (MSTAR) data sets show that the proposed method can effectively solve the overfitting problem of SAR-ATR when the data is scarce.

articleTitle: Target Localization under Multi-Target Scenario with PA and FDA Radars
abstract: Target localization is an important task of radar and multiple targets may appear inside and outside the scanning beam in the surveillance area. This paper proposes a method for range and angle estimation under multi-target scenario with PA and FDA radars, i.e., dual-mode array radar. With the proposed method, the superiorities of PA and FDA in transmit are obtained simultaneously, providing the ability to improve the performance of parameters estimation for multiple targets. The algorithm firstly estimates the angles with received dual-mode array radar data, and then the ranges are estimated with the estimated angles using the FDA data. Simulation experiments are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed estimation method.

articleTitle: A method for the precession period estimation based on the recurrence plot
abstract: The estimation of the micro-motion period of ballistic target is of great significance for extracting target's features and distinguishing different targets. Taking the cone-cylindrical precession target as the research object, a method for estimating the precession period based on the recurrence plot is proposed. On the basis of analysis of the echo model, the time-frequency instantaneous power is calculated to estimate the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the echo, and the estimated value is used to solve the optimal distance threshold and thence the recurrence plot is conducted. The recurrence plot statistics is employed to estimate the period. Simulation experiment verifies the feasibility and robustness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Aiding AUV Localization Using a Dual-Sided Synthetic Aperture Sonar
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) navigation and localization is crucial and challenging in Global Positioning System-denied environments. AUV carrying synthetic aperture sonars (SASs) can provide precise motion estimation of the platforms. This study focuses on enhancing the performance of AUV localization using dual-sided SASs. The two-dimensional velocities of AUV are estimated using dual-sided SAS echoes. An extended Kalman filter (EKF) is then adopted for dead reckoning using the estimated velocities. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method has better localization accuracy than that of the Doppler velocity log (DVL).

articleTitle: Dimensionality reduction by regularized least squares weighted discriminant projection
abstract: In this paper, a new dimensionality reduction method, named regularized least squares weighted discriminant projection (RLSWDP), is developed to process high-dimensional signal which widely exists in real-world applications. In RLSWDP, all the representation coefficients are involved for samples reconstruction to improve reconstruction accuracy. Besides, the representation coefficients of each training sample are further used for weighting the reconstructed between-class scatter and within-class scatter which can preserve structural similarity between the samples resulting in better discrimination in projection space. Thirdly, a scale factor is introduced into the within-class weighting matrix to enhance the within-class compactness. Using the idea of maximum margin criterion, the optimal subspace projection matrix is obtained by eigenvalue decomposition. Experimental results on three face datasets demonstrate that the proposed method has promising performance compared to some popular dimensionality reduction methods.

articleTitle: L2.1/2-norm Regularization Based Unambiguous Sparse SAR Imaging
abstract: Sparse signal processing technique has shown signif-icant potential in high-resolution synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging. Compared with typical matched filtering (MF) based method, it can obtain high-quality image of sparse surveillance region from down-sampled echo data. In this paper, with the help of approximated observation technology, we propose an <tex>$L_{2,1/2}$</tex> -norm regularization based sparse SAR imaging method to process the echo data of large-scale sparse scene. Compared with typical <tex>$L_{q}$</tex> -norm <tex>$(0 < q\leq 1)$</tex> regularization based method, it can well suppress the azimuth ambiguity caused by the down-sampling. While compared with <tex>$L_{2,1}$</tex> -norm regularization based sparse SAR imaging algorithm, the proposed method can further improve the performance of recovered image and hence obtain the well focused sparse SAR image.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional imaging using the electromagnetic vortex synthetic aperture radar
abstract: The electromagnetic vortex (EMV) wave is so called for carrying the orbital angular momentum (OAM). It introduces the diversity in not only the along track propagation, but also in the wavefront plane. Combining the EMV wave with the traditional synthetic aperture imaging (SAR), this paper proposes a novel 3D imaging scheme, namely the EMV-SAR. First, the SAR echo is extended into 3D after involving the OAM mode domain. The 2D instantaneous information is thus obtained by one single pulse, not only the range information, and also the azimuth by simply applying Fourier transform to the OAM mode domain. Then a joint two-dimensional azimuthal compression algorithm is proposed for generating the 3D target imaging. The simulation results have validated the performance of the proposed system and algorithms, and demonstrated the superiority of the EMV-SAR for the 3D radar imaging.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Phase Noise Filtering Approach For Multi-Frequency Interferometric SAR
abstract: Multi-frequency (MF) interferometric SAR (InSAR) provides an effective way for the surveying of steep terrains. Phase noise filtering is a key step in MF-InSAR processing which determines the quality of the interferograms and affects the accuracy of inversed elevation. Different from the traditional filtering method of single frequency (SF) InSAR, an adaptive filtering approach for MF-InSAR based on MF phase fusion is proposed in this paper. The main contributions of this method is summarized into two aspects. First, the local fringe frequency estimation (LFFE) is extended from SF to MF case. Second, the non-linear model is introduced in the adaptive phase filtering in the local window based on MF-LFFE to adapt to complex terrains. The computer simulation and the real dual-frequency airborne experiment validate the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Effective minimum entropy algorithm for SAR ground moving target imaging
abstract: Ground moving target (GMT) is defocused and displaced in conventional synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image, because there exists the residual phase error of non-cooperative GMT motion. In this study, an effective minimum entropy algorithm (EMEA) for SAR ground moving target imaging (GMTIm) is proposed based on the range migration algorithm and region of interest (ROI) data. The moving target ROI data is extracted from conventional SAR image after RMA processing. Then, the image entropy function and its first-order derivative are constructed with respect to phase compensation parameter. EMEA uses the idea of bisection to shrink the parameter value range. The key point of this method is to shrink the parameter value range according to the sign of derivative of entropy function and ensure that the optimal parameter is always within the value range. When the algorithm converges, the optimal parameter occur and the refocused GMT image can be obtained using this parameter to compensate the residual phase error.

articleTitle: A novel Conformal T/R Module Based on Low Loss Flexible Printed Circuit Board
abstract: The research of the conformal T/R module based on low loss flexible PCB has been carried out in this study. Conventional microstrip and curved microstrips with a curved radius of 20mm, 15mm, 10mm and 5mm were fabricated using flexible PCB. The S-parameters measurement results showed that the insertion loss of curved microstrips was only reduced by 0.3 dB at 12 GHz. The conformal T/R module was developed, and the curved radius of the flexible PCB and the T/R chip were ∼40 mm and ∼35 mm, respectively. The transmission channel gain, receiver channel gain and receiving input VSWR of the conformal T/R module were 15.32 dB∼21.92 dB, 14.87 dB∼20.57 dB and 1.03-3.99 in the 8 GHz∼12 GHz bandwidth, respectively. And there was no RF performance deterioration compared with conventional components, which indicated that the conformal T/R module will have a great development prospect in the conformal active phased array antenna application.

articleTitle: A Novel Intelligent Wireless Sickroom Monitored by Micro-wave Sensors
abstract: Patients in traditional sickroom have to be connected with many cables to monitor the patient condition. In many conditions, the patient has to lie down on the sickbed. It confines the patient activity remarkably. In this paper, we propose a new king of sickroom which can monitor the patient condition intelligently with micro-wave sensors. The micro-wave sensors transmit pulses to illuminate the sickroom. The patient condition is recognized based on the Doppler effect caused by the patient activity. Compared to the traditional sickroom, our intelligent sickroom can provide more convenience. It will help increase the patient's lift quality in the hospital greatly.

articleTitle: A Blind Localization Method With Multi-point Scatterer Targets for BiSAR
abstract: Localization plays an important part in bistatic SAR (BiSAR). The accuracy of traditional localization method for BiSAR depends on whether the measurement position of platforms are precise or not. The lower the measurement accuracy, the higher imprecise the localization error of targets. This paper proposes a blind localization method with multi-point scatterer targets for BiSAR, which don't relays on the Global Position System (GPS) or Inertial Navigation System (INS) deeply. Firstly, Keystone Transform (KT) is used to realize range cell migration correction (RCMC). Next, the fractional Fourier transform (FrFT) is applied to estimate Doppler parameters. At last, establishing localization equation with the estimation parameters, and the Differential Evolution (DE) Algorithm is devoted to solve localization model constructed above. The effectiveness of the localization method proposed in this paper has been demonstrated and illustrated by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Adaptive detection of point-like target in presence of disturbance and wideband interference
abstract: In this paper, the problem of detecting point-like target in presence of both homogeneous disturbance and nonstationary interference is addressed. First, we propose a modified generalized likelihood ratio test (MGLRT) algorithm which restricts the received signal into a reasonable subspace to avoid the influence of unwanted interference. Meanwhile, to determine the parameters of the subset space, a representation subspace to describe the wideband interference signals is adopted. Secondly, we give the expressions for the false alarm probability and detection probability. Finally, extensive simulations are conducted to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed detector. It is demonstrated that the proposed detector has a constant false alarm rate (CFAR) property against homogeneous disturbance.

articleTitle: Data Classification Algorithms for Complex Heavy-Tailed Distributions
abstract: This paper deals with the adaptive classification problem of heavy-tailed data drawn from a multivariate distribution of the complex elliptically symmetric family. The authors assume that the collected data is either homogeneous or partially homogeneous. Based on the GLRT criterion, two adaptive classifiers are devised for the scenarios of Hermitian and persymmetric scatter matrices, respectively. To estimate the unknown parameters, iterative algorithms with convergence property are introduced to solve the developed non-convex maximum likelihood optimization problems. The simulation results show that, compared with the Hermitian scenario, the exploitation of persymmetric structure information can lead to an obvious performance improvement.

articleTitle: Vegetation Height Retrieval Based On Linearity Selection Of Polarimetric Interferometry SAR
abstract: At present, the vegetation height retrieval methods are based on the random volume over ground (RVOG) model to analyze the distribution of coherence coefficient (CC) of Polarimetric interferometry synthetic aperture radar (PoIInSAR) in complex unit circle under different polarization states. However, most of these methods do not consider the distribution shape of CC of PoIInSAR. In practice, due to the influence of noise, the distribution shape of Polarimetric interferometry CC may be irregular or even circular. At this time, there is a large error in the surface fitting. In order to solve the problems, this paper proposes a linear measurement criterion for the distribution region of the CC of Polarimetric interferometry. When the linearity of CC distribution is higher than a certain threshold, the terrain phase of pixels participating in vegetation height inversion is obtained directly according to the straight line fitting; on the contrary, the terrain phase at the point is obtained by the complex value interpolation of adjacent pixels. At the same time, the volume scattering phase is obtained by maximizing the interferometry complex CC difference, so as to effectively improve the accuracy of vegetation inversion. The PolSARpro software provided by ESA is used to simulate the vegetation at different heights in L-band, and the effectiveness of the vegetation height retrieval method proposed in this paper is verified.

articleTitle: Land-Sea Contamination Analysis for the Interferometric Radiometers Onboard the Chinese Ocean Salinity Satellite
abstract: The Chinese Ocean Salinity Satellite is part of the Chinese ocean dynamic satellite series, and is dedicated to global SSS observation with two payloads onboard. These two payloads, named the Interferometric Microwave Radiometer (IMR) and the Microwave Imager Combined Active and Passive (MICAP), both adopt interferometric aperture synthesis technology. To analyzes the Land-Sea Contamination (LSC), which is one of the mainly issues that degrades the salinity measurement in coastal areas for an interferometric radiometer, we perform a simulation to compare the LSC effect for the two different L-band interferometric radiometers. Results and a preliminary strategy to mitigate the LSC are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Research on integrated wireless communication and control Microsystems with thick-thin film hybrid technology based on double-sided cavity
abstract: In this paper, a wireless communication and control microsystem based on double-sided cavity with thick and thin film hybrid integration is designed. The system adopts the form of fully sealed ceramic and metal mixed double-sided cavity. The digital analog hybrid circuit and RF transceiver circuit are physically isolated in separate cavities. The cavities are electrically interconnected through the coaxial vertical transmission structure surrounded by copper column medium; The substrate adopts BCB/Cu thin film multilayer interconnection technology based on L TCC to realize high-density integration of Microsystems and high-quality signal transmission. The overall dimension of the sample is only 40mm × 40 mm ×10 mm, weighing 40g. The volume is reduced by two-thirds compared with the traditional LTCC single-sided cavity integration. The test results show that the return loss of RF signal transmission of vertical interconnection structure is less than − 20dB and the insertion loss is less than 0.5dB, which meets the requirements of S/X-band signal transmission performance; The functions of data acquisition, processing, modulation and demodulation of baseband digital analog circuit are normal. The transmission power of microwave circuit is 38dBmw; The clutter suppression is no less than 55dBc;The third harmonic suppression is no less than 45dBc, and the reception sensitivity of microwave circuit is no more than − 98dBm.

articleTitle: An Offboard Active Jamming Countermeasure Based on Monopulse Three-Dimensional Imaging
abstract: Offboard active jamming is an important means for warships against monopulse radar. By amplifying and forwarding radar signal, offboard active jammer forms centroid jamming with the actual warship echo. This paper proposes a new method based on monopulse three-dimensional(3-D) imaging against this kind of jamming. Firstly, the monopulse radar performs Inverse synthetic-aperture radar(ISAR) imaging and motion compensation processing on the three-channel signals to obtain the high-resolution distribution in range and Doppler. Then monopulse angle measurement is performed on each high-resolution cell of imaging. According to the range, azimuth and elevation information of each resolution cell, three views of the warship with jamming can be reconstructed. Finally, according to the three views, the singular points outside of the warship caused by jamming can be eliminated by setting appropriate threshold. The simulation results verify the effectiveness of the monopulse 3-D imaging in offboard active jamming mitigation. The technology has important significance for monopulse radar against angle deception of mainlobe interference.

articleTitle: Ship Target Recognition in SAR Image with Implicit Complex Information Enhancement
abstract: At present, most scholars treat Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images as optical images when deep learning methods are used to study them, and only the amplitude information of SAR images is applied while the complex information is ignored. However, SAR images are essentially complex images, so this paper proposes a SAR image ship target recognition method with implicit complex information enhancement in the input layer, which implicitly provides a complex information representation of the input data by combining the real, imaginary and amplitude three-channel information of SAR images. Experimental validation on the OpenSARShip dataset and experimental comparison using classical neural network methods can reveal that the method in this paper improves the effect of neural network-based ship target recognition to a certain extent.

Index Terms: ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge

articleTitle: Joint translational and rotational compensation for space target ISAR imaging
abstract: Joint motion compensation can simultaneously correct the range shift and phase error caused by translational motion, which is convenient for high-resolution inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging. In ISAR imaging of space targets, the rotation of space target is the combination of the change of radar line of sight and the rotation caused by the target spin. Most works ignore the relative rotation caused by the target spin and thus deteriorate the performance of this promoting method. Therefore, this paper proposes a joint translational and rotational phase compensation method, which considers the effects of target motion and body rotation on joint motion compensation, constructs the compensation formula according to the minimum entropy criterion, and then uses the quasi-Newton method to solve the minimum entropy optimization problem.

articleTitle: Ground Clutter Suppression for Weather Radar Using An Improved Wavelet Method
abstract: For removing ground clutter signals in weather radar, we propose an improved wavelet method based on an adaptive threshold in this paper. In the wavelet domain, ground clutter signals are distributed in the low-frequency layer after wavelet decomposition and the meteorological signals usually exist in other high-frequency layers. We process wavelet coefficients using the threshold to suppress clutter signals, and reserve meteorological signals as many as possible. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified using real weather radar data. It has a small computational load and is easy to implement.

articleTitle: Design of Pulse-Coded Waveforms Resilient to Pulse Eclipsing via Majorization-Minimization Framework
abstract: For a duplex radar, especially which operates with high pulse repetition frequency (PRF), the eclipsing phenomenon leads to a significant increase in sidelobe levels after matching filtering, which is due to the loss of return echoes when the receiver is turned off during the transmission of a pulse. The solutions of this problem mainly focus on signal processing that requires high computational complexity. In this paper, we establish a criterion to assess the sidelobe levels with pulse eclipsing taken into consideration, and then we propose a majorization-minimization based method to reduce the sidelobe levels in this scenario. Numerical experiments show that the proposed algorithm is effective.

articleTitle: A Novel Radar Antenna Design by an Adaptive Tent Chaotic Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm
abstract: In this work, the Adaptive Tent Chaotic Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm is used to design a shaped radiation pattern of 77GHz Millimeter Radar antenna. This algorithm searches the optimized amplitude and phase weights for antenna elements to form a Flat-Shoulder beam pattern. And according to these data, the six-way power divider is designed for the 6*10 plane antenna array. This approach gives satisfactory results for the radar flat-shoulder beam array antenna design.

Author Keywords: Adaptive Teant Chaotiv Artificial Bee Colony algorithm

articleTitle: Robust Direction of Arrival Estimation Method after Clutter Cancellation in Passive Radar
abstract: In a passive radar, target signals will be inevitably mixed in the reference channel due to the existence of antenna sidelobes. In this case, adaptive clutter cancellation will cause an error on the target's steering vector, which results in a direction of arrival (DOA) estimation bias. To this end, this paper proposed a DOA estimation method to correct the bias. Simulations verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: BRIMA Model: Innovation Shapes Radar Future
abstract: Glorious development of radar in the past century is actually a history of radar innovation, focusing on the continuous and innovative evolution in multiple dimensions such as requirements, technology, engineering and support to satisfy the increasing detection needs. From the perspective of organic thinking or system engineering, this paper comprehensively explores the universal laws and innovation-driving model in radar technology innovation, and puts forward RTES radar innovation ecosystem and a BRIMA radar technology innovation model. Finally, future technical development trends of radar are briefly described based on this BRIMA model.

articleTitle: A New Polarimetric Decomposition Method for Compact Polarimetric SAR Data
abstract: The compact polarimetric (CP) synthetic aperture radar (SAR) can alleviate the drawbacks of the fully polarimetric (FP) SAR and provide more target information compared to the conventional single polarimetric and dual polarimetric mode. However, the present decomposition methods for CP SAR have the problem of overestimation of volume scattering (OVS) among urban areas, especially the obliquely oriented buildings (OOBs). In this paper, a new descriptor of OOBs for the CP SAR is introduced to reduce the volume scattering in the urban areas. Then a new model-based decomposition method, which is applicable for the π/4 mode, is proposed based on the urban descriptor. The Radarsat-2 FP SAR data is used to simulate the CP SAR data to validate our algorithm. The proposed method improves the double-bounce scattering component in different types of urban areas by above 10%.

articleTitle: Radar Target Data Association with Amplitude and Tracking Information
abstract: In the radar data association problem, amplitude and state information of target returns are widely used in tracking algorithms, and typically many methods combine them. However, except from uniting them, constructing the correlation model among different instants returns is rarely considered. It is known that there is numerous information in radar target returns, but it is complicated to make comprehensive consideration. In this paper, we not only approximate the joint distribution of squared amplitudes based on the Copula function but unite the state information of target returns. Regarding squared amplitudes as statistics to derive the conditional probability density function (PDF), combine with state information to predict the scope of latter instant statistics, which can be used to improve certain anti-interference performance in the target-detection-during-tracking problem. Furthermore, this algorithm will consider about kinematic state and give the most reasonable measurement the highest possibility among the numerous ones radar receiving. And numerical results will be utilized to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Clutter Spectrum Estimation for Distributed Small Satellite Space-based Early Warning Radar
abstract: Distributed small satellite space-based early warning radar has the problem of grating lobes and obvious clutter, which has a negative effect on clutter suppression. To solve this problem, we establish the clutter signal model of the system and propose the combination of virtual and real apertures. In this method, the echo signal of the subsequent pulse is equivalent to the echo signal of the virtual array elements by using time for space. The simulation results of clutter spectrum and minimum detectable velocity show the effectiveness of the proposed method and we can get the same performance as a large ULA.

Author Keywords: distributed small satellite space-based early warning radar
combination of virtual and real apertures

articleTitle: Frequency-Phase Coded Waveform Analytic Design Method for Transmit Beampattern Synthesis of MIMO Radar
abstract: Time-space-frequency related transmit beampattern can be obtained by circulating coded MIMO radar. However, the existence of relative time delay between elements will cause transient interval problem. Therefore, avoiding transient interval problem and obtaining a time-space-frequency related transmit beampattern have become the interest of research. To solve this problem, a novel waveform analytic design method based on frequency-phase coded waveform is proposed. Firstly, the relationship between parameters set of frequency-phase coded waveform and the instantaneous beampattern of MIMO radar is derived. Then, the analytical solution for parameters of frequency-phase coded waveform is provided for arbitrary transmit beampattern synthesis based on such relationship. The transmit beampattern obtained is still time-space-frequency related. The computational burden of this method is negligible. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Progress and Prospects of Anti-drone Radar Detection Technology
abstract: In recent years, with the high-speed development of digital signal processing technology (DSP) and very large scale integrated circuit technology (VLSI), the current hardware platform provides good technical support for radar signal processing technology towards the development direction of more refined and intelligent processing. Radar signal processing technology is no longer satisfied with the level of detecting the presence or absence of targets; by extending the information dimension and acquiring the ability to refine target characteristics, radar signal processing for target detection and identification technology will also see greater development. This paper summaries the problems and difficulties of existing radar research on small UAV detection, and provides an outlook on the development of UAV target detection and recognition technology in complex scenarios in the future.

Author Keywords: universal and software-based signal processing platforms

articleTitle: Dinkelbach-Based Algorithm for Transmit Sequence Design in MIMO Radar with One-bit DACs
abstract: In this paper, the problem of waveform design for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar which deploys one-bit digital-to-analog converts (DACs) is investigated. To reach a good radiation property, we consider to minimize the integrated sidelobe to mainlobe ratio (ISMR) of the transmit beampattern via designing the one-bit transmit sequence. However, the resulting optimization problem, which consisted of quadratic fractional objective function and binary constraint, is NP-hard and difficult to solve directly. To this end, a continuous and differentiable function is first utilized to approximate the one-bit waveform. By doing so, the discrete constraint is automatically removed and hence a novel optimization problem will be recast. Leveraging on the Dinkelbach method, the reformulated problem is well solved with the closed-form solution. Numerical simulation results are utilized to demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method compared with some existing method.

articleTitle: Application of Steering Vectors Rotation Invariance in DOA Estimation with Mutual Coupling
abstract: The mutual coupling phenomenon between the array elements adversely affects the mutual position estimation in a uniform linear array (ULA). Inspired by the idea of ESPRIT, a novel direction of arrival (DOA) estimation algorithm based on the rotation invariance of the modified steering vectors is proposed to estimate DOAs under mutual coupling error by blind signal separation (BSS). The algorithm denoise at the beginning with the help of the signal subspace. To estimate the modified steering vector, a BSS algorithm named Joint Approximate Diagonalization of Eigenmatrices (JADE) is presented. Finally, the rotation invariance between particular elements of the modified steering vector can be used to estimate the DOAs. The proposed algorithm only needs to solve several one-variable equations to obtain the DOA estimates, which reduces the amount of calculation. The simulation results show that the algorithm can obtain more accurate estimates under the condition of low SNR.

articleTitle: A Moving Target Detection Method Based on NPET-RPCA for SAR Systems
abstract: Robust principal component analysis (RPCA) is an important method for synthetic aperture radar-ground moving target indication (SAR-GMTI). However, the phase difference among channels caused by the velocity of the moving target is not sensitive to the correlation coefficient. It results in that the conditions of applying RPCA method cannot be satisfied in an arbitrary environment. To solve the problem, a novel phase envelope transform-robust principal component analysis (NPET-RPCA) method is proposed. The correlation coefficient among channels for moving target is decreased by the proposed method under the condition that the sparsity of the target remains unchanged. Meanwhile, the azimuth velocity could be estimated by the positions of the focused points. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Simplified Simulation Method of Actuators for Active Adjustment of Panels of Large Antennas
abstract: The structures of actuators are complicated. In the simulation process of active adjustment of large reflector antenna, it takes more time and effort to model the actuator, and the calculation time will be longer, so the actuator should be simplified. A short beam is used instead of the actuator to realize the simulation process of active adjustment of the antenna. The finite element method is used to give the relationship between the actuator adjustment and the load. The load of each actuator is calculated when the adjustment quantity is entered. Applying the load to ANSYS results in an error of less than 10<sup>−10</sup> mm.

articleTitle: JCMF: A Novel Wideband DOA Estimator
abstract: Covariance matrix fitting is a classic problem in direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation, but there has been little discussion about wideband signals. In this paper, a novel wideband DOA estimation method based on covariance matrix fitting is developed. First of all, a novel wideband signal model is proposed and the wideband joint covariance matrix is formulated. The fitting criterion is deduced by the statistical characteristics of this model. Then the optimization problem of the criterion is transformed into a block sparsity problem using Holder's inequality. The problem can be divided into two subproblems and the closed-form solution of each part is obtained by dual method. The result of our wideband estimator can be solved by alternating iteration. Finally, the Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) is derived for wideband signals. Compared with other algorithms, the presented estimator has higher accuracy. Simulation results show the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Angle-Doppler Channel Construction in Reduced Dimension STAP for Sparse Nonuniform Array
abstract: This paper considers the channel construction problem for the reduced dimension space-time adaptive processing (RD-STAP) for the sparse nonuniform array. Typical channel construction method is not appropriate to the sparse nonuniform array. To address this issue, a novel channel construction method based on the zero points of the array pattern is proposed. The proposed method can provide more suitable angle-Doppler channels for the sparse nonuniform array with better performance. Simulations are conducted for validating the proposed method and demonstrating their high performance.

articleTitle: Transmit Beamforming Design for LPI of Frequency Diverse Array MIMO Radar
abstract: The paper considers the design of the transmit beamforming for low probability of intercept (LPI) of multiple-input multiple-output with frequency diverse array (FDA-MIMO) radar in the presence of signal-independent interference. The design criterion is minimizing the ratio of the transmit power level to the output SINR level under energy constraint at each transmitter. Since the objection function is single-ratio fractional programming (FP) problem, a cyclic optimization algorithm based on the minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) and the power method-like iterations (PMLI) technique is proposed to solve it. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed joint designs in terms of the output SINR value, the transmit and receive beampattern.

articleTitle: Ship Classification in High-Resolution SAR Images Based on CNN Regional Feature Fusion
abstract: Ship classification is a multi-level and multi-category target recognition research, among them, military-civilian ship classification plays a significance role in maritime target monitoring. Nowadays, with the development of spaceborne SAR systems, the resolution and quality of SAR images have further been improved. Ship targets in high-resolution SAR images show clear geometric structure and scattering characteristics, which is conductive to military-civilian ship classification. Considering the adaptive feature extraction ability of convolutional neural network (CNN) and the structural characteristics of ships in high-resolution SAR images, a military-civilian ship classification method based on CNN regional feature fusion is proposed in this paper. Proposed method can be divided into three parts: obtaining Minimum Bounding Rectangle (MBR) of ship target in SAR images, global and local CNN feature extraction, and adaptive feature fusion for ship classification. To verify method proposed in this paper, we conducted extensive experiments on the high-resolution SAR images obtained by GF-3 satellite. The experimental results show that our method can effectively classify military and civilian ships with an accuracy rate of over 90%.

articleTitle: Design of Echo Information Processing Platform Based on VPX Bus
abstract: The echo information processing platform is an important part of the phased array radar system. With the increasing demands of the airborne phased array radar mission on bus transmission bandwidth, computational processing speed, system response time, and data processing capability, the traditional echo information processing platform has been difficult to meet the requirements of technological development. Based on the advantages of high transmission bandwidth, rich I/O resources and strong scalability of VPX bus, this paper proposes a design scheme of echo information processing platform based on VPX bus, focusing on the composition of information processing platform and the design principle of each functional module. Based on the idea of dataflow driving, a new peer-to-peer backplane architecture is adopted. The test results show that the information processing platform only needs 20.2s to complete 32K*32K complex image processing. The performance is superior, stable and reliable.

articleTitle: Analysis on Wind Profiling Radar Data of a Rainstorm at Lin’an
abstract: A Meiyu front rainstorm process from June 23rd to June 24th, 2017 has been analyzed in detail by using CFL-03 boundary-layer wind profiling radar at Lin'an, and the results show that wind profiling radar observations are able to reflect characteristics of meso-scale vortex shear line during the meiyu front system. The main reason why the precipitation was relatively concentrated at the beginning and end of this process is that low-level wind shear happened to move over Lin'an during those periods. Due to upper level jet this rainstorm has lasted for a long time. Except wind profiles, radar echo intensity has been estimated by power spectrum data to analyze the details of developments of the rainstorm, and it is found that precipitation clouds have developed vigorously with height over 5 km. Other wind profiling radar products, such as, vertical velocity and atmospheric refractive index structure constant, both have changed in a identical way comparing with the precipitation. When the precipitation is above 10 mm, vertical velocity is around 7 m/s and logarithm of atmospheric refractive index structure constant is about -11. Consequently wind profiling radar products can be used to monitor rainstorms and serve in operational systems.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Multi-beam Forming Method for Planar Array based on Improved Gravitational Search Algorithm
abstract: In this paper, an improved gravitational search algorithm (IGSA) is proposed for the requirements of the simultaneous multi-beam forming (SMBF) of large scale planar array. Here, the SMBF of large scale planar array is viewed as an optimization problem with excitation amplitudes and phases being the optimization variables, attaining sidelobe suppression, pencil beams and high gains being the optimization objectives. For this optimization problem, IGSA is introduced, and the adaptive modified particle structure is used to enhance the capability of global explorating, which further improves IGSA's performance. For this multi-objective optimization problem, inverse gradient weighting operation is used to enhance the capability of multi-objective optimization. Finally, IGSA is verified in simulation experiments of the SMBF of planar array, and the results are compared with other excellent random optimization algorithms. The results demonstrate that the proposed IGSA is superior to other algorithms in the SMBF of planar array performance with a lower sidelobe level, more satisfactory pencil beams and higher gains and realizes SMBF for 100–200 array elements while performance of other algorithms is insufficient.

articleTitle: Multi-Feature Fusion Recognition of Space Micromotion Target
abstract: This paper proposes a recognition method of space micro-motion targets based on decision fusion. The proposed method extracts a 7-dimension(7D) feature vector including the information of time, Doppler, joint time-frequency(JTF) domains from the radar cross section (RCS); while extracts the inverse Radon transform pseudo-Zernike (IRT-pZ) feature from the JTF image. Finally, particle swarm optimization (PSO) is adopted to decision-level fusion, so as to realize high-precision recognition. The recognition results of electromagnetic simulated data under various conditions have demonstrated the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Single Encoder-decoder Network for both Sea-land Segmentation and Small Vessel Detection in SAR Images
abstract: The detection performance of small vessels in n-earshore SAR images is easily affected by land false alarms. Therefore sea-land segmentation is usually performed before vessel detection. However, it requires separate training and inference for the segmentation and detection tasks which are time-consuming. Moreover, the two tasks do not benefit each other in sharing global semantic and feature information. In this paper, a single encoder-decoder network for both sea-land segmentation and small vessel detection was proposed. The global semantic information of sea-land segmentation is introduced in the optimization process of the small vessel detection model by back-propagating the joint sea-land segmentation loss and vessel detection loss. Considering the sampling differences between sea-land segmentation and small vessel detection, a dilate-encoder module was added to the sea-land segmentation layer to extract global semantic information to optimize the sea-land segmentation performance. Experimental results on the Sentinel-l data set verified that the proposed method not only reduced miss detections and land false alarms but also improved the accuracy of sea-land segmentation.

articleTitle: Estimation of 2-D DOA for Coherently Distributed Non-circular Sources
abstract: The paper presents a novel estimator for two-dimensional (2-D) direction-of-arrival (DOA) of coherently distributed (CD) non-circular signals utilizing two uniform linear arrays (ULAs). The proposed method firstly divides the two ULAs into three subarrays, thus three output matrices can be obtained and the generalized steering vector has the rotational invariance characteristic. Then extend the array output matrices using the non-circularity of the signals, and the extended generalized steering vector still has the rotational invariance characteristic. At last, the central DOAs can be calculated by ESPRIT-like method. This paper also provides examples to validate the performance of the novel estimator. Simulation results validated that the proposed estimator owns the best performance compared with two existing methods.

articleTitle: A Method to Improve OAM Mode Purity Based on Antenna Array
abstract: OAM (Orbital angular momentum) waves have infinite orthogonal modes. The azimuth information of the target and the number of modes have dual relations. Thus, OAM waves have huge potential in improving imaging resolution. However, OAM waves generated by many methods in microwave field have the problem of superfluous modes. Thus, a method based on antenna array to reduce the number of superfluous OAM modes is proposed in this paper. Besides, the antenna array can improve the mode purity of OAM waves.

articleTitle: Space mapping based extracts parasitic parameters of movable lead interconnection in microwave circuits
abstract: As a bridge between circuit modules, microwave circuit interconnection not only needs to meet the reliability of mechanical connection, but also needs to ensure the complete transmission of electromagnetic signals between circuits. With the increase of the operating frequency of microwave circuits, circuit interconnection has significantly restricted the improvement of microwave circuit signal transmission performance. Aiming at the active phased array antenna T/R component circuit movable lead interconnection structure, this paper establishes the movable lead interconnection parametric characterization model and equivalent circuit model. The space mapping method is used to extract the parameters of the interconnected equivalent circuit, so that the response of the equivalent circuit model is close to the response of the fine structure electromagnetic model, and the correctness of the equivalent circuit model is verified. This paper can quickly and accurately obtain the equivalent circuit parameters of the movable lead interconnection, so as to provide theoretical guidance for the accurate and rapid realization of electromagnetic transmission performance prediction and interconnection optimization design control.

articleTitle: Narrow-Band Interference Suppression Method for SAR Based on CEEMD
abstract: Narrow-band interference (NBI) is a common form of interference in SAR systems, severely reducing the quality of SAR images. The NBI suppression method based on empirical mode decomposition (EMD) can adaptively split the raw signal into multiple independent intrinsic modal functions (IMFs), and reconstruct the useful signal after removing the IMFs of the NBI. However, the mode mixing problem it brings will cause part of the useful signal to be removed simultaneously when removing the NBI. A novel NBI suppression method based on complementary ensemble EMD (CEEMD) is proposed in this paper to solve this problem. First, the moment kurtosis coefficient is used to detect the presence of NBI in the raw echo, and CEEMD is used to decompose the NBI-contained raw echo into a series of IMFs. Then, the second-order difference of permutation entropy (PE) of all IMFs is calculated to obtain the global threshold for distinguishing IMFs with NBI and useful signal. Finally, the target IMF is used to reconstruct useful signals to remove the NBI. Experimental results based on real C-band spaceborne SAR data with simulated NBI verify the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Sparse Aperture ISAR Imaging Based on UNet++
abstract: This article proposes a modified UNet++ for effective sparse aperture inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging. Firstly, Mapping from the true distribution of scattering centers to the original ISAR images is established. Then, modified UNet++ is used for sparse aperture ISAR imaging. The optimal network parameters can be obtained by end-to-end training using simulated data with different SNR. Experimental results have shown that the UNet++ can achieve noise-stable sparse aperture ISAR imaging with superior performance on both simulated and measured data.

articleTitle: Superpixel Generation for SAR Image Based on Fast Clustering and Merging with Edge Penalty
abstract: In this paper, we propose an adaptive superpixel generation algorithm for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image, which is implemented based on fast clustering and merging with edge penalty. The superpixel generation algorithm consists of two stages, i.e., fast clustering and merging. In the clustering stage, we define a new adaptive pixel dissimilarity measure for SAR image and then optimize the Density Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) strategy, which considers the edge information and achieves rapid clustering. In the merging stage, based on the initial superpixels, a new superpixel dissimilarity measure is defined, which can merge the small local superpixels into their neighborhood superpixels, making the final superpixel segmentation compact and regular. Experimental results on real SAR images demonstrate that our method outperforms the state-of-the-art superpixel generation methods in terms of both efficiency and accuracy.

articleTitle: Improved Chirplet time-frequency atom for signal decomposition and its application to micro-Doppler analysis
abstract: Radar micro-Doppler (m-D) is the phenomenon of the observed micro-motions on top of the bulk main Doppler component of a target's motion. The micro-Doppler features of radar target returns were extracted through various time-frequency (T-F) analyses. The new method for T-F analysis is based on dictionary decomposition, in which the time-frequency signal is decomposed into a combination of time-frequency atoms. In view of the weak decomposition performance of Chirplet time-frequency atoms for sinusoidal type nonlinear frequency modulated (NLFM) signals, an Improved Chirplet (IChirplet) T-F atom is proposed. Firstly, the mismatch problem of T-F distribution of Chirplet time frequency atom to sinusoidal type is analyzed theoretically. Secondly, sinusoidal frequency modulation factor is added to Chirplet time frequency atom to make the time frequency curve of the atom produce the flexural performance of the sine like shape. Finally, the genetic algorithm is used instead of matching pursuit algorithm to improve the efficiency of the atomic search. The simulation results show that the decomposition performance of the IChirplet atom for the NLFM signal has greatly improved compared with the Gabor, Chirplet, and FM<sup>m</sup>let atoms. We apply the IChirplet T-F atom to m-D signals analysis. The simulation results show that it is capable of separating the micro-motions from translation in IChirplet parameter domain.

articleTitle: Multi-aspect Tomographic SAR Imaging Approach via Distributed Compressed Sensing and Joint Sparsity
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) tomography (TomoSAR) is a novel technique that enables three-dimensional (3-D) imaging and plays an important role in urban remote sensing by utilizing multiple observations of the same target scene from various baselines. Canonical TomoSAR observations are from a single aspect, which has been well studies already. However, modern SAR sensors such as Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) allow us to achieve multi-aspect TomoSAR data of the same target scene. This paper proposes a novel framework named “Multi-aspect TomoSAR,” which takes advantage of rich TomoSAR data from multiple observation aspects. We derive the multi-aspect TomoSAR signal model using distributed compressed sensing (DCS) and adopt a simultaneous sparse approximation algorithm named SOMP to solve the joint sparsity model. Numerical results on synthetic simulated data show that the multi-aspect estimation can provide more accurate estimation, yield a promising perspective.
