Experimental results on real airborne data will be reported in the journal version of this work later.

articleTitle: An Effective and Efficient Synthesis Technique for Linear Array Thinning
abstract: In this contribution we will discuss the fast synthesis of thinning uniformly spaced linear arrays that are going to become a key technology of 5G. The new technique is proposed for the synthesis of linear array thinning which aims at reducing peak sidelobe level. By means of the iterative Chirp-Z transform integrated with an adaptively changing fill factor mechanism, a modified iterative Chirp-Z transform (MICZT) technique is then presented. This technique solves the problems of the huge amount of computation and ease to fall into local optimal. Moreover, the technique can ensure that some characteristics of the optimized element distribution are similar to the uniform counterparts. And the effectiveness and efficiency of the MICZT technique will be validated by two representative examples and compared with the published results.

articleTitle: Hybrid Transmitter and Radar Receiver Design for OFDM Dual-Functional Radar-Communication
abstract: This paper considers the design of hybrid transmitter and radar receiver for broadband orthogonal frequency division multiplexing dual-function radar-communication (OFDM-DFRC) systems. A weighted optimization problem which takes the performances of radar and communication into account is formulated. Specifically, the analog beamformer for the entire bandwidth and the digital beamformer and radar receiver for each subcarrier are jointly optimized. In order to solve the weighted optimization problem, a consensus alternating direction method of multiplier (CADMM) based on linear approximation (LA) is proposed. Numerical simulation results are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

Author Keywords: consensus alternating direction method of multiplier (CADMM)

articleTitle: Matching of Scattering Centers Based on 3-D Scattering Center Model with Application to SAR ATR
abstract: This letter proposes a scattering center matching method based on 3-D scattering center model with application to synthetic aperture radar (SAR) automatic target recognition (ATR). The 2-D scattering centers predicted by 3-D scattering center model are matched with the extracted scattering centers from the test image using a neighbor matching algorithm. The matching result is quantitatively evaluated by five indexes. The neighbor matching efficiently builds robust correspondences between the model-predicted and extracted scattering center sets. And the five indexes comprehensively evaluate the similarity between the two scattering center sets. Afterwards, a one-against-one voting strategy is performed based on the five indexes for target recognition. To evaluate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method, experiments are conducted on the simulated data of three ground targets by electromagnetic (EM) code under various conditions.

articleTitle: A New Feature Extraction Method Based on Micro-Doppler Signature of Ground Moving Targets
abstract: Since some discriminative features are required for ground moving targets classification, we propose a new feature extraction method based on micro-Doppler signature. Firstly, the time-frequency analysis of measured data indicates that the time-frequency spectrograms of the three kinds of ground moving targets, i.e., single walking person, two people walking and a moving wheeled vehicle, are discriminative. Then, a 3-dimensional time-frequency feature vector is extracted from the time-frequency spectrograms to depict these differences. At last, a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier is trained with the proposed 3-dimensional feature vector. The classification accuracy to categorize ground moving targets into the three kinds on the measured data is found to be over 96%, which demonstrates the good discriminative ability of the proposed micro-Doppler feature.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Metasurface Aperture Imaging via Information-Theoretic Waveform Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Computation microwave imaging with frequency diverse metasurface (FDM) is an emerging technology. In this paper, we introduce our unique completed FDM microwave imaging system and address the problem of waveform design based on the information-theory to enhance the advantages of the FDM imaging. The waveform design methods for the FDM imaging system to decrease the reconstruction mean square error (MSE) with determined energy is proposed. The performances of the proposed methods are evaluated by the data gathered by the experimental FDM imaging system. The results show that the proposed methods can improve the quality of the imaging of the FDM imaging system.

articleTitle: Research on FMEA and FTA of displacement actuator for radio telescope
abstract: In order to improve the reliability of the displacement actuator used in the active surface of large aperture radio telescope, the Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) and Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) of the actuator are carried out based on the meta action theory. On the basis of the original method, this paper balances the analysis proportion of mechanical transmission unit and electronic and electrical unit, and applies it to actuator, an electromechanical equipment. Through the structural decomposition of FMA, the failure mode of meta action unit is studied. Furthermore, the complete failure analysis results of the displacement actuator are obtained.

articleTitle: A-RANSAC Instantaneous Frequency Estimator for Multicomponent Signals in Heavy-noise Environments
abstract: An adaptive random-samples-consensus (ARANSAC) algorithm is proposed for the instantaneous frequency (IF) estimation of multicomponent signals. This estimator can work for low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) environments without the prior knowledge of component numbers. The estimation performance is tested on overlapping frequency modulation (FM) signals. Obtained results show that the estimator achieves a lower SNR threshold than 0 dB.

articleTitle: Vortex Radar Super-resolution Imaging Based on Iterative Adaptive Approach
abstract: The vortex radar transmits electromagnetic waves carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM), which obtains more azimuthal information than the plane wave, and has great application potential in the field of radar detection and imaging. However, the azimuth resolution is limited to OAM modes. In this paper, an iterative adaptive super-resolution method is proposed for vortex radar imaging. Firstly, the azimuthal targets detection problem is transformed into a parameter estimation problem, the echo autocorrelation matrix is reconstructed. Then the weighted cost function is updated iteratively based on the weighted least-squares criterion. Finally, the targets are obtained after iterations. Simulation results showed the effectiveness of the iterative adaptive approach on azimuth super-resolution of vortex radar with fewer OAM modes.

articleTitle: Influence of Marine Climate on Corrosion of Common Materials for Electronic Equipment
abstract: According to the corrosion status of electronic equipment in service in many places along the coast, the corrosion and aging characteristics of common materials and protection technology of electronic equipment caused by main coastal environmental factors were analyzed. And puts forward some suggestions for material selection and protection of equipment, which plays an important role in improving the adaptability of electronic equipment in marine environment and has certain reference significance for other equipment to carry out similar research.

articleTitle: Robust Beamforming Based on Covariance Matrix Reconstruction and ADMM
abstract: Considering at the issue that the performance of the traditional beamforming algorithm will decrease sharply when the disturbance occurs at the disturbed position and the steering vector mismatch occurs, a new robust beamforming method based on covariance matrix reconstruction and Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) is proposed. Firstly, based on the maximum output power criterion of beamformers, an optimization model is designed to solve the optimal steering vector. Then, the covariance matrix is reconstructed by using the defined interference range to widen the nullity and enhance the anti-motion interference ability of the system. Then, for the quadratic inequality constraint problem of the steering vector, this paper uses ADMM to solve the model iteratively, and obtains the specific solution of the steering vector in each iteration. In addition, the complexity of the algorithm is also analyzed. The experimental results show that, compared with the existing beamforming algorithms, the proposed method Widen the width of zero notch in the interference area, improves the anti-interference performance of the beam, and can well correct the mismatched steering vector.

articleTitle: A Synthetic Wideband Profiling Method for High-Speed Target Based on Echo Model Inversion
abstract: Synthetic wideband high-resolution range profile is one of the important fields and it has great prospect in the field of imaging and feature extraction. In this paper, a synthetic wideband profiling method for high-speed target based on echo model inversion is proposed. Base on the derivation of echo model, the influence of target high-speed motion is analyzed and concluded in three aspects: the intrapulse Doppler modulation, the range migration and the modulation factor. The influence of the intrapulse Doppler modulation and the range migration could be well compensated and eliminated after obtaining the high accurate phase-derived velocity measurement results. In order to suppress the influence of modulation factor, a novel matched reference signal containing the modulation factor is constructed and applied in the matched filtering process. After that, the proposed wideband synthesis algorithm is presented. Simulations are conducted to verify the proposed method and high quality focused high-resolution range profiles are obtained.

articleTitle: Improved SSD Framework for Automatic Subsurface Object Indentification for GPR Data Processing
abstract: Problems such as high attenuation cause the hyperbolic characteristics of B-scan being interfered by clutter in ground penetrating radar (GPR). To address this challenge, this paper introduces deep learning to feature extraction. Considering the similarities of GPR B-scan images and digital images, a new buried target detection method is proposed, which is based on Single shot multi-box detector (SSD). On the basis of the SSD, the Feature Pyramid Networks (FPN) is added as Neck part in whole network, and the bounding box regression loss function is improved from Smooth Ll loss to Generalized Intersection over Union (GIoU) loss. The proposed method achieves detection of buried target positions and identification of materials with an accuracy rate of 92 %. Compared with the conventional SSD, the mean Average Precision (mAP) of the proposed method is improved by 8.2%. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed GPR-Star is confirmed using experimental data.

articleTitle: Target Detection in sea clutter Based on Wasserstein Distance
abstract: It is a challenging problem for sea surface surveillance radar to detect small floating targets. The electromagnetic scattering properties of targets are different from those of sea surface, which will change the probability distribution of radar echo amplitude. In this paper, the difference between probability distributions is measured by Wasserstein distance and a target detection method is proposed. The method first calculates the probability density distribution of sea clutter and echoes containing targets. Then, the sea clutter closet to the barycenter of sea clutter probability distribution sample is selected as the reference which minimize the sum of Wasserstein distances from the rest of sea clutter to it. Finally, echoes containing targets and pure sea clutter are distinguished according to the Wasserstein distance between each distributions to reference distribution. Since the calculation of barycenter is cumbersome, a fast method is proposed by analogy with sloving the distribution closet to barycenter of Gaussian distribution sample whose Wasserstein distance has analytic expression. The experiments with IPIX radar data show that the proposed target detector has excellent detection ability for small floating targets on the sea surface.

articleTitle: Phase Coupled Frequency Analysis Based on Time-Varying Bispectrum in Sea Clutter
abstract: The properties of phase coupled frequency distribution are seldom mentioned in the analysis of sea clutter properties. In this paper, the phase coupled frequency information of sea clutter is extracted from the time-varying bispectrum estimates of transient sequences separated from the total radar echo by a sliding window. By analyzing CSIR data, it is found that the distribution of phase coupled frequency is more concentrated and the coupling strength is stronger when a target is contained in sea clutter This property can provide a new research direction for target detection in sea clutter.

articleTitle: A new shift pulse compression method for multiple targets' detection
abstract: The detection of multiple targets is always a difficult problem in radar. The core point is that the multiple targets cover each other, which makes it difficult to detect small targets. In order to solve above problem, a new detection method for multiple targets based on shift pulse compression (shift PC) is proposed in this paper. The idea of sum-difference amplitude ratio is used to suppress mutual masking problem caused by main broadening of multiple targets, where the difference channel is constructed by shift PC of left and right with each half range cell. The experimental results for the detection of multiple targets show that the proposed method can improve 20% the detection probability of small targets among multiple targets when the false alarm rate is 10<sup>−5</sup>.

articleTitle: Broadband Orbital Angular Momentum Beam Generation Based on the Discrete Dielectric Lens antenna
abstract: The electromagnetic waves carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) have great potential for applications. Broadband OAM beams are the preference in many sectors. Existed studies show that the beams have been widely explored. Considering the narrow bandwidth of the existing lens antenna carrying OAM we engineer a new discrete dielectric lens (DDL) antenna carrying broadband OAM. The antenna adopts a dielectric unit with an anti-reflection structure and is a cross-shaped air column. By increasing the phase compensation range, the bandwidth of the vortex beam is effectively increased. A broadband OAM generator is designed based on the DDL from 22 to 30 GHz. A proof-of-concept example was proved and validated by simulation. Above 31% vortex beam bandwidth and 64.6% OAM average energy weight are measured throughout the entire design band. This kind of structure offers an alternative mechanism to realize broadband high-efficiency microwave, millimeter-wave, terahertz, or optical OAM generation and can hereafter get position in high-capacity communications and imaging.

articleTitle: Sandbox: a novel algorithm for object recognition using millimeter wave radar
abstract: Focusing on the millimeter wave (MMW) radar classification and recognition problem of objects on the road, such as pedestrians, cyclists, and cars, a sandbox algorithm based on a three-dimensional feature vector, including the target motion feature and electromagnetic (EM) scattering feature radar cross section (RCS), is proposed. And then, a new machine learning algorithm suitable for MMW radar target classification is proposed and verified in the self-test data set. Compared with conventional algorithms, such as k-nearest neighbor (KNN) and support vector machine (SVM), it has better classification accuracy and faster classification speed.

articleTitle: Passive Source Localization using Coprime Arrays in Matched Field Processing
abstract: Matching field processing is one of the most common and important methods for locating underwater sound sources. However, sometimes there are some problems such as fuzzy localization, and localization failure caused by large localization error under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), which limit the application of matching field. In this paper, the coprime array is used for matching field processing, which can effectively solve the above problems. The coprime array method breaks the limitation of the traditional uniform linear arrays which are limited by the physical array elements, expands the array aperture, improves the degree of freedom, and combines the characteristics of ocean acoustic field to locate the sound source. The simulation results show that this method can greatly reduce the localization ambiguity and is more effective under the noise conditions. Compared with the traditional uniform linear array, it has the advantages of better performance and higher probability of effective localization, which has a good significance for future engineering applications.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Scattering Characteristics from Wind-Driven Sea Surface in Low Frequency Terahertz
abstract: According to the terahertz environment detection, the scattering characteristics of the wind-driven sea surface in the lower terahertz frequency band are investigated. The tilted facet modulation model is used to study the scattering characteristics of terahertz waves under different sea conditions from both the Bragg and the non-Bragg scattering characteristics. Comparing the calculated results of low frequency terahertz backscattering with that of the microwave backscattering, it is shown that the non-Bragg scattering plays a dominant role at the near normal incidence, and the sea surface scattering characteristics are consistent in low frequency terahertz band and the microwave range. At a medium incident angle, Bragg scattering plays a dominant role. Because of the shorter wavelength of the terahertz wave, the corresponding lower Bragg scattering intensity, the intensity of the lower terahertz backscattering from the sea surface at medium incident angles is significantly lower than that of the microwave backscattering. This paper also studied the terahertz sea surface scattering characteristics under different sea conditions, and found that as the sea conditions increase, the intensity of the terahertz echoes at medium incident angles decreases sharply under the influence of the Bragg scattering characteristics.

articleTitle: Simulation and Interpretation of Multi-path Propagation in Multi-layer Structure by Ray-Tracing Algorithm
abstract: Ultra wide-band (UWB) signal is a kind of penetrating radio signal, which will produce multi-path effect when propagating in the interface of different dielectric constant medium. The multi-path propagation has an impact on the applications of the UWB signal and affects the accurate identification of the measurement results. In order to identify and remove the effects of multi-path propagation interference, it is of great significance to study the generation of multi-path propagation and the difference from direct propagation path. Since ray-tracing(RT) algorithm of optical geometry can simulate the propagation characteristics of electromagnetic waves, it can be used to track the propagation path of electromagnetic waves, and thus it can clearly distinguish the direct reflection echo and multi-path reflection echo of UWB signal. The simulation model result is compared with the measurement result to verify the multi-path echo of UWB signal and interpret the actual measurement result in the building tier structure.

articleTitle: Multi-Frame Clutter Suppression and Weak Target Detection for Non-side-looking Airborne Radar
abstract: Weak target detection is a challenging problem in non-side-looking airborne radar (non-SLAR) system due to the strong near-range clutter. Traditional clutter suppression algorithms for non-SLAR usually use single frame data to estimate the covariance matrix or power spectrum, and the lack of samples makes the suppression performance weaker. Furthermore, the detection of targets is usually a single frame decision after clutter suppression, in which case, the missed detection of weak targets is extremely likely to occur. Based on these problems, a multi-frame joint clutter suppression and target detection (MF-CS-TD) algorithm is proposed in this paper. Through multi-frame weighted clutter energy estimation and automatic calibration of the measurement in clutter area during the energy iteration, clutter is effectively suppressed, target energy is successfully accumulated, thereby achieving the goal of weak target detection in the near-range clutter background. Numerical simulation results show that the proposed algorithm is able to provide better detection capabilities for targets with low signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR) compared with single-frame clutter suppression and target detection method.

articleTitle: Underdetermined DOA Estimation for Coherent Signals With Moving Sparse Circular Array
abstract: With a small number of array elements and the mutual coupling effect, direction of arrival (DOA) estimation for coherent signals will suffer from performance degradation, in underdetermined scenario. To solve the problem, this paper proposes a sparse uniform circular array (SUCA) on moving platform for mutual coupling reduction, and then employs a sparse signal reconstruction method for underdetermined DOA estimation of coherent signals with single snapshot. There is a systematic procedure to determine the inter-element spacing of the original SUCA and number of shifted SUCAs for the synthetic UCA, to achieve more degrees of freedom (DOF) than the number of elements. The construction of mutual coupling matrix is investigated to demonstrate the lower mutual coupling in the synthetic array. On the basis, the underdetermined DOA estimation of coherent signals is performed by using the sparse signal reconstruction method. Simulation results are given to illustrate the superiority of the proposed array in terms of DOF enhancement and mutual coupling reduction.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Simulation Aided SAR Target Classification Via Deep Domain Adaptation
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have made tremendous success in optical images classification recently. However, in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) target classification, it is difficult to annotate a large amount of real SAR images to train CNNs. Sufficient annotated images can be easily obtained through simulation, but the disparity between the simulated images and the real images makes them difficult to directly apply to the real images classification. In this paper, we propose a model that integrates multi-kernel maximum mean discrepancy (MK-MMD) and domain-adversarial training to alleviate this problem. Simulated SAR images with annotation and unlabeled real SAR images are used to train our model. First, we use domain-adversarial training to prompt the model to extract domain-invariant features. Then, the MK-MMD between the hidden representations of simulated images and real images is reduced to narrow domain discrepancy. Experimental results on the real SAR dataset demonstrate that our method effectively solves the domain shift problem and improves the classification accuracy.

articleTitle: A New Conception of Multi-Stage DBF Based Spaceborne High-Resolution Wide-Swath SAR System
abstract: To meet the requirements of reconnaissance, surveillance, and target detection in large-scale sea areas, this paper proposes a new conception of space-based high-resolution ultra-wide-swath SAR system. Specifically, a high-dexterity beam group network is constructed to acquire wide-area information with high degree of freedom. and a pseudo-random space-time sampling is adopted to achieve pseudosparse coverage of wide swaths. The system meets the demands of large-scale reconnaissance and continuous target monitoring. In this paper, the key technology of the system is refined, and the corresponding solutions and processing methods are given.

articleTitle: A Novel Strong Clutter Suppression Algorithm for Airborne Passive Radar
abstract: Owing to the continuous random and non-periodic characteristics of the passive signal, the random range sidelobe coupling (RRSC) effects of the strong clutter will exacerbate the performance of space-time adaptive processing (STAP) algorithm in airborne passive radar (APR). In this paper, a cascaded least square algorithm (CLS) based on the directional dependence of clutter Doppler frequency is proposed for side-looking APR to suppress strong clutter. The advantage of the method is that it cannot only cancel clutter along the clutter ridge, but also effectively prevent the suppression of targets falling in the clutter Doppler band. A series of simulations are conducted to test the proposed algorithms.

articleTitle: A Novel Waveform Design for Moving Target Detection in MIMO Radar
abstract: This paper proposes a frequency-modulated continuous-wave(FMCW) waveform design for multiple input multiple output(MIMO) radar, which improves the speed limit under the condition of ensuring the direction of arrivals(DOA) estimation performance. Through simulation, this method can achieve better performance in moving target velocity and angle measurement compared with MIMO radar system of classical triangular waveform or multi period sawtooth waveform. This method fully considers the performance of mainstream traffic MIMO radar and is easy to be implement in engineering.

articleTitle: Robust Waveform and Filter Bank Design of Polarimetric Radar under Local Waveform Constraints
abstract: Joint design of transmit signal and receive filter bank for polarimetric radar with local waveform constraints is considered. Assuming Target Aspect Angle (TAA) unknown but belong to an interval, we consider the worst-case Signal to Interference plus Noise Ratio (SINR) at the output of the filter bank as the figure of merit to optimize transmit waveform in horizontal and vertical polarization channels, respectively, subject to energy and similarity constraints. An iterative optimization procedure that effectively solves the non-convex optimization problem is developed. The proposed method is validated through experimental results and compared with existing global design, thus showing its attractiveness.

articleTitle: Detection from Phaseless Measurements of Block-Sparse Signals Using Convex Programming
abstract: In this paper we study the problem of hypothesis testing for detection of a block-sparse signal, which consists of clusters of non-zero elements, from the magnitude-only measurements. As a typical phase retrieval problem, the detection is solved by a method based on convex programming. We derive a detector for the measurement model of this paper and analyze the theoretical performance of the proposed detector. The advantages of our method are indicated in numerical experiments of region of convergence and noise-robustness, etc.. Specifically, the number of requiring measurements of our method for a successful detection is apparently lower than counterparts.

articleTitle: Complementary Mismatch Filter Group Design for Joint Radar and Communications Waveforms
abstract: In the traditional joint radar and communications (JRC) system, the receive filter outputs for unambiguous returns have high sidelobe level (SLL), and the outputs of range ambiguity returns have high energy. These problems degrade the performance of the traditional JRC system. To solve these problems, we design the complementary mismatch filter group (CMFG) for the JRC system in this paper. Compared with the matched filter, the output of the CMFG has signal to noise ratio (SNR) loss. Hence, in this method, the SNR loss and the SLL of the summation of filter outputs of unambiguous returns as well as the energy of summation of filter outputs of range ambiguity returns in each CMFG are jointly minimized. To achieve this, the multi-objective optimization problem for CMFG design is established, and the Block Coordinate Descent algorithm is employed to solve this optimization problem. Finally, simulation results show that the output of the designed CMFG has low SLL, low energy of the range ambiguity output, and low SNR loss.

articleTitle: A Layered Tracking Method for Group Space Object
abstract: It is a great challenge to accurately estimate space target state with low SNR induced by long range. And power acting on space target is complex and difficult to be exactly described. Thus, a layered tracking method (LTM) is proposed for simultaneously tracking the centre and individuals of dispersed-spaced space target group. Based on the difference between target and centre of group, the model of local motion defined as the target motion relative to the centre is derived to be simply linear. And the error in space target motion model is counteracted. Accordingly, a two-layer tracking scheme is presented, in which the top and bottom layers are respectively represented by the centre and individuals. At the top layer, with more accurate centre measurement via fusing measurements of each target, the centre of space targets can be estimated more accurately than individual target within the group. At the bottom layer, the local motion state is estimated and combined with relatively more accurate centre state estimate to acquire each target state, as opposed to tracking space target directly. Compared with other traditional methods, it is validated that the proposed tracking method can provide higher target state estimation accuracy. Numerical simulations are performed to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: A Tensor-Based Target Extraction Scheme for Forward-Looking Scanning Radar
abstract: Robust and efficient target detection for forward-looking scanning radar has very important applications in military and civilian fields. In this paper, a tensor-based target extraction scheme for forward-looking scanning radar is proposed. Firstly, the echo model is established and the superresolution image with better azimuth resolution is obtained. Then, considering the non-local self-correlation of the image, the image patch tensor is constructed. Secondly, the target extraction problem is transformed into an optimization problem, which is constrained by a weighted factor to suppress the background. Finally, the targets we are interested in are extracted by using the alternating direction multiplier method (ADMM) algorithm to solve the optimization problem. At last, simulation results are given to illustrate the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: A Maritime Targets Tracking Algorithm
abstract: In order to solve the problem of tracking for maritime targets, this paper proposes Probability Hypothesis Density algorithm with amplitude information(APHD). Traditional radars only use position information for target tracking, however, the amplitude measurement is introduced to track the target with traditional position information measurement in this paper. First, this work assumes that the background is K-distribution, the amplitude measurement is introduced into traditional probability hypothesis density algorithm to establish the amplitude measurement likelihood function between the target and clutter. Second, the amplitude measurement likelihood function is introduced into the update stage, and the updated posterior intensity of Gaussian mixture is used for the estimation of the state of the next frame. The simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A 0.4-to-6-GHz LTCC-based Common Receiver Module for Multi-band Passive Radar
abstract: This paper presents a 0.4-to-6-GHz common receiver module for multi-band passive radar systems. In order to improve the anti-interference ability of the passive radar receiver, a super-heterodyne architecture with two optional channel bandwidths is proposed, which was realized by film bulk acoustic resonator (FBAR) filters for narrowband application and integrated low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) filters for wideband application. The prototype of the common receiver module with a size of <tex>$\boldsymbol{22 \times 15\times 3 \text{mm}^{2}}$</tex> has been designed and fabricated based on LTCC process. The test results show that the two optional channel bandwidths of the receiver are 65 MHz and 447 MHz. The total gain is no less than −9 dB and the gain flatness is 4.5 dB from 400 MHz to 6 GHz. The output 1-dB compression point <tex>$\boldsymbol{(\mathrm{P}_{-1\text{dB}})}$</tex> is around 5 dBm. The common receiver module can be used for passive radar systems covering P-, L-, S- and C-band.

articleTitle: Adaptive Monopulse Based Estimation in FDA-MIMO radar
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of angle and incremental range estimation for a frequency diverse array multiple-input multiple-output (FDA-MIMO) radar using a single data snapshot. To tackle the formulated maximum likelihood estimation problem, an adaptive monopulse procedure (AMP) based method, employing real slope/bias corrections, is designed. At the analysis stage, the estimation accuracy of both the devised strategy and its variants is assessed also in comparison with the Cramer-Rao lower Bound (CRB). Numerical results are provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the devised estimation strategies.

articleTitle: Shafting Precision of Antenna Pedestal and Dynamic Characteristics of Angular Servo for Measurement Radar
abstract: A three-dimensional model of the two-dimensional antenna pedestal structure of a high-precision measurement radar was established, and the influence of the two-axis shafting accuracy of the antenna pedestal on the radar angle measurement error was analyzed. Then the shafting accuracy of the actual antenna pedestal was measured by a laser tracker, which was basically consistent with the theoretical analysis value. In addition, the angle servo control system model was established to simulate the position loop bandwidth of the azimuth axis and the elevation axis. In the actual antenna pedestal system, the servo bandwidth of the azimuth and elevation was obtained through the step signal response curve, which was consistent with the simulation analysis result. Finally the feasibility of the servo system was further verified, and the index requirements were meet.

articleTitle: Radar Signal Retrieval for Multiple Measurement via Iterative Reweighted Approach
abstract: This work deals with the joint estimation of radar signal waveform and angle in the presence of impulse noise. Firstly, considering spatial sparsity of radar echo signals and multiple measurement vectors (MMV) model, the estimation problem is formulated as an optimization in terms of least-absolute-shrinkage-and-selection-operator (LASSO) form with <tex>$(\ell_{2.1}+\ell_{2.1})$</tex>-norm minimization. Then, the original problem is transformed into a constrained minimization problem which is more suitable for iterative reweighed technique encouraging sparse solution. Furthermore, one iterative reweighted scheme and Lagrange multiplier technique are employed to solve the optimization problem and get an iterative closed form solution. At last, experimental results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the state-of-the-art approaches in terms of the convergence rate and steady-state value.

articleTitle: Few-Shot ISAR Target Recognition Based on Gaussian Prototypical Network
abstract: With insufficient training samples, the available inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) target recognition methods based on deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) have degraded performance or even become invalid. To deal with this issue, a few-shot ISAR target recognition method based on Gaussian prototypical network (GPN) is proposed. In GPN, ISAR images are firstly mapped into embedding vectors by the embedding network. Then, Gaussian prototypes are constructed according to the weighted embedding vectors. Finally, target categories are predicted according to the Mahalanobis distance between test samples and prototypes. Recognition results of measured data consisting of three categories of aircraft show that the proposed method can obtain high recognition accuracy when there are only a few training samples.

articleTitle: Study on Lightweight MMW 3D Transmitter Subarray
abstract: In this paper, a new three-dimensional assembly method of 64-way integration for phased-array with tight size and high operating frequency is proposed. The multifunctional monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) chip technology, multi-chip assembly (MCM) technology and multilayer mixer and pressing technology are used to develop a transmitter subarray with a size of only 48 mm X 48 mm X 9 mm and mass of less than 50 g. The output power is greater than 21 dBm, the output power consistency among channels is better than ± 0.5 dB, and the transmit shift accuracy is <3.5°. The subarray is highly integrated and has breakthrough advantages in size and weight compared with traditional components, which greatly reduces the size of phased array radar and make it better meet the needs of high performance conformal active phased array radar. It can be widely used in space platforms with high space size requirements or conformal needs.

articleTitle: A Four Bands Absorber Based on Zigzag Metamaterial
abstract: We numerically and experimentally investigate the absorption and reflection property of a zigzag meta material (ZM) in the microwave regime. The results demonstrate that the ZM can perform sharp absorption peaks and deep reflection valley at four frequencies bands. Its performance remains steady even if the dihedral angle of sawtooth changes in a specified range. This simple structure is desirable for potential applications in improving absorbance performances and reducing the radar cross section.

articleTitle: An Efficient Scattering Simulation Method with Application to Electrically Large Planetary Terrains
abstract: The scattering simulation is fundamental to analyze the physical characteristics of planetary surface. In practice, the detected region is extremely large, thus it will bring great burden on the scattering simulation. In this paper, we use the coherent and incoherent model to calculate the radar cross section (RCS) of electrically large planet surfaces. Compared with the PO method with quasi-specular-facet model, the simulation efficiency is improved by 347 times. As the typically physical properties, the surface roughness is concerned. By simulating the RCSs of two different topographies, it is demonstrated that the surface roughness has a significant influence on the scattering properties of the planetary surface in microwave band.

articleTitle: Keystone Transform Based UAV Detection by Utilizing MillimeterWave Radar
abstract: Due to the small radar cross section (RCS), the detection of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is a challenge task for traditional surveillance radar. In this paper, a linear frequency modulation continuous wave (FMCW) millimeter-wave radar is presented for UAV detection and a keystone transform (KT) based long-time coherent integration method is employed for the sake of improving the output signal-to-noise ratio, which is essential for UAV detection. Specifically, the KT is first utilized to correct the range migration induced by the movement of UAV. Then, the two dimensional fast Fourier transform (2D-FFT) along the fast time and slow time directions is addressed to realize the long-time coherent integration. After that, the constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detection is used to achieve the UAV detection. Finally, the simulation results are given to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Preliminary Results of Near Field RFI Localization Based on Virtual Large Aperture with Compressed Sensing
abstract: Radio frequency interference (RFI) has great negative impact on the precision of the geophysical parameters retrieved from the microwave synthetic aperture interferometric measurements, so accurate localization of RFI sources is an important issue. In this paper, a method called near field localization based on virtual large aperture with compressed sensing is proposed to improve the localization accuracy and deal with the localization of weak RFI sources. By utilizing the movement of the platform and combing the measurements at different positions, a large virtual aperture can be formed, and the RFI sources are in the near field of the large virtual aperture, which is similar to the supersynthesis radiometer. The equation is established according to the concept, and based on the sparsity characteristic of RFI sources, compressed sensing technique is adopted to reconstruct the location of the RFI sources. In order to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed method, numerical simulation and indoor prototype experiments are conducted, and preliminary results show the method can handle the problem.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Expanding and Shift Scheme for Underdetermined DOA Estimation
abstract: An enhanced expanding and shift (EEAS) scheme, which is based on the original expanding and shift (EAS) scheme with coprime array (CPA), is proposed. By suitably exploiting the relationship among the sub-arrays in the fourth-order difference co-array (FODC) of the original EAS scheme and further enlarging the sensor spacing in the expanded sparse array, the proposed EEAS scheme can achieve increased consecutive sensors in its FODC. Compared with some representative FODC based sparse arrays, the proposed one can achieve much longer consecutive virtual array. Especially, when the sensor number approaches large, the number of consecutive virtual sensors will be significantly improved. Simulations experiments are carried out to verify the performance. Though the preliminary study is confined to some conditions, the proposed sparse array is effective and expected to be extended to a generalized condition.

articleTitle: Stereo Radargrammetric Location of GF-3 SAR Images with Descending and Ascending Multi-Angle Acquisitions
abstract: The Gaofen-3 (GF-3) is the first civil C-band Synthetic Aperture Radar(SAR) satellite in China, which has a variety of imaging modes and plays an important role in many fields. Stereo radargrammetry is an effective method to obtain the target elevation, which has a great advantage in the non-coherent area. In this paper, a first application of stereo radargrammetry to obtain the digital surface model (DSM) of GF-3 was taken with the data obtained from the descending and ascending multi-angle acquisitions, applied with real-time orbit data. After accurate coregistration of SAR images obtained from different view angles, the target elevation is obtained by the stereo radargrammetry, and the height accuracy of obtained DSM is evaluated. The experimental results show that the target elevation with the stereo radargrametry method can be obtained of GF-3.

articleTitle: High Resolution Two-Dimensional Imaging Algorithm Based on Rotating Antenna
abstract: Radar image can provide an important basis for target recognition, which has been a hot area of radar technologies. In vortex electromagnetic radar imaging, it is necessary to transmit multi-mode vortex electromagnetic wave, but pure multi-mode vortex electromagnetic wave is difficult to obtain. Inspired by the generation of vortex electromagnetic waves, a rotating antenna is used to achieve high resolution two-dimensional radar imaging in this paper. The azimuth angle of the target in the range of radar beam can be reconstructed by using the Doppler effect generated by the rotation of the antenna when the radar transmits the linear frequency modulation (LFM) signal, and then the high resolution two-dimensional image of the target can be obtained by combining the one-dimensional range image obtained by the dechirp operation. Compared with the existing algorithms, the proposed algorithm has lower requirements on radar performance, and can generate two-dimensional image of the target under staring condition without transmitting complex signals. Simulation results show that the algorithm is effective and robust.

articleTitle: ISAR Imaging Algorithm Based on High-Order Synchrosqueezing Transform
abstract: Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) plays an irreplaceable role in the field of national defense surveillance and civilian. Due to the target to be observed with complex motions, the classic range-Doppler (RD) imaging algorithm is unsuitable to obtain a well-focused ISAR image, which brings a serious challenge for ISAR imaging design. To overcome those problems, in this work, we propose a new ISAR imaging method based on High Order Synchrosqueezing Transform (HOSST). Firstly, the method models the echo signals of each range bin as multi-component polynomial phase signals after translation compensation; Secondly, uses HOSST to perform time-frequency analysis on the signals, the two-dimensional range-Doppler matrix can be transformed into a three-dimensional range-time-Doppler matrix. And then, take a slice at a certain time dimension, ISAR image of the target can be obtain. Compared with the exciting methods, the well-focused ISAR image can be obtained by the proposed method. Finally, the real results are presented to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Fast Compensation Method of Minimum Entropy Based on Polynomial Fitting
abstract: Due to the influence of various factors such as weather, the platform cannot keep a uniform linear motion during flight, phase error is introduced leading to image defocusing. The minimum entropy autofocus is an echo compensation algorithm that takes the corrected phase vector to be estimated as the independent variable and the image entropy as the dependent variable. As an image-based autofocus method, this algorithm has the advantages of good aggregation effect and high robustness, but in practical application, it is very time-consuming due to too many azimuth samples. In this paper, a minimum entropy autofocus algorithm based on polynomial fitting optimization is proposed. The proposed method effectively reduces the number of independent variables by estimating the polynomial coefficient of phase error. Some comparison experiments are performed to verify the estimation efficiency and accuracy of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: An efficient scheme of source localization using TDOA
abstract: This paper focuses on the problem of source tracking in the 3-D space using a time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA)-based localization system. Different from existing studies, the new scheme considers a more realistic data model that includes synchronization offsets, sensor location errors and distance-dependent noises, which dramatically complicates source tracking with a TDOA-based localization system. First, we derive the Fisher information matrix (FIM) and then address the optimal sensor placement under the restriction of geographical conditions. Finally, combining with the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE), Kalman filtering and sensor motion strategy, we propose a source tracking algorithm guided by the optimal sensor placement configuration. Mathematical analyses and numerical simulations validate the optimal sensor placement and efficiencies of the source tracking algorithm.

articleTitle: Continuous Distributed Processing of Software Defined Radar
abstract: Software-defined radar has been an active research field for more than ten years. However, the low performance and low scalability of the traditional processing techniques of SDR make it hard to deal with complex radar tasks. The stream processing engine is a software that supports low latency and high scalability distributed data processing. It is widely used in log, image, and video processing scenarios but rarely used in radar applications. This paper reviews processing software-defined radar data by using the stream processing engine, and we illustrate the differences between processing log data and radar data. Furthermore, we discuss some optimizations for stream processing engines to get better performance in the radar data processing.

articleTitle: Cognitive Radar Waveform Synthesis with Desired Spectrum and Autocorrelation Shapes
abstract: This paper presents a more generalized and flexible waveform design to minimize both the spectrum band notch and local autocorrelation peak sidelobe level, containing out-of-band spectrum restriction and peak-to-average power ratio constraint. To tackle the resultant nonconvex problem, an iterative majorization minimization proximal method of multipliers (M-PMM) algorithm is developed. In each iteration, it can transform the original problem into multiple subproblems with closed-form solutions or solved by majorization method. Extensive numerical examples highlight that the synthesized waveform shares the desired spectrum-autocorrelation properties and is applied to radar detection.

articleTitle: Automatic Modulation Recognition for Radar Signals Based on ACSE Networks
abstract: Automatic modulation recognition for radar signals plays a significant role in electronic warfare. Conventional recognition methods may suffer from the recognition accuracy and the computation complexity under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). In this paper, a novel method based on Asymmetric Convolution Squeeze-and-Excitation (ACSE) networks and a fusion strategy is proposed to recognize seven kinds of radar signals automatically. First, features in these three domains are converted into images. Then the images are as inputs for ACSE networks which can extract and learn deep features without complex data pre-processing. Finally, inference results in the three domains are fused using voting strategy of ensemble learning to output the final inference result. Via simulations, the robustness and effectiveness of voting strategy are proved. The results on simulation signals show that the proposed method can achieve more than 95% accuracy at −6dB. Compared with SVM method and three typical neural networks, the ACSE networks owns better recognition performance especially under low SNRs. The results on measured signals also demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other methods.

articleTitle: Mutual coupling estimation method of metasurfaces system based on sparse Bayesian learning
abstract: The radar system based on metasurfces is a new technology that can realize single-channel imaging. However, for the coupling between metasurface elements in a single-channel system, there are no effective solution at present. In this paper, we focus on the estimation of the mutual coupling between the coding metasurface elements. First, this paper establishes a mathematical model of a single-channel system including coupling parameters. Then by assuming the prior distribution of the parameters, the Bayesian method is used to obtain the posterior probability distribution of the parameters, and the expectation maximization (EM) method is used to estimate the unknown parameters in the model. Finally, numerical experiments verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Automatic Extraction of Supraglacial Lake using SAR Imagery and Deep Learning
abstract: Supraglacial lake plays an important role in ice sheet dynamics, mass balance and sea level rise. Therefore, it is of great importance to extract supraglacial lake and obtain its spatial-temporal distribution or change. This study provides an automatic extraction model for supraglacial lake, using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery based on deep learning. First, select 19580 Sentinel-1 SAR imagery patches in eight typical areas for manual labeling. Second, the GPU-based U-Net model is used to implement the training of the supraglacial lake, and the results are evaluated in different sites. Finally, the training model is used to perform the supraglacial lake extraction. In addition, this article also introduces ArcticDEM to remove shadow confusion in the margin of the ice sheet. The global-local threshold segmentation method is used to extract the supraglacial lake on the Sentinel-2 MSI imagery, which is a comparative analysis and information supplement for the extracted results in this paper. The results show that: (1) The U-Net network selected in this paper is suitable for processing small sample size SAR data and multi-modal feature extraction. The GPU parallel processing method can achieve rapid extraction of massive data and reduce time cost. (2) The Dice coefficient of the training model reaches 0.98, which can be used for effective extraction of supraglacial lake. (3) Compared with the results of optical image extraction, the algorithm proposed in this paper can identify lakes in areas covered by snow or thin ice, which truly reflects the supraglacial lake temporal and spatial distribution characteristics.

articleTitle: RFI Localization Algorithm Based on Sparse Bayesian Learning for Synthetic Aperture Radiometers
abstract: For synthetic aperture imaging radiometer (SAIR), the effect of radio frequency interference (RFI) is affecting the quality of the brightness temperature (BT) retrieval. RFI detection and localization are essential for RFI mitigation, which contributes to the retrieved data improvement. Sparse Bayesian spatial spectrum estimation algorithm has been proposed and simulated for traditional radar DOA, and experiments shows that its performance is better than traditional compressed sensing methods. Considering the common characteristic of traditional array signal processing and SAIR, This paper proposes an RFI localization method based on sparse Bayesian learning. The undersampling information is and combine it with Expectation-Maximum (EM) algorithm for joint parameter estimation. The proposed method is validated through simulation of generated RFIs and SMOS L1a data, which shows the precise performance of the proposed method for RFI detection and localization.

articleTitle: Phase-Only Beampattern Synthesis via Iterative Convex Optimization
abstract: This paper addresses the phase-only beampattern synthesis via minimizing the peak sidelobe level under the constraints of controlled mainlobe level. The resulting design model is a challenging NP-hard problem due to the existence of the constant modulus constraints. To this end, we propose a novel Approximation Iterative Convex Optimization (AICO) algorithm to convert the constant modulus restrictions into convex constraints invoking first-order Taylor expansion. By doing so, the original problem can be solved sequentially over the resultant convex-hulls until convergence. Finally, numerical examples are presented to verify the superiority of the proposed algorithm in comparison with the available methods.

articleTitle: Weighted Group Sparse Bayesian Learning for Human Activity Classification
abstract: Recently, many researchers have focused on the human behavior recognition based on micro-Doppler signal. In this paper, we propose a sparse representation classification approach based on weighted group sparse Bayesian learning (SRC_WGSBL) for human activity classification, which introduces the property of group sparsity to distinguish the sparse coefficients between different classes. In addition, the use of Bayesian model for sparse coding is helpful to have robust classification performance in practice. Extensive experiments on a public database have been carried out to compare the performance of the proposed approach with support vector machine (SVM) and sparse representation classification based on orthogonal matching pursuit (SRC_OMP). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach is effective and has better performance.

articleTitle: Imaging Strategy Design for Multi-Rotor UAV SAR Real Data
abstract: For multi-rotor unmanned aerial vehicles(UAVs) synthetic aperture radar (SAR), motion errors are divided into low-frequency (LF) components and high-frequency (HF) components. In general, the HF errors are rarely considered which will deteriorate the image quality. In order to solve this problem, an imaging strategy for high-resolution multi-rotor UAV SAR is proposed. Motion compensation (MoCo) techniques based on motion sensors and echo signal are applied to compensate for LF motion errors. A data-based phase estimation method is employed to remove the HF errors. After imaging by the range Doppler algorithm (RDA), the phase gradient autofocus (PGA) techniques can achieve further improvements in imaging results. The real data experiments prove the effectiveness of this algorithm for multi-rotor UAV SAR imaging.

articleTitle: CNN-Based SAR Automatic Target Recognition Using SAR Raw Data
abstract: Automatic target recognition (ATR) for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has been a significant research topic for decades. Existing methods of ATR perform the task after image formation. However, the imaging process of target information may lose the target abstract feature information hidden in the original data. Motivated by this, we feed the SAR raw data to a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) that does not require image reconstruction. To evaluate the method, we trained two well-known CNN networks, VGG19 and ResNet18, on the simulated dataset and MSTAR dataset. The results show that both CNN network architectures can achieve good results for classification.

articleTitle: SAR Altimeter Data Processing and Airborne Experiment
abstract: Using radar altimeter to observe the dynamic height of the sea surface is an effective means for global-scale ocean monitoring. In recent years, the radar altimeter has gradually developed from the real aperture mode to the synthetic aperture mode, and from the Ku band to the Ka band. The accuracy and resolution of the observation have been greatly improved. This paper firstly presents the echo model and re-tracking method of conventional radar altimeter and synthetic aperture radar altimeter, and re-tracks the Sentinel-3 echo data to verify the effectiveness of the echo model and re-tracking method; the obtained Sentinel-3 sea surface height data are analyzed afterwards using wavenumber spectrum method, which verifies that the synthetic aperture mode has higher ranging accuracy and ocean signal resolution compared with the conventional mode; finally, the airborne calibration data of Ka band synthetic aperture radar altimeter are re-tracked, and the correctness of the parameter retrieval is verified by comparing with the Mean Sea Surface model.

articleTitle: An Evaluation Method of Traffic Radar Tracking Performance in No-truth System
abstract: Aiming to solve the problem of tracking performance evaluation of traffic radar, an evaluation method without a truth system is proposed. Firstly, observe the traffic radar data and divide the track into unique ID track and three types of non- ID unique track. Unique ID track refers to the trajectory of a target corresponding to a trajectory. We analyze and propose the corresponding type recognition strategies. Then four performance indexes are established based on different track types to evaluate the tracking performance of traffic radar. Finally, through the verification of the radar data collected on the highway, this method can evaluate the tracking performance of the radar accurately and effectively when real road driving information cannot be obtained.

articleTitle: Human Behavior Recognition Method Based on CEEMD-ES Radar Selection
abstract: In recent years, the millimeter-wave radar to identify human behavior has been widely used in medical, security, and other fields. When multiple radars are performing detection tasks, the validity of the features contained in each radar is difficult to guarantee. In addition, processing multiple radar data also requires a lot of time and computational cost. The Complementary Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition-Energy Slice (CEEMD-ES) multistatic radar selection method is proposed to solve these problems. First, this method decomposes and reconstructs the radar signal according to the difference in the reflected echo frequency between the limbs and the trunk of the human body. Then, the radar is selected according to the difference between the ratio of echo energy of limbs and trunk and the theoretical value. The time domain, frequency domain and various entropy features of the selected radar are extracted. Finally, the Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) recognition model of the ReLu core is established. Experiments show that this method can effectively select the radar, and the recognition rate of three kinds of human actions is 98.53%.

articleTitle: Translational Motion Compensation Method Based On Global Butterfly Optimization Algorithm for ISAR Imaging
abstract: The complex motion of ISAR maneuvering targets can be fitted by high-order polynomials. Under the condition of a low signal-to-noise ratio, the existing ISAR translational compensation methods are difficult to evaluate the motion error efficiently and accurately. In response to these problems, this paper proposes an ISAR translational compensation method based on the Global Butterfly Optimization Algorithm (GBOA). First, the target translational component is modeled as a high-order polynomial form and the objective function is constructed with image entropy as the evaluation criterion. Then, the initial value of the optimization iteration can be achieved by rough estimation of the translational component. Finally, the Global Butterfly Optimization Algorithm is used to estimate and compensate for the translational error efficiently and accurately. In addition, based on the Butterfly Optimization Algorithm, the proposed method introduces a global variable factor, which makes GBOA has a higher convergence speed and the ability to avoid falling into a locally optimal solution. The experimental results of Yak-42 measured data verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Time-Invariant Transmit Beampattern Synthesis Via Genetic Algorithm for FDA Radar
abstract: This paper investigates the design of frequency offsets in frequency diverse array (FDA) radar to achieve a time-invariant transmit beampattern without range-angle-coupling. At the design stage, the root-based nonlinear time-modulated frequency offset (NFO) is proposed. Then, the offsets are further optimized resorting to the Genetic Algorithm (GA), which is referred to as the GANFO-FDA. At the analysis stage, a comparison of the transmit beampattern among the GANFO-FDA and other offset strategy counterparts is carried out. Numerical results verify the superiorities of the time-invariant transmit beampattern with the GANFO-FDA in focused energy and low sidelobes.

articleTitle: Rebar Radius Retrieval by Deconvolution and Convolutional Neural Network in Ground Penetrating Radar
abstract: The ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) is an effective method for construction quality inspection, typically of the ‘thin’ reinforcing rebars. However to the best of the author's knowledge, there is no widely-adopted method in detecting the rebars radius in concrete. Hereby, this paper proposes a novel machine learning framework to accomplish accurate and real-time estimation for the radius of the rebars, which can simultaneously estimate the burial depth of the rebars and the water content of the concrete. The proposed method mainly consists of two parts. First, a data pre-processing based on deconvolution is used to derive the reflectivity series of the rebars from a single A-scan. Then, a regression scheme based on one-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) uses the reflectivity series as input to accomplish the estimation. Simulation shows that the proposed method yields a high estimation accuracy of the radius.

articleTitle: Sparse Aperture ISAR Imaging using Joint Constraits of Low-Rank and Sparsity
abstract: Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging of sparse aperture (SA) is very important in some practical applications. The compressed sensing (CS) methods can resolve the SA problem using a sparse prior, known as sparse representation, which has some limitations due to the model of algorithm architecture. In this paper, a novel sparse ISAR imaging algorithm using joint constraints of sparsity and low-rank is proposed for enhanced performance. In the scheme, the low-rank property of range profiles and the sparsity of desired ISAR image are modeled by the nuclear norm and L1 norm, respectively. Then, an effective solution based on alternating direction method of multiplies (ADMM) is employed to solve the convex optimization problem with high computational efficiency. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is further validated using experimental analyses based on measured data.

articleTitle: Reliability of Physical Layer in Context of Sensing and Communication Coexistence Environment
abstract: The performance of integrated sensing and communication (ISC) networks with an illegitimate eavesdropper under the spectrum sharing strategy is developed, where the cross interference is considered to be unavoidable. To minimize the impact of cross-interference caused by the sensing and communication signals, non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) is taken into account. The physical layer reliability (PLR) performance of a NOMA ISC system is studied in terms of reliability in the communication side. Meanwhile, the sensing performance is evaluated in the presence of communication interference. The performance of the considered system is investigated by deriving the outage probability (OP) and intercept probability (IP) in the communication side, and the sensing probability (SP) in the sensing side. It is revealed that increasing the sensing power can improve the overall performance of the users and sensing positively.

articleTitle: Structure Design of Wideband Receiver Based on Two-stage Dynamic Channelization
abstract: Because of the superior performance, channelized receivers are widely used in modern electronic warfare. However, traditional channelization often has certain blindness in channel division, and it is difficult to ensure the average signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) while avoiding cross-channel. This article focuses on large instantaneous bandwidth scenarios, and a more flexible two-stage channelization design scheme is proposed. First, for different bandwidth signal, this design scheme can divide and conquer as much as possible in the frequency domain by the dichotomy filter bank; after that, a four-channel polyphase filter bank is used for finer signal processing. This scheme can maximize the average bandwidth ratio of signals in the sub-channel, so that the average output SNR of the signal can be maximized without cross-channel, so as to achieve higher quality channeled reception.

articleTitle: Emergency application of Surface Water Detection Based on GF-3 Images—A Case Study from Henan
abstract: SAR images have powerful advantages in emergency response to natural disasters such as torrential rains and floods. It can still monitor water in heavy rains day because it is not affected by clouds and fog. In order to explore the capabilities of SAR images in emergency applications, the Zhengzhou rainstorm event was token as an example, a short-time series of water dynamic detection research was conducted. However, due to the inherent characteristics of SAR images such as mountain shadows and noise, high-precision and rapid water extraction are still difficult points to be overcome. This paper proposed a water detection framework based on a semantic segmentation network to reduce false alarms caused by mountain shadows. Our experiments with Gaofen-3 images show the effectiveness of the proposed framework, and were compared with traditional method. Finally, the thematic maps of water detection in each period and water dynamic changes are generated.

articleTitle: Compact Bandpass Filter Using Quarter-Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide and Coplanar Waveguide with High Selectivity
abstract: This paper presents a bandpass filter based on a hybrid structure of quarter-mode substrate integrated waveguide (QMSIW) and coplanar waveguide (CPW). By incorporating CPW structure into QMSIW, the proposed filter gets advantages of miniaturized circuit size and high selectivity due to the fact that the CPW not only works as resonator but also introduces electric coupling between two magnetically coupled QMSIW resonators which generates extra transmission zero (TZ) because of two coupling paths. To further enhance the selectivity of the proposed filter, mixed source and load coupling which realized by two open loop resonators is employed that results in another three TZs. In order to verify the design, a bandpass filter with center frequency of 8.625GHz is fabricated and measured. The experimental results show good agreement with the simulated results.

articleTitle: Adaptive interference cancellation based on transmitted waveform matching in array radar
abstract: The interference suppression performance of the traditional adaptive beamforming method is affected by the collected interference samples. In this work, we proposed a method for interference cancellation in array radar. The problem of interference suppression is transformed into finding a weight vector to minimize the mean square error between the array output signal and the desired signal. According to the time-delay relationship between the target reflection echo and the radar transmitted signal, an auxiliary vector with constant modulus constraint is introduced to construct the desired signal expression. The alternative projection method is used to solve the non-convex optimization problem and obtain the optimal weight. The introduction of prior information on transmitted waveform avoids the interference sample selection and improves cancellation performance. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Multi-Channel Convolutional Neural Network for Soil Moisture Estimation Using Combination of Polarimetric Channel in PolSAR Data
abstract: Soil moisture estimation using polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) data is of great interest and difficult issue in SAR quantitative research. One of the key issues to separate the effects of vegetation and soil roughness. In this paper, the polarization parameters used to describe the roughness of vegetation and soil are obtained by different combinations of polarization channels. A multi-channel convolutional neural network (MCCNN) is proposed to extract different polarization parameters for soil moisture classification and regression. In the network, we subtract the features extracted from different polarization parameters so as to effectively weaken the influence of vegetation and soil roughness on soil moisture estimation. The experimental results show that the classification network can achieve up to 94 % classification accuracy. Meanwhile, the root mean square error and the determination coefficient of the regression network are 2.46% and 0.92 respectively.

articleTitle: An Efficient Coherent Integration Method for High-Speed Maneuvering Target with Nonlinear Motion
abstract: Long-time coherent integration (LTCI) can effectively improve the target detection and motion parameters estimation ability of radar for high-speed maneuvering target. However, the range migration (RM) and Doppler frequency migration (DFM) effects caused by maneuvering target will defocus the signal energy, which may seriously degrade the performance of detection and estimation. In this paper, an efficient coherent integration approach based on second-order keystone transform (SKT), modified axis rotation (MAR) and linear canonical transform (LCT), i.e., SKT-MAR-LCT, is proposed to accomplish target detection and motion parameters estimation. The proposed algorithm first uses SKT to eliminate the range curvature, and then uses the geometric relationship between the radial velocity and the slope angle of pulse compression signal to correct the linear range walk through MAR. Finally, after the target energy is concentrated in one range bin, we extract the signal and complete the energy integration via LCT. In comparison with the existing representative coherent detection methods, SKT-MAR-LCT can achieve a better balance between target detection performance and computational complexity. Mathematical analysis and simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of SKT-MAR-LCT.

articleTitle: Design of Radar Target Detector based on CFAR Feature Plane
abstract: The processing framework resorting to the constant false alarm rate (CFAR) feature plane interprets CFAR detector design as a learning machine composed of input layer, hidden layer (invariant feature extraction), design layer and output layer, which provides a novel way to the design of CFAR detector. In this paper, we investigate the design criterion to the design layer under this framework. On the CFAR feature plane composed of two maximum invariant statistics, two new detectors with simple controllable parameters are designed through feature fusion by weighted arithmetic mean and weighted geometric mean. Finally, simulation experiments verify the effectiveness of the two methods.

articleTitle: A Method of Using Multichannel SAR Spatial Phase Information for Moving Target Positioning
abstract: Multichannel synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has the ability of high-resolution and wide-swath (HRWS) imaging. Therefore, it has become a vital means of marine surveillance. Moreover, the target positioning using SAR is essential in ship monitoring, and it is mainly concentrated on the image domain at present. This paper proposes a novel method of positioning the target using the spatial phase information of SAR echo without imaging. The multichannel SAR antenna can be regarded as an array composed of multiple elements, and based on the array signal processing theory, the target cone angle at the imaging moment can be obtained. Then, according to the range-Doppler equation and the geometric model of the earth, the target coordinates can be calculated with the cone angle known. Finally, the results of the simulation experiment illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Performance of Automotive SAR System with Field Experiment
abstract: To satisfy the requirements for finer resolution in automotive industry, in this paper, a realistic mini-SAR system is presented. Which is a vehicle-mounted SAR system utilizing a low cost short range Frequency Modulation Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar. The components of the whole system are introduced in detail firstly, including the radar RF board and the robot mobile platform. Furthermore, the imaging geometry of system has been analyzed. In which the specific problems that cannot be ignored in systematic designing and signal processing are discussed. After that, based on the analysis, the system parameters are designed and the field experiments is carried out. The high-resolution imaging result of experiments is demonstrated and validate the automotive SAR system we set up.

articleTitle: The Influence of Interval Error of Different Interval Index and Weighting Conditions on the Electrical Performance of Active Phased Array Antennas
abstract: Strong anti-interference capability and fast beam scanning speed are the main advantages of active phased array antennas (APAA). The key factors to consider when studying the effect of interval error on AP AA electrical performance are its design parameters, such as weighting conditions. The variation of the peak power interval, peak sidelobe level interval, and half power beam width interval of an active phased array antenna is investigated in this paper under array element position error interval, excitation amplitude interval, and phase error interval of different interval index and under different weighting conditions. The results show that as the interval index increases, the deterioration of electrical performance increases. As the Taylor-weighted sidelobe level gradually decreases, the supremum of the peak sidelobe level caused by each parameter error decreases, while the excitation amplitude error causes the infimum of the peak power interval and the supremum of the half power beam width interval to become larger.

articleTitle: Micro-vibration Signal Extraction for Radar Based on Additive Constant in Low SNR
abstract: Micro-vibration measurement based on millimeter wave radar is a non-contact and high-precision measurement method, which plays an important role in the field of bridge health monitoring. Extraction of micro-vibration signal for radar usually obtains differential phase information by differential interference processing of radar echo signal. Then the high precision target deformation is obtained by integrating the difference phase. Under high background noise, the differential phase faces wrapping problem, which causes the jump of deformation and destroys the vibration information. Based on additive constant, micro-vibration signal for radar in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is extracted in this paper to solve the jump of deformation jump. The method can accurately obtain the deformation of vibration signal at the same time. Finally, the simulation and the real data results have showed the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Deep Model Based Road User Classification Using mm-Wave Radar
abstract: For autonomous driving, the classification of road user is an important task. Millimeter wave radar (mm-Wave radar) is usually more robust than the camera in severe autonomous driving scenarios, like weak, strong lighting and bad weather. In this work, we propose a method to classify five categories of Range-Doppler (RD) map. We design a deep model which contains a convolutional neural network (CNN) module and a multi-head attention module for this task. The basic idea of this design is to use CNN to capture RD features, and then use attention mechanism to globally correlate high-order features. To evaluate the proposed method, we build our RD datasets using mm-Wave radar in real road scenarios. The experimental results show that our model gets favorable classification performance with the total accuracy of 92%.

articleTitle: Coherent and Noncoherent Multi-Subband Time Delay Estimation: Analysis and Solutions
abstract: High accurate estimation of time delay (TD) is required in many applications, e.g., source localization. The recently proposed method based on multi-subband signals (MSS) considers the situation that a source emits or reflects multiple bandpass signals with different center frequencies. It performs magnitude-level higher TD estimation accuracy than the existing methods. This paper will conduct a deeper investigation on the MSS-based TD estimation. We first derive two approaches to estimate TD, which process the MSS by coherent and noncoherent processing. Then the performance of these two processing methods is analyzed through Cramer-Rao bound (CRB). A brief discussion compares the coherent CRB, noncoherent CRB and traditional CRB.
