Theoretical result and numerical simulations validate both coherent and noncoherent methods can improve the accuracy of TD estimation. The coherent method lowers the root-mean-square error (RMSE) over 90% compared to the noncoherent method, while the noncoherent method has a higher signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) threshold tolerance.

articleTitle: Radial Velocity Ambiguity Resolution Method in Azimuth Multichannel HRWS SAR
abstract: For moving targets in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images, the obvious features are defocusing and dislocation. To estimate motion parameters accurately is a premise for the precise imaging of moving targets. However, when the radial velocity of the target exceeds the maximum detectable unambiguous velocity, the estimated value by the existing methods is no longer the real value. A radial velocity ambiguity resolution method based on Imaging Space-Time Adaptive Processing (ISTAP) is proposed in this paper. The proposed method has no search or iterative process and is suitable for the azimuth multichannel SAR with low pulse repetition frequency (PRF). Finally, the simulated data from an x-band azimuth six-channel SAR system verify the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Wall Effect Mitigation for Through-the-Wall Human Motion Detection Using a GAN Network
abstract: In the context of through-the-wall human motion detection, the DC clutters, indoor multipath clutters and environmental noises introduced by the wall media and indoor static objects often obscure the important motion information, thus affecting the effective recognition of the target motions. Many strategies have been proposed to suppress such effect, including spatial filtering, high-pass filtering, subspace decomposition, etc. However, these methods either rely heavily on manual intervention or not robust to noises. This paper attempts to cope with these challenges using Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN). More specifically, a Pix2Pix network is applied to learn the mapping from the wall corrupted raw range map to its de-walled counterpart. Our implement shows that the DC clutters and noises can be effectively removed in the raw range map, with human motion information being preserved with high fidelity. Also, this result outperforms our previous proposed optimization based RPCA approach.

articleTitle: A Multi-layer Feature based Registration Method for SAR Images on Unstable Aerial Platforms
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging has been widely applied in drones for its consistent surveillance capability and invulnerability to smoke or cloud. Yet drone platform is unstable and observing distance is much shorter than satellite. As a consequence, the SAR image registration, which is a crucial process in SAR imaging, is influenced by sparkling scattering spots and coherent speckle noise. In this paper, we propose a multi-layer method to improve SAR registration performance on drones. ORB method is applied to mitigate sparkle scattering spot. Multi-layer feature clustering can eliminate the error matches by coherent speckle noise. Experiments were carried out to valid the proposed method. Results demonstrate that the proposed method can improve SAR image registration performance on unstable aerial platforms.

articleTitle: Wind speed estimation for tropical cyclone from combined active and passive measurements
abstract: Sea wind speed (SWS) plays a key role for understanding air-sea interactions and marine physical processes. Both microwave radiometer and scatterometer can provide SWS products. However, under high wind speeds (HWS), especially during tropical cyclones (TCs), these products have larger errors. This paper proposes a method of combining active and passive observations to invert the SWS based on random forest (RF) regression during the global TCs. The estimation results indicated the good accuracy of the RF-AP model with the root mean square error (RMSE) about 2.09m/s and coefficient of determination was 0.89 for validation dataset. In contrast, the estimation results of the RF-active regression model (RMSE-3.63m/s) and the RF-passive regression model (RMSE-2.38m/s) alone are not as good as the RF-AP model. Overall, the proposed method in this study shows the potential for application in SWS inversion, and the results will be helpful for the inversion of SWS under TCs.

articleTitle: Improving Black-box Adversarial Attacks on HRRP-based Radar Automatic Target Recognition
abstract: In the field of high-resolution range profile (HRRP)-based radar automatic target recognition(RATR), deep learning has gradually become the mainstream. However, crafted adversarial samples will cause misclassification of deep neural network (DNN), which has not attracted extensive attention in the RATR community. In this paper, we first systematically study the robustness of several state-of-the-art neural networks in the face of adversarial attack. Experiments show that the existing methods can not deceive some robustness neural network with high probability in the black-box setting. To improve cross-model transferability, we introduce a data augmentation strategy, which performs a simple transformation on the input data. Extensive experiments on HRRP dataset show that our proposed method can greatly enhance the attack success rates.

articleTitle: A jamming angles estimation method based on STAP for airborne radar with conformal array
abstract: For the sparse recovery space time adaptive processing (SR STAP) methods, the jamming spread cannot be obtained by the prior information. Therefore, the clutter and jamming cannot be effectively suppressed at the same time. A method for estimating the jamming angles in clutter environment is proposed. The proposed method selects the data of a single Doppler bin in the clear area of the range Doppler domain to estimate the sample covariance matrix. The covariance matrix is used to estimate the power of each point in the azimuth-elevation space, and the location of peak power points correspond angles of jamming. After the jamming angles are obtained, the jamming and clutter steering vectors dictionary matrix are constructed combining with the prior information. The interference covariance matrix of each range gate can be estimated by SR-STAP methods. Verified by simulation data, the proposed method can accurately estimate the interference angle.

articleTitle: A Novel Frequency Domain based Axis Rotation Transform for Radar Weak Target Detection
abstract: Developing a valid and rapid detection algorithm of a maneuvering weak target has always been a challenging task, where Range Migration (RM) must to be solved. Recently, axis rotation moving target detection (AR-MTD) was proposed to compensate for linear range walk. But this method cannot compensate completely some range cell only by time domain processing. In this paper, a novel frequency domain based axis rotation transform implementation is put forward to supplement the traditional axis rotation transform method. Numerical simulation experiments prove that this method is effective in Radar Weak Target Detection.

articleTitle: Performance Bounds for Joint Estimation of Target Parameters and Radar System Deviations Based on Direct - Path Signal
abstract: In this paper, performance bounds for joint estimation of the Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar deviations and target parameters are discussed. Due to the wide spatial distribution of MIMO radar, it inevitably generates position and velocity deviations, which deteriorate the performance of target parameter estimation. The signal model is reconstructed based on direct-path waves and target echoes. And the performance bounds of the system are derived using Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB). The numerical simulation results show that the CRLB of radar deviations estimation under the method of this paper is lower, which improves the estimation performance of the target parameters.

articleTitle: A Low-complexity Hand Gesture Recognition Method Based on 2D-Trajectory Feature Using Bistatic Radars
abstract: Radar-based hand gesture recognition is robust to the line-of-sight and lighting environments, and has the advantages of non-contact, strong penetrability and protection of user privacy. It is becoming one of the hottest topics in the area of gesture recognition. Most of the existing radar-based hand gesture recognition methods are based on images such as time-distance map and time-frequency map, and have the problems of large model and high computational complexity. To handle these problems, this paper proposes a low-complexity hand gesture recognition method based on two-dimensional trajectory feature using bistatic radars. First, signal preprocessing and target detection are carried out on the radar data. Then, the adaptive order polynomial fitting method is used to fit the centroid and two-dimensional trajectory is then synthesized. After that, a lightweight variable-length long short term memory (LSTM) is designed for identifying hand gestures. The experimental results show that the average recognition rate of the trained people and the untrained people are 98% and 92.0% respectively.

articleTitle: Entangled Photons Based Particle-Level Temporal-Spatial Matching Processing in Quantum Radar
abstract: With the continuous development of quantum technology, entangled signal has been used in more and more fields. Due to the unique temporal-spatial correlation characteristics of entangled signal, it provides promising solutions to problems such as super-resolution and anti-interference. Especially in the context of weak signal, the entangled signal-based sensing is more prominent. In this paper, we present a quantum imaging framework based on particle level matching processing under the correlation characteristics of entangled photons. The temporal-spatial correlation property of the entangled photon is used to realize the matched filtering to accumulate the weak signals in time domain and reconstructed the target image in spatial domain.

articleTitle: Neural Network Residuals Kriging Surrogate and Sobol Method-Based Geometric Sensitivity Analysis for Wire Bonding in T/R Module
abstract: A surrogate model based on neural network residuals kriging (NNRK) method for coupling geometry parameters and transmission performance of wire bonding in T/R Module is established. Compared with traditional electromagnetic (EM) simulation methods, NNRK method maintains the calculation accuracy while significantly reducing the calculation cost of wire bonding interconnection transmission performance, making fast analysis of its transmission performance a reality. By using Sobol sensitivity analysis method and coupling the NNRK surrogate model of wire bonding interconnection, the geometric parameters that affect the transmission performance of wire bonding are calculated, which provide theoretical guidance for the design and optimization of wire bonding interconnection.

articleTitle: An Efficient Frequency-Domain Imaging Algorithm for Medium Targets in Half Space for Single-Input Multiple-Output Array
abstract: Millimeter wave (MMW) and terahertz (THz) have the advantages of short wave length, large bandwidth and high resolution, more than that they have moderate penetration to most non-metallic dielectric materials. So, all these advantages make MMW/THz three-dimensional (3D) imaging technology have the potential for Nondestructive Testing (NDT) of dielectric materials. In order to achieve fast 3D imaging detection of media targets, a MMW/THz 3D media imaging algorithm based on Single-Input Multiple-Output (SIMO) array is proposed in this paper. This algorithm can efficiently realize the 3D reconstruction of media targets, and can provide support for the detection of defects and foreign bodies in media targets.

articleTitle: Polarization Time Reversal Detector with the Time- varying Channel
abstract: Polarization diversity radar enhances the performance of target detection. Time reversal exploits the multipath effect by adaptive matching propagation channels to improve the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and realize high detectability. This paper combines polarization diversity and time reversal technology to propose a time reversal detector suitable for polarization array radar. We carry out the maximum likelihood estimate for the time-varying channel response to solve the channel mismatch problem, which may cause the degradation of time reversal performance. The polarization detector we proposed can take advantage of the channel variations to improve the detectability, and the greater the energy brought by the channel changes, the better the detection performance achieved.

articleTitle: A noise robust forward-looking super-resolution imaging method based on compressive sensing
abstract: The forward-looking imaging technique based on compressive sensing (CS) has attracted wide attention due to its ability to break through the limitation of actual aperture resolution. However, strong noise is usually inevitable in radar imaging, which challenges traditional CS-based imaging method. To enhance the robustness against noise, a two-step processing imaging method is proposed by echo denoising and noise weighting sequentially. Firstly, the echo denoising is completed by using the low rank characteristic of the signal, and then the <tex>$l_{1}$</tex> norm is weighted to suppress the strong noise. Results on simulation data show that the proposed method can estimate the position and amplitude of scatterers precisely at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

articleTitle: Wideband Radar Target Recognition Based on Polarization Features and Double Layer K-LightGBM
abstract: To improve the shape-similar target recognition performance, a polarization features-based double layer K-LightGBM model is proposed in this paper. First, a target features dataset is built, which is based on polarization invariants and two kinds of polarization decompositions of targets. Then, a double layer K-LightGBM model is set up by improving StackNet with <tex>$K$</tex> LightGBM stacked. Finally, the dataset is fed into the proposed model for training and testing. The experimental results show that the proposed method in this paper has better performance in terms of generalization and denoising, compared to many existing state-of-the-art methods, including LightGBM.

articleTitle: In-Vehicle Occupant Detection Based on Zone Source Feature Using MM-Wave MIMO Radar
abstract: Millimeter wave (mm-wave) radar is generally used as an autonomous driving sensor for road environment detection, but it can also play an important role in vehicle interior sensing. In this paper, we propose an in-vehicle occupant detection method based on zone source feature using mm-wave multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar. The zone source feature is extracted from super-resolution range-azimuth (RA) map constructed by multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm. Whether the seat is in absence or occupancy status, the zone source feature basically follows normal distribution and have very little overlap according to the experiment data. Therefore, low constant false alarm rate (1%) can be obtained by setting an appropriate threshold while achieving high detection rate (99.09%). Moreover, the proposed method is implemented on embedded digital signal processor (DSP) and verified in real-time stationary and driving experiment. The high accuracies indicate its robustness and practicability.

articleTitle: Design of Space-borne Deployable Mesh Antennas with Joint Clearances
abstract: The reflector of many space-borne deployable antennas is usually supported by a deployable arm which consists of more than one joints. To deployed successfully, existence of the clearances in the joints is necessary. However, on the other respect, existence of the clearances will degrade the electromagnetic performance, especially the beam pointing error. Therefore, it is of key importance to study the influence of the joint clearances on the electromagnetic performance and make some efforts to reduce this impact. Using the proposed method by the authors previously, the present paper predicts the EM performances of a 10 m diameter deployable reflector antenna with a deployable arm which has 3 joints with clearances. Based on the which, optimization design is performed to decrease the influence of the joint clearances. Optimal size of the clearance, preinstallation angle of the beams in the arm and the jointed components are obtained. The results show that, after design of the present study, the worst-case beam pointing error is reduced by more than 99%, which is of great significance in the engineering practice.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Interference Mitigation in Time-Frequency Maps of FMCW Radars
abstract: With the substantial increase of the FMCW radars used for autonomous driving and other applications in the area of surveillance, mutual interference has become a major concern. Recently, Deep Learning (DL) models have been used in FMCW radar interference mitigation with great success, but no research has been conducted in processing the time-frequency (t-f) maps of acquired beat signals. Considering the different distributions of useful beat signals and interferences in the t-f domain, a fully convolutional network (FCN) is proposed to suppress the interference and noise in the t-f spectrum obtained by the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) algorithm. The experimental results on the simulated radar signals show that the proposed FCN provides superior interference suppression with few parameters. Moreover, the qualitative results on the measured radar signals collected in real-world scenarios emphasize the excellent generalization capacity of the model. Finally, we show that our proposed approach achieves the best performance compared to state-of-the-art techniques.

articleTitle: An Adaptive DoA Estimation Strategy for UAVs Detection
abstract: This paper presents a new strategy to estimate Direction of Arrival (DoA) of UAVs which relies, as first step on a binary test to establish the number of targets present in a given cell under test. Specifically, based on the result of the mention binary test, different DoA estimation algorithms are employed to minimize the computational burden required for the entire processing. The performance of the signal processor is assessed on measured data collected by a C-band radar equipped with a 12-channel phased-array. The results confirm that the proposed strategy is able to discriminate the single from the multiple targets scenario and resolve the UAVs when they are located in one range-Doppler-angle cell.

articleTitle: Multiple information cognition of interrupted sampling repeater jamming in complex scenes
abstract: The dense and varied jamming signals in complex electromagnetic environment pose a great threat to radar detection, especially coherent repeater jamming affects anti-jamming ability seriously. The sufficient cognition of jamming signals is of great significance for effective countermeasures. This paper proposes a multiple information cognition framework and method for interrupted sampling repeater jamming(ISRJ) in complex scenes. Firstly, two one-dimensional convolutional neural networks(1D-CNN) are used to identify jamming types and repeater strategies hierarchically. The various jamming types in complex scenes are identified coarsely, and the specific repeater strategies of ISRJ are identified in detail. Secondly, a one-dimensional parameter estimation deep complex-valued convolutional network (PE-DCCN) is applied to estimate the slice width of ISRJ. Simulation results prove the proposed method can obtain multiple cognition results of ISRJ with high recognition precision and low estimation error.

articleTitle: Multi-Spectral-Attention Dual-Channel Network for Radar-Based Human Gait Recognition
abstract: Deep learning techniques have gained success in radar-based human gait recognition in recent years. To exploit the time-varying micro-Doppler information of human gait, most existing methods generate samples using short time Fourier transform (STFT). By extracting the features of STFT images with different sliding window lengths, dual-channel deep convolutional neural network (DC-DCNN) can obtain high accuracy for human gait. To further improve the performance of the network, this paper designs a multi-spectral-attention dual-channel network for gait recognition. Combined with the channel attention mechanism, the proposed method can achieve higher recognition accuracy without incurring additional radar resources. Experimental results have demonstrated the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: A Target Reconstruction Method for Coherent Multistatic Synthetic Aperture Radar
abstract: Multistatic synthetic aperture radar (MuSAR) has the potential for obtaining a high-resolution radar image by coherently collecting echo data of multiple stations. However, the point spread function (PSF) of coherent MuSAR may present split mainlobes and high sidelobes because its topology structure of multiple stations is distributed. In this paper, a target reconstruction method based on complex-Radon transform (CRT) is proposed to focus the PSF of coherent MuSAR. First, the echo model of coherent MuSAR is introduced. The wavenumber spectrum distributions of MuSAR based on different topology structures are analyzed. Then, the CRT method is adopted to avoid the coupling of two-dimensional wavenumber spectrum. Following, based on the projected wavenumber spectrum slices, a generalized nonuniform sampling iterative adaptive approach (GIAA) is proposed to reconstruct the targets along different directions. Finally, the high resolution imaging result in the ground plane is obtained based on coordinate transform. Simulations are carried out to verify the proposed method.

articleTitle: 3D MIMO ISAR Imaging Using Automotive Millimeter Wave Radar Sensor
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar can achieve high-precision measurements of distance and velocity, which has drawn much attention for both academic research and industrial applications. Traditional inverse synthetic aperture radar can produce two-dimensional (2D) imaging of target's reflectivity. By combing multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) and inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) techniques, it is possible resolve multiple scatters in a range-Doppler cell. In this paper, we present two-dimensional (3D) MIMO ISAR imaging experiments using automotive cascaded mmWave radar sensor. Turntable ISAR imaging results demonstrate the effectiveness of high-resolution 3D imaging. Experimental results on concealed targets show the 3D penetrating imaging ability of mmWave MIMO radar.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Phased Array Radar for High-resolution Imaging
abstract: We have demonstrated a millimeter wave phased array radar prototype which operates in Ka band. After compensating the original echo, the sidelobe of the high resolution range profile (HRRP) can be reduced from −5 dB to −40 dB, which is crucial for the radar aiming of high resolution imaging. Next, we have also proposed an effective method which can extend the usable range of the measured compensation factor. Finally, the inverse synthetic-aperture radar (ISAR) image of plane and drone are also obtained in the experiment. Our work may promote the future design of millimeter wave phased array radar for high resolution imaging.

articleTitle: Cooperative Enhancement of Ship Targets in SAR Images Based on Density Features
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new method to improve the target-to-clutter ratios (TCRs) of SAR image chips cropped from a large SAR image from the perspective of cooperative enhancement (CE) with the density features. First, the superpixel-based saliency map of each SAR image chip is independently obtained. Then, we innovatively design the superpixel-histogram density (SHD) feature of salience maps to accumulate target cues from all the SAR image chips containing ship targets, where the weight of cues from each SAR image chip is calculated in accordance with its self-quality. The SHD feature exploits the dependence of all the SAR image chips, i.e., sparse ship targets and non-sparse sea clutter. Finally, we fuse the salience maps and SHD features of SAR image chips. In this way, the ship target therein is enhanced and the sea clutter is relatively suppressed from the CE viewpoint. Experimental results on Gaofen-3 SAR images are reported to demonstrate that the newly proposed method provides higher TCRs than the state-of-the-art with better target enhancement performance.

articleTitle: Study on Horn Antenna with a High Gaussian Coupling Efficiency
abstract: In this paper, a fast and accurate design method, combining the mode coupling technique and the full-wave simulation, has been introduced to design the smooth-walled horn antenna with a high Gaussian coupling efficiency. As a demonstration, a smooth-walled horn antenna working at terahertz band has been simulated, confirming that the method we proposed can help design horn with high symmetric, low sidelobe patterns in E-plane, H-plane and 45 degree plane.

articleTitle: Selected Pseudo-Labelling With Class Confusion Regularization For Semi-supervised SAR Target Recognition
abstract: SAR images are highly sensitive to imaging conditions, e.g., depression angle, polarization mode and wave band. It is notable that existing enhanced structure in deep learning method does not consider domain discrepancy between training and testing data. In this paper, we employ the target domain selective pseudo-labeling to align the data distribution. To alleviate the mis-labelling issue, we introduce a novel regularization method, class confusion, the probability that neural networks misclassify the prediction between correct and ambiguous classes on target samples. Experimental results on the moving and stationary target acquisition and recognition (MSTAR) dataset can achieve state-of-the-art performance compared to other domain adaptation and model-based methods.

articleTitle: Sidelobe Suppression of SAR Image based on MSVA
abstract: Modified Spatially Variant Apodization (MSVA) is one of the nonlinear apodization methods used for sidelobe control in SAR image while maintaining mainlobe resolution unchanged. In this paper we propose PFA-MSVA algorithm which combines polar format algorithm (PFA) and MSVA. Also, we apply this algorithm to process airborne SAR data and show that by using MSVA one can get better resolution and lower sidelobe level compared with using classic windowing techniques such as Hamming, etc. The simulated and experimental data results demonstrate the effectiveness and practicability of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A Time-domain strip-map processing scheme for FMCW imaging
abstract: For strip-map frequency-modulated continuous wave synthetic aperture radar (FMCW-SAR) imaging, a time-domain processing scheme is proposed in this paper. For no loss of resolution, the angle-overlapped unified polar coordinate is established. Time-domain FMCW back-projection integration is carried out in sub-aperture(SA) process. And the SA wavenumber fusion and full-strip-map wavenumber fusion are successively performed to obtain whole strip-map image. Simulation and real SAR data mapping are used to demonstrate the effectiveness of proposed scheme.

articleTitle: SAR Target Recognition Using Improved Monogenic-Based Feature Extraction Framework
abstract: Applying computer vision methods to synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image recognition is a research trend in recent years, and a series of valuable results have been achieved. In order to use machine learning classifiers for recognition, it is necessary to extract effective features, and most of these features are directly extracted based on grayscale SAR images. SAR data is usually rare, and more difficult to collect than optical images. Therefore, the problem of recognition using a small-size training set for SAR is more challenging to practical pattern recognition methods. The monogenic signal is an extended version of analytic signals in high-dimensional space which has attracted attention. In this paper, a new recognition framework which is based on feature dimensionality augmentation using combined multi-scale monogenic components and histogram of oriented gradient (HOG) feature is proposed. Proposed feature is named as MONO-HOG. This letter focuses on recognition under both standard operating condition (SOC) and small-sample scene. Experiments on moving and stationary target automatic recognition (MSTAR) data set show that our proposed framework has satisfying performance.

articleTitle: Jamming Resource Allocation for Multi-jammer Cooperatively Suppressing Netted Radar Systems
abstract: In this paper, aiming at the scenario of the escort support jamming (ESJ) formation reconnoiters the netted radar system (NRS), a joint jamming beam assignment and power allocation (JJBAPA) strategy is proposed for multi-jammer cooperatively suppressing the NRS. First, we establish the radar echo model based on the transmitted suppressive jamming signal and the geometric position of the NRS and the ESJ system. Then, according to the characteristics of the radar echo, the detection probability of the NRS is derived and used as a performance metric to quantify the detection performance of the NRS. Finally, combined with the practical jamming resource constraints, the JJBAPA optimization problem is formulated and solved. To allocate jamming resources reasonably, we consider the frequency alignment problem between the radars and the jammers. Simulation results verify the effectiveness and superi-ority of the proposed JJBAPA strategy in terms of degrading the detection performance of the NRS.

articleTitle: Two-order Motion Compensation Method based on the Deramp Operation for Spotlight Airborne SAR
abstract: The deramp operation is an essential method to deal with the airborne spotlight SAR data with large azimuth bandwidth by adjusting the azimuth sampling rate. To deal with the mismatch between the radar data and the navigation data in the motion compensation processing, a novel two-order motion compensation method is proposed. In the technique, a reference function based on the residual phase error is constructed and deramped. Furthermore, the second-order motion compensation is implemented in the range-Doppler domain. Simulated experiments demonstrate the validity of proposed approach.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation for Coherent Integration with Partially Correlated Signals
abstract: In this paper, the performance of using coherent integration to detect partially correlated signals is investigated. Firstly, the model of the partially correlated signals is given and their correlations are discussed. Then, the detection and false-alarm probabilities of detecting such signals are mathematically derived. Finally, representative simulations are provided to illus-trate the theoretical results.

articleTitle: An Adaptive SVT-Based Matrix Completion Method for DOA Estimation in Nonuniform Noise
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation in the presence of nonuniform noise. It is known that in most of the existing DOA estimation methods are based on the uniform white noise assumption. In many applications, however, the noise across the array may be nonuniform. To tackle this problem, the matrix completion via adaptive singular value threshold (SVT) is used to find the noise-free covariance matrix. On this basis, the signal and noise subspaces are obtained from the eigendecomposition of the noise-free covariance matrix. Finally, traditional subspace-based DOA estimation can be employed to determine the DOAs. Numerical simulation results are performed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: High Fidelity Simulation of Radar Signatures for Low-flying Targets above Land Surfaces
abstract: This paper proposes a new procedure for high fidelity simulation of radar scattering signatures for low-flying targets above land surfaces. A digital elevation model (DEM) grid pre-processing technique is first developed, which results in terrain DEM with finer grid and rough surface from commercially available low resolution DEM data. Land scattering echo is then generated by combining the grid-refined DEM and a modified semi-empirical model of backscattering coefficient for typical terrains with different covers. A multipath scattering model combined with high frequency approximation techniques for electromagnetic (EM) scattering calculation is adopted for target scattering calculation. Simulation results for different phenomenological signatures, such as radar clutter maps, Doppler spectra and high resolution range profiles (HRRPs) of a complex scene for a generic missile low-flying above typical terrains are presented, demonstrating the validity and usefulness of the proposed high fidelity simulation procedure.

articleTitle: Design of Ultra-Low Cross Polarization Aperture-Coupled Phased Array
abstract: This article presents a microstrip patch planar array with low cross polarization (lower than −40dB simulated for the E- and H-plane) and wide impedance bandwidth (more than 25%). Aperture coupling technique is adopted for reduction of cross polarization and comprehensive methods are employed to realize broad BW. The aperture is excited by a special stripline to avoid background radiation. To increase the scanning angles, blind via holes were designed around radiation patches. An embedded element simulation using periodic boundary conditions was performed in HFSS to validate scanning performance.

articleTitle: CFAR Ship Detection Method of Polarimetric SAR Imagery Based on Whitening Filter Under $\mathcal{G}$ Distribution
abstract: Polarimetric Whitening Filter (PWF) can be used to filter Polarimetric Synthetic Aperture (PolSAR) images to improve the contrast between ships and sea clutter background. For this reason, the output of the filter can be used to detect ships. This work deals with the setting of the threshold over PolSAR images filtered by the PWF. The threshold is mainly determined by the statistics of the clutter. Many distributions according to the polarimetric covariance matrix such as Wishart, <tex>$\mathcal{k}$</tex> -Wishart, <tex>$\mathcal{G}_{0}$</tex> -Wishart, Fisher-Wishart, Beta-Wishart, IBeta- Wishart and <tex>$\mathbf{G\Gamma D}$</tex> -Wishart have used to model sea clutter, whose probability density function (PDF), probability of false alarm (PFA) and the corresponding thresholds based on the PWF have also been obtained recently. In fact, the general inverse Gaussian (GIG) distribution can model many heterogeneous areas, which can also be used in the texture variable in the product model. In this paper, we deal with the PFA and the threshold in the case of GIG districted texture in the multivariate product model, which can be named <tex>$\mathcal{G}$</tex> -Wishart model for the polarimetric covariance matrix. The PDF is derived in closed form with the Fox <tex>$\mathbf{H}$</tex> function, and the PFA is derived in closed form with the multivariate Fox <tex>$\mathbf{H}$</tex> function on special cases. The threshold is derived by the bisection method when the false alarm rate (FAR) is constant. Then, the correctness of PFA is proved by simulation. Finally, experimental results are compared using real data with <tex>$\mathcal{K}$</tex>-Wishart, <tex>$\mathcal{G}_{0}$</tex>-Wishart, Fisher-Wishart demonstrate that the derived forms and the constant false alarm rate (CFAR) algorithm based on PWF are valid and robust.

articleTitle: Optimal Power Allocation for the Joint Radar and Communications With OFDM Waveform Transmission
abstract: In this paper, we propose an optimal power allocation strategy for the joint radar and communications (JRC) with orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveform transmission to improve the performance of radar detection, where the performance of radar detection is measured by kullback-Leibler divergence (KLD). The strategy maximizes the KLD and controls the total transmit power of radar under the constraint of the achievable communication rate to implement the match between radar transmitted powers in subcarriers and the corresponding subchannel conditions of radar and communications. The match can mitigate the noise and interference from the radar point of view, and meanwhile it can keep the achievable communication rate within an acceptable range. Simulation results show that the design based on KLD is effective, and it is also preferable to mutual information (MI).

articleTitle: A Quantization based Censoring Detection Method with Limited Communication Rates for Distributed MIMO Radar
abstract: This paper considers the detection problem for distributed multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar in extreme environments where the communication rates are severely limited. Since both the quantization method and censoring method can reduce the amount of data transmission, we combine them and propose a quantization based censoring detection method. The echo data of different paths are censored by a censoring probability and quantified to different sequences according to the coding guidelines agreed with the fusion center. Then the code sequences will be transmitted and decoded for global decision in the fusion center. Besides, we consider the trade-off between the local censoring probability and the number of quantization, which can achieve the best detection performance under fixed limited communication rates. Eventually, numerical results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method with very little communication rates, and the best trade-off to make the detection probability maximum is found.

articleTitle: Design of Metasurface Aperture for Super-Resolution Computational Microwave Imaging
abstract: Based on the concept of superoscillation, one kind of transmitarray (TA) antenna is proposed to achieve far-field super-resolution focusing in single-frequency (10 GHz) for computational microwave imaging systems. The TA consists of an illuminating feed source and double-layer flat transmitting surfaces, which includes a passive TA (PTA) and a reconfigurable TA (RTA) respectively. The PTA is designed to convert the spherical phase front from the feed to a planar phase front. Dynamic metasurface apertures (DMAs) were obtained by randomly coding RTA aperture. The experimental results of this paper suggest that the double-layer TA antenna can generate a multitude of highly uncorrelated and far-field super-resolution radiation patterns, that is, it has the ability to capture more high-frequency detail information in the scene which cannot be captured by traditional computational imaging systems. In addition, this paper proposes a method for the rapid design of PTA and RTA by extracting the incident field data and using MATLAB to perform numerical approximate calculation. Compared with the calculation depends entirely on full-wave simulation software, such as ANSYS Electronics Desktop, our method ensures a certain accuracy and significantly shorten the period of antenna design.

articleTitle: Mainlobe Coherent Interference Suppression Method Based on Weighted Spatial Smoothing and Eigen-Projection Matrix Preprocessing
abstract: When array radar faces the coherent interference situation, the received expected signal will be erroneously cancelled. Especially when the coherent interference approaches the expected signal and becomes mainlobe coherent interference, the performance of adaptive beamforming method will degrade seriously. In order to solve these problems, a method based on weighted spatial smoothing and eigen-projection matrix preprocessing is proposed to suppress the mainlobe coherent interference in this paper. Firstly, the coherent interference is decorrelated with the expected signal by the weighted spatial smoothing algorithm, then the mainlobe interference is eliminated by the eigen-projection matrix preprocessing matrix. Finally, the effect of covariance matrix mismatch is reduced by diagonal loading. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A Compact Low-power ISM-band Harmonic Radar for RF Receiver Detection
abstract: Harmonic radars have received sustained attention in recent years for unique capability on clutter suppression, which demonstrates huge potential in detecting and locating RF receivers in harsh environment. We implemented a laboratory-level harmonic detection system with a compact single-antenna setup by using standard general instruments and commercial RF modules. The system successfully detected the simulated RF receiver with 0 dBm transmitting power at about 8 m. Furthermore, we revised classical harmonic radar equation by introducing the receiver modules' nonlinear characteristics and updated the relations between the receiving harmonic power, transmitting power and range, which were validated by the observed data by the system. The system could be the test bench for related indoor and outdoor experiments in the future.

articleTitle: Atmospheric Effects on Ultra-High-Resolution Millimeter-Wave ISAR Imagery for Space Targets
abstract: In order to get more detail information about targets, ultra-high-resolution (UHR) millimeter-wave radar (MMW) is widely used. UHR MMW radar is sensitive to errors, and the atmosphere effect is one of the major factors affecting the final imaging quality during the exploring of space targets. In this paper, high-precision radar signal propagation models of the background troposphere and ionosphere are established. Based on the models, the influence mechanism of the atmospheric effect on radar signal echo is investigated. The simulation results show that the tropospheric effect lead to azimuth defocusing and a large shift in the range direction on the image. The ionospheric effect produces the intra-pulse phase error which is inversely proportional to frequency.

articleTitle: SAR Target Detection Based on Improved SSD with Saliency Map
abstract: A target detection method based on improved single shot multibox detector (SSD) is proposed to solve insufficient training samples for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) target detection. Firstly, a residual network is introduced in the feature extraction structure for extracting deep features of the target; then, the aspect ratio of default boxes is redesigned to match different sizes of target detection; finally, the existing dataset is expanded with small samples based on saliency map. The experimental results based on the simulated SAR data and the real SAR data prove that the proposed method has better performance in SAR target detection.

articleTitle: Radar Fusion Imaging Based on Attributed Scattering Center Model
abstract: In this paper, the attributed scattering center model based on a fast feature parameter extraction method is introduced to obtain the geometric electromagnetic characteristics of the target form the radar echo availably. It is time-consuming and computation-difficult to estimate the parameters of the scattering center model. In this paper, an orthogonal matching tracking-relaxation iterative algorithm is adopted. Next, the fusion imaging based on the missing part of the echo data for signal reconstruction is discussed. The proposed method can effectively solve the local discontinuity problem existed in the traditional point-scattering model. Finally, the results show that the proposed method can describe the geometry, location and direction of the target more accurately.

articleTitle: First Demonstration of Small UAV SAR Tomography Using Multibaseline P-Band Data
abstract: Small unmanned-aerial-vehicle (UAV) synthetic aperture radar (SAR) tomography can provide 3-D radar images of targets flexibly and cheaply without layover and geometric distortion. In 2020, a P-band ultrawideband ultrawidebeam (UWB) SAR system was designed and mounted on a multi-rotor UAV. The first multibaseline small UAV SAR tomographic data was collected using the UAV-based UWB SAR system in March 2021, in Chongqing, China. In this paper, the first small UAV SAR tomography experiment is demonstrated including the system and experiment design, data processing and 3-D imaging results.

Index Terms: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Synthetic Aperture Radar

articleTitle: Improved S2ANet based on attention mechanism for small target detection in remote sensing images
abstract: Deep learning has achieved remarkable results in the field of target detection and recognition. For small targets in images, image pyramid can be used to fuse multi-scale features to improve detection performance. However, when test on remote sensing images, it is found that some important small goals will still be missed. Aiming at the problems of small target detection in remote sensing images, this paper proposes two S2ANet improved network variants based on the attention mechanism for synthetic aperture radar(SAR) payload and optical payload: for SAR images, CBAM(Convolutional Block Attention Module) attention is added to the backbone network to increase the attention of the feature extraction network for small targets in the channel and space dimensions; For optical images, firstly increase the CBAM channel attention and spatial attention in the backbone, secondly, the SE(Squeeze And Excitation) channel attention is added to the input features before the channel dimension fusion of the pyramid structure, then the attention-enhanced targets are fully integrated through up-sampling and horizontal splicing operations to improve the missed alarm rate and recall rate of small remote sensing targets. Finally, a comparative verification was carried out on the constructed airborne KU-band SAR data set and the optical remote sensing aircraft data set composed of some DOTA1.5 and FAIR1M data sets. The experimental results proved that the designed two variant networks can be used for small remote sensing. There have been certain improvements in the missed alarm rate, accuracy rate, and recall rate of the target.

articleTitle: The Detection of Range Spread Target Based on Weighted Amplitude Iteration
abstract: Improving the target detection performance in a complex environment is of great significance for low probability of intercept (LPI) radars. To make full use of the target echo energy scattered on multiple range resolution cells, one detection scheme for the detection of a spatially distributed target in Weibull clutter is developed, which is called weighted amplitude iteration-range spread target detector (WAI-RSTD). The detector utilizes the prior information of target scatterer density and realizes the effective accumulation of target multi-scattering center energy based on the ordered statistical detection theory. At the same time, the thought of weighted amplitude iteration is introduced in the algorithm, which has a good suppression effect on Weibull clutter with the shape parameter less than 1.5. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has better detection performance than several existing typical range spread target detectors under various target models, regardless of whether the background clutter is Gaussian or not.

articleTitle: High-Resolution 3-D and 4-D SAR Imaging-The Case Study of Shenzhen
abstract: As an extension of synthetic aperture radar (SAR), SAR tomography (TomoSAR) has the ability of three-dimensional (3-D) reflection reconstruction and multi-scatterers separation, and hence obtains the high-resolution 3-D image of focused target. Differential SAR tomography (D-TomoSAR) extends the synthetic aperture principle into the height direction and the time direction, simultaneously. Different from TomoSAR, it can obtain not only the 3-D structure, but also the deformation information of the observed target, which makes four-dimensional (4-D) SAR imaging become possible. Nowadays, it has proved that it is feasible to achieve 3-D and 4-D imaging of urban buildings. However, the performance of TomoSAR and D-TomoSAR still needs to be further improved, especially when the number of used baselines is limited. In this letter, we introduce compressive sensing (CS) technique into TomoSAR and D-TomoSAR imaging. Using 19 meter-resolution spaceborne TerraSAR-X complex image data, we have achieved TomoSAR and D-TomoSAR imaging of artificial targets, and obtained the high-resolution 3-D and 4-D SAR image of representative buildings in Shenzhen.

articleTitle: Cognitive Waveform Designing Based on Cognitive Radar Theory
abstract: The signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) plays an important role in radar target recognition or target detection. Designing appropriate transmit waveforms to effectively improve the SNR of the echo signal has always been an interesting topic in the field of radar signal processing. A novel cognitive waveform designing method is presented for radar target detection based on cognitive radar theory. Cognitive waveforms are waveforms that are individually designed according to targets and environment. Compared with the traditional Linear Frequency Modulated (LFM) signals, this method uses the range profile of the target to construct cognitive waveforms in the frequency domain which makes full use of the prior knowledge of target and environment. This method can make the SNR of echo signals be maximum after matching filtering under certain energy conditions, and effectively improve the recognition performance of radar targets.

articleTitle: A Prototype for Wideband Forward-looking Imaging Radar in W-band
abstract: Due to the aperture limitation, using wideband signals to improve the performance of forward-looking imaging radar is a very valuable topic. In order to verify that bandwidth can improve the performance of forward-looking imaging, a W-band wideband forward-looking imaging radar prototype is proposed in this paper. It operates at 92 GHz - 96 GHz and provides a three-dimensional image on the illuminated scenes. The prototype uses frequency modulated continuous wave signals to obtain range information and consists of a transmitting antenna and a T-shaped receiving array. Two two-dimensional images are obtained by T-shaped receiving array echoes and are fused with range information to obtain a three-dimensional image of the scene of interest. The prototype mainly consists of a W-band transceiver component, a data acquisition device, and a host computer. Such wideband prototypes possess high range resolution, enables successful separation of closely located targets, and verifies the benefits of wideband signals on improving the performance of forward-looking imaging radar.

articleTitle: DOA Estimation of Compact HFSWR by the Virtual Array Synthesis Algorithm
abstract: Direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation using a small-aperture compact high-frequency surface wave radar (HFSWR) remains challenging due to its poor azimuth resolution. To solve this problem, a novel DOA estimation method is proposed by exploring virtual array synthesis in this paper. The principle of virtual array synthesis is put forward, which is based on the motion of the target relative radar. Then, the rearrangement of the received signals is executed by satisfying the conditions of the virtual array synthesis. Finally, array snapshots are formed by rearranged signals for DOA estimation. Additionally, considering that the target speed is unknown, the maximum peak sidelobe ratio (PSLR) criterion be used for the selection of optimal results. The numerical simulation verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: PolSAR Ship Detection via a Refined Polarimetric Notch Filter
abstract: Detection of ships using polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) data has become a promising research area. The polarimetric notch filter (PNF) detector has demonstrated superior performance in PolSAR ship detection. In this work, a refined PNF based on patch variation indicator is proposed for ship target detection. Meanwhile, a standard polarimetric whitening filter (PWF) is applied to reduce the variation of sea clutter. The experimental results on simulated data and measured data demonstrate that the refined PNF detector exhibits a better performance than the original PNF.

articleTitle: Mainlobe Deceptive Jammer Suppression based on Secondary Frequency Compensation in FDA-MIMO Radar
abstract: The mainlobe deceptive jammers are located in the same angle with the target, degrading the detection and parameter estimation performance of the radar system seriously. To solve this problem, a method based on the secondary compensation with the frequency diversity array-multiple-input multiple-output (FDA-MIMO) radar, is proposed. Firstly, the jammers are moved from the mainlobe to the sidelobe through the secondary frequency compensation. Then, the jammers are suppressed with transmit-receive two-dimensional data-dependent beamforming. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed jammer suppression method is verified with simulations.

articleTitle: High-power X-band dual-channel transmitting module for shipborne radar
abstract: Shipborne radar is an important part of modern maritime combat system. With the improvement of the requirements of the new generation of shipborne radar in low-altitude detection and anti-jamming, multi-function phased array shipborne radar arises at the historic moment. Among them, compared with passive phased array, active multi-function phased array has advantages in detection distance, anti-interference, reliability and so on. The microwave transmitting module, which is an important part of active phased array radar, is the key to its technology. A high-power X-band dual-channel microwave transmitter module for active phased array radar is studied in this paper. The microwave transmitting module is composed of multi-function chip, power amplifier, detection circuit, isolator and so on. It uses gallium arsenide monolithic microwave integrated circuit. This paper focuses on a number of technologies related to microwave emission, including the principle of microwave transmission module, the calculation of microwave transmission circuit, the control mode of microwave amplifier, the thermal design and simulation of the module, the manufacturing process, and the design of three defenses adapted to the marine environment. After the above design and precision manufacturing, a 8.5-10.5GHz dual-channel transmission module with transmission power of CW 10W is realized. It has excellent performance in high-power heat dissipation, so its reliability is very high, especially it can adapt to the harsh environment such as high temperature, high humidity and salt fog at sea.

articleTitle: Array Partition Angle Measurement Method for Distributed Array Radars in Mainlobe Jamming
abstract: In the modern complex electromagnetic environment, array radar systems usually apply adaptive beamforming techniques to form nulls toward the jamming angles for jamming cancellation. However, for mainlobe jamming, the nulls lead to beam distortion, which degrades the performance of angle measurement dramatically. This paper proposes an angle measurement method based on array partition for distributed array radars in the presence of mainlobe jamming. First, the distributed array is partitioned into a subarray-level large aperture virtual array and an element-level small aperture array. Then the adaptive beamforming is performed for the large virtual array to generate narrow nulls at the jamming direction, while the small aperture array forms monopulse sum and difference beams to measure the target angle. Thus, the proposed method effectively suppresses the mainlobe jamming and measures the target angle accurately. Finally, the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method are verified by simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Target Detection and Localization using an EMVS in the Presence of a Strong Jamming
abstract: The problem of detection and localization of a target signal using an electromagnetic vector sensor (EMVS) in the presence of a powerful jammer is addressed in this paper. Drawing upon our recently proposed sliding beamforming concept, a novel sliding beamforming preprocessing for EMVS is designed to cancel the jamming signal entirely, while at the same time, preserving the target signal's EMVS steering vector intact. Target detection and localization strategy are presented subsequently in detail. An example of employing our approach for radar target detection and localization is provided finally.

articleTitle: Waveform Design for Dual-Function Radar Communications Based on the MIMO Platform
abstract: Due to its flexibility in waveform design, multiple input multiple output (MIMO) radar has the superior advantage of transmitting the same waveform for target detection and communication information delivery at the same time. To overcome spectrum congestion and improve the performance of the dual-function radar-communication (DFRC) system further, we propose a new approach for optimizing the beamspace weighting matrix, which can focus the transmit power into the desired spatial region. Furthermore, we provide an effective method for communication information embedding by using the combination of beamspace weighting vectors. Compared with the method based on sidelobe control and waveform diversity, the proposed method has the advantage of a low bit error ratio (BER) when the transmission rate is same. Finally, simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Micro-Doppler Based Human Pose Estimation Framework for Single-channel Ultra-Wideband Radar
abstract: Human pose estimation based on optical sensors is difficult to solve the situation under harsh environment and shielding. In this paper, a Micro-Doppler (MD) based human pose estimation for the single-channel ultra-wideband (UWB) radar, called MD-Pose, is proposed. It is found that the MD signature contains the time-varying motion of the human torso, arms, legs, hands, and feet, which can be used in the pose estimation task. The MD spectrum of human echo is obtained by the STFT transform, which is the input of proposed MD-Pose. An asymmetric U-Net network is trained with UWB radar MD spectrum, which can estimate the human keypoints. The experimental results of a single-channel UWB radar validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Automotive radar 4D Point-cloud Imaging with 2D Sparse Array
abstract: The automotive radar plays an important role in the field of advanced driver assistant systems (ADASs), the detection for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV), etc. However, most automotive radar products can only estimate the azimuth, and it is necessary for automatic driving technology to acquire the height information. In this paper, we propose a signal processing algorithm based on the 2D sparse multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) antenna array, which can detect the range, the velocity, the azimuth, and the elevation of target scatters respect to the radar, and those information can form a clear point-cloud image. The 2D hybrid sparse receiver array is firstly designed with the advantage of reducing the hardware resources, such as the number of transceiver channels. Sequentially, through the fast algorithm of 2D-FFT digital beamforming (DBF), the matrix completion (MC) and the correction of motion-induced phase by the switch delay of the time-division MIMO (TDM-MIMO), the azimuth and elevation of scatters can be presented. Finally, the experiment validates that a point-cloud image like lidar can be presented by the algorithm we propose.

articleTitle: Joint power and bandwidth allocation algorithm for radio frequency stealth radar
abstract: Radio frequency stealth has always been one of the key problems to be solved in combat. Aiming at the problem of multi-target tracking in radar network, an optimal allocation algorithm of joint power and bandwidth based on radio frequency stealth is proposed. Since the posterior Cramer Rao lower bound (PCRLB) can be used as the performance index to measure the target tracking accuracy, the algorithm takes the weighted sum of the transmitting power and bandwidth of each radar irradiating the target as the cost function, and takes the performance parameters of the netted radar system and the tracking accuracy threshold greater than or equal to PCRLB as the constraint condition to construct the algorithm including radar selection, The optimization model of transmission power and bandwidth. Then, fix the radar target selection, use particle swarm optimization algorithm to solve, get the optimal allocation value of power and bandwidth, and then use Hopcroft Karp algorithm to select the best match between radar and target. Finally, the simulation results show that compared with the average resource allocation algorithm, the proposed algorithm can effectively reduce the resource consumption of netted radar and improve the RF stealth performance.

articleTitle: CNN Based Joint Positioning and Pose Recognition of Concealed Human for 3D Through-Wall Imaging Radar
abstract: Information about concealed human targets behind wall including target position, pose, etc. is crucial for the through-wall sensing applications. In this paper, we propose a convolutional neural network (CNN) based through-wall multi-task processing framework, using a low-frequency 3D ultra-wideband (UWB) multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) radar. First, we use the 3D UWB MIMO radar to capture the concealed human echoes at different ranges and under different motions including standing, sitting, squatting and lying, with back-projection algorithm adopted to construct the 3D radar images. We label the obtained 3D radar images according to the human target motions, and divide them into the training and validation datasets at the ratio of 3:1 randomly. Then, we design a mini end-to-end full convolutional consisted of 2 modules for 3 tasks: human detection, positioning and pose recognition. One is convolutional module to extract the features of the azimuth and distance for the first two tasks, the other is residual module to extract height features for the last task, with different features contacted to improve performance of our network. The loss function of each task are: binary cross entropy, mean square error and cross entropy, with the moment estimation (Adam) as an optimizer. Finally, we get the confidence, normalized coordinates and pose category of human targets from the network. Field experimental shows that the proposed method can be used for the joint positioning and pose recognition multi-task application with high accuracy.

articleTitle: Wide-Band Interference Mitigation for SAR Based on Generative Adversarial Network
abstract: The presence of wide-band interference (WBI) seriously affects the imaging quality of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) as well as the target scattering characteristics, which reduces the accuracy of subsequent SAR image interpretation. This paper proposes a WBI interference mitigation algorithm for SAR based on generative adversarial network (IM-GAN), which can extract the time-frequency features of WBI in time-frequency domain to achieve low-loss reconstruction of the target echo signal. Firstly, the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) is used to transform the radar echo signal into the time-frequency domain. Then, the GAN is utilized to reconstruct the target signal by extracting the characteristic differences between WBI and target echoes. Finally, the time-frequency spectrogram of SAR echo signal after interference mitigation is transformed to the time domain using inverse short-time Fourier transform (ISTFT). The effectiveness of IM-GAN is verified by the WBI mitigation experiments of the measured dataset in TOPSAR mode recorded by the Sentinel-1B, and its superiority is demonstrated by the comparison results of different SAR interference mitigation methods.

articleTitle: Novel SAR Autofocus Method Based on Deep Learning with GAN Network
abstract: This paper focuses on SAR autofocus based on deep learning. Firstly, considering the influence of phase on radar imaging results, aiming at the problem of defocus of SAR imaging results and poor focusing effect of some SAR imaging results by traditional autofocus methods, a SAR autofocus complex generation adversarial network model is constructed by using the method of deep learning, and the key parameters of the network are given. Then, the network training set and test set are constructed, and using the realistic measured SAR imaging results to train and test the network. Finally, the autofocus results of the network are displayed, and the autofocus results of GAN network are evaluated by using image entropy as an objective evaluation index, which proves the feasibility of using deep learning to solve the problem of SAR autofocus.

articleTitle: Design of Ridge Gap Waveguide Slot Antenna Array for Millimeter Wave Radar
abstract: This paper presents a slot antenna array with three transmitting and four receiving based on ridge gap waveguide (RGW). The proposed antenna uses the structural characteristics of electromagnetic band gap (EBG) to solve the problems of high dielectric loss and limited gain of the traditional microstrip millimeter wave radar antenna. The simulation results show that the bandwidth of the proposed RGW slot receiving antenna array is about 2GHz and the operating band gain is more than 21dB. The bandwidth of RGW slot transmitting antenna array is about 2.64GHz while the operating band gain is more than 13dB. The proposed antenna has high radiation efficiency which is suitable for millimeter wave radar antenna application.

articleTitle: The Design and Implementation of Multi-radar Signal-level Cooperative Detection System
abstract: Distributed multi-radar cooperative detection can effectively detect stealth targets based on backscattering characteristics, and with the rapid development of communication and computing technology, signal-level fusion will become the development trend of multi-radar data fusion in future. Multi-radar signal-level cooperative detection technology is systematically studied in this paper. The concept, system composition, and work flow of multi-radar signal-level cooperative detection is given, and the realization process of signal-level cooperative detection and anti-jamming technology is researched. A cooperative detection test system consisting of 5 radars was constructed to test the feasibility of multi-radar signal-level cooperative detection and anti-jamming technology, and the test results show that, compared with single radar detection, the performance of multi-radar signal-level cooperative detection is greatly improved.

articleTitle: Radio Tomographic Imaging in Wide-Beam Transmission and Narrow-Beam Reception Mode
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel wide-beam transmission and narrow-beam reception mode in radio tomographic imaging (RTI) field. Specifically, we first introduce the ellipse model in the wide-beam transmission mode which approximately describes the propagation of the signal in the unknown scenario. Then, a joint iterative reconstruction method based on the initial value of average intensity is proposed. Finally, the numerical results validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed wide-beam transmission and narrow-beam reception mode and reconstruction method.

articleTitle: Detection of weak target based on stretch processing and chirp-z transform in Passive Bistatic Radar
abstract: This paper considers the range migration problem for realizing the long-time coherent integration of a weak target in passive bistatic radar (PBR). In particular, we analyze the causes of range migration in PBR system in terms of the detection characteristics of continuous wave. We also propose a novel range migration correction method in the frequency domain, where stretch processing and chirp-z (CZT) transform are adopted to eliminate the range migration and thus obtain long-time coherent integration of the target's energy. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Fast Pattern Synthesis for Nonuniform and Conformal Antenna Arrays
abstract: A fast algorithm is introduced for the pattern synthesis of the nonuniform and conformal antenna arrays. It is based on the principle of the planar/cylindrical/spherical near-field technique. It transforms a nonuniform or conformal array to a uniform one by establishing a virtual uniform grid, so that the Fast Fourier Transform Algorithm (FFT) can be implemented to decrease the computation time significantly. The new method is validated through numerical examples.

articleTitle: Design of an S/X Dual-Band Shared Aperture Antenna Array
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band shared aperture antenna array operating at S- and X-band is presented. In the topology, microstrip patch structure at S-band is stacked by X-band patch antennas. By means of structure reuse technology and physical isolation of feed networks, high channel isolation between the two frequency bands has been achieved. Measured results agree well with the simulations. The proposed antenna array has an impedance bandwidth of 6.1% at S-band and 14.8% at X-band.

articleTitle: Ground Moving Target Focusing via TRP-SCFT-DPT for SAR
abstract: Range migration (RM) and Doppler frequency migration (DFM) will occur in the moving target signal due to the influence of along-track velocity and cross-track velocity. The moving target in SAR image is usually defocused. To solve these problems, a new and effective method of ground moving target imaging is proposed. Firstly, the influence of cross-track velocity of the moving target is eliminated by using the time reversal process-scaled Fourier transform (TRP-SCFT), and the along-track velocity of the moving target is estimated. Secondly, a method based on discrete polynomial-phase transform (DPT) and phase correction function is proposed to estimate the cross-track velocity of moving target. Finally, the estimated along- and cross-track velocities are used to construct the matched filter function to focus the target. The developed method can effectively focus the moving target without the residual correction errors. In addition, the proposed method avoids exhaustive searching operation and has an advantage in the computational complexity. Simulation and real data processing results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A method of automatic ISAR Image quality evaluation
abstract: It is of great significance to select high quality ISAR imaging results from massive data processing results to effectively obtain target information for target recognition. In this paper, an automatic quality evaluation method for ISAR images is proposed, which can automatically filtering and excluding low-quality images. Firstly, the quality evaluation standard image database was established by expert evaluation and objective model evaluation. Then, the features of ISAR images are extracted by convolutional neural network. Finally, SVM classifier is used to evaluate the image quality. Experimental results show that the proposed method is more reasonable, accurate and efficient than the objective image quality evaluation method without reference.

articleTitle: Non-line-of-sight SAR imaging by multi-scattering of millimeter-wave
abstract: Non-line-of-sight (NLOS) imaging aims to reconstruct the image of hidden targets with the property of multi-scattering, which tremendously broadens the detectable range of sensors and has the potential in the fields of autonomous driving, anti-terrorism, etc. However, in the field of radar, most of the researches on NLOS focus on extracting signal characteristic, hidden targets localization, and hidden targets tracking, etc. The corresponding models and algorithms of NLOS imaging are urgently needed to be developed. In this paper, we establish a novel imaging model of looking around corner (LAC) scene. Based on the model, a time-domain coherent algorithm is proposed, the method has the capability of extracting the surface and accurate position of hidden target without prior knowledge. Finally, several metal balls are placed in the NLOS area to construct a LAC observation scene. In the line-of-sight area, a millimeter-wave multi-input-multi-output radar is exploited to synthesize a one-dimension (1-D) antenna array with the framework of 1-D scanning. The experimental results verify the effectiveness of our NLOS technique with the clear geometric features and the accurate position of targets.

articleTitle: Research on the Wind Resistance Method of Valley Mouth based on Numerical Simulation
abstract: The larger the aperture of the radio telescope and the higher the operating frequency band, the more serious the observation performance will be affected by the environmental wind load. Optimizing the wind field environment of the site is one of the important tasks to ensure the stable operation of high-performance telescopes. Based on the analysis of the geomorphology and wind condition of the site for the Qitai 110 m Radio Telescope(QTT), it is proposed to use the landform of the valley mouth of the site as the research object to establish a simplified geographical model of wind field simulation, and wind field simulation is carried out under three conditions of no wind resistance measures, windbreak wall and windbreak net at the valley mouth. Based on the simulation results, both the windbreak wall and the windbreak net can effectively reduce the wind speed at the antenna position. In terms of wind speed reduction value, the wind speed reduced by the windbreak wall is slightly greater than that of the windbreak net, but the turbulence caused by the windbreak is also stronger. Through this research, it can provide a preliminary reference for wind resistance design of antenna site, and also provide a foundation for further research.

articleTitle: Multi-channel SAR moving target detection based on simulation samples and transfer learning
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) moving target detection is always a key technology in the field of radar signal processing. However, due to the unique military background of radar, the real SAR data containg ground moving targets is hardly to obtain, and leading to the lack of labeled moving target data when applying a network. Therefore, an improved convolutional neural network (CNN) is proposed in this paper, in which local maximum mean difference (LMMD) is added to the loss function of the neural network as a measurement method, and neural network parameters are trained by stochastic gradient descending, so that the difference in distribution between the source domain and the target domain is constantly reduced in the representation of the neural network. The results show that the recognition accuracy is better than the previous deep learning, which verifies the effectiveness of the proposed deep transfer learning (TL) model based on the simulation of multi-channel SAR moving target in the case of scarce measured data.

articleTitle: Target Spatial-Frequency Scattering Response Sparse Approximation using Multi-static Radar Observations
abstract: Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) can form an image of the target with a sequence of wideband coherent observations, but it is generally difficult to generalize ISAR images from other directions. In this paper, with observations of a noncoherent multistatic radar system to the same target, we study how to approximate the target spatial-frequency joint response by the scattering centers target model. We optimize the scattering intensities of the scatterers such that the target response at selected frequency ticks and spatial directions, under sparse constraints to select proper number of scattering centers. Numerical results with a 3D plane model indicates that the target response can be approximated by a few scattering centers in a good accuracy, even for spatial directions in which the target is not probed before.

articleTitle: Track-Before-Detect Method for Targets with Appearance Time Uncertainty
abstract: Traditional velocity filtering based track-before-detect (VF - TBD) methods jointly process multiple successive frames in a processing batch. However, the target appearance time is uncertain in practice. When a target appears after the first frame of the current processing batch, energy integration may be corrupted by the noise-only frames and performance loss may occur. In this paper, a VF - TBD method to detect and track targets with uncertain appearance time is proposed. The number of jointly processed frames is adjusted by matching the target appearance time. Each measurement cell in every informative frame is converted to Cartesian coordinates and predicted according to a hypothetical velocity. Measurement of every cell in each informative frame is added onto the cell closest to the predicted position. Effective energy integration and superior performance can be obtained since the interference of noise-only frames can be well eliminated. An additional target appearance time estimation can be supplied. Procedures for the proposed method are derived in detail. Simulation experiments show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm compared with conventional VF - TBD methods.

articleTitle: An Overview of Terahertz Beam Scanning Antenna
abstract: This paper overview of the design and technical route of terahertz beam scanning antenna. Firstly, the applications of THz beam scanning antenna array are briefly reviewed. Then, the design route of THz beam scanning antenna array summarized. After that, the mechanical scanning antenna, the frequency scanning antenna array, and the phased array antenna which include of liquid crystal, graphene, diode, MEMS, CMOS and HEMT phase modulation technology introduced in detail.

articleTitle: GMT Imaging of Synthetic Aperture Radar Based on Spectra Recognition
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is an all-weather high resolution imaging radar. When there is a moving target, the target is often submerged by the surrounding strong background. Therefore, it is very hard to detect the moving target. In this paper, we proposed a new ground moving target (GMT) imaging method based on spectra recognition. Firstly, the velocity and position of the moving target is obtained based on GMTI method. And the spectra of GMT is recognized. Then, the squint angle and the pulse repeat frequency (PRF) is well designed, which can guarantee that the clutter and GMT spectra can be separated clearly. Unpolluted GMT spectra is obtained by a band-pass filter. Lastly, for GMT SAR imaging, a moving target is regarded as a steady target under an equivalent geometry with a new equivalent squint angle and a new SAR platform velocity. The SAR image is obtained with the range-Doppler algorithm. The experimental results obtained by simulation show the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Interferometric Phase Measurement Using Reduced Azimuth Multichannel SAR Based on Sparse Regulariztion
abstract: Azimuth Multichannel SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) system has been well studied in recent years, for its capacities for high resolution and wide swath (HRWS) imaging. In this study, we further extend its capacity for interferometric phase measurement.
