First, based on common azimuth multi-channel mode, to form additional interferometric baseline vertical to flight path, three different extensions of channel modes are designed utilizing effective phase center (EPC) principle. Among them, one named reduced-SIMO (Single Input and Multiple Output) mode outperforms, which only needs one additional channel. Furthermore, the signal model in this mode is established and the interferometric phase is solved based on sparse regularization. Experimental results based on simulated data and equivalent measured data verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed reduced-SIMO mode and the interferometric phase solving method. With this extension capacity for interferometric phase measurement, it becomes available for both high resolution imaging and terrain profile measuring of wide-swath scene.

articleTitle: Automatic Target Recognition Based on Time Reversal HRRP
abstract: Aiming at the problem of high altitude target recognition in wideband radar, a method of high altitude target identification based on time reversal (TR) is proposed. First, a wideband radar time reversal high resolution range profile (TR-HRRP) is constructed. Then, the central moment and waveform entropy features of TR-HRRP are extracted and introduced into support vector machines (SVM) as classification features. Finally, the high altitude target of wideband radar is classified and recognized. The established simulation data are used for validation of identification effect. The experimental results show that the method has a high recognition rate for high altitude targets, which has good fitness in application value.

articleTitle: Height Error Analysis of Range Migration in Interferometric Imaging Radar Altimeter Onboard Processing
abstract: As a new type of radar altimeter, interferometric imaging radar altimeter (InIRA) is used to realize high accuracy of sea-level elevation measurement and wide swath observation. Compared with traditional radar altimeter, InIRA applies the technology of interferometric synthetic aperture radar (SAR), so there is a high requirement of onboard memory and downlink speed for InIRA. In order to reduce data rate, InIRA must adopt onboard real-time processing. After image focusing and interferometric processing, the radar echo data will be transformed into interferometric phase, and the data rate will be greatly reduced. Range migration correction is a part of InIRA real-time processing, but range migration correction requires interpolation calculation, which requires long computing time and high resource consumption. Based on the InIRA simulation model, this paper analyzes the height measurement error caused by range migration, and verified by the processing result of Tiangong-2 InIRA. The results show that the height measurement error introduced by range migration is small enough to ignore range migration correction in InIRA real-time processing under certain condition.

articleTitle: Transmit Signal Design for Polarimetric Radars under Local Waveform Constraints
abstract: The joint design of transmit signals and receive filters for polarimetric radars is investigated. For an extended target with different polarimetric responses, the detection performance can be improved by leveraging polarization diversity of the transmit waveform, i.e., matching the horizontal and vertical polarization signals to counterparts of the target response. Besides, to meet some system requirements, each polarization signal is expected to approach some reference signal with good properties. Hence, we aim to maximize the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) while maintaining a closeness to a particular reference waveform, as well as an energy constraint. The resulting problem is solved based on the majorization-minimization (MM) method. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, the advantages of polarization diversity and local design.

articleTitle: Analysis of THz electromagnetic characteristics for passive jamming corner reflectors
abstract: Corner reflectors have the characteristics of low costs, wide frequencies, omni -directionality, easy to use, long-lasting interference and obvious interference effects. A corner reflector has a strong backscattering cross section(RCS), which can produce strong false targets for radar detection, so as to cover up the real targets and therefore plays the role of interference, deception and inducement. By comparing the RCS of an icosahedral reflector at terahertz (220GHz) and X-band (10GHz), and the RCS as well as images of the icosahedral reflector with the octahedral reflector, it is concluded that the reflection intensity of the icosahedral reflector is obviously better than the octahedral reflector, and the directivity is better than the octahedral reflector, which is more suitable for a false target to decoy radars; the peak sidelobe ratio of octahedral reflector is higher than that of the icosahedral reflector, which is more suitable for target calibration.

articleTitle: Multi-scale Broad Learning System for SAR Automatic Target Recognition
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) Automatic Target Recognition (ATR), as a frontier topic in the domain of artificial intelligence regarding anthropology, has witnessed some good results as deep learning technology progressively develops. However, it is still limited by the complexity of the deep structure network in need of a large number of parameters and high dimensions, easily leading to a great consumption of time. To solve this problem, this paper proposes an effective and efficient method, which is called multi-scale Broad Learning System (BLS). First, the SAR images is down-sampled to obtain images of different sizes and feature extraction. Then, the multi-scale images are concatenated. Finally, it is input to the broad learning network for training to obtain the final prediction results. Extensive experiments with the proposed method on SAR datasets can be conducted within 11.35s while sustaining an accuracy of 97.55<sup>%</sup>, impressively outstripping other state-of-the-art methods both in speed and accuracy.

articleTitle: Tensor-based SR-STAP for PA-MIMO Airborne Radar
abstract: Phased-array multiple-input multiple-output air-borne Radar faces a severe sample shortage problem in space-time adaptive processing (STAP) applications. Fortunately, the sparse recovery STAP (SR-STAP) offers a new perspective to drastically reduce the requirement of training samples, however, its application is greatly limited by the high complexity of SR algorithms. This paper attempts to introduce the tensor representation to reformulate the SR-STAP problem. We give a basic tensor-based SR-STAP problem formulation and further develop a novel fast OMP SR-STAP method with the tensor representation. The numerical experiments show that the proposed tensor-based method has a great advantage in complexity over the conventional SR-STAP methods.

articleTitle: DOA estimation of unknown frequency for vector hydrophone array based on baffle
abstract: When the rectangular air cavity sonar baffle is applied to the direction estimation of vector hydrophone uniform linear array, the performance of the direction estimation algorithm based on the reflection coefficient of the baffle is degraded due to the unknown reflection coefficient, In order to reduce the influence of the reflection coefficient of the baffle on the azimuth estimation results, the training set and the test set are obtained under the condition of considering the vibration and sound structure coupling of the steel plate layer of the rectangular air cavity baffle, Through the training and testing of the network, it is proved that the machine learning algorithm can solve the azimuth estimation problem of the vector hydrophone array based on the baffle when the frequency of the incoming wave is unknown, and obtain better performance than the algorithm based on the reflection coefficient of the baffle.

articleTitle: TI-ADC System Mismatch Error Estimation and Compensation
abstract: With the development of radar technology, the system bandwidth has become wider and wider, and the sampling rate of the single-chip analog-to-digital converter (Analog to Digital Converter, ADC) can no longer meet some high-performance applications. Time Interleaved ADC (TI-ADC) technology uses multiple low-speed ADCs to achieve high-speed acquisition, which solves the contradiction between ADC chip sampling rate and resolution, and is currently the most commonly used high-speed acquisition solution. Due to the system architecture, the TI-ADC acquisition process will produce offset mismatch, gain mismatch, delay mismatch and frequency-related mismatch, which seriously affects system performance. This paper improves the TI-ADC system mismatch error estimation algorithm and proposes a compensation algorithm based on the perfect reconstruction filter model.

articleTitle: Quad-Pol Reconstruction from Compact Polarimetric SAR Data Based on Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: Compact polarimetric (CP) synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has attracted much attention in recent years due to its large swath and capacity of the polarimetric information. Pseudo quad-polarimetric (quad-pol) data reconstruction is an important technology. In this work, we propose a novel pseudo quad-pol reconstruction method. A complex-valued dual-branch convolutional neural network (CV-DBCNN) is proposed for the reconstruction of the pseudo quad-pol data, which utilizes complex-valued convolutional layers and complex-valued activation function to fully extract the polarimetric information of the CP data. The experiments are carried on three quad-pol images acquired by three different sensors, the results show that the proposed method has higher accuracy than other state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: NLOS Vehicle Detection and Localization for Automotive Application
abstract: This paper considers the detection and localization problem for the non-line-of-sight (NLOS) front-front vehicle obscured by the line-of-sight (LOS) front vehicle. Specifically, we first analyze the exploration effects of the radar echoes propagating along the ground reflection path and the side vehicle reflection path via the real data and confirm the ground reflection path can be reliably utilized to detect the front-front vehicle. Then, we establish the ground reflection electromagnetic wave propagation model and the CFAR technique is utilized to acquire the front-front vehicle's range. Next, the multi-channel phase comparison method is exploited to obtain the position of the NLOS front-front vehicle. Finally, the experiment results validate that the NLOS front-front vehicle can be detected and located depending on the ground reflection path.

articleTitle: A noise-robust ISAR imaging method for GEO satellite-based passive ISAR
abstract: The geosynchronous broadcasting satellite-based passive ISAR (GEO satellite-based P-ISAR) always suffers from the extremely low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) condition, which is caused by the great distance between the satellite transmitter and the terrestrial receiver. The low SNR condition yields the main challenge on ISAR imaging of the target. In the case where the SNR is so low that the target information in the range profiles is submerged by noise, the existing ISAR imaging methods will no longer be valid, and novel methods are required. In this paper, a batch width extension (BWE) method is proposed to deal with the extremely low SNR condition, where the batch width refers to the duration of the signal that generates a range profile. By extending the batch width and using a target shift compensation process, the energy of the target signal can be well accumulated to corresponding range cells so that the SNR of the range profiles can be improved. Then the conventional autofocusing method can be employed to obtain the target image. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Sparse Time-Frequency Reconstruction of Weighted ADMM Based on Single-Window
abstract: Feature extraction and recognition of micromotion targets based on the joint time-frequency (JTF) analysis has received extensive attention in the field of radar imaging and automatic target recognition in recent years. Compressed sensing theory uses the sparsity of the radar signal JTF representation to solve the problems of low resolution and cross terms caused by traditional JTF analysis methods. However, the available methods mostly use high-dimensional non-parametric dictionaries, and when the number of samples of the signal is large, the calculation complexity is relatively high. To solve this problem, this paper constructs a single-window JTF model, which effectively reduces the dimension of non-parametric dictionaries. Then, a weighting term is proposed, which can extract the time-frequency ridges and enhance the weaker components in the JTF distribution. Finally, the Alternating Direction Multiplier Algorithm (ADMM) is used to solve the optimal sparse JTF distribution. The validity of the method has been proved by simulated data.

articleTitle: A New Method of Vehicle Target Radar Data Segmentation Based on DBSCAN and Lane Recognition
abstract: Since the raw radar data is always seriously mixed with echoes from multiple targets in a complex traffic environment, it is extremely difficult to segment the target data for feature extraction. In this paper, a new method of vehicle target radar data segmentation based on Density Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) and lane recognition is proposed. After signal preprocessing, the vehicle features with lane label are used to train lane recognition model. Then, the coarse segmentation can be obtained by DBSCAN. Finally, the coarse segmentation results are further finely segmented through the above trained lane recognition model. By real-data comparative experiment based on a millimeter-wave (MMW) radar, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method for vehicle targets data segmentation in complex traffic environment over the DBSCAN are verified.

articleTitle: Research on The Application of Track Association of Multi-target Continuous Tracking Based on Regional Radar Chain
abstract: In this paper, the problem of track association in multi-target continuous tracking scenario of regional radar chain in aerospace monitoring is studied. The key problems of track association in multi-target continuous tracking scenario of regional radar chain are analyzed, and the corresponding algorithm flow is proposed. The feasibility of the algorithm process is verified by simulation experiments. Through the test of the measured data of aerospace launch activities over the years by a regional radar chain, the success rate of track association is 91.67%, which proves the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Iceberg Detection Based on L-band Compact Polarimetric SAR
abstract: Iceberg monitoring is of great significance to navigation safety in polar region. This paper carried out iceberg detection research based on L-band Compact Polarimetric SAR. Firstly, the iceberg detection performance of 23 Compact Polarimetric SAR features in complex sea conditions was evaluated comprehensively by using three indexes of Euclidean distance, Bhattacharyya distance and target-background contrast. The Compact Polarimetric SAR features with better iceberg detection potential were screened out: the second eigenvalue <tex>$\lambda_{2}$</tex> of covariance matrix. Then, the polarization feature <tex>$\lambda_{2}$</tex> was used to detect iceberg by the generalized gamma distribution CFAR method. Compared with the classical single-polarization (BV-CFAR) and full-polarization (GNF) detection methods, the method proposed has a good detection performance for icebergs of different sizes in complex sea conditions, and the developed method has a good application prospect.

articleTitle: 3D Imaging for 77 GHz MIMO-SAR
abstract: With the development of millimeter-wave radar technology, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging with millimeter-wave radar has been widely investigated in both academic research and industrial applications. However, traditional SAR imaging algorithms mostly focus on two-dimensional information of detected targets which restricts the development of 3D scenes reconstruction applications. In this paper, a novel low-cost 3D imaging algorithm based on 77 GHz commercial millimeter-wave radar is proposed by fusing the advantages of wideband radar, SAR, and multiple-input multi-output(MIMO) radar. Through processing real data collected by a 77 GHz MIMO-SAR, the proposed algorithm is verified successfully with extracted range-azimuth-height information and is capable of reconstructing the real-world 3D scenes with high spatial resolution.

articleTitle: Multi-Object Tracking with Adaptive Trajectory PMBM under Limited Field of View Radars
abstract: This paper addressed the challenging problem of Multi-Object Tracking (MOT) without prior knowledge of clutter rate and detection probability under limited Field of View (FoV) radars, which will result in biased estimates. The robust filter is that of cardinality Probability Hypothesis Density (CPHD) filter applied to adaptively learn the clutter rate and detection profile. Moreover, the track initiation in the limited FoV is clearly inefficient due to the object birth intensity without covering the whole state space for multi-object. An adaptive trajectory Poisson multi-Bernoulli mixture (A-TPMBM) tracker is proposed to adaptively design the object birth intensity by the received measurements at multi-scan, which can proceed to improve performance of track initiation. The proposed measurement-driven birth intensity benchmarks the tracking accuracy of against three idea filters for MOT with radar network.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of Abnormal Shape Trihedral Corner Reflector Scattering Characteristics
abstract: In this paper, two kinds of abnormal-shaped trihedral corner reflectors are designed, including circular arc and convex surface type. The radar cross section (RCS) of corner reflectors is simulated and analyzed in detail. In circular trihedral corner reflector structure, the width of 3dB scattering pattern is narrower than regular trihedral corner reflector of the same size, and the center of scattering pattern is also rotated. In convex surface corner reflector structure, its RCS is significantly lower compare to regular reflector of the same size.

articleTitle: Wide-region Instantaneous Imaging Radar: Prototype System and Preliminary Results
abstract: This paper proposes a wide-region instantaneous imaging radar (WIIR) concept. Similar as ubiquitous radar in some way, WIIR can be able to simultaneously realize the persistent observation of wide-region and achieve the instantaneous two-dimensional high-resolution imaging. The prototype system of WIIR is described and some preliminary experimental results are presented. It is verified by these experimental results that the proposed WIIR is suitable for time-sensitive targets imaging and may be able to provide a potential alternative for urban sensing missions.

articleTitle: LPI Waveform Design by Utilizing Environmental Background Power Spectrum
abstract: We investigate the problem of low probability interception (LPI) waveform design by utilizing power spectrum of the practical electromagnetic environment. Firstly, the ambient power spectrum at the interception receiver is estimated to obtain the power spectrum template with LPI performance. The autocorrelation template is added to the model to obtain the required detection performance. To jointly optimize the LPI performance and the detection performance, an optimization problem with variable weight is formulated. To address the optimization, the template fitting approach (TFA) is utilized to solve the problem and obtain a satisfied performance. Finally, the simulation and analysis of LPI performance and detection performance of the proposed signal are given.

articleTitle: MIMO-based Terahertz Radar for Forward-Looking 3-D Imaging at 340 GHz
abstract: An all-solid-state terahertz imaging system based on 2-D sparse MIMO array is presented to achieve 3-D forward-looking imaging. The sweep bandwidth of the system ranges from 335.04 GHz to 340.08 GHz, which guarantees the range resolution. A 2-D MIMO array is designed for realizing high cross-range imaging resolution. The 3-D images are reconstructed by back-projection algorithm. The experimental results verify the imaging capability of the system.

articleTitle: Multi-human Separation Method Based on CNN-Mask-PIT
abstract: Human activities classification based on micro-Doppler effect is a hot topic in the field of radar detection. However, when there are multiple humans, the motion mechanism of the multi-human target is complex, the components are mixed, and the micro motion features of each component are highly similar, which lead to difficulties in the classification of the multi-human activities. In order to overcome these problems, a multi-human separation method based on convolution neural network Mask generation and permutation invariant training (CNN-Mask-PIT) is proposed in this paper. In this method, the multi-human target is separated on the time-frequency (TF) images. The Mask matrixes are generated by CNN, and then the generated multiple Mask matrices are multiplied with the original TF image to obtain the separated TF images, so as to realize the effective separation of multi-human separation. The permutation invariant training (PIT) is introduced to solve the label arrangement problem by minimizing the separation error. Finally, the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method are verified on the multi-human TF images generated based on motion capture data.

articleTitle: Wideband Adaptive Beamforming for Mainlobe Interferences Based on Angle-frequency Reciprocity and Covariance Matrix Reconstruction
abstract: The conventional wideband adaptive beam-forming method would deteriorate severely when the interferences are present in mainlobe. To overcome this problem, a wideband adaptive beamforming method for mainlobe interferences is proposed based on angle-frequency reciprocity and covariance matrix reconstruction. In the proposed method, the received wideband signals are firstly decomposed into narrow sub-bands. Based on the angle-frequency reciprocity in steering vector, the wideband matrix filter is constructed to estimate the number of mainlobe interferences. Sequentially, the echo data in element space is transformed to that in beam space, and then the beam-space eigen-projection matrix of each sub-band is calculated to suppress the mainlobe interferences. In the following, the array covariance matrix of each sub-band is reconstructed to eliminate the effect of noise perturbation and mainlobe interferences. Finally, the wideband adaptive weight vector is calculated based on the reconstructed covariance matrices. The effectiveness of proposed method is verified by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Energy-Constraint Resilient Consensus for Multiagent Systems under Denial-of-Service Attack
abstract: This article investigates the problem of energy-constraint resilient consensus for multi-agent systems under denial-of-service (DoS) attack. First, second-order multi-agent systems and DoS attacks are described. Second, considering the Dos attack, a new consensus control protocol, is proposed, where the whole energy supply is limited. Then, sufficient conditions on the control gain and duration of the DoS attacks are given in terms of linear matrix inequalities. Finally, an example is given to verify the feasibility of a resilient consensus scheme.

articleTitle: An Electromagnetic Parameter Estimation Method for Microwave Photonic Signal Based on PSO
abstract: Microwave photonics radar generates cross-band signals, which provides a basis for precise electromagnetic characteristics description and accurate identification of targets. As a result, a corresponding electromagnetic model parameter extraction method is urgently required under the cross-band and wide-angle condition. This paper proposes a parameter estimation method based on an improved Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The representation dictionary without range-azimuth coupling of scattering behavior for the data processed by PFA is firstly formed based on the attributed scattering center (ASC) model. Based on the proposed scattering behavior dictionary, the improved PSO algorithm and the CLEAN algorithm are implemented to estimate the electromagnetic parameters of each scattering center. Further, the simulated annealing (SA) algorithm is introduced to improve the method's capacity to find the global optimum. Finally, the structure of each scattering center can be identified according to the parameter estimation results. The processing results of simulation data verify the effectiveness of the algorithm. Compared with traditional algorithms, the proposed algorithm is insensitive to the initialization value and does not require image segmentation, which reduces the complexity of computation.

articleTitle: Nested Inter-element Spacing Constrained Array
abstract: Due to the mutual coupling effect, the performance of direction of arrival estimation and adaptive beamforming can be reduced to a certain extent. The interelement spacing constraint (ISC) array can maintain low mutual coupling via constraining the minimum inter-element spacing. However, the ISC array has no closed-form expressions for the sensor positions, so designing such arrays for large number of sensors is difficult. In this paper, we will design a nested interelement spacing constrained array (N-ISC) using the ISC and other sparse arrays to meet the requirement for the large number of sensors. Numerical simulations are conducted to verify the superiority of the N-ISC array.

articleTitle: Wideband Aperture-Coupled Antenna Based on Silicon-On-Glass
abstract: A wideband aperture-coupled antenna based on Silicon-On-Glass is presented. The proposed design consists of an aperture-coupled patch. The aperture is made some improments to broadening the bandwidth. Also, the metal columns on silicon suppress undesired surface-wave propagating on the Silicon-On-Glass, and consequently, enhance the radiation performances. The final design achieves <tex>$\text{VSWR} < 2.5$</tex> and peak <tex>$\text{gain} > 21.19\text{dBi}$</tex> at bandwidth of 17% (32 - 38 GHz) and this antenna has excellent radiation pattern performance from 32GHz to 38GHz. Simultaneously, the main beam of the E-plane and H-plane can scan from −30° to +30° with a gain fluctuation less than 1 dB and SLL less than −11 dB.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of change detection methods in Polarimetric SAR images based on probability statistical models
abstract: Change detection method in polarimetric SAR images considers polarization information and features. In order to make better use of polarization information and features for change detection, this paper compared and analyzed different change detection methods in polarimetric SAR image based on probability statistical method. Firstly, based on RADARSAT-2 polarimetric SAR data, four change detection methods were used to generate four change degree maps. Then, through four probability statistical model, we built the fitting models for the four kinds of change degree maps, and obtained 16 kinds of change detection results. The results showed that the 16 combination of change detection methods made full use of more ground information which contains in different polarization modes. Compared with other distribution fitting, the lognormal fitting distribution function can better fit the four change degree maps, and the change detection results are better. The overall accuracy (OA) can be improved by more than 1.53%, and the kappa coefficient can be improved by no less than 0.026. In addition, compared with 16 combined change detection methods, the Wishart-lognormal distribution change detection results are the best. The overall accuracy is 87.76% and kappa coefficient is 0.7469, which realizes the high-precision change detection of the study areas.

articleTitle: Joint Transceiver Design for Radar Communications Spectrum Sharing via Alternative Minimization
abstract: In this paper, we propose an alternative interference minimization method to design MIMO transceivers of radar and <tex>$K$</tex> communication systems. By alternating design radar waveform, filter, communication precoders and decoders, the overall interference can be minimized while guaranteeing the signal subspace is orthogonal. In order to analysis the feasibility of perfect interference cancellation, we firstly analyze its feasible conditions. Moreover, benefit from interference alignment constraints, radar system could still transmit orthogonal waveform to fully exploit the spatial degree of freedoms (DoF). We also analysis its feasibility conditions. The simulation result demonstrates the convergence and superiority of our proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Rao Test for Radar Target Detection in Sub-Gaussian Symmetric Alpha-Stable Sea Clutter
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive detector based on maximum a posteriori (MAP) Rao test specially for the sub-Gaussian symmetric alpha-stable (SGSαS) sea clutter background. Since SGSαS distribution does not have a closed-form probability density function (PDF) expression, there are few researches on the problem of target detection in SGSαS clutter background. In this paper, firstly the closed-form PDF expression of the SGSαS distribution is given in terms of the Fox's H-function. Then the MAP Rao-SGSαS detector in alpha-stable clutter is designed based on two-step MAP Rao test. Experimental results based on the simulated data verify the effectiveness of the proposed detector.

articleTitle: Research on the influence of track unevenness on the pointing errors of NSRT
abstract: NanShan 26 m Radio Telescope (NSRT) constructed in Nanshan Urumqi, Xinjiang, China, it is a fully steerable radio telescope, with the observing frequency up to 43 GHz. The antenna structure of NSRT is on track-roller. After a long period of operation, we found that the track unevenness is one of the factors that limit its pointing accuracy. To solve this problem, we measured the track profile curve and evaluated the mechanical axis deflection caused by the unevenness of the track by finite element analysis. The correctness of the pointing error evaluation result is verified by deploying a two-axis tilt meter on the antenna and using the actual pointing measurement on radio sources.

articleTitle: Fusion Classification of Finer-grained Human Activity Using MIMO UWB Bio-Radar
abstract: Channel to channel micro-Doppler signature (μDs) difference severely affects the comprehensive classification of human activity using multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) bio-radar. This paper combined our previously proposed channel evaluation technology, called relative signal-noise ratio in the time-frequency (T-F) domain (RSNR<inf>TF</inf>), with standard support vector machine (SVM) and K-Nearest neighbour (KNN) classifiers to realize improved fusion classification. Experimental results show that the RSNRtf-based classifiers could averagely improve the classification accuracy with 5% compared to conventional reference methods, although under a relatively narrow through-wall detection field (within ±20°). Under free-space or wide-flied (wide angle) detection conditions, this improvement performance of fusion classification would be more significant.

articleTitle: A Multi-Task Quadrotor Uumanned Aerial Vehicles Swarm Control System
abstract: This electronic document introduces a swarm control system of quadrotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV), which has the ability to perform multiple tasks simultaneously. The system adopts a multiple commanders in the loop control method that is different from the traditional single commander in the loop. In this system, the quadrotor UAV swarm is divided into several groups, and each group is controlled by the leader-followers mode. The leader of each group is controlled by the master commander or the slave commander. This control architecture ensures that each UAV group has good flexibility and safety when performing multiple tasks. In order to verify the ability of the quadrotor UAV swarm system, we have carried out a large number of outfield flight experiments. Some experiment results are presented in the end of this paper.

articleTitle: Generalized Zero-Shot Recognition of SAR Target via Conditional Disentangled Learning
abstract: Most of the existing methods for automatic target recognition (ATR) in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images only focus on the seen classes in the testing stage, but ignore the possibility of the unseen classes. To address this problem, a generalized zero-shot SAR target recognition method based on conditional disentangled representation learning is proposed, which can be used for both seen and unseen classes. The recognition framework is based on the variational autoencoders (VAE) to disentangle the continuous and discrete latent variables. The unseen classes are recognized by continuous variables, while the discrete ones are used for the seen classes. In addition, the class labels of seen classes are incorporated as condition information to improve the inter-class discrimination in two disentangled variable spaces. The generalized zero-shot experiment results show that the proposed method achieves considerable recognition accuracy for both seen and unseen classes.

Author Keywords: Synthetic aperture radar automatic target recognition

articleTitle: Beamforming Based on Multi-Kernel Support Vector Machine
abstract: The performance of beamforming based on support vector machine is affected by many parameters of support vector machine. The selection method of parameters is limited. So there is no general method at present. In this paper, a beamforming algorithm based on multi-kernel support vector machine is proposed. Firstly, multi-kernel support vector machines are constructed by combining multiple kernel functions, and then the multi-kernel support vector machines are applied to the beamforming problem. The algorithm can avoid the problems of complex parameter selection and large amount of computation in support vector machine. The simulation results show that the algorithm has good performance.
